articles.headline: Update: peace table — Kushner says Europe was kept out of Abu Dhabi because Putin finds it "provocative", and calls the war "a proxy war where Europe is funding and arming Ukraine"
articles.summary:
**Lede.** In the MD MEETS podcast of Axel Springer CEO Mathias Döpfner, released on 25 November, US envoy Jared Kushner said: "Europe was not included in Abu Dhabi because President Putin sees a lot of provocative statements out of Europe and a lot of provocative actions out of Europe." He described the war as "effectively ... a proxy war where Europe is funding and arming Ukraine against Russia", and said Putin "has showed restraint. He's agreed not to use nuclear weapons" (Kyiv Post, Clash Report, dpa).

**Context.** Kushner said Washington now works with an expanded group of eight European and NATO representatives (including Germany, the UK, France, Italy, Poland and EU institutions) and that "we are not going to decide anything without agreement with Europe and without agreement of Ukraine". He proposed permanent communication channels, hotlines and de-escalation mechanisms between Moscow and NATO, said that "most lines in Europe have changed over time", and expects the largest prisoner exchange of the war "very soon, before" the holidays (Kyiv Post; Anadolu Agency, Turkish state agency). The same evening Trump and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte met at Mar-a-Lago; the White House statement said they discussed "the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war", the war with Iran and defence spending (RTÉ). Russia's side: TASS (Russian state agency), in a post reposted by @F_CEAFE, quoted Yulia Zhdanova, Russia's chief delegate to the Vienna talks on military security, as saying the European Commission's rejection of Moscow's proposal for bilateral consultations on European security "demonstrates that Brussels is not prepared to ease tensions".

**Background (CEAFE archive):** @F_CEAFE has followed the Witkoff–Kushner channel since their arrival in Moscow (repost of Kirill Dmitriev, 5 Sep. 2026: https://x.com/i/status/2096221861180833918). On 11 November 2026 it reposted Kushner saying that Europe identifying one person to speak on its behalf would be "a bigger achievement" than other steps in the talks (https://x.com/i/status/2120598300671832248), the same theme of a Europe without a single voice at the table.

**CEAFE comment:** For as long as Europeans keep measuring our weight country by country, the comparison with the United States or China is lost in advance.

**What to watch:** the European Council's answer today (story 2); the date and size of the prisoner exchange; any Russian confirmation of Kushner's nuclear assurance (none found in Kremlin or MFA sources at the time of writing).

**Sources:** Kyiv Post: https://www.kyivpost.com/post/91223 ; Clash Report: https://clashreport.com/world/articles/kushner-putin-nuclear-weapons-restraint-nk573kns11 ; @F_CEAFE reposts of Kushner's clips (Clash Report, M. Simonyan): https://x.com/i/status/2125697236055281758 , https://x.com/i/status/2125720925303906587 ; Kushner on X: https://x.com/i/status/2125686466336489970 ; dpa: https://x.com/i/status/2125828649387499663 ; RTÉ on the Trump–Rutte statement: https://www.rte.ie/news/ukraine/2026/1126/1600710-trump-nato-ukraine/ ; NATO advisory: https://www.nato.int/en/news-and-events/events/media-advisories/2026/11/24/nato-secretary-general-to-visit-the-united-states-of-america ; TASS via @F_CEAFE: https://x.com/i/status/2125678724578218178
articles.why: Washington's envoy confirms that Moscow decides whether Europeans sit at the table, and that the US describes the war Europe pays for as Europe's proxy war. The EU is the largest financier of Ukraine, yet its seat depends on Putin's approval and Washington's goodwill. The number of national envoys in the "group of eight" shows the cost of not speaking with one voice: the Union already has a High Representative.

articles.headline: European Council opens on a €45 billion loan for Ukraine split by an opt-out, and on a budget fight that includes a 30% cut to defence and space
articles.summary:
**Lede.** EU leaders meet in Brussels on 26–27 November with a proposed €45 billion loan to fund Ukraine in 2027 on the table. Slovakia, Czechia, Hungary and Bulgaria object to taking part, especially in the €25 billion military strand; the Commission has offered them an opt-out from that part while keeping the €20 billion civilian strand, and Chancellor Merz has threatened to block the 2028–2034 budget unless all 27 contribute (Euronews; France 24; EUalive).

**Context.** Defence Commissioner Andrius Kubilius told the EU Military Committee at chiefs-of-defence level that the CARD Report 2026 "shows that we risk missing our strategic target of defence readiness by 2030", and relayed the space industry's warning that the proposed 30% cut to the MFF defence and space line "would make it impossible to deliver the EU's space ambitions" (@F_CEAFE reposted him). Marine Le Pen wrote that she "will not pay €20 billion of net contribution to the European Union" and wants to bring it back to €6 billion, "the level accepted by Jacques Chirac at the time of enlargement" (@F_CEAFE repost; CEAFE translation), and Euronews reports that member states are discussing new EU-wide taxes to fund the next budget.

**Background (CEAFE archive):** The financing fight is not new: in December 2025 @F_CEAFE reposted Sweden's EU representation and Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo calling for a reparations loan to Ukraine based on frozen Russian assets (https://x.com/i/status/1998190157556765179).

**CEAFE comment:** If Europe wants to sit as an equal, it has to pool what is today fragmented.

**What to watch:** the conclusions on the loan and the opt-outs; whether the MFF defence and space line is restored; Hungary's and Slovakia's positions; the December follow-up summit.

**Sources:** European Council meeting page: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/meetings/european-council/2026/11/26-27/ ; Euronews: https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/26/eu-budget-and-ukraine-aid-headed-for-collision-at-turbulent-summit ; France 24 live: https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261126-live-eu-leaders-face-showdown-over-ukraine-funding-as-divisions-deepen ; EUalive: https://eualive.net/eu-tables-e45bn-ukraine-loan-as-slovakia-hungary-czechia-and-bulgaria-opt-out/ ; Kubilius keynote: https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/speech_26_2586 ; Kubilius on X: https://x.com/i/status/2125700387936108785 ; @F_CEAFE reposts of Kubilius and Le Pen: https://x.com/i/status/2125661996825907429 , https://x.com/i/status/2125763994220630043

**Images:** France 24 live-page image of EU leaders (https://pbs.twimg.com/news_img/2125828765762920449/BrAO08jM?format=jpg&name=orig).
articles.why: the same summit has to decide whether the Union pays for Ukraine as one, or as a coalition with opt-outs, and whether it cuts the budget line for its own defence and space. An opt-out on the military strand would turn a common effort into a menu, as Washington and Moscow decide the table without the EU (story 1). Only a common budget gives the scale no EU member state has alone.

articles.headline: Update: NATO allies expect Washington to delay its troop-cut decision for Europe; the US stands down an Apache squadron in South Korea
articles.summary:
**Lede.** NATO countries expect the US to delay past early December, possibly to late December or after the new year, its final decision on cutting troop numbers in Europe, as the administration focuses on a Ukraine deal, Bloomberg reported. Allies now expect a cut of about 5,000 of the 80,000 US troops in Europe, mostly from Germany, with eastern-flank countries, especially Poland, expected to gain troops; the Pentagon said its posture review is ongoing.

**Context.** Bloomberg adds that Washington "wants to use its bases in Europe to project power in the Middle East and elsewhere", and recalls Under Secretary Elbridge Colby's remark that the US "will be prepared to adapt to support those peace negotiations" when asked whether Russia's demands would count in the review. In Asia, US Forces Korea confirmed the inactivation of an Apache helicopter squadron in South Korea (Yonhap), and Defense Secretary Hegseth may visit Japan on 8 December (The Japan Times), after Washington asked Tokyo to triple its payments for US bases (20:30 brief).

**What to watch:** Hegseth's posture announcement; Germany's and Poland's reactions; whether Russia's demands on NATO deployments appear in the peace texts.

**Sources:** Bloomberg via Mint: https://www.livemint.com/politics/nato-allies-expect-us-to-delay-decision-on-troop-cuts-in-europe-11795637091706.html ; TASS on X (Russian state agency): https://x.com/i/status/2125808970778485010 ; Yonhap: https://x.com/i/status/2125823275997835579 ; The Japan Times on Hegseth: https://x.com/i/status/2125798390726303850.
articles.why: Europe's defence posture is again set by a US review whose timing is linked to talks with Moscow, while the bases are kept because they serve US power projection. A smaller US presence is coming in any case; the question is whether Europe fills the gap with its own forces and industry, or waits.

articles.headline: Update: Section 301 — Tokyo protests, Singapore is "very disappointed", Brazil denounces pressure; Beijing signals no retaliation, while the EU still has no answer
articles.summary:
**Lede.** Japan protested to Washington over the proposed 15% levy and the allegation of excess capacity (The Japan Times; Bloomberg). Singapore said it was "very disappointed" and disagreed with the USTR findings (CNA). Brazil voiced outrage at proposed tariffs on its aircraft and sugar, saying they aim to pressure it to change rules on PIX payments and digital commerce (Xinhua, Chinese state media). China rejected the overcapacity claims but signalled it is unlikely to retaliate against tariffs that stay within the bounds of the trade truce (Bloomberg).

**Context.** On 25 November USTR found the practices of 14 economies, including the EU, "unreasonable" and proposed a 15% tariff on all EU goods (20:30 brief, story 1). The Global Times (Chinese state media) reported that MOFCOM welcomed the EU's removal of the Chinese firm Yusha Group from its Russia-related list. The WSJ noted that the new tariff round came as a key inflation measure hit a three-year high.

**What to watch:** the Foreign Affairs Council (Trade) on 30 November; any EU statement after the European Council; MOFCOM's formal position.

**Sources:** The Japan Times: https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/2026/11/26/economy/japan-protests-trump-new-tariff/ ; CNA: https://www.channelnewsasia.com/singapore/singapore-us-tariffs-meti-trump-6583911 ; Xinhua on Brazil: https://x.com/i/status/2125799840248664078 ; Bloomberg on China: https://x.com/i/status/2125800493721010494 ; WSJ: https://x.com/i/status/2125825425381142929 ; USTR release: https://ustr.gov/about/policy-offices/press-office/press-releases/2026/november/ustr-makes-determinations-and-proposes-actions-14-section-301-investigations-relating-structural ; @F_CEAFE repost of USTR: https://x.com/i/status/2125669000369917960
articles.why: Tokyo, Singapore and Brasília answered within hours; Brussels' line remains to "study" the findings and keep the 15% ceiling. China's restraint is calculated, but it is backed by countermeasures it has already used. A Union that does not answer as one invites the next round.

articles.headline: The "USAID Files": Washington publishes 248 internal documents on the agency's media and Big Tech work, including Ukraine and Russia
articles.summary:
**Lede.** USAID's website now opens on a "USAID Files" page with 248 internal memos, emails, briefings and videos about its work on disinformation and its contacts with Meta, YouTube and Google, posted on 24 November "in the interest of transparency and accountability" (The Boston Report). An undated "Big Tech Engagement Action Plan" proposed private "inclusion lists" of Russian independent media and civil-society groups, curated by trusted NGOs, so that platforms would favour them in search, recommendations and ads; the State Department had opposed the idea over freedom-of-expression concerns (Reclaim The Net; The Boston Report).

**Context.** The documents mix drafts, proposals and finished memos, and do not show whether the companies adopted the lists (The Boston Report). A Greek outlet's tally of the files puts Ukraine-related media funding at more than $267 million, while warning that it mixes approved grants and draft budgets (ELTV, not re-verified). @F_CEAFE reposted eight posts on the files the same evening, framing USAID as an instrument of influence over media in Ukraine, Russia and Europe. The usaid.gov page itself was not opened for this brief.

**What to watch:** official State Department or USAID statements on the release; European reactions; claims about specific European outlets, which need verification document by document.

**Sources:** The Boston Report: https://thebostonreport.com/2026/11/24/usaid-files-disinformation-meta-youtube-google/ ; Reclaim The Net: https://reclaimthenet.org/usaid-files-the-inclusion-list-the-state-department-opposed ; ELTV: https://eltvnews.com/en/news/ekatommyria-dolaria-se-mesa-enimerosis-mi-kerdoskopikoys-organismoys-kai-influencers-ti-deichnoyn-ta-archeia-tis-usaid/ ; @F_CEAFE reposts: https://x.com/i/status/2125675503566647414 , https://x.com/i/status/2125675762174845055 , https://x.com/i/status/2125764255190544702
articles.why: whatever one thinks of the programmes, the files show a foreign government planning how platforms rank news seen by Europeans and Ukrainians. Information sovereignty is part of sovereignty: Europe's media pluralism should not depend on decisions taken in Washington, by one administration or the next.

articles.headline: Asia: Kim calls for more nuclear weapons after declining to meet Trump; Japan to deploy hypersonic Type-25 missiles on Hokkaido
articles.summary:
**Lede.** North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, touring nuclear facilities, inspected warheads and a fissile-material plant and urged a wider deployment of tactical nuclear weapons, KCNA (North Korean state media) reported, days after declining Trump's offer to meet in China (Reuters, Al Jazeera, Politico). TASS (Russian state agency), citing NHK, reported that Japan's Ministry of Defense plans to deploy Type-25 missile systems with hypersonic glide vehicles on Hokkaido, the island closest to Russia, in early December (@F_CEAFE repost).

**Context.** On Taiwan, the island's defence ministry reported 2 PLA aircraft sorties and 6 PLAN vessels around Taiwan up to 06:00 local time. China urged Japan at the Chemical Weapons Convention conference in The Hague to speed up the destruction of chemical weapons abandoned in China (Xinhua, Chinese state media).

**What to watch:** KCNA's next statements; any Russian reaction to the Hokkaido deployment; Hegseth's possible visit to Japan on 8 December.

**Sources:** Reuters on X: https://x.com/i/status/2125816894917640344 ; Al Jazeera: https://x.com/i/status/2125794171340624270 ; Politico: https://x.com/i/status/2125768045742153852 ; TASS via @F_CEAFE: https://x.com/i/status/2125663708038787479 ; Taiwan MND: https://x.com/i/status/2125756427130302732 ; Xinhua: https://x.com/i/status/2125772569546764319
articles.why: the Indo-Pacific arms race, nuclear and conventional, is speeding up while US attention and forces are spread thin (story 4). Europe has partners in Asia but no seat in these equations, unless it acts as one.

articles.headline: Israel: the court recommends dropping the most serious case against Netanyahu; Israel adds $5 billion to its defence budget
articles.summary:
**Lede.** Judges in Netanyahu's corruption trial recommended that the prosecution drop Case 4000, reconsider Case 2000 and seek a deal in Case 1000; Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara said the prosecution would review the recommendations (Times of Israel; Jerusalem Post; i24NEWS). Netanyahu wrote on X: "Today the trial collapsed" (CEAFE translation from Hebrew). Haaretz's editorial urged the attorney general to refuse ("the judges chose the easy way out"; Haaretz often paywalled, headline only).

**Context.** Breaking Defense reported that Israel increased its defence budget by $5 billion amid concerns over future funding (@F_CEAFE repost). In Gaza, Al Jazeera reported at least 16 Palestinians killed in Israeli attacks in 24 hours; the IDF said it struck a senior Hamas member. Israel's MFA said 65,000 tents approved for Gaza remain undelivered by the UN.

**What to watch:** the attorney general's decision; the Knesset vote on the inquiry commission; US aid talks.

**Sources:** Times of Israel: https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/court-recommends-dropping-or-reconsidering-2-out-of-3-cases-against-netanyahu-in-severe-blow-to-prosecution/ ; Jerusalem Post: https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/crime-in-israel/article-916054 ; i24NEWS: https://www.i24news.tv/en/news/israel/politics/artc-judges-in-netanyahu-trial-to-ag-we-recommend-dropping-case-4000-re-examining-case-2000 ; Haaretz on X: https://x.com/i/status/2125828186315325496 ; Breaking Defense via @F_CEAFE: https://x.com/i/status/2125666882531533074 ; Al Jazeera: https://x.com/i/status/2125797946109132801
articles.why: a strengthened Netanyahu, with a larger defence budget, faces the Knesset's debate on an inquiry commission (his own reposts refer to the vote). European governments that buy Israeli weapon systems should note that each such purchase is jobs, R&D and control lost for European industry.

- **EU–Western Balkans:** the Council published the Brussels declaration of 25 November; von der Leyen said the EU is "on track to open and close over 100 chapters" this year. https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/11/25/brussels-declaration-25-november-2026/

- **Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia:** Canada "strongly condemns" strikes on Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District and Türkiye's presidency condemned the attack; CENTCOM's commander issued a statement (see Conflicts). https://x.com/i/status/2125765557593231751

articles.headline: Update: Section 301 — Washington finds the EU and 13 other economies "unreasonable" and proposes a 15% tariff on all EU goods; Brussels rejects the premise, Beijing reserves countermeasures
articles.summary:
**Lede.** US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer determined on 25 November that the "acts, policies, and practices" of 14 economies relating to structural excess capacity "are unreasonable and burden or restrict U.S. commerce", making them actionable under Section 301(b) of the 1974 Trade Act: China, the European Union, Singapore, Switzerland, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Japan and India. No determination was made on Mexico or Norway.

**Context.** For the EU, USTR lists "industrial plans to expand manufacturing", export credit, "sustained market access barriers", "preferential lending through centralized investment banks" and "failure to address global excess capacity", including imports and FDI from non-market economies. It proposes to "consider applying on all goods of the EU a tariff rate of 15 percent, net of MFN rates and existing Section 301 tariffs, with exemptions for certain goods", taking into account Section 232 duties and the EU–US framework agreement. Other proposals: China up to 20% on goods not listed in the annexes and up to 10% on Annex A goods, with Annex B exemptions, reflecting the Kuala Lumpur arrangement of 30 Oct 2025, Japan and Switzerland up to 15%, Singapore up to 20%, India up to 25% (17% with a trade agreement), Vietnam up to 35% (20% with an agreement). Written comments are due by 5 January 2027 and hearings start on 25 January 2027; a senior US official told Politico the duties would take effect "in January at the earliest" and that the higher of this tariff and the 10% forced-labour tariff would apply, not both. Commission deputy chief spokesperson Olof Gill: "We will study the findings. At the same time we strongly reject the premise that Europe is a source of structural overcapacity… We regret the lack of joint action", adding that the 15% all-inclusive ceiling of the joint statement must be respected "in full, including when combined with existing duties". China's Ministry of Commerce called the finding unilateralism and protectionism, urged dialogue and reserved "the right to take necessary measures" (China Daily, Chinese state media). Same day, USTR also proposed tougher Section 301 measures on Brazil (Embraer shares fell almost 10%, Bloomberg). @F_CEAFE quoted USTR's post listing the 14 economies and posted the EU and China paragraphs of the notice.

**Background (CEAFE archive):** @F_CEAFE has tracked the Section 301 "overcapacity" probe since it was opened against 16 economies (Global Times repost, 27 Aug. 2026), after Washington's earlier 10–12.5% tariff threat on EU goods over forced labour, which @F_CEAFE quoted on 24 July 2026 asking "Is there a limit to what we Europeans have to put up with?". Today @F_CEAFE also reposted USTR's separate Section 301 proposal on Brazil.

**CEAFE comment:** The EU as a whole can bear comparison; each capital on its own cannot. That is the difference that matters.

**What to watch:** Greer's expected call-in to the Foreign Affairs Council (Trade) on 30 November (Politico Europe); member states' positions; the 5 January comment deadline and the 25 January hearings; any MOFCOM countermeasure list.

**Sources:** USTR press release (25 Nov): https://ustr.gov/about/policy-offices/press-office/press-releases/2026/november/ustr-makes-determinations-and-proposes-actions-14-section-301-investigations-relating-structural ; USTR on X: https://x.com/i/status/2125593464138072571 ; @F_CEAFE quote: https://x.com/i/status/2125594279724597323 , notice excerpt: https://x.com/i/status/2125594889010479332 ; Politico Europe: https://www.politico.eu/article/eu-rejects-donald-trump-case-for-new-tariffs/ ; Eunews: https://www.eunews.it/en/2026/11/25/threats-of-new-tariffs-from-the-us-the-commission-responds-overcapacity-is-affecting-us-we-are-not-the-cause/ ; Reuters via Business Recorder: https://www.brecorder.com/news/40450714 ; China Daily (state media): https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202611/25/WS6b06a88ee4b03ebf8519ea08.html ; USTR Brazil: https://x.com/i/status/2125581264031817919 ; Bloomberg (Embraer): https://x.com/i/status/2125620654368014599

**Images:** USTR notice excerpt (EU, China, India paragraphs), posted by @F_CEAFE: https://pbs.twimg.com/media/HX-hIhIWAAEs7Oh.png
articles.why: the 2025 Turnberry deal did not end the pressure; it set the level. Washington now lists the EU's industrial policy, the EIB's lending and its trade defence choices as "unreasonable" practices, while Brussels' only stated line is that the total must stay at 15%. The contrast with Beijing is plain: China reserves countermeasures, the EU says it will "study" the findings. Only a common EU answer has the weight to change Washington's calculation; no member state can do it alone.

articles.headline: The Netherlands tells Washington and Beijing it wants the US MATCH Act stopped: "We don't want unilateral decisions that have extraterritorial effect"
articles.summary:
**Lede.** In the same line as the Section 301 proposal for a 15% tariff on all EU goods (story 1), Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen said in Beijing on Wednesday that the Netherlands is working to prevent the US Congress from passing the Multilateral Alignment of Technology Controls on Hardware (MATCH) Act: "Our focus is on making sure that the MATCH act will not be passed" (Reuters).

**Context.** Congress is debating whether to attach the bipartisan bill to the National Defense Authorization Act before the outgoing Congress ends. It would force allies, including the Netherlands and Japan, to adopt tougher export controls on chipmaking tools or face unilateral US restrictions on their equipment, including ASML's immersion DUV lithography machines. ASML expects China to account for about 20% of this year's sales. On Tuesday Dutch MPs called the bill "disastrous" for ASML (VVD) and "unacceptable" (JA21); Volt's Laurens Dassen asked for European measures to shield the company (Reuters). Berendsen met Foreign Minister Wang Yi and Vice-Premier Ding Xuexiang; he told de Volkskrant his message to Beijing was the same as to Washington and that the Netherlands decides its own export system. Xinhua (Chinese state media) reported Wang Yi saying China "stands ready to work with the Netherlands in a spirit of openness and pragmatism". The SCMP (owned by Alibaba) links the renewed US push to the Nvidia saga.

**Background (CEAFE archive):** On 24 May 2026 @F_CEAFE reposted that the Dutch government was pushing back against new US restrictions affecting ASML exports to China.

**CEAFE comment:** Here is another example of why Europeans need to act together.

**What to watch:** the NDAA text in December; whether The Hague asks for EU backing (anti-coercion instrument); any Chinese gesture to the Netherlands on Nexperia or rare earths.

**Sources:** Reuters via Euronext: https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/dutch-government-working-prevent-passing-us-match-bill-minister-says ; Reuters on Dutch MPs (24 Nov), via StreetInsider: https://www.streetinsider.com/Reuters/Dutch+lawmakers+urge+government+to+resist+US+MATCH+bill+targeting+ASML/27395726.html ; de Volkskrant: https://www.volkskrant.nl/economie/nederland-wil-geen-amerikaanse-bemoeienis-bij-export-machines-asml-naar-china~bcc262190/ ; Reuters post: https://x.com/i/status/2125645730442277295 ; Xinhua (state media): https://x.com/i/status/2125625700938113235 ; Global Times (state media) on the visit: https://x.com/i/status/2125644685410750617 ; SCMP: https://www.scmp.com/economy/policy/article/3375565/dutch-minister-heads-china-nvidia-saga-revives-us-push-tougher-asml-curbs
articles.why: this is the pattern CEAFE has flagged, in the same line as the Section 301 tariffs on EU goods (story 1): the Netherlands already applies US-driven restrictions on China, and Washington now wants to legislate the rest for it. A single member state is caught between two powers; the instrument that could balance it, a common EU export-control and anti-coercion response, is not on the table. Europe's leverage (ASML is a chokepoint for US chipmakers too) remains unused.

articles.headline: Update: peace table — Lavrov says Europeans would "put their feet up" on the table; Rutte says Trump is "testing Putin"
articles.summary:
**Lede.** Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, speaking in Gomel after a joint board meeting of the Russian and Belarusian foreign ministries, accused the European Commission of "megaphone diplomacy" and said: "We have never had any contact with the European Commission about negotiations to resolve the Ukrainian crisis" (TASS, Russian state agency).

**Context.** Lavrov said Moscow wants to know what role the "European five" (France, Germany, the UK, Italy, Poland) plus the EU and NATO would play in the talks resumed in Abu Dhabi: "With those manners and those intentions, they'll sit down at the negotiating table and immediately put their feet up on it. We don't need that." Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Europe keeps putting out "contradictory statements" on dialogue (TASS). The Commission said on 23 November that it is aware of Putin's invitation to Moscow but will take part only in a multilateral format, and that talks on Europe's security architecture can start only after a ceasefire (EC midday briefing). NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, asked about Trump calling Putin "my friend", said Trump is "testing Putin", including at the Shenzhen meeting, and that Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff "are working" on the issue; on Kushner's claim that Russia might accept Article 5-like guarantees, Moscow has said it does not (Clash Report clips). Zelensky repeated that withdrawing from Donbas would mean losing the war (post reposted by @F_CEAFE).

**What to watch:** the European Council on 26–27 November; the date and format of the next Abu Dhabi round; any written European position sent to Moscow.

**Sources:** TASS (state agency): https://tass.com/politics/2224711 ; BelTA (Belarusian state agency): https://belta.by/politics/view/glava-mid-rossii-evrokomissija-zanimaetsja-megafonnoj-diplomatiej-812609-2026/ ; Russian MFA on X: https://x.com/i/status/2125649353062912054 ; TASS on Peskov: https://x.com/i/status/2125610495734616169 ; EC midday briefing 23 Nov: https://audiovisual.ec.europa.eu/en/media/video/I-298394 ; Rutte (Clash Report): https://x.com/i/status/2125617132700377433 , https://x.com/i/status/2125617663942512721 , https://x.com/i/status/2125618941133484135 ; Zelensky on Donbas (repost by @F_CEAFE): https://x.com/i/status/2125588267718308255
articles.why: Moscow is using the EU's own ambiguity (who speaks, with what mandate) to keep it out, while Washington mediates. The "European team" is a group of national capitals plus the institutions, not a single negotiator with its own means. As CEAFE has argued (peace-table framing, 18 Nov), the EU is absent where the decisions are taken because no member state has the weight alone.

articles.headline: Update: eastern flank — Poland plans a no-fly zone on its border with Ukraine; RAF hides aircraft from drones; Norway and the UK pool P-8 support
articles.summary:
**Lede.** Poland plans a no-fly zone along its eastern border, reaching from about 10 to several dozen kilometres inland, with rules expected to apply from late December 2026 or early January 2027, while its request that NATO intercept Russian missiles over Ukraine has found no support so far (Kyiv Independent, Anadolu, Rzeczpospolita).

**Context.** Deputy Defence Minister Cezary Tomczyk told Rzeczpospolita that NATO does not want to shoot down Russian missiles over Ukraine and that a no-fly zone is needed in eastern Poland. In the UK, Sky News reported that the Royal Air Force is moving aircraft into hangars and hardened shelters at night against possible drone threats (reposted by @F_CEAFE). Norway and the UK signed an agreement letting each country receive, handle, service and inspect the other's P-8A Poseidon maritime patrol aircraft (Norwegian Armed Forces). @F_CEAFE also reposted a Finnish MP recommending a WSJ report that the Baltic Sea came closer to a Russia–NATO military clash this autumn than publicly known (WSJ article not re-read here). Sweden announced an extra winter support package for Ukraine (Swedish MFA).

**What to watch:** Polish regulation on the zone; NATO's response; UK MoD statement on RAF dispersal.

**Sources:** Kyiv Independent: https://kyivindependent.com/poland-plans-no-fly-zone-near-ukraine-border-asks-nato-to-intercept-russian-missiles-over-ukraine/ ; Anadolu (state agency): https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/poland-plans-no-fly-zone-along-eastern-border-to-bolster-nato-flank/4137749 ; Rzeczpospolita: https://www.rp.pl/wojsko/art45541251-wiceszef-mon-nato-nie-chce-zestrzeliwac-rosyjskich-rakiet-nad-ukraina ; Sky News (repost by @F_CEAFE): https://x.com/i/status/2125568013885755540 ; Forsvaret: https://www.forsvaret.no/en/news/articles/nor-uk-p8 ; Henri Vanhanen on WSJ (repost by @F_CEAFE): https://x.com/i/status/2125592293096767870 ; Swedish MFA: https://x.com/i/status/2125560426402382330
articles.why: each frontline state is taking its own measures (no-fly zone, shelters, bilateral maintenance pools) because the collective decision is not coming. The Norway–UK P-8 deal is useful but shows the dependence: both fly a US aircraft. A shared European air-defence and maritime-patrol capability would give Europeans the decision and the industrial base.

articles.headline: North Korea expels Switzerland's new diplomatic office over sanctions on a camp linked to Ukrainian children
articles.summary:
**Lede.** North Korea ordered Switzerland to close its diplomatic office in Pyongyang, declared its head, Sylvain Astier, persona non grata and gave him 48 hours to leave, in response to Swiss sanctions on the Songdowon International Children's Camp (KCNA, North Korean state media, via Yonhap and AP).

**Context.** Switzerland adopted the measures in line with the EU's 21st sanctions package against Russia; the EU says the camp hosts children from Russian-occupied areas of Ukraine in coordination with Russia, and Bern says it is responsible for "forced assimilation, including indoctrination, and militarized education of Ukrainian minors" (Kyodo). The Swiss foreign ministry "regrets this decision"; relations continue through the Swiss embassy in Beijing and North Korea's embassy in Bern. The office had reopened on 19 October. Kim Yo Jong had threatened the closure on Tuesday.

**What to watch:** whether Sweden, Poland or other European states with a presence in Pyongyang face similar pressure; any Russian comment.

**Sources:** Yonhap: https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261125005600315 ; AP: https://apnews.com/article/north-korea-switzerland-diplomat-russia-ukraine-a39dbc92d195e69443ce66913a3dff7e ; Al Jazeera: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/25/switzerland-regrets-closure-of-north-korea-office-over-sanctions-feud ; swissinfo (Keystone-SDA): https://www.swissinfo.ch/ger/aussendepartement-best%c3%a4tigt-schliessung-von-b%c3%bcro-in-pj%c3%b6ngjang/92437428 ; Kyodo: https://english.kyodonews.net/articles/-/92578 ; Al Jazeera on X: https://x.com/i/status/2125649322197090413
articles.why: a neutral state that aligns with EU sanctions pays a diplomatic price, and North Korea openly defends a site the EU links to the deportation of Ukrainian children, another sign of the Moscow–Pyongyang alignment. It also shows the reach of EU sanctions when partners adopt them.

articles.headline: EU–Western Balkans summit: "the future is in the EU", but Growth Plan money tied to the Belgrade–Pristina dialogue
articles.summary:
**Lede.** EU and Western Balkans leaders met in Brussels for their second summit this year; the declaration reaffirms that the region's future lies in the EU, calls for faster credible reforms and links funds from the Reform and Growth Facility to measurable progress in the Belgrade–Pristina dialogue (Council; RTS; Srpske Novine).

**Context.** European Council President António Costa opened the summit ("our second Summit this year, reflecting the intensity of our political engagement"). The Council says the EU is the region's leading economic partner and investor. According to Serbian media, the text also demands implementation of the remaining Succession Issues obligations and rejects the glorification of war crimes, genocide denial and revisionism. Euronews asked whether Serbia's new government can revive its accession bid. The European Parliament the same day welcomed the EU's new political partnership with Syria.

**What to watch:** Serbia's reform steps; Kosovo's reaction to the conditionality; the next accession clusters (Montenegro, Albania).

**Sources:** Council: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/meetings/international-summit/2026/11/25/ ; Costa on X: https://x.com/i/status/2125642945168867454 ; EU Council on X: https://x.com/i/status/2125622892503212221 ; Commission (enlargement): https://enlargement.ec.europa.eu/news/turning-momentum-lasting-progress-president-von-der-leyen-eu-western-balkans-summit-2026-11-25_en ; RTS: https://www.rts.rs/vesti/politika/6092096/deklaracija-samita-eu-zapadni-balkan-prosirenje-je-realna-mogucnost-koju-treba-iskoristiti.html ; Srpske Novine: https://srpske.rs/en/news/politika/2026/11/25/brussels-declaration-ties-growth-plan-money-to-pristina-dialogue ; Euronews: https://x.com/i/status/2125647777711423699
articles.why: enlargement is the EU's main geopolitical tool in its own neighbourhood; conditioning money on the Kosovo–Serbia dialogue keeps leverage where Russia, China, Türkiye and the Gulf states compete for influence.

articles.headline: Asia: Washington wants Japan to triple its payments for US bases; Tokyo eyes a new anti-ship missile
articles.summary:
**Lede.** The United States is asking Japan to triple its spending on maintaining US military bases, to more than $19 billion over the next five years, while Japan has offered a 40% increase to $1.9 billion a year, according to Nikkei as relayed by TASS (screenshot posted by @F_CEAFE); the two sides hope to agree by the end of 2026.

**Context.** @F_CEAFE also posted Kyodo's report that Japan is eyeing a new anti-ship missile in its updated defence build-up plan; TASS (Russian state agency) reports Japan's MoD will deploy Type-25 missile systems with hypersonic glide vehicles on Hokkaido in early December. Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi held a phone call with British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband (Chinese MFA spokesperson). China's Shenzhou-24 took a Pakistani astronaut, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, to the Tiangong station with two Chinese crew, the first foreign astronaut there; Xi and Zardari exchanged messages (Xinhua, Chinese state media).

**What to watch:** Japan–US host-nation support talks; Japan's revised build-up plan; any readout of the Wang–Miliband call from London.

**Sources:** @F_CEAFE (TASS screenshot): https://x.com/i/status/2125598264573726990 ; Kyodo (posted by @F_CEAFE): https://english.kyodonews.net/articles/-/92619 ; TASS on Type-25: https://x.com/i/status/2125619437101523192 ; Chinese MFA (Lin Jian, Wang–Miliband): https://x.com/i/status/2125597718735388854 ; Xinhua (Shenzhou-24): https://x.com/i/status/2125628845776879664

**Images:** TASS Telegram post citing Nikkei (screenshot): https://pbs.twimg.com/media/HX-kWrHXIAEIPPj.png
articles.why: the same "pay more for protection" demand Europeans hear is being made of Japan, in figures. Allies that rely on US bases pay the bill without control. In parallel, China is turning space cooperation into diplomacy with Pakistan.

articles.headline: In brief
articles.summary:
- **Israel.** Judges in Netanyahu's corruption trial cast heavy doubt on the most serious charges and urged prosecutors to reconsider Cases 4000 and 2000; there is no acquittal and Case 1000 continues (Times of Israel; Straits Times). Netanyahu claimed vindication. Likud challenged results at 120 polling stations (Anadolu). A bill to set up a state commission of inquiry into 7 October passed a preliminary Knesset reading (Gadi Eisenkot, reposted by @F_CEAFE). https://www.timesofisrael.com/court-casts-heavy-doubt-over-most-serious-netanyahu-charges-in-huge-blow-to-prosecution/ ; https://x.com/i/status/2125636758041743489 ; https://x.com/i/status/2125571072313655604

- **Iran.** Foreign Minister Araghchi rejected Israeli accusations that Iran is developing chemical weapons, saying Israel wants to drag the US into another war (Al Jazeera; post reposted by @F_CEAFE). Treasury Secretary Bessent said Iran has not loaded a single tanker since "Operation Economic Outcast" began in August (reposted by @F_CEAFE). Mines and tanker attacks in Hormuz: see Conflicts. https://x.com/i/status/2125618474340823311 ; https://x.com/i/status/2125592759344287920

- **Ukraine and international justice.** Ukraine's parliament backed joining the management committee of the Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression; the EU backed Ukraine against the IAEA giving a lead role to a Russian official (Kyiv Independent). https://x.com/i/status/2125620616292147242 ; https://x.com/i/status/2125620853916230014

- **Libya / Türkiye.** Erdoğan received Khalifa Haftar in Ankara, ahead of his first trip to Libya in 15 years (Turkish Presidency; Euronews). https://x.com/i/status/2125602939750244453 ; https://l.euronews.com/yO7Y

- **Israel in Central Europe.** Israel joined a Political Directors' meeting of the Slavkov format (Austria, Czechia, Slovakia) for the first time (Israel MFA). https://x.com/i/status/2125643655184576904

- **Germany–Ukraine.** Germany has given €34.35 billion in military aid since 2022; five joint production projects worth €1.1 billion are under way and €11.6 billion is planned for 2027 (Ukrainian MoD, reposted by @F_CEAFE; see Defence Industry). https://x.com/i/status/2125591334903837066

- **EU competition.** The Commission fined Firmenich, Givaudan and IFF €471.9 million for a fragrance cartel (EU Commission). https://x.com/i/status/2125625810715328963

articles.headline: Poland asks NATO allies to consider shooting down Russian missiles over Ukraine; Warsaw says it sees "no determination"
articles.summary:
**Lede.** Poland has asked NATO allies to look at intercepting Russian missiles and drones over Ukrainian territory when they are heading for NATO airspace, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday; according to agency accounts of the report, the idea was raised at a meeting of NATO ambassadors in Brussels on 23 November, some allies were supportive, and no decision was taken.

**Context.** Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski told Polish Radio Three that Ukraine itself is asking for "threatening objects over its territory" to be shot down, and that doing so "over Ukraine, at Ukraine's request, would fall within the definition of necessary self-defence" (PAP via Onet). Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz told RMF that "once again, as in July", Poland would probably not get the reaction it expected: "I see perhaps a greater willingness to talk, but I do not see determination" (EFE). He asked whether the lukewarm response was about "appeasement" and recalled that US experts are also examining the debris; President Trump had called the incident "a couple of little missiles" fired by mistake (EFE). On 20 November three objects entered Polish airspace and two missiles and a suspected jet drone fell on Polish soil; a Swedish Gripen under NATO command could not engage a suspected Kh-101 because NATO rules require visual identification, while Poland changed its own rules in October to allow shoot-downs on radar data (Clash Report, citing Polish command, Kyiv Independent and EFE). Russia's MFA warned in 2024 that it could respond if Poland shot down Russian missiles over Ukraine (RBC, Russian business daily).

Separately, the Italian Navy said its destroyer Giovanni delle Bande Nere intercepted a high-speed ballistic target with two Aster 30 missiles, which La Repubblica called Europe's only operational sea-based ballistic-missile shield (Clash Report).

The conclusion is the same once again: either Europe acts as one, or each country is left in a supporting role.

**What to watch:** NATO military advice on interceptions over Ukraine; the European Council (26–27 Nov); any Russian MFA reaction to the Polish proposal (none found so far).

**Sources:** Clash Report: https://x.com/i/status/2125555722033205515 and https://clashreport.com/world/articles/poland-nato-shoot-down-russian-missiles-ukraine-mip2wfksx6 ; Bloomberg post: https://x.com/i/status/2125550101896561041 ; PAP/Onet (Sikorski): https://wiadomosci.onet.pl/kraj/radoslaw-sikorski-o-zestrzeliwaniu-rosyjskich-rakiet-na-prosbe-ukrainy/qex6chs ; EFE/Infobae (Kosiniak-Kamysz): https://www.infobae.com/america/agencias/2026/11/25/polonia-presiona-a-otan-para-derribar-misiles-rusos-sobre-ucrania-tras-ultimas-incursiones/ ; RBC: https://www.rbc.ru/politics/25/11/2026/6b06c39476b4eed1329dac9a ; Italian Navy Aster 30 (Clash Report): https://x.com/i/status/2125558870240079943

**Images:** Clash Report article image: https://pbs.twimg.com/news_img/2125555722159108096/Pl53UyZp?format=jpg&name=orig
articles.why: the frontline state most exposed to Russian strikes is asking for a collective decision that the alliance has not taken, and its ministers openly doubt that their allies, Washington included, will back it. The Aster 30 test shows that a European-built answer to ballistic threats exists; the question is whether Europeans decide together to use it. Here is a further example of why Europeans need common rules of engagement and their own air-defence chain, rather than waiting for a consensus that depends on others.

articles.headline: Update: peace table — von der Leyen says a "strong European team" will join the next round, as Washington rules out troops and bases in post-war Ukraine
articles.summary:
**Lede.** Commission President Ursula von der Leyen told the European Parliament that "a strong European team will participate in the next round of talks" and that the EU will "judge progress based on Russia's actions, not simply its words"; Russia should accept a winter ceasefire on energy infrastructure and a truce guaranteeing safe passage of food exports through the Black Sea, as discussed at last week's Coalition of the Willing meeting.

**Context.** She said Ukraine faces a gap of about €70 billion next year; the proposed Instrument for Coordinated Support to Ukraine would provide €45 billion in 2027 (€20 billion budget support, €25 billion military), "two thirds" of the need, repayable only once Russia pays for the damage; she also said the EU is on track to open the last two accession clusters this year. Meanwhile the Kyiv Independent reported (exclusive) that US negotiators have privately ruled out US troops or military bases in post-war Ukraine as part of security guarantees, preferring an "Article 5-like" commitment whose obligations remain undefined. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the deployment of any foreign military contingents in Ukraine is "unacceptable" to Russia, responding to Boris Johnson's call for NATO troops (TASS, Russian state agency). Belarus' Alexander Lukashenko told Le Point he does not rule out the withdrawal of nuclear-capable Russian missiles from Belarus as part of a settlement (TASS; BelTA). The Wall Street Journal reported that Zelenskyy would turn to the incoming Democratic-controlled Congress for aid and sanctions if Trump fails to get a deal by year-end (via Clash Report).

**What to watch:** composition of the "European team" and date of the next round; the European Council on Ukraine financing (26–27 Nov); Moscow's answer to the winter-ceasefire request.

**Sources:** von der Leyen speech (Commission text via 1848.nl): https://app.1848.nl/document/item/583309 ; Commission Representation in Germany: https://germany.representation.ec.europa.eu/nachrichten-und-veranstaltungen/pressemitteilungen/prasidentin-von-der-leyen-sicherheit-der-ukraine-wirkt-sich-unmittelbar-auf-unsere-sicherheit-aus-2026-11-25_de ; von der Leyen on X: https://x.com/i/status/2125527771468177539 ; Anadolu: https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/von-der-leyen-says-strong-european-team-to-join-next-round-of-ukraine-peace-talks/4136998 ; Kyiv Independent: https://kyivindependent.com/exclusive-us-rules-out-troops-military-bases-in-ukraine-under-post-war-security-guarantees-falling-short-of-kyivs-expectations/ and https://x.com/i/status/2125508306227622080 ; TASS (Peskov): https://x.com/i/status/2125543787137208759 ; TASS (Lukashenko): https://tass.com/world/2224477 ; BelTA: https://esp.belta.by/president/view/lukashenko-respondi-a-una-pregunta-sobre-la-posibilidad-de-retirar-de-belars-misiles-capaces-de-96749-2026/ ; WSJ via Clash Report: https://x.com/i/status/2125531137485205513

**Images:** von der Leyen video (23 s): https://video.twimg.com/amplify_video/2125527389656539137/vid/avc1/720x720/el8chlGJHG7PgwNf.mp4
articles.why: Brussels wants a seat, but the security guarantee on offer from Washington carries no American soldiers, so any force on the ground would be European. That makes the gap between what Europe is asked to underwrite and what it is allowed to negotiate obvious. A European seat at the table only carries weight if Europe brings its own military means.

articles.headline: Merz in the Bundestag: "Russia wants more than Ukraine", as Berlin cuts other spending and AfD calls for an end to aid
articles.summary:
**Lede.** Opening the debate on the 2027 federal budget, Chancellor Friedrich Merz said: "Russia knows exactly what it wants. And Russia wants more than Ukraine," adding that Russia is "escalating" in the Baltic, Poland, the Black Sea, in space "and by now also massively here in our own country" (Reuters via Straits Times; AFP).

**Context.** The core 2027 budget totals €560.9 billion with net borrowing of almost €123 billion (AFP); the draft plans to double defence spending to over €200 billion by 2030, 3.7% of GDP (Reuters). Anadolu reports that the Merz government plans nearly $153 billion in defence spending for 2027 while cutting aid and UN contributions. "We no longer have the money for everything," Merz said. AfD co-leader Tino Chrupalla cited a poll showing a majority of Germans no longer accept military aid to Ukraine, and AfD leader Alice Weidel said "peace in Europe is only possible with Russia and the US" (Clash Report clips). On the EU's 2028–2034 budget (Costa's new box: €1.582 trillion, about €40 billion below the Irish presidency proposal), Merz wants spending "limited and focused" on "security and competitiveness" ahead of Thursday–Friday's special summit (Reuters). @F_CEAFE this morning reposted two German posts attacking Foreign Minister Wadephul's line that peace in Europe can only be had "against" Russia.

**What to watch:** final Bundestag vote on the 2027 budget this week; the special European Council on the MFF (26–27 Nov); Russian reaction to Merz (none found so far).

**Sources:** Straits Times (Reuters): https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/germanys-merz-defends-aid-for-ukraine-says-russia-poses-growing-threat-to-europe ; AFP via newsworm: https://www.newsworm.de/news/merz-defends-2027-budget-and-ukraine-support ; The Guardian live: https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/nov/25/ukraine-russia-energy-strikes-mark-rutte-donald-trump-friedrich-merz-germany-latest-news-updates ; DW: https://x.com/i/status/2125536831039062076 ; Anadolu: https://x.com/i/status/2125536241156231570 ; Clash Report (Merz, Chrupalla, Weidel): https://x.com/i/status/2125540192345846128 , https://x.com/i/status/2125540094899892373 , https://x.com/i/status/2125550934621409495 ; @F_CEAFE reposts: https://x.com/i/status/2125487471357988882
articles.why: Germany is rearming nationally while asking for a smaller common EU budget. The scale Europe needs for its defence will not come from 27 national budgets competing with each other; a German build-up without a stronger common European instrument risks creating a dominant national army instead of a European one.

articles.headline: Update: the EU tightens export controls on 15 more entities tied to Russia's military industry; Kallas promises a hit on energy revenues
articles.summary:
**Lede.** The Council of the EU added 15 entities that are part of, or support, Russia's military-industrial complex to the list subject to tighter export restrictions on dual-use goods and advanced technology (Annex IV), citing the EU's "determination to increase pressure so that Russia stops its brutal war".

**Context.** The Council did not name the entities in its posts. High Representative Kaja Kallas, reposted by the EEAS spokesperson, said the 22nd package will add "dozens of actors in Russia's energy sector", including shadow-fleet enablers, and "over 60 shadow fleet vessels", and tighten export bans on LNG and oil projects. Energy Commissioner Dan Jørgensen told Euronews the EU "will never return to Russian energy": "We do not trust Russia, even if there's peace." Von der Leyen told Parliament the 22nd package was adopted by the Commission on Monday (see story 2).

**What to watch:** Council adoption of the 22nd package; names of the 15 entities in the Official Journal and whether third-country firms (China, UAE, Türkiye) are among them; Russian countermeasures.

**Sources:** Council of the EU: https://x.com/i/status/2125533454779765119 and https://x.com/i/status/2125534992931696641 ; press release: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/11/25/russia-s-war-of-aggression-against-ukraine-eu-restricts-trade-with-15-entities-linked-to-russia-s-military-and-industrial-complex/ (timed out at access; content from Council posts and Kommersant https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/9130305) ; Kallas via EEAS spokesperson: https://x.com/i/status/2125548943912427943 ; Euronews (Jørgensen): https://x.com/i/status/2125559756815519829
articles.why: sanctions are one of the few areas where the EU acts as one actor with real leverage. Their impact depends on unanimity in the Council, which the Hungarian and Slovak governments have used before to delay packages.

articles.headline: Iran war: Washington tells Americans to leave Iran "immediately"; Tehran ties Hormuz to the US blockade; Houthis threaten Jeddah
articles.summary:
**Lede.** The US Virtual Embassy in Iran told US citizens to leave the country immediately and not to travel there for any reason, warning that hostilities, including Iranian attacks on US assets in Bahrain and Kuwait and Houthi actions, could escalate rapidly (security alert of 24 Nov; Euronews).

**Context.** Trump said the US has the funds to sustain the Iran war until January and can "put that war to bed anytime we want" (Anadolu). An Iranian diplomat said Iran will not allow ships through the Strait of Hormuz while the US blockade remains (IRNA, Iranian state agency, via Al Jazeera). The Houthis' military spokesman said Jeddah and all Saudi Red Sea ports will be targets if Saudi Arabia bombs Hodeidah and told workers to evacuate (Yahya Saree on X); Sweden condemned the attacks on Riyadh's financial district. US officials consider Iran a leading suspect in cyberattacks on up to 50 energy tankers (WSJ via Clash Report). In Israel, opposition figure Avigdor Lieberman said there is no justification for an immediate strike on Iran (Haaretz, reposted by @F_CEAFE), and the judges in Netanyahu's trial proposed that the Attorney General drop the bribery charge in Case 4000 (Haaretz, Times of Israel). Greece's FM Gerapetritis received Yemen's FM to discuss maritime security.

**What to watch:** US or Israeli strike decision; Saudi response to Houthi threats; Hormuz traffic; EU Aspides mandate.

**Sources:** US Virtual Embassy Iran: https://ir.usembassy.gov/security-alert-iran-november-24-2026/ ; Euronews: https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/25/us-tells-citizens-to-leave-iran-warns-hostilities-could-escalate-fast ; Anadolu (Trump): https://x.com/i/status/2125525415577964871 ; Al Jazeera (IRNA): https://x.com/i/status/2125523772723921073 ; Houthi spokesman: https://x.com/i/status/2125555253676331501 ; Sweden MFA: https://x.com/i/status/2125472667868512387 ; WSJ via Clash Report: https://x.com/i/status/2125521029434913204 ; Haaretz: https://x.com/i/status/2125541295762395227 ; @F_CEAFE reposts (Lieberman, Ofgem): https://x.com/i/status/2125511678590845163 , https://x.com/i/status/2125511776317985211 ; Greece MFA: https://x.com/i/status/2125558163428770170
articles.why: Europe imports the war's costs through energy (Ofgem raised the UK price cap by 26% citing Middle East gas prices, reposted by @F_CEAFE) and Red Sea shipping, without any say in the decision to escalate.

articles.headline: China and Taiwan in Europe and Asia: Lithuania asks Taiwan to rename its office; Taiwan and the Philippines sign a space MOU; Japan and Singapore issue their first joint defence statement
articles.summary:
**Lede.** A Lithuanian presidential aide called on Taiwan to rename its "Taiwanese Representative Office" in Vilnius, according to the Global Times (Chinese state media), which quoted a Chinese expert saying "blame-shifting won't help mend ties"; @F_CEAFE reposted it.

**Context.** Taiwan and the Philippines signed their first space-cooperation MOU (Taiwan MOFA). Japan's Defence Minister Koizumi and Singapore's Defence Minister Chan issued their first-ever joint press statement on defence cooperation. articles.headline: Washington thins NATO's eastern flank: a Republican congressman says the Pentagon misled Congress, as Poland ties its defence R&D to the US
articles.summary:
Rep. Don Bacon (Republican, Nebraska; a retired US Air Force general) wrote on 24 November that "withdrawing two armor brigades from Eastern Europe and with no warning to Polish, Romanian and Baltic leaders prior weakened the alliance and deterrence, while emboldening Putin", and that "Congressional leaders were mislead by the Pentagon that these withdrawals would not occur". He was quoting a post by the Pentagon's policy chief Elbridge Colby, who said the Pentagon's approach is to make alliances "stronger and more secure *in reality*", which "requires being *realistic*" about threats and resources. @F_CEAFE reposted Bacon's post. The same day, at the Pentagon, Polish deputy defence minister Cezary Tomczyk and US Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering Emil Michael signed a Defense RDT&E Agreement, ending 17 years of negotiations; it lets Polish universities, institutes and companies join US research, development, test and evaluation projects, with high-energy materials and ammunition as the first pilot area (Polish MoD).

**Context.** In a statement to Congress at the end of September, Colby confirmed that US brigade combat teams in Europe had been cut from five to three, one of the withdrawn brigades having rotated through Poland and the other through Romania, and that the Pentagon was exploring a permanent US base in Poland (PAP, Polish Radio). On 15 November Stars and Stripes reported that about 78,000 US personnel were assigned to EUCOM, close to the 76,000 floor set by Congress in the FY2026 NDAA; Hegseth is due to present the final posture recommendations to Trump on 1 December (Bloomberg via RO Times). In Warsaw, the Foreign Ministry said it had summoned Russia's ambassador and handed him "a very strongly worded diplomatic note" over the violation of Polish airspace by three Russian cruise missiles last week. Home Affairs Commissioner Magnus Brunner told the European Parliament that the EU would set up a Frontex rapid reaction force, deployable at a member state's request, plus an EU counter-drone centre of excellence and a large drone exercise in the Baltic region; about €500 million is available for border surveillance and counter-drone measures and €50 million for a Bulgarian–Romanian maritime security hub in the Black Sea. "You will definitely not stand alone," he told frontline states (Anadolu).

**What to watch:** Hegseth's force-posture recommendations (1 December) and Congress's 76,000 floor; any Pentagon reply to Bacon; the first RDT&E project arrangements; the Frontex recast proposal in Parliament and Council.

**Sources:** Rep. Don Bacon: https://x.com/i/status/2125358495662817659 (original https://x.com/RepDonBacon/status/2125299577100042670, quoting https://x.com/i/status/2125285480400908739) ; @F_CEAFE reply: https://x.com/i/status/2125347435476144484 ; Polish MoD, 24 Nov: https://www.gov.pl/web/obrona-narodowa/od-badan-do-nowych-zdolnosci-polska-wzmacnia-wspolprace-obronna-z-usa ; Anadolu, 25 Nov: https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/poland-us-sign-defense-research-agreement-after-17-years-of-negotiations/4136545 ; Defence24: https://defence24.pl/przemysl/mon-i-pentagon-zaciesniaja-wspolprace-technologiczna ; Polish Radio (PAP), 30 Sep: https://www.polskieradio.pl/395/7785/artykul/3737255,pentagon-confirms-review-of-possible-permanent-us-base-in-poland ; Stars and Stripes, 15 Nov: https://www.stripes.com/theaters/europe/2026-11-15/us-troop-levels-europe-eucom-nato-23470991.html ; Polish MFA: https://x.com/i/status/2125299037838393508 and https://www.gov.pl/web/diplomacy/statement-on-the-summoning-of-the-russian-federation-ambassador-to-the-mfa ; Anadolu on Brunner, 25 Nov: https://aa.com.tr/en/europe/eu-to-step-up-eastern-border-defenses-with-rapid-response-force-counter-drone-capabilities/4136542 ; Commission (Frontex proposal): https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/ip_26_2260
articles.why: the American presence the eastern flank relies on is being cut by decisions taken in Washington, without warning to those most exposed, a Republican lawmaker says. At the same moment Poland, already one of the biggest buyers of US equipment, ties its early-stage defence research to the Pentagon, where results fall under US rules on technical data. Commenting on X the same evening, @F_CEAFE wrote that "member states are expected to contribute to the project, not to divert resources away from it by giving them to third parties." The Commission's answer (Frontex, counter-drone and Black Sea funds) is still small, but it is joint and European.

articles.headline: Update: peace table — Washington drops business deals as bait for Moscow; Putin threatens to retaliate for refinery strikes
articles.summary:
The Trump administration has quietly shelved proposals to use business deals as an incentive for Russia to end the Ukraine war, after Moscow showed little interest in the proposed energy and aviation ventures, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday, citing five officials (relayed by Reuters, which could not verify it). Envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner told European officials that corporate tie-ups were no longer a core part of the US pitch; ideas had included US investment in Russian oil and titanium projects, restarting pipeline gas to Europe (a US investor in Nord Stream had been discussed in October) and opening Russian airspace to US airlines. According to Kommersant's account of the FT report, Russian negotiators in Abu Dhabi made clear economic offers would not soften Putin's terms (all of Donbas); a US official called the report inaccurate and said post-war economic engagement "remains one of the elements". On Tuesday Putin said that "despite the appeal and direct request from the US President" to refrain from attacks, "the Kyiv authorities are not listening", announced "retaliatory actions" for strikes on Russian refineries, and warned that attempts to restrict Russian energy exports have "serious consequences, primarily for Europeans themselves". The EU's energy commissioner told Euronews that Brussels will press ahead with its ban on Russian gas whatever the outcome of the US–Russia talks. Lukashenko said he is ready to accompany Zelenskyy to talks with Putin (TASS, Russian state agency).

**What to watch:** the White House's answer to the FT; Russia's "retaliation" for the refinery strikes; the next Abu Dhabi round; the European Council (26–27 November) on Ukraine.

**Sources:** Investing.com (Reuters), 25 Nov: https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/us-shelves-proposals-to-use-business-deals-with-russia-to-end-ukraine-war-ft-reports-5049739 ; Kommersant, 25 Nov: https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/9129851 ; Clash Report (FT): https://x.com/i/status/2125468183448445151 ; Putin (Clash Report clips): https://x.com/i/status/2125315235389038812 , https://x.com/i/status/2125315659760337293 ; Bloomberg: https://x.com/i/status/2125350028684214731 ; Euronews: https://x.com/i/status/2125354392903934199 ; TASS: https://x.com/i/status/2125313352687890894
articles.why: the economic side of the US plan (Nord Stream, oil, aviation) was being negotiated over Europe's energy future without Europe at the table. If it is shelved, the talks narrow to territory and security guarantees, the very issues on which Europeans pay the cost and have the least say. The Commission's gas ban is one of the few levers the EU keeps for itself.

articles.headline: Two days before the European Council, EU states agree Ukraine needs money but not on how much or who pays
articles.summary:
EU ambassadors held a first discussion on 24 November of the Commission's proposal to lend Ukraine €45 billion in 2027 and of António Costa's compromise for the 2028–2034 budget, which earmarks €100 billion for Kyiv, according to national dispatches seen by the Kyiv Independent. Estonia called the €100 billion an "absolute minimum"; Italy and Bulgaria questioned whether interest on existing EU loans to Ukraine (a Commission analysis puts it at €55.4 billion over the next budget cycle) would really be paid "in addition"; Austria rejected a bespoke instrument for it. Hungary, Czechia and Slovakia opted out of the €90 billion loan in April, and diplomats expect Bulgaria to join them on the new €45 billion; France warned that pressure is mounting in Paris against any deal before its April presidential election. Slovakia's Robert Fico said "Slovakia will not go into debt for Ukraine. It is not a loan but a gift", accusing the EU of "blackmail" for linking the loan to the budget (post. Zelenskyy said Ukraine will seek €115 billion in foreign aid for 2027 (France 24) and, per Bloomberg, will turn to the new Democrat-controlled US Congress if Trump fails to reach a deal with Putin.

**What to watch:** the European Council of 26–27 November; Bulgaria's position; whether interest costs are kept outside the €100 billion.

**Sources:** Kyiv Independent, 25 Nov: https://kyivindependent.com/days-before-key-summit-eu-countries-want-to-help-ukraine-but-cant-agree-on-how/ ; @F_CEAFE repost (Fico, via @cuprwarszawa): https://x.com/i/status/2125297333076406297 ; France 24: https://x.com/i/status/2125399282878386404 ; Bloomberg: https://x.com/i/status/2125363878959747417 ; Euronews: https://x.com/i/status/2125330814850187455
articles.why: the Union is now Ukraine's main financial backer, yet it decides by unanimity and member states opt in and out one by one. Each opt-out leaves the others to pay more and weakens the Union's voice at a table where it is already absent.

articles.headline: Update: Zelenskyy says the 48 Patriot interceptors depend "exclusively" on Hegseth's signature
articles.summary:
Speaking in Uzhhorod alongside Hungary's Prime Minister on Tuesday, Zelenskyy said that for the Patriot anti-ballistic interceptors "the document is currently in the United States. Unfortunately, Hegseth has not signed it yet, so it depends exclusively on him" (Clash Report clip; RBC-Ukraine and UNN report the figure of 48 missiles agreed and say Kyiv would welcome 60). TASS (Russian state agency) carried the same statement. It follows the FT report covered at 14:30 that Washington is holding up about 60 Patriot interceptors already paid for by Europeans.

**What to watch:** a Pentagon decision; whether European buyers of Patriot (Germany, the Netherlands, Poland and others) raise the delays at the European Council.

**Sources:** Clash Report: https://x.com/i/status/2125339204154720687 ; TASS: https://x.com/i/status/2125426996301680972 ; RBC-Ukraine: https://newsukraine.rbc.ua/news/hegseth-has-yet-to-approve-transfer-of-48-1795554783.html ; UNN: https://unn.ua/en/news/hegseth-has-still-not-approved-the-allocation-of-missiles-for-patriot-systems-to-ukraine-zelenskyy ; earlier: 2026-11-24 14:30 brief, story 4.
articles.why: European money buys the missiles, but a single US official decides if and when they are delivered. This is the "kill switch" in practice: control over supply rather than over the software.

articles.headline: Iran war: US embassies tell Americans to locate shelters as Washington debates targeting Iran's leaders
articles.summary:
On 24 November US missions in Israel, Iraq, Kuwait, Bahrain and the virtual embassy for Iran issued security alerts warning of possible attacks by Iran and the Houthis, airspace closures and flight cancellations; in Israel, US citizens were told to know their nearest shelter (US Embassy Jerusalem, US Mission Iraq). @F_CEAFE reposted Hormuz Report on the alerts and on an NBC News report that Trump administration officials are debating whether to target senior Iranian leaders to end the nine-month war; opponents warn it could harden Tehran, wreck future talks and expose US personnel, and no decision has been taken (NBC News). Trump said on Tuesday: "We had a little moratorium with Iran, and we learned that you can't trust them." Iran's army said it destroyed a US "Lucas" drone over the western Strait of Hormuz and an MQ-9 over the eastern strait (IRNA, Iranian state agency; not confirmed by the US); the IRGC Navy said two "rogue" tankers hit naval mines while using an "unauthorized route", and Iran blacklisted 26 tugboats that assisted ships using an alternative southern route (Anadolu). Israel's defence minister Israel Katz claimed Iran is developing chemical weapons and plotting to kill Trump (Haaretz, paywalled); Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi accused the US of "crippling" the OPCW. In Yemen, the Saudi-led coalition told civilians to leave Hodeidah port and then struck it; the Houthis' military spokesman said Jeddah and all Saudi Red Sea ports would be targets (Al Jazeera, Reuters); the coalition reported drones downed over Ras Tanura.

**What to watch:** any US decision on leadership strikes; independent confirmation of the drone losses and the mine strikes; Houthi action against Jeddah. Military detail: see Conflicts.

**Sources:** US Embassy Jerusalem: https://il.usembassy.gov/security-alert-u-s-embassy-jerusalem-november-24-2026/ ; US Mission Iraq: https://iq.usembassy.gov/security-alert-u-s-mission-iraq-november-24-2026/ ; US Virtual Embassy Iran: https://ir.usembassy.gov/security-alert-iran-november-24-2026/ ; NBC News: https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/national-security/trump-administration-officials-debating-targeting-irans-leaders-source-rcna610889 ; @F_CEAFE reposts: https://x.com/i/status/2125356386389479773 , https://x.com/i/status/2125293040868655528 , https://x.com/i/status/2125292835448475852 ; Trump (Clash Report): https://x.com/i/status/2125312295345570234 ; IRNA: https://x.com/i/status/2125315704622850490 ; Anadolu: https://x.com/i/status/2125461478505632085 , https://x.com/i/status/2125341202127950155 ; Haaretz: https://x.com/i/status/2125314802092327004 ; Al Jazeera live, 25 Nov: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/11/25/iran-war-live-houthis-threaten-saudi-ports-over-coalitions-hodeidah-order ; Houthi statement (Yahya Saree, Houthi): https://x.com/i/status/2125351835947106539
articles.why: a strike on Iran's leadership would widen a war that already chokes Hormuz and the Red Sea, the routes for Europe's energy and trade. Europe has no seat in these decisions, even though it bears their economic cost.

articles.headline: Update: the EU caps Chinese hybrid imports at 191,780 cars; Beijing invokes the WTO
articles.summary:
The Commission imposed provisional import quotas on hybrid passenger cars (HEV, PHEV and MHEV) under a safeguard investigation: from 1 December 2026 to 18 June 2027, 191,780 new hybrids from China may enter (86,301 in the first quarter, 88,219 in the second, 17,260 in the final period), and imports beyond the quota cannot enter (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/2614; Commission press release; electrive). China "urged the EU to honor bilateral consensus, strictly abide by WTO rules and uphold the principle of non-discrimination" and vowed to protect its industry (Global Times, Chinese state media;. EU member states are also leaning toward including British-made EVs in the "Made in Europe" scheme (Reuters), and BYD is in talks to buy Ineos Automotive's French factory (Reuters). This follows the 14:30 story on China's WTO warning.

**What to watch:** whether China retaliates (past targets: brandy, pork, dairy); the definitive safeguard measure; the "Made in Europe" rules of origin.

**Sources:** EUR-Lex: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg_impl/2026/2614/oj/eng ; Commission: https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/api/files/document/print/en/ip_26_2564/IP_26_2564_EN.pdf ; electrive, 24 Nov: https://www.electrive.com/2026/11/24/eu-introduces-import-quotas-for-hybrids-from-china-and-other-countries/ ; Reuters: https://x.com/i/status/2125298449402777936 , https://x.com/i/status/2125312291692302700 , https://x.com/i/status/2125306010717872586 ; @F_CEAFE repost (Global Times): https://x.com/i/status/2125330264922398890
articles.why: this time the Union uses its trade instruments as a bloc to defend its car industry; the contrast is with US tariffs, which the EU has so far accepted without a counter-measure. Chinese investment in European plants (BYD) is how Beijing gets around the quota.

articles.headline: Israel: Eisenkot signs his first coalition deal; the White House says Trump's position on military aid is "unchanged"
articles.summary:
Prime Minister-designate Gadi Eisenkot clinched his first coalition agreement, with Yashar and Yisrael Beiteinu, and aims to announce a government next week, while the Democrats halted talks with him over his unity negotiations with Likud (Reuters, Haaretz, Anadolu). After US Ambassador Mike Huckabee told an INSS conference he was unsure whether US military aid would end abruptly at year's end, a senior White House official told the Jerusalem Post that Trump's position is "unchanged", without saying whether the funds have been halted. Trump announced on 3 November that the roughly $4 billion a year would stop after this year; the 2016 memorandum ($3.3 billion in FMF and $500 million for missile defence a year) runs to 2028, and the Senate's FY2027 bills still include it (JNS). The Times of Israel reports worries about US aid to Egypt and Jordan. Israel's Supreme Court said West Bank settlers are acting "like militias" (Haaretz), and Amnesty called for an ICC genocide investigation over Israel's impact on births in Gaza (France 24).

**What to watch:** formation of the Eisenkot government; Congress's appropriations; any US statement on Egypt and Jordan.

**Sources:** Reuters: https://x.com/i/status/2125424337226236136 ; Haaretz: https://x.com/i/status/2125375210027102333 , https://x.com/i/status/2125360149170696209 , https://x.com/i/status/2125405396621816125 ; Anadolu: https://x.com/i/status/2125308486539993588 ; Jerusalem Post, 25 Nov: https://www.jpost.com/international/article-916041 ; JNS: https://www.jns.org/news/u-s-news/senate-includes-israel-aid-in-funding-bills-despite-trumps-call-for-year-end-halt ; Times of Israel: https://x.com/i/status/2125394193707069881 ; France 24: https://x.com/i/status/2125440706944860638
articles.why: a smaller US subsidy pushes Israel towards more domestic defence production and arms exports, many of them to European buyers (Elbit, Rafael, IAI). Changes in its government matter for Gaza, the West Bank and the Iran war on Europe's southern flank.

- **Australia–Solomon Islands (Update).** The two signed a security treaty that makes Canberra the "defence partner of choice" and affirms there will be no foreign military base in the Pacific country, while Honiara reviews its ties with China (Reuters, Japan Times, Kyodo; see 24 Nov 14:30, story 8). https://x.com/i/status/2125439711166550221 ; https://x.com/i/status/2125424457837580662

- **Japan and the ICC.** Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi moved forward Japan's financial contribution to the ICC in her first meeting with court President Tomoko Akane since the US sanctions (Japan Times). https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/11/24/japan/politics/japan-pm-takaichi-icc-akane/
