articles.headline: Compradores de EE. UU. toman el control de proveedores europeos de defensa: Red Cat oferta por Steyr Motors, Fairbanks Morse compra Truflo Marine y NUBURU se queda con Tekne
articles.summary:
**Tres proveedores europeos especializados en defensa, en Austria, el Reino Unido e Italia, han pasado o están pasando a manos estadounidenses desde mediados de octubre, justo cuando Europa aumenta su gasto en defensa.**

(1) **Red Cat Holdings** (EE. UU.) ha lanzado una oferta en efectivo por **Steyr Motors AG** (Austria), fabricante de motores de alto rendimiento para vehículos militares especiales y embarcaciones y de unidades auxiliares de potencia para carros de combate: 39,00 euros por acción, unos 205 millones de euros en total, una prima del 28,9 % sobre el cierre del 16 de octubre. Los consejos de dirección y de supervisión de Steyr Motors recomendaron aceptarla el 2 de noviembre; el plazo de aceptación vence el 18 de diciembre de 2026 y la oferta está condicionada a las autorizaciones de inversión extranjera directa de Austria, Australia, Italia y el Reino Unido. (2) **Fairbanks Morse Defense** (EE. UU.), propiedad del fondo de capital riesgo estadounidense Arcline Investment Management, completó el 9 de noviembre la compra de **Truflo Marine** (Birmingham, Reino Unido): sus válvulas navales están en servicio en más de 37 marinas aliadas y cuenta con unos 270 empleados. (3) **NUBURU** (EE. UU.) completó el 15 de octubre la compra del 70 % de **Tekne S.p.A.** (Italia), fabricante de sistemas de guerra electrónica, vehículos especiales y movilidad de defensa, tras la autorización del Golden Power italiano del 5 de agosto; pagó un precio fijo de 5,2 millones de euros por el 67,1 % adicional, más un pago variable de hasta 20 millones.

**Contexto:** bajo propiedad estadounidense, las futuras exportaciones y muchas decisiones de suministro de estas empresas pueden quedar sometidas a la ley estadounidense de control de exportaciones: el ITAR para el material de defensa y el EAR para los productos de doble uso. Las operaciones coinciden con la petición de Washington de que los europeos no excluyan a las empresas estadounidenses de su mercado de defensa (véase Actualidad, el «NATO 3.0» de Colby). En el caso de Tekne, el Gobierno italiano autorizó la venta con su Golden Power; en el de Steyr, la decisión corresponde a las autoridades de control de inversiones de Austria, Italia, el Reino Unido y Australia, no a la UE.

**Qué vigilar:** el nivel de aceptación de la oferta por Steyr Motors y las decisiones de control de inversiones antes del 18 de diciembre; si el Reino Unido revisó la compra de Truflo con su Ley de Seguridad Nacional e Inversiones.

**Fuentes:** [Steyr Motors AG](https://ir.steyr-motors.com/en/2026/11/02/management-board-and-supervisory-board-of-steyr-motors-ag-recommend-acceptance-of-red-cats-purchase-offer/), [Fairbanks Morse Defense](https://www.fairbanksmorsedefense.com/blog/fairbanks-morse-defense-completes-acquisition-of-truflo-marine-expanding-mission-critical-valve-capabilities-for-allied-navies/), [NUBURU](https://ir.nuburu.net/news-details/2026/NUBURU-Completes-Tekne-Acquisition-Adding-a-93-Million-Defense--Dual-Use-Program-Portfolio-and-Advancing-Expansion-Across-NATO-and-Allied-Markets/default.aspx), [ITAR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-22/chapter-I/subchapter-M), [EAR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-15/subtitle-B/chapter-VII/subchapter-C)
articles.why: especialistas en motores, componentes navales y guerra electrónica pasan a control estadounidense mientras crecen los pedidos europeos, de modo que parte del valor y del control sobre el suministro cruza el Atlántico. Cada venta es un pequeño paso más en la desindustrialización y la pérdida de soberanía europeas, decidido Estado por Estado. El contraste de escala deja claro que las estrategias nacionales, por ambiciosas que sean, no bastan frente a competidores de otro orden de magnitud.

articles.headline: El turco Fidan pregunta por qué solo Ankara fue sancionada por la CAATSA por comprar el S-400
articles.summary:
**El ministro de Exteriores turco, Hakan Fidan, preguntó el 21 de noviembre por qué Washington eximió a «montones de países que compraron sistemas de defensa rusos» de las sanciones de la CAATSA que impuso a Turquía por el S-400 ruso, y culpó a los grupos de presión israelí y griego en Washington de bloquear su levantamiento (entrevista en TGRT Haber, vía Anadolu).**

Dijo que hay voluntad política en Ankara y en Washington para resolver sus disputas de defensa y que se han levantado los retrasos de EE. UU. en «algunas compras de munición largamente bloqueadas», pero que el margen de maniobra de la Administración es «muy limitado» en lo que fija la ley.

**Contexto:** EE. UU. sancionó en 2018 al Departamento de Desarrollo de Equipamiento de China por la compra de Su-35 y S-400, y en diciembre de 2020 a la agencia de industria de defensa turca; India, que también compró el S-400, no ha sido sancionada porque las sucesivas administraciones decidieron no aplicarle la CAATSA (Foreign Policy). Turquía fue excluida del programa F-35 en 2019, y la ley de defensa NDAA del año fiscal 2020 prohíbe transferirle el F-35 mientras posea el S-400 (Servicio de Investigación del Congreso).

**Qué vigilar:** cualquier paso de EE. UU. para aliviar las sanciones de la CAATSA a Turquía; la elección de Ankara entre volver al F-35 o comprar más Eurofighter.

**Fuentes:** [Anadolu](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/turkiye/turkish-foreign-minister-says-political-will-exists-to-solve-us-defense-disputes-but-congress-limits-maneuvering-room/4133284), [Anadolu en X](https://x.com/i/status/2124306883095740650), [Greek Reporter](https://greekreporter.com/2026/11/22/fidan-greek-israeli-lobbies-us-sanctions-turkey-s-400/), [Mario Nawfal](https://x.com/i/status/2124284223603503594), [Servicio de Investigación del Congreso](https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/IN12710), [Foreign Policy](https://foreignpolicy.com/2026/07/17/trump-russia-turkey-arms-sales-caatsa-sanctions-india-erdogan-f35/)
articles.why: la CAATSA es una ley de sanciones secundarias: la ley y el Congreso de EE. UU. deciden qué aliados pueden comprar qué armas, y el acceso a los sistemas estadounidenses y a su apoyo puede depender de decisiones políticas de Washington durante las décadas de vida de un sistema.

articles.headline: El dilema de soberanía de la OTAN: los ejércitos dependen de tecnología privada, IA y redes como Starshield
articles.summary:
**En la conferencia NATO Edge celebrada esta semana en Turquía, responsables de la OTAN y expertos en defensa debatieron cómo pueden los ejércitos usar la inteligencia artificial y la alta tecnología sin perder el control de datos y capacidades sensibles, según France 24.**

El reportaje describe la tensión entre empresas tecnológicas «controladas por capital privado que exige beneficios, independientes de cualquier control político» y unos mandos militares que responden ante la autoridad política, y cita como ejemplo la red Starlink de SpaceX y su equivalente militar, Starshield, de las que depende Ucrania. Por otra parte, SpaceNews informa de que la Fuerza Espacial de EE. UU. acelera el despliegue de la Space Data Network Backbone, una red militar de datos por satélite construida con un contrato de 2.290 millones de dólares con SpaceX, con tres lanzamientos en dos semanas.

**Contexto:** los demócratas del Senado de EE. UU. prevén investigar los recortes del acceso de Ucrania a Starshield (véase la edición de las 20:30 del 21 de noviembre).

**Qué vigilar:** la investigación del Senado sobre Starshield; el calendario de IRIS².

**Fuentes:** [France 24](https://x.com/i/status/2124445467127746704), [SpaceNews](https://spacenews.com/space-force-speeds-satellite-network-launches/), [SpaceNews en X](https://x.com/i/status/2124461545283260785)
articles.why: la conectividad, la nube y la IA son ya tan decisivas como la munición, y la mayoría de los proveedores privados son estadounidenses; quien gestiona la red puede restringirla. La constelación europea de conectividad segura, IRIS², aún tardará años en entrar en servicio.

articles.headline: El torpedo ORKA de Roketsan, lanzado desde un dron Bayraktar AKINCI de Baykar
articles.summary:
**Baykar y Roketsan informaron el 22 de noviembre de que el torpedo ligero de nueva generación ORKA, desarrollado por Roketsan, fue lanzado con éxito desde un avión no tripulado Bayraktar AKINCI.**

Según Anadolu, el AKINCI despegó de Çorlu (Tekirdağ) y soltó el torpedo en el golfo de Saros; el ORKA usa sonar activo y pasivo y puede guiarse de forma interna o externa mediante fibra óptica. Medios turcos lo describen como el primer lanzamiento de este torpedo desde una aeronave no tripulada.

**Qué vigilar:** la calificación y las ofertas de exportación del conjunto AKINCI–ORKA.

**Fuentes:** [Selçuk Bayraktar](https://x.com/i/status/2124398186689069474), [Baykar](https://x.com/i/status/2124397625055060339), [Roketsan](https://x.com/i/status/2124401006297403459), [Anadolu](https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/bilim-teknoloji/milli-torpido-orka-bayraktar-akinci-ile-denizle-bulustu/4133381)

articles.headline: Honeywell now owns the SABRE engine patents of Britain’s collapsed Reaction Engines, bought for £884,000 after about £60m of UK public funding
articles.summary:
US patent records show that on 28 July 2026 the patents of Reaction Engines Ltd, the British developer of the SABRE air-breathing rocket engine and its micro-tube pre-cooler, were assigned to Honeywell Aerospace US LLC by the administrators PwC (Google Patents record for US11162424B2, “Heat exchangers”, inventors Alan Bond and Richard Varvill). Reaction Engines went into administration in October 2024, owing more than £160m. PwC’s progress report (covering to end-April 2026, dated 29 May) said the IP sale was concluded in April with £884,000 in non-refundable deposits, the value the directors had put on the IP, but did not name the buyer (FlightGlobal, 14 June; Oxford Chronicle, 9 July). The buyer’s identity surfaced on X on 27 November from the patent assignment. The UK Space Agency put about £60m into SABRE, and ESA validated the pre-cooler in 2019 (Inngot, 16 June). Before it collapsed, Reaction Engines supplied heat exchangers to a Honeywell-led consortium in an EU Clean Aviation hydrogen fuel-cell project (FlightGlobal). Reaction: no statement from Honeywell, the UK government or ESA found.

**Key facts**

- Patent assignment to Honeywell Aerospace US LLC recorded 28 Jul 2026; assignors PwC and Reaction Engines Ltd (in administration) (Google Patents).

- IP sale concluded April 2026; £884,000 deposits; buyer not named in PwC’s report (FlightGlobal, Inngot).

- Public funding: about £60m from the UK Space Agency for SABRE (Inngot); about 170 of 208 staff were made redundant in 2024 (Oxford Chronicle).
articles.why: this is the pattern the owner has flagged for years: technology started with European money (the EU-funded LAPCAT project in 2008, then ESA from 2010, as @F_CEAFE recalled in 2021) ends in US hands. Here thirty years of hypersonic and thermal-management know-how went for less than £1m, a small fraction of the public money invested, through an insolvency sale that no European buyer contested. Neither the UK nor ESA had a mechanism to keep the IP in Europe. Once again, Europe pays for the research and the US collects the results.

articles.headline: Update: France joins the Netherlands against the US MATCH Act, while Beijing keeps its side of the truce
articles.summary:
French Trade Minister Nicolas Forissier told Bloomberg on 27 November that France shares Dutch concerns over the extraterritorial reach of the proposed US MATCH Act, which would force allies to tighten controls on chip equipment such as ASML’s immersion DUV machines sold to and serviced in China. “All European Union instruments remain available,” he said, “but we will not react impulsively.” The bill is being considered for the annual US defence package, which usually passes in December. EU trade ministers meet in Brussels on Monday 30 November, with US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer joining remotely. Forissier also warned of the “gradual erosion of the benefits of the Turnberry agreement” (Bloomberg via Mint). The Dutch prime minister plans to raise the MATCH Act with Trump at the G20 (Reuters, X). The Dutch minister Sjoerd Sjoerdsma said he works with the Commission, Germany and France against the bill; an expert cited by Reuters mentions the EU Blocking Statute (TrendForce). Reaction side: China has so far not retaliated against the latest US chip curbs. Its MOFCOM Announcement No. 59 keeps the suspension of the gallium, germanium and antimony ban on the US in force from today, 28 November, to 27 January 2027 (covered 24 Nov); Bloomberg reads this as Beijing “holding up its side of the bargain — for now”.

**Key facts**

- ASML: China expected to be about a fifth of revenue in 2026 (Bloomberg).

- MATCH Act: bipartisan; would extend restrictions from EUV to immersion DUV sales and servicing (Bloomberg, TrendForce).
articles.why: two large member states now say openly that US law should not dictate what European firms sell. A credible response needs the EU as a bloc: Monday’s trade council is the first test. This is the reciprocity CEAFE has called for.

articles.headline: Update: EU sanctions — Bulgaria blocks the 22nd Russia package to reopen imports of Russian pig iron
articles.summary: Bulgaria is holding up the EU’s 22nd sanctions package against Russia and asks for earlier bans on imports of Russian pig iron and mining equipment to be lifted (Kyiv Independent, 27 Nov). It also opposes listing a Russian chemicals company, citing fertiliser supplies, and a person linked to a dual-use nuclear facility. EU and Ukrainian officials suspect a commercial motive. Italy has also raised objections, to the proposed ban on Europeans sitting on Russian company boards.
articles.why: sanctions need unanimity, so one member state can stall the package. Pig iron is an input for steel, a sector where Ukraine’s industry is under Russian attack.

articles.headline: US trade — goods deficit widens to $149.5bn in October as AI imports hit a record
articles.summary: The US advance goods trade deficit widened 10.7% to $149.5bn in October; imports rose 6.1% to a record $365.3bn, led by capital goods (+8.5% to $171.4bn, up about 80% on a year earlier) linked to AI data centres; exports rose 3.2% to $215.8bn (US Census Bureau; Anadolu; Reuters). It is the fourth straight monthly widening (Bloomberg).
articles.why: despite the tariffs, the US deficit keeps growing, which strengthens the case in Washington for more Section 301 tariffs on partners, the EU included.

articles.headline: Tesla files to buy assets of EMAG, the German machine-tool maker
articles.summary:
Tesla has notified Germany's Federal Cartel Office (Bundeskartellamt) of a plan to buy assets of the EMAG group, a machine-tool maker based in Salach, near Stuttgart (Reuters; tagesschau/SWR). The cartel office lists it as an asset acquisition, case B5-132/26, notified on 23 November and published on 27 November. The markets named are machines for precise and electrochemical machining of metal parts, and laser processing. No price, list of assets or head count has been disclosed. Tesla declined to comment and EMAG did not reply to Reuters. Tesla had already set up a company, "Tesla Machining Technologies Management SE", with EMAG's Salach headquarters as its business address (tagesschau; Automotive World, citing Business Insider). The Stuttgarter Nachrichten reports that about 220 EMAG employees would move to Tesla; neither company has confirmed this. EMAG makes turning, grinding and gear-cutting machines for car drivetrains. More recently it also makes them for the small precision gears in the joints of humanoid robots, a known weak point of Tesla's Optimus robot. EMAG was founded in 1867. According to Business Insider, it lost about €42m on €496m of revenue in 2024 and announced 455 job cuts in November 2025. So far there has been no reaction from EMAG, the German government or the state of Baden-Württemberg; the cartel review is the only scrutiny on record.

**Background (CEAFE archive):** this is the latest case in CEAFE's tracker of US takeovers of European firms. On 19 October US drone maker Red Cat launched a bid of about €205m for Austria's Steyr Motors, which makes engines for military vehicles; the offer runs until 18 December and foreign-investment approvals are pending (https://ir.steyr-motors.com/en/2026/10/21/steyr-motors-ag-business-combination-agreement-signed-with-red-cat-holdings-inc-and-smot-acquisition-gmbh-binding-commitments-agreed-for-the-steyr-site-and-employees/). In 2024 Honeywell bought Italy's Civitanavi Systems, a navigation-systems maker, for about €200m. @F_CEAFE posted the EMAG story today as "Another 🇪🇺 tech gem acquired by the U.S." (https://x.com/i/status/2126367050469638297).

**What to watch:** the cartel office's decision (first phase of one month); whether Berlin opens a foreign-investment review; the price, the assets and the jobs once Tesla or EMAG comment.

Sources: @F_CEAFE https://x.com/i/status/2126367050469638297, Reuters https://x.com/i/status/2126325232927461743 (reprint https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/tesla-plans-acquire-german-manufacturing-systems-group-emag), tagesschau/SWR https://www.tagesschau.de/inland/regional/badenwuerttemberg/swr-tesla-uebernimmt-maschinenbauer-emag-spezialmaschinen-fuer-humanoide-roboter-100.html, Automotive World https://www.automotiveworld.com/news/tesla-files-plan-to-acquire-german-machine-maker-emag/, Servospace https://servospace.io/news/tesla-machining-technologies-emag-salach-220-staff-optimus-gears, Teslarati https://www.teslarati.com/tesla-bolster-optimus-company-acquisition-emag-germany/.
articles.why: EMAG is a typical German family-scale industrial firm with 159 years of know-how that is hard to rebuild. Precision gear machining is becoming a bottleneck for humanoid robots. The car-industry crisis has weakened the company, and a US buyer can now take machines, people and know-how through an asset purchase, without taking over the whole group. This is the pattern CEAFE has followed all month: high energy costs and weak demand weaken European industry, and US capital buys the best parts. A machine-tool maker is not a defence firm, so a German foreign-investment review is not certain. No single member state has a tool to keep this kind of capability in Europe unless a European buyer steps in.

articles.headline: France is officially in recession: GDP fell 0.2% in the third quarter
articles.summary:
France's statistics office, INSEE, published its detailed accounts on 27 November. Gross domestic product (GDP) fell 0.2% in the third quarter, revised down from a first estimate of −0.1%. The second quarter was also revised, from 0.0% to a very slight fall. France has therefore been in "technical" recession since the second quarter (franceinfo; AFP via France 24). GDP has now fallen three quarters in a row, to €662.6bn. Exports dropped 1.6% after rising 2.9%, and foreign trade took 0.6 points off growth. Business investment fell 0.8% and investment in manufactured goods 1.8%. Household consumption rose 0.3%. The Wall Street Journal links the fall in exports to summer heat waves that slowed Airbus's factories. The growth already "carried over" for 2026 is only 0.1%, against the government's forecast of 0.5%; INSEE says reaching that forecast would need 1.4% growth in the fourth quarter. The public deficit rose to 5.6% of GDP in the quarter. The same afternoon, two members of the European Central Bank's Governing Council, Joachim Nagel and Primož Dolenc, said the bank will probably have to raise interest rates again in December because inflation is stubborn (Bloomberg). Al Jazeera notes that euro-area inflation is at a three-year high, driven by energy prices.

**Background (CEAFE archive):** on 30 January 2024 CEAFE shared Reuters' report that the French economy had failed to grow in the fourth quarter of 2023, according to INSEE (https://x.com/i/status/1752316330617839681). The 26 November 14:30 edition compared Germany's 2027 budget, with €139bn for defence, with France's; the 08:30 edition today covered job cuts at SAP and plant stoppages at Stellantis.

**What to watch:** the euro-area flash inflation figure on 2 December; the European Central Bank's December meeting; the budget debate in Paris with a deficit of 5.6% of GDP.

Sources: INSEE https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/9165918, France 24 (AFP) https://www.france24.com/fr/info-en-continu/20261127-france-le-pib-recule-de-0-2-au-troisi%C3%A8me-trimestre-apr%C3%A8s-r%C3%A9vision-%C3%A0-la-baisse, franceinfo https://www.franceinfo.fr/economie/croissance/le-pib-recule-de-0-2-en-france-au-troisieme-trimestre-apres-une-revision-a-la-baisse-de-l-insee_8302671.html, Wall Street Journal https://x.com/i/status/2126345006419955875, Bloomberg https://x.com/i/status/2126362955906183217, BFMTV https://x.com/i/status/2126368613389205534, Bloomberg (Nagel) https://x.com/i/status/2126342820176740417, Bloomberg (Dolenc) https://x.com/i/status/2126331492963942794, Al Jazeera https://x.com/i/status/2126305037303615601.

**CEAFE:** A graphic reminder that the market and the politics of a single European state do not equal those of a global power.
articles.why: the euro area's second-largest economy is shrinking while the European Central Bank is still raising rates against energy-driven inflation. Industry is squeezed from both sides: expensive energy and expensive money. Falling exports and falling investment in manufacturing are the signs of deindustrialisation that CEAFE follows. They come as US buyers pick up weakened European firms, such as EMAG today. No single member state can fix this alone; a common energy and industrial policy is the only scale that works.

articles.headline: Update: US chip controls in Southeast Asia — the Nvidia shipment halt freezes data-centre financing
articles.summary:
The New York Times confirmed on 27 November that data-centre operators in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia have had orders for Nvidia's most advanced chips put on hold. The Financial Times adds that Aolani, a Singapore-based cloud company that planned to lease computing power to ByteDance, is affected: banks have stopped about $500m of credit, and ByteDance may drop the deal. The halt follows the rule issued on 16 November by the US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security. It requires licences to export advanced chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, and restricts remote access to them; cloud providers have 90 days to obtain a licence. "There's this new rule but no guidance on execution… It's causing sheer chaos in the region," a cloud executive told the Financial Times. According to the same newspaper, Nvidia booked $104bn of revenue through its Singapore subsidiary in 2025. Meanwhile, President Trump plans to visit a chip factory in Phoenix next week (Washington Post). There is no official statement yet from the four governments or from China.

**Background (CEAFE archive):** the 26 November 08:30 edition first reported that Nvidia had frozen AI-server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia. The Commerce Department rule of 16 November is at https://www.bis.gov/press-release/bis-issues-rule-addressing-remote-access-american-super-intelligence-technology.

**What to watch:** US guidance on the licence process; reactions from Malaysia and Singapore; China's Foreign Ministry briefing on Monday.

Sources: Reuters https://x.com/i/status/2126357884778733732, Financial Times https://www.ft.com/content/7838a715-07d4-4605-aa60-21f5af2b2370, New York Times https://cn.nytimes.com/business/20261127/nvidia-southeast-asia-sales/dual/, Data Center Dynamics https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/nvidia-halts-server-shipments-to-malaysia-singapore-thailand-and-indonesia-in-wake-of-new-dept-of-commerce-export-rule-report/, US Commerce Department https://www.bis.gov/press-release/bis-issues-rule-addressing-remote-access-american-super-intelligence-technology, Washington Post https://x.com/i/status/2126307587448611085.
articles.why: this is US extraterritorial power in practice: a rule written in Washington stops private investment in third countries within days. The same remote-access rule also covers data centres in the EU. Europe does not make AI chips at scale, so its cloud and AI plans also depend on US licences.

articles.headline: Update: Iraq asks OPEC for a higher quota instead of leaving, ahead of Sunday's OPEC+ meeting
articles.summary:
Iraq's oil minister, Basim Mohammed Khudair, said in Kirkuk on 27 November: "We are negotiating with OPEC to raise Iraq's production ceiling" (Bloomberg; Reuters via Devdiscourse). He asked members to consider Iraq's "exceptional circumstances" over five decades. He also said Baghdad wants more US investment in its oil sector (Shafaq News). The Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) reports that Iraq has rejected OPEC's independent assessment of its maximum sustainable capacity, 4.9 million barrels a day. Iraq wants recognition of about 6 million barrels a day; its current quota is about 4.4 million. OPEC+ ministers meet online on Sunday 29 November and are expected to keep current targets. The minister also opened a pumping station on the rehabilitated Iraq–Turkey pipeline, starting at 300,000 barrels a day. In the Gulf, US Central Command said it disabled a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman on 26 November after its crew tried to run the US naval blockade from Bandar Abbas. OPEC has not commented on Iraq's request.

**Background (CEAFE archive):** the 14:30 edition reported a Reuters exclusive that the US pushed Iraq and Venezuela to consider leaving OPEC, and that Iraq's oil ministry advised asking for a higher quota instead (https://x.com/i/status/2126213852572639277). On 28 August CEAFE shared a Bloomberg report, via The Kobeissi Letter, that Venezuela had discussed leaving OPEC with US officials (https://x.com/i/status/2093242918030938214).

**What to watch:** the OPEC+ decision on Sunday; any statement from Venezuela; the outcome of Iraq's quota request.

Sources: Bloomberg https://x.com/i/status/2126350386130817194 and https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-27/iraq-talking-to-opec-about-its-production-ceiling-minister-says, MEES https://www.mees.com/2026/11/27/opec/iraqs-msc-rejection-clouds-opec-meeting-build-up/2037d770-ea6e-11f1-ab06-41c99db91919, Shafaq News https://shafaq.com/en/Economy/Baghdad-seeks-higher-OPEC-quota-US-oil-investment, Reuters (reprint) https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/international/4013283-iraq-in-talks-with-opec-for-higher-oil-production-ceiling-minister-says, US Central Command https://x.com/i/status/2126367015493603807, International Energy Agency https://x.com/i/status/2126338265103974871.
articles.why: Baghdad is following the line Reuters described: stay in OPEC but ask for more barrels. This keeps OPEC together for now, but US leverage over Iraqi oil money remains. Europe imports almost all its oil. The International Energy Agency says the Hormuz crisis is now the main driver of new renewable capacity worldwide, which is also Europe's own route to lower dependence.

articles.headline: Argentina's audit office: a third of the central bank's gold sits in London
articles.summary:
Argentina's General Audit Office (AGN) approved by majority, on 26 November, its report on the central bank's transfer of gold abroad. Between June and August 2024 the central bank sent 1,000 gold bars in four shipments to the Bank of England in London. The Bank of England acted as custodian for the Bank for International Settlements, the central banks' bank based in Basel. 115 bars were recast to London market standards (La Nación; El Cronista; Infobae). The ounces were credited to an "unallocated gold" account. This means Argentina now holds a claim on a quantity of gold, not on specific bars. The share of its 61.7 tonnes of gold held in that account rose from 11.3% to 31.6%. The auditors found no approved procedure for the transfer and no full risk assessment, including of a clause that sends disputes to arbitration in Zurich. They had no access to the insurance policy. They also found three placements of 32,000 ounces each in late 2024 that the central bank had denied. They asked for a more cautious strategy and for the gold to be brought back (Perfil). The central bank says the shipments were documented and approved, and that its denial referred only to 2025. Three auditors voted against the report. The audit office's president, Juan Manuel Olmos, is also the legal representative of the opposition Peronist party (La Nación). Some posts on X claim the gold was "stolen" or sent to the United States; the audit does not say that.

**Background (CEAFE archive):** in August 2024 CEAFE shared posts reporting that President Milei's government had begun shipping part of Argentina's gold abroad (https://x.com/i/status/1818974494712635538). The 14:30 edition today covered US control of Venezuelan and Iraqi oil money.

**What to watch:** the central bank's formal reply; any request to bring the gold back.

Sources: General Audit Office (AGN) https://x.com/i/status/2126309467264524721 and https://x.com/i/status/2126309428559290660, La Nación https://www.lanacion.com.ar/economia/tras-el-envio-de-1000-lingotes-el-banco-central-paso-a-tener-casi-un-tercio-de-su-oro-en-el-exterior-nid26112026/, El Cronista https://www.cronista.com/economia-politica/oro-del-bcra-la-agn-aprobo-una-auditoria-con-hallazgos-que-complican-al-central/, Perfil https://www.perfil.com/politica/el-oro-argentino-esta-en-londres-y-el-pais-ya-no-tiene-custodia-fisica-de-los-lingotes-segun-auditoria-de-la-agn-aZBqT8U8aLA8, EFE https://efe.com/economia/2026-11-27/auditoria-envio-lingotes-de-oro-banco-central-argentino-inglaterra/, Infobae https://www.infobae.com/economia/2026/11/26/segun-la-agn-el-bcra-envio-1000-barras-de-oro-al-banco-de-inglaterra-y-fundio-115-lingotes/, Steve Hanke https://x.com/i/status/2126309075877048341.
articles.why: reserves held abroad can be frozen or used as leverage, as Venezuela's gold at the Bank of England and US control of Venezuelan and Iraqi oil money show. Where a country keeps its gold is a question of sovereignty. Europe has the same debate about reserves held in New York.

articles.headline: Update: Section 301 tariffs — China's business council demands withdrawal and India says its US deal is nearly done
articles.summary:
Chinese business groups, through the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade, urged the US to withdraw the proposed extra tariffs on China and 13 other economies (Xinhua, Chinese state media). The tariffs follow the US "Section 301" investigation into "structural excess capacity". South Africa's foreign minister, Ronald Lamola, said: "We have been very cordial. Unfortunately the aggression has been coming from the US." He kept the door open to more talks (Bloomberg). India's trade minister said the India–US trade deal is nearing completion (Reuters). An Al Jazeera analysis notes that the new tariffs hit China hardest, weeks before Trump and Xi meet again at the G20 summit in Miami. Reuters describes them as an attempt to "prise global trade from China's grip". Global Times, a Chinese state outlet, ran an opinion piece arguing that the EU should move beyond "deficit anxiety" in its trade with China. Bloomberg reports that the US goods trade deficit widened in October for a fourth month in a row. The European Commission has still not responded.

**Background (CEAFE archive):** on 25 November the US Trade Representative said that "with Section 301, President Trump is going country-by-country" (https://x.com/i/status/2125669000369917960). The 25 November 20:30 edition covered the proposed 15% duty on all EU goods, and the 14:30 edition today reported that Japan, India and Vietnam were seeking their own way out.

**What to watch:** the Commission's response; the deadline for public comment on the Section 301 action; the G20 summit in Miami.

Sources: Xinhua https://x.com/i/status/2126295651642482711, Bloomberg (Lamola) https://x.com/i/status/2126296535361065439, Reuters (India) https://x.com/i/status/2126311366717780216, Al Jazeera https://x.com/i/status/2126312051551469731, Reuters https://x.com/i/status/2126313844779933733, Global Times https://x.com/i/status/2126338861760667840, Bloomberg (US deficit) https://x.com/i/status/2126321426449703119.
articles.why: each partner is again looking for its own way out. The EU is one of the 14 targets but has not answered. A Union of 27 that does not respond as a bloc invites separate deals and turns its members into clients.

articles.headline: The Commission clears Deutsche Börse's €5.3 billion takeover of Allfunds without conditions
articles.summary:
The European Commission approved without conditions, on 27 November, Deutsche Börse's purchase of Allfunds, the fund-distribution platform founded in Madrid and listed in Amsterdam (Commission press release IP/26/2592; Deutsche Börse). The deal is worth about €5.3bn (Bloomberg). It still needs other supervisory approvals and the approval of an English court for the UK scheme of arrangement. Deutsche Börse expects to close it in the first quarter of 2027. Brussels Times notes that the approval came despite overlaps in some markets.

**What to watch:** the remaining approvals and closing in the first quarter of 2027.

Sources: European Commission https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/api/files/document/print/it/ip_26_2592/IP_26_2592_EN.pdf, Deutsche Börse https://www.deutsche-boerse.com/dbg-en/media/news-stories/press-releases/Deutsche-B-rse-Group-Receives-Unconditional-Clearance-of-Allfunds-Acquisition-from-European-Commission--5789320, Bloomberg https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-27/deutsche-boerse-s-5-3-billion-allfunds-deal-gets-eu-approval, Reuters https://x.com/i/status/2126362972620468384.
articles.why: here a European buyer takes over a European financial-infrastructure firm, the opposite of the Tesla–EMAG case. Larger European capital-market players are part of the savings and investment union, which is meant to finance European industry and defence.

articles.headline: Reuters: the US used its control of Venezuelan and Iraqi oil money to push both to consider leaving OPEC
articles.summary:
The Trump administration encouraged Venezuela and Iraq to consider leaving OPEC earlier this year and stopped Venezuela from paying its annual membership dues, according to ten people familiar with the matter (Reuters exclusive, 27 November). Both are founding members of the cartel. After the US seized Nicolás Maduro in January, the State Department opened talks with Venezuelan officials on leaving OPEC, because Trump wanted US oil majors to revive Venezuelan output without OPEC limits. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman intervened this summer and persuaded Washington not to press further. In Iraq, Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi raised leaving OPEC at a government meeting after talks with US officials, while Exxon Mobil and Chevron were planning big investments there; his oil ministry talked him out of it and suggested asking for a higher quota instead. The leverage is financial: Washington controls Venezuela's state funds in a US-run account set up after Maduro's removal, and Iraq's oil revenues still pass through an account at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. The State Department said leaving OPEC "has not been among the issues raised by high-level officials". The same morning Trump wrote on Truth Social that he supports al-Zaidi's efforts to "stop the smuggling of Iraqi oil" and "bring all weapons under the exclusive control of the state".

**Background (CEAFE archive):** on 28 August CEAFE shared a Bloomberg report, via The Kobeissi Letter, that Venezuela had been discussing leaving OPEC with US officials (https://x.com/i/status/2093242918030938214).

**What to watch:** reactions from OPEC, Riyadh, Caracas and Baghdad, which did not respond to Reuters; Iraq's quota request; the next OPEC+ meeting.

Sources: Reuters https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/us-pushed-venezuela-iraq-consider-leaving-opec-sources-say-2026-11-27/ (reprint https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/exclusiveus-pushed-venezuela-iraq-to-consider-leaving-opec-sources-say-5052970; post https://x.com/i/status/2126213852572639277), The Independent https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/trump-admin-venezuela-iraq-oil-ope-b3092708.html, Truth Social (Trump) https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/117687912933180934, Al Jazeera https://x.com/i/status/2126279019364544591, @KobeissiLetter https://x.com/i/status/2093242918030938214.
articles.why: this is economic coercion through control of another country's money, a tool that could be used against any state whose reserves or revenues sit in US accounts. A weaker OPEC would leave oil prices more exposed to US decisions, and Europe imports almost all of its oil.

articles.headline: Beijing calls in the state "national team" and Chinese chip stocks post their biggest one-day gain on record
articles.summary:
Premier Li Qiang chaired a State Council executive meeting on Friday that called for stronger market-stabilising mechanisms, more dividends and buybacks, a bigger role for state-backed funds in "steadying the market" and a stronger quasi-"stabilization fund" role for the state-owned Central Huijin Investment "to provide sufficient liquidity" (gov.cn, Chinese government; Xinhua, Chinese state media). The readout came out at about 06:00 Madrid time, during trading hours, which is unusual. The Shanghai Composite closed up 3.73%, the Shenzhen Component 7.24% and the STAR board 14.21% (Xinhua). The CSI Semiconductor index of 40 chip stocks jumped 17.6%, its biggest one-day gain on record, led by CXMT, Cambricon and SMIC, and the CSI 300 rose 4%, its biggest gain since October 2024 (CNBC). It was the first time a State Council meeting explicitly referred to the "national team" (analyst Bob Chen, quoted by CNBC).

**Background (CEAFE archive):** on 20 November CEAFE shared Reuters' report that US AI-chip curbs had hit Chinese tech stocks and spurred a self-sufficiency push (https://x.com/i/status/2123839200390684841). The 08:30 edition reported that profits in China's electronics industry doubled in January–October on AI demand.

**What to watch:** whether the rally holds next week; any Central Huijin purchases.

Sources: State Council (gov.cn) https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202611/27/content_WS6b091065c6d00ca5f9a0ea19.html, Xinhua https://english.news.cn/20261127/cc3749512b134b3aa6a653dd558e9621/c.html, CNBC https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/27/china-chip-stocks-beijing-market-support.html, Reuters Tech https://x.com/i/status/2126272361032765715, Reuters https://x.com/i/status/2123839200390684841.

**CEAFE:** The contrast in scale makes clear that national strategies, however ambitious, are not enough against competitors of a different order of magnitude.
articles.why: Beijing is using state money to back its chip companies on the stock market just as Washington tightens controls on advanced chips. Europe has no comparable tool to back its own semiconductor companies.

articles.headline: Huawei starts selling its Ascend 950 AI chips in South Korea, a US ally
articles.summary:
Huawei has started selling the Ascend 950PR (inference) and 950DT (training) chips and the Atlas 950 SuperNode computing system in South Korea, its first sales of Ascend chips in a new foreign market, with partners including SK Shieldus (Huawei Central, citing DigiTimes). According to Huawei's own figures, the 950PR costs about a quarter of the price of Nvidia's H20 and gives about 2.87 times its inference performance; these are company claims, not independent tests. South Korea's market is booming on AI demand: a Reuters poll forecasts that November exports rose 96.8% year on year, the fastest growth since January 1974, and in 1–20 November chip exports rose 294.4% to $38.5bn, 49.7% of all exports (Reuters; Yonhap). A DDR5 16Gb DRAM chip cost $50 in October 2026, against $8.7 a year earlier (Seoul Economic Daily).

**Background:** Huawei's US court case and its semiconductor push were covered on 25 and 26 November.

**What to watch:** any US Commerce/BIS or Seoul reaction; full Korean November trade data on 1 December.

Sources: @BaiZhongzh20198 https://x.com/i/status/2126248600980119954, Huawei Central https://www.huaweicentral.com/huawei-ascend-ai-chips-made-way-to-south-korea/, Reuters poll https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/south-korea-november-exports-seen-posting-fastest-growth-in-over-50-years-on-ai-chip-surge-reuters-poll-5052897, Yonhap https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261123002551320, Seoul Economic Daily https://en.sedaily.com/economy/2026/11/27/half-of-koreas-export-growth-came-from-higher-prices-not.

**CEAFE:** Figures that illustrate, once again, why European sovereignty is only credible if it is exercised together.
articles.why: Huawei now offers a Chinese alternative to Nvidia in a US ally's market. The AI-chip market is splitting into two blocs, and Europe produces neither leading-edge AI chips nor memory: it buys both, and the memory price boom is raising the cost of its data centres.

articles.headline: Kazakhstan opens its AI market to Russia's Sberbank and Yandex while buying Nvidia's newest chips
articles.summary:
At Sberbank's AI Journey conference in Moscow on 26 November, Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev told Vladimir Putin that Sberbank and Yandex were welcome in Kazakhstan: "they can rely on our comprehensive assistance" (Reuters). A month earlier, during Nvidia chief Jensen Huang's visit to Astana, Kazakhstan's Freedom Holding said it was ordering Nvidia's latest B300 chips (up to 300 servers) for a planned $2bn "Sovereign AI Hub". Russia is cut off from US AI chips by sanctions. A new Russian decree lets Russian companies use data centres abroad with the permission of the security services. Reuters did not report any transfer of US chips from Kazakhstan to Russia. Kazakhstan joined the US Pax Silica initiative in June.

**Background (CEAFE archive):** on 17 November CEAFE shared China's protest against the new US restrictions on remote access to advanced semiconductors (Global Times, https://x.com/i/status/2122715421203935438), the BIS rule of 16 November aimed precisely at computing power used from third countries.

**What to watch:** BIS or OFAC action on Central Asian data centres; Nvidia B300 delivery terms.

Sources: Reuters (Euronext reprint) https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/kazakhstan-boosts-ai-cooperation-russia-which-hungry-advanced-us-chips, Mint https://www.livemint.com/technology/kazakhstan-boosts-ai-cooperation-with-russia-which-is-hungry-for-advanced-us-chips-11795718842030.html, Airpress.kz https://airpress.kz/politics/kazahstan-rasshiryaet-ii-sotrudnichestvo-rossiya-reuters/, Reuters https://x.com/i/status/2126272353654940131, BIS https://www.bis.gov/press-release/bis-issues-rule-addressing-remote-access-american-super-intelligence-technology, Global Times https://x.com/i/status/2122715421203935438.
articles.why: EU sanctions on Russia face the same problem with Central Asia. Kazakhstan's membership of Pax Silica and its opening to Russian AI firms show the limits of US-led technology blocs.

articles.headline: Update: Section 301 tariffs — Japan, India and Vietnam seek their own way out while Brussels has yet to respond
articles.summary:
Japan's trade minister Ryosei Akazawa said on Friday that "we cannot say that there won't be a significant impact": the US plan would restore duties on most Japanese goods to 15% from 12.5% and says they could rise to 20% (Japan Times). Indian Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said talks were "close to culmination"; USTR has proposed a 25% Section 301 tariff on India, falling to 17% with a trade deal (Business Standard; Indian Express). Vietnam expects a deal with "a significantly lower final tariff rate" (Bloomberg). The China Council for the Promotion of International Trade urged the US to withdraw the proposed hikes (Global Times, Chinese state media). The European Commission, whose bloc is one of the 14 targets, had not said publicly by 12:40 Madrid time how it will respond. On Euronews, ECIPE's Hosuk Lee-Makiyama called the tariffs a way of "reconstituting the old tariffs that were necessary to force Europe into a deal".

**Background (CEAFE archive):** on 25 November USTR said that "with Section 301, President Trump is going country-by-country" (https://x.com/i/status/2125669000369917960); the 25 November 20:30 edition covered the proposed 15% duty on all EU goods.

**What to watch:** the Commission's response and comment filing; a MOFCOM statement.

Sources: The Japan Times https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/2026/11/27/trump-tariff-japan/, Business Standard https://www.business-standard.com/economy/news/india-us-trade-deal-close-to-culmination-piyush-goyal-ustr-tariff-126112700570_1.html, Indian Express https://indianexpress.com/article/business/united-states-proposes-25-percent-section-301-tariffs-india-17-percent-trade-deal-ustr-10978398/, Reuters https://x.com/i/status/2126249719374516431, Bloomberg https://x.com/i/status/2126219508473839957, Global Times https://www.globaltimes.cn/page/202611/1375183.shtml, Euronews https://x.com/i/status/2126241252660351212, USTR https://ustr.gov/about/policy-offices/press-office/press-releases/2026/november/ustr-makes-determinations-and-proposes-actions-14-section-301-investigations-relating-structural, @USTradeRep https://x.com/i/status/2125669000369917960.

**CEAFE:** The EU as a whole can bear comparison; each capital on its own cannot. That is the difference that matters.
articles.why: Washington negotiates country by country, and each partner seeks its own exemption. The EU only carries weight if it answers as a bloc; so far it has not said how it will respond. The tariffs are still proposals open to public comment.

SAP prepares at least 10,000 job cuts for its AI shift; Stellantis plans more plant stoppages

articles.headline: Update: Imperial Brands — Japan Tobacco shares jump on a possible joint break-up bid with Altria
articles.summary:
Japan Tobacco shares rose 4.1% to ¥5,754 in Tokyo on Friday and were up about 4.6% at ¥5,779 at the midday break, after Bloomberg reported that JT and Altria are considering a joint all-cash offer for Imperial Brands (Investing.com; Minkabu). The idea is to buy Imperial and split its assets by region. JT declined to comment. Imperial says it has received no approach but would consider any proposal (CNA/Reuters). Analysts say JT would take Imperial’s US brands to become a “3rd-place US competitor” (Jefferies) and could add Imperial’s African and Middle Eastern businesses. That would help replace revenue lost after President Putin ordered the seizure of JT’s Russian assets this month; JT expects an $8.7bn loss from the seizure (Investing.com). For Altria it would mean a return to selling cigarettes outside the US, two decades after it spun off Philip Morris International.

**Key facts**

- Imperial market value about £25.9bn (US$34bn) (CNA); a deal would be the largest in the sector since BAT–Reynolds (US$60bn, 2016).

- JT cash: ¥887.3bn (US$5.6bn) at end-September; it could reissue treasury shares worth about $7.4bn (BTIG).

- UK “put up or shut up” deadline for Altria: 24 December.
articles.why: a US–Japanese pincer on one of the last big European tobacco groups (Davidoff, Gauloises, West). Tobacco is outside CEAFE’s strategic US-takeover list, so the tracker is not updated. JT is 37.6% owned by the Japanese state (CNA).

articles.headline: SAP prepares at least 10,000 job cuts for its AI shift; Stellantis plans more plant stoppages
articles.summary:
SAP is preparing a plan to cut at least 10,000 positions, at least 9% of its global workforce, to rebuild its software business around AI, Bloomberg reported on 26 November, citing people familiar with the matter. The number is not final and could change after labour talks. Product and engineering and sales are the main focus. SAP would only say that it “continuously reviews its organization to ensure it remains aligned with its strategy and customer needs” (Bloomberg; Irish Examiner). SAP employs more than 110,000 people. In Germany, the works council has negotiated a job guarantee to 2028. Its last restructuring, announced in 2024, cut about 10,000 positions and cost about €3bn (Irish Examiner; Calcalist). The same evening, Bloomberg reported that Stellantis is planning further plant stoppages in Europe in the coming weeks, and Reuters quoted the carmaker as saying that keeping production in Italy is a “daily challenge” amid rising costs (posts reposted by @F_CEAFE; full articles not checked).

**Key facts**

- SAP: ≥10,000 positions, ≥9% of the workforce; headcount 111,397 at end-2025; hiring frozen except core AI roles since July (Calcalist).

- SAP usually announces restructurings with its full-year results in late January.

- Stellantis: further European stoppages planned (Bloomberg); rising costs in Italy (Reuters).
articles.why: Europe’s most valuable tech company and one of its largest carmakers are both cutting European capacity in the same week. That follows the Renault job cuts already in the briefs. AI-driven restructuring at SAP shows that Europe’s software champion is also under cost pressure from US AI platforms.

articles.headline: Update: two more tankers hit mines near Hormuz, a Saudi refinery is attacked and Brent stays near $96; Turkey extends Iranian gas imports to 2032
articles.summary:
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said two oil tankers struck sea mines and caught fire north of Oman’s Khasab port while using an “unauthorised” route; one was a supertanker carrying more than 2 million barrels (Arab News; IRNA). Separately, an attack on Saudi Arabia’s Jazan refinery temporarily halted some operations and killed one worker (Bloomberg). Brent settled at about $96.57 on 26 November and traded around $96.2 on Friday morning, on track to end a three-week losing streak (Yahoo Finance; CNBC; Reuters). OPEC+ meets on Sunday and is likely to roll over output targets for at least Q1 2027 amid disputes over capacity assessments (Reuters via Kitco). Turkey has extended its gas import contract with Iran for five years at 10 bcm a year, with volume and pricing unchanged; BOTAŞ’s import licence now runs to 18 April 2032 (Turkish press; carci.news). Australia’s parliament passed a gas reservation scheme requiring LNG exporters to set aside up to 20% of output for the domestic market from 2028 (Reuters).

**Key facts**

- Brent ~$96.6 settle (26 Nov); WTI ~$84.8 (Yahoo Finance).

- Iran–Turkey: 10 bcm/yr, extended after the 25-year contract expired in July.

- Australia: up to 20% domestic reservation from 2028.
articles.why: with EU gas storage already low, a Gulf risk premium that will not go away, Turkey locking in Iranian gas and Australia reserving LNG for home use all tighten the supply that Europe competes for. @F_CEAFE reposted the Iran–Turkey renewal.

articles.headline: China's industrial profits up 16% in January–October, doubled in electronics on AI demand; carmakers down 26%
articles.summary:
China’s National Bureau of Statistics said on 27 November that profits of industrial firms above designated size rose 16.0% year on year to ¥6.737tn (about US$1tn) in January–October, up from 15.5% in January–September. October alone was up 20.1% (NBS). Electronics profits doubled and contributed 9.7 percentage points of the growth, driven by AI computing demand for memory chips. High-tech manufacturing profits rose 50.9%; optical fibre manufacturing profits rose 6.7-fold on data-centre construction (Xinhua). Non-ferrous metals rose 71.7% and coal mining 61.4%. Automakers fell 26.0%, electrical machinery fell 8.0% and the power sector fell 18.4% (NBS). Foreign-invested firms’ profits rose only 0.2%. The EIU said the recovery “has yet to broaden into a more durable improvement in corporate profitability” (CNBC).

**Key facts**

- Mining +38.8%, manufacturing +17.5%, utilities −14.8% (NBS).

- Profit margin 5.69%, +0.45 pp; finished-goods inventories +12.0% (NBS).

- State-controlled firms +13.0%; private firms +11.4%; foreign-invested +0.2%.
articles.why: China’s profit rebound is concentrated in AI hardware and raw materials, where Europe depends on Chinese supply, while Chinese carmakers’ profits are collapsing. That is the pressure behind cheaper Chinese car exports to Europe and the “overcapacity” dispute.

articles.headline: Update: Section 301 — Embraer and Brazil fight a new 10% US duty on aircraft; Beijing calls "overcapacity" a false pretext
articles.summary:
USTR proposed on 25 November to end the exemption for finished aircraft in its Section 301 action on Brazil and impose an extra 10% duty, plus a higher out-of-quota sugar tariff; a hearing is set for 14 January 2027 (USTR). Embraer said it was “caught off guard” and warned the duty would raise US airline costs and airfares. Its E175, the most flown aircraft in the US, has no US-made competitor and more than 40% US content. Brazil’s Vice President Geraldo Alckmin called the proposal “completely unreasonable” (Reuters via StreetInsider). At the 26 November MFA press conference, spokesperson Guo Jiakun rejected the US tariff escalation and called “industrial overcapacity” a false pretext (MFA).

**Key facts**

- Brazil already faces a 25% Section 301 tariff on certain goods (since July 2026); aircraft are Brazil’s fourth-largest export to the US (USTR).

- Embraer: US$3.5bn of assets and 2,500+ employees in the US; no effect on 2026 deliveries.
articles.why: the 10% aircraft duty breaks the zero-tariff aerospace regime in place since the 1980s, the same regime that shields Airbus. If Washington starts taxing foreign airliners, the EU–US aircraft truce is next in line.

articles.headline: Altria confirms it is considering an all-cash offer for Britain’s Imperial Brands; Japan Tobacco is also studying a deal
articles.summary:
US group Altria (Richmond, Virginia; Marlboro in the US) confirmed on 26 November that it is “considering a possible offer” for London-listed Imperial Brands and that any offer “is likely to be solely in cash”. It also said it is “in discussions with a third party regarding its possible acquisition of part of the business of Imperial Brands”, with no agreement yet (Altria, Rule 2.4 statement). Imperial’s board said it “has not had any discussions with, or received any approach or proposal from, Altria or the third party” and told shareholders to take no action. Under the UK Takeover Code Altria must make a firm offer or walk away by 17:00 London time on 24 December 2026 (Imperial Brands RNS). Bloomberg reported that Japan Tobacco is also studying a deal, possibly with a partner, splitting Imperial’s assets by region. Imperial shares jumped as much as 17.6% to 3,562p, valuing it at £26.77bn (about US$35bn) (Reuters via Investing.com).

**Key facts**

- Buyer: Altria Group (US), market value about US$126.9bn; possible partner: an unnamed third party for part of the business. Rival interest: Japan Tobacco (Japan), about US$69.5bn.

- Target: Imperial Brands plc (UK), market value £26.77bn after the jump.

- Deadline: “put up or shut up” by 24 December 2026.

- Altria and JT already run a smoke-free joint venture (2022). RBC says a joint bid “would neatly swerve anti-trust objections”.
articles.why: it would be one of the largest takeovers of a British company in a decade. London-listed firms are cheap: Imperial trades at 8.3 times forward earnings against 12.6 for Altria and 17.7 for JT (LSEG via Reuters). Tobacco is not a strategic sector under CEAFE’s US-takeover list, so it is not added to that list. But it shows the same pattern: depressed European valuations make European headquarters and brands (Davidoff, Gauloises) easy prey for US and Asian capital. Imperial announced up to 4,600 job cuts last week.

articles.headline: Update: Section 301 “overcapacity” tariffs: Singapore is “very disappointed”, partners hit back, and Global Times says Brussels “waved the white flag”
articles.summary:
The US Trade Representative’s Section 301 findings on “structural excess capacity” in 14 economies, including the EU, published on 25 November (US time), keep drawing replies. Singapore’s Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry said: “Singapore disagrees with the USTR’s findings and we are very disappointed with the proposed actions.” The USTR proposes up to 20% on Singapore’s exports, cut to 10% with a reciprocal trade agreement. METI stressed that the US has run a trade surplus with Singapore for over 20 years, US$33bn in 2025 (METI). Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong said the effective levy on Singapore’s exports would rise from 7.8% to 10.3% (Reuters). AP reports that China and other partners are pushing back and that the duties are likely to take effect early next year. They are intended to rebuild the tariffs the Supreme Court struck down in February. European stocks nonetheless rallied as “tariff fears ease” (Reuters).

The reaction to Europe’s reply is the new element. On 25 November Commission spokesman Olof Gill said the EU “strongly reject[s] the premise that Europe is a source of structural overcapacity” and that “Europe is among those most exposed to overcapacity… much of it state-driven and concentrated in third countries. We regret the lack of joint action” (RTÉ). A Global Times [Chinese state media] editorial answered: “The moment Washington raised its tariff stick, the European Commission immediately waved the white flag, willingly offering itself as an accomplice in exchange for being spared.” It said that “what Europe needs is strategic autonomy, not strategic subservience”.

**Key facts**

- 14 economies targeted; Singapore up to 20% (10% with a deal); EU expects the 15% cap to be respected “in full, including when combined with existing duties” (Gill).

- US trade surplus with Singapore: US$27bn (2024), US$33bn (2025) (METI).

- Public consultation period still to come; measures likely early 2027 (AP).
articles.why: the EU’s 15% ceiling from the 2025 Turnberry deal is again on the table, and the Commission’s first instinct was to offer Washington a joint front against China rather than defend the rules. Beijing is exploiting the contradiction. Europe is caught between US tariffs and Chinese pressure, and has no reciprocity tool of its own in use.

articles.headline: The EU Quantum Act shuts Chinese firms out of quantum procurement but leaves the door open to US suppliers; Beijing calls it discrimination
articles.summary:
The draft Quantum Act unveiled by the Commission on 25 November says that “given the possible impact of quantum technologies for security and the Union’s strategic interests and technological autonomy, it is necessary to restrict procurement procedures to products, systems and services that are provided by Union controlled entities”. Suppliers from countries with a reciprocal partnership or that belong to the WTO Government Procurement Agreement (GPA) may also bid (draft quoted by Reuters, via Global Times). China is not a GPA party, so Chinese firms are excluded, while US firms can sell computers, simulators and imaging systems to EU governments (SCMP). An EU official added that Chinese-controlled entities in Hong Kong, a GPA member, could be excluded on security grounds (SCMP). Huo Jianguo of the China Society for WTO Studies told Global Times [Chinese state media] the exclusion is “outright discrimination” and that it “will only hold back the EU’s own progress in quantum technology”.

**CEAFE comment:** Technological and defence dependence is not abstract: it shows up in the number of companies, in spending and in the presence on the ground.

**Key facts**

- Criterion: EU-controlled entities plus GPA/reciprocal partners; security exception case by case.

- Linked to the Sovereign Tech Equity Fund proposal (covered 25 Nov 20:30).

- EPRS (Sept 2026) notes the same GPA logic in the Industrial Accelerator Act would exclude China and admit the US.
articles.why: the Commission’s own figures show the EU hosts 32% of the world’s quantum companies (US 25%, China 5%) but holds just 6% of quantum patents (US 23%, China 46%) (European Commission report published in 2025, cited by GT). Closing the market to China while opening it to the US follows the pattern of the Industrial Accelerator Act and the procurement reform (EPRS). It protects European champions from Chinese competition but not from US competitors. That is a half-sovereignty that matches Washington’s technology-control line.

articles.headline: OPEC+ set to roll over output targets; refining margins slump; Iraq–Kurdistan oil standoff; refinery blast in Bangkok
articles.summary: OPEC+ is likely to roll over its oil output targets for the first quarter, as disputes over capacity persist and the Iran war adds uncertainty (Reuters and Bloomberg, citing sources). Refiners’ margins on turning crude into fuel have slumped to their lowest in months as supply recovers and demand stays sluggish (Bloomberg). In Iraq the federal government and the Kurdish region are in their sharpest confrontation in years over control of oil fields and border crossings, and thousands rallied in Kurdistan (Al Jazeera English). An explosion and fire at the Phra Khanong refinery in Bangkok injured at least seven people (Reuters; Japan Times; Xinhua [Chinese state media]).
articles.why: after this morning’s Gulf supply shock (14:30 edition, topic 5), an OPEC+ rollover keeps supply tight while Europe already pays a war premium on LNG. Lower refining margins give some relief on diesel prices.

articles.headline: Huawei’s patent licences exceed US$6.9 billion, with Qualcomm, HP Inc. and Harman among its licensees
articles.summary:
At its seventh Innovation and Intellectual Property Forum in Beijing on 24 November, Huawei said that the cumulative value of its outbound patent-licensing agreements now exceeds US$6.9 billion. Its patent-licensing revenue in 2025 was about US$800 million, and it signed 20 new licensees that year in network equipment, consumer electronics and computing, IoT, automotive, streaming and semiconductors (Huawei newsroom). According to Global Times [Chinese state media], foreign companies that took licences directly from Huawei in 2025–26 include Qualcomm, HP Inc. and Harman in the US, Mercedes-Benz and Volkswagen Group companies in Germany, and Seiko Solutions, Mitsubishi Fuso and Fujitec in Japan. The US deals are public. On 26 August 2026 Huawei and HP Inc. signed a multi-year global cross-licence that includes certain Huawei Wi-Fi patents. On 5 October 2026 Huawei and Qualcomm announced a multi-year, broad cross-licence covering 5G, compute, AI and networking, together with Qualcomm’s purchase of certain Huawei US patents. Huawei said that deal would close after regulatory approval (Huawei newsroom). Terms are confidential, and neither side has published amounts. A Qualcomm spokesperson said that “reports characterizing Qualcomm as a net payor on the license agreement are incorrect” and that the patents it is buying are “non-cellular US patents” (ip fray; Huawei Central). Huawei’s chief IP officer Alan Fan (Fan Zhiyong) said: “At Huawei, a patent represents more than a legal right. It represents an innovative achievement and a source of pride for the people behind it.” Huawei added that it received 3,052 US patents in 2025, ranking fourth in the US according to IFI Claims (Global Times).

**Linked story (Update, US case against Huawei):** on 24 November (US Eastern time) a jury in the US District Court for the Eastern District of New York convicted Huawei of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and of fraud linked to its business in Iran, but acquitted it of the racketeering (RICO) charge (AP; BBC; TIME). In its official statement Huawei said: “Huawei welcomes this decision. It confirms that these allegations lack factual basis and vindicates our consistent position over the past eight years.” It added: “We believe the government’s remaining charges are equally without legal or factual merit… We will thoroughly review the relevant verdicts and take all necessary legal actions to defend our rights and interests.” Lead defence counsel Brian Heberlig called the acquittal a “profound rejection” of the government’s case (AP; BBC; statement posted by @Huawei on X). China’s Foreign Ministry had already said on 25 November that it “firmly opposes US suppression of Chinese companies” (14:30 edition, 25 Nov).

**Background (CEAFE archive):** On 27 August 2026 @F_CEAFE reposted the announcement that Huawei and HP Inc. had signed a multiyear global patent cross-licence ([repost](https://x.com/i/status/2093031520235561408)), one of the licensing deals now counted in the total.

**Key facts**

- Cumulative value of Huawei’s outbound patent-licensing agreements: over US$6.9bn (to November 2026); licensing revenue about US$800m in 2025 (Huawei, 24 Nov).

- Huawei says it holds over 165,000 active granted patents and has invested more than US$270bn in R&D since 2007 (Huawei statement, 25 Nov).

- Share of active granted patents: wireless communications 41%, terminal hardware 16%, AI and computing 13% (Huawei).

- US licensees named: Qualcomm (cross-licence plus patent purchase, 5 Oct 2026), HP Inc. (cross-licence incl. Wi-Fi, 26 Aug 2026) and Harman (named by Global Times; Harman is US-based and owned by Samsung Electronics). No amounts disclosed.

- Qualcomm’s purchase of Huawei patents is subject to regulatory approval, which ip fray says is an antitrust (HSR Act) review.
articles.why: a company that Washington has been trying to cut off from US technology since 2019, through the Entity List and the foreign direct product rule, now collects royalties from US champions such as Qualcomm and HP. The flow of dependence in standard-essential technologies (5G, Wi-Fi, video codecs) has partly reversed. Huawei says its patented technologies were used in more than 3.2 billion 5G devices by the end of 2025. Europe’s car industry is also paying: Mercedes-Benz and Volkswagen are on the licensee list. Meanwhile European governments have been excluding Huawei from 5G networks at Washington’s urging. Here is another case where Europe applies US-driven restrictions while US companies themselves keep doing business with the target. A Qualcomm purchase of Huawei US patents still needs regulatory clearance, which turns a court and export-control battle into a commercial negotiation.

articles.headline: US chip curbs and anti-distillation defences slow Chinese AI models; Moonshot looks to rent computing power in Europe
articles.summary:
Reuters reports, citing people familiar with the matter, that Z.AI (Zhipu) has fallen behind schedule on its next flagship model, GLM-5.5, with about 3 trillion parameters. The model was due this month, and the new US rule could push it into the first quarter of 2027 or later. Moonshot AI expects the interval between its major releases to double from six months to a year or more if it loses access to overseas computing power, and its Kimi K4 could slip to around mid-2027. The cause is twofold. A Commerce Department rule in force since 19 November requires licences for Chinese access to large amounts of US-chip computing power in overseas data centres. And OpenAI and Anthropic have strengthened their defences against “distillation”, i.e. training models on the answers of stronger ones. Anthropic said in September it had seen nearly 200 million exchanges with Claude linked to suspected distillation campaigns, which it attributed to Chinese developers including Alibaba, Moonshot and Z.AI. According to Reuters, Moonshot has stepped up efforts to rent computing power in Europe and plans to approach Chinese chipmakers about training on their processors. No official Chinese response yet.

**Key facts**

- US Commerce compute-access licensing rule in force since 19 Nov 2026 (Reuters).

- Z.AI released GLM-5.4 on 23 Nov, built on a 750bn-parameter model (Reuters).

- Moonshot releases: K2 (July 2025), K2.5 (January 2026), K3 (July 2026) (Reuters).
articles.why: European data centres are becoming the next front of US extraterritorial controls. If Chinese developers turn to rented European compute, the remote-access rule and future US pressure will land on European cloud operators, who would have to police their customers on Washington’s terms. This follows the Nvidia shipment freeze to South-East Asia (topic 2, 08:30 edition).

articles.headline: Update: UniCredit obtains every clearance for Commerzbank; new shares to be credited by 7 December
articles.summary: UniCredit announced at 07:45 on 26 November that the Polish Financial Supervision Authority (KNF) has approved the indirect change of control of Commerzbank’s Polish operations, including mBank (69.1% owned by Commerzbank, about 5.9 million customers). With that, all regulatory clearances are in place and all conditions of the exchange offer launched on 5 May 2026 are met. New UniCredit shares for the tendered Commerzbank shares are expected to be credited by 7 December 2026. UniCredit has asked Commerzbank to convene an extraordinary general meeting to elect new shareholder representatives to the supervisory board. The European Commission had cleared the deal unconditionally on 16 November, and the US Federal Reserve also approved it (Euronews). The breakthrough came from the deal with Berlin in mid-November. In a letter of 18 November to Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil, CEO Andrea Orcel set out eight “binding principles”: Frankfurt as German headquarters, keeping the listing and the AG legal form, German nationals on UniCredit’s board from the 2027 renewal, and support for Mittelstand exporters. The German state still holds about 13.3% of Commerzbank and has not announced a sale. Reuters Breakingviews values the deal at nearly US$45bn.
articles.why: this is a major cross-border banking combination inside the euro area. It shows that European champions can be built across borders, though only after two years of political resistance from Berlin. It is an example of the intra-European consolidation CEAFE considers necessary, since no single member state’s banking sector can match the scale of the US giants on its own. Not posted by @F_CEAFE.

articles.headline: Update: Beijing answers the EU hybrid-car safeguard: “protectionism leads nowhere”
articles.summary: At MOFCOM’s regular press conference on 26 November, spokesperson He Yadong responded to the Commission’s preliminary ruling of 24 November. The ruling sets provisional quotas for hybrid vehicles from 1 December for up to 200 days, with China’s share about 192,000 units during the period (350,000 annualised), the largest of nine suppliers. He said the two sides had held pre-initiation consultations and “reached an understanding on hybrid vehicle trade arrangements” on three principles: WTO compliance, non-discrimination and respect for facts. China “hopes the EU will earnestly abide by the consensus” and investigate fairly under WTO rules, and “will keep a close watch… and firmly protect the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese industries” (MOFCOM; Xinhua [Chinese state media]). An opinion piece in Global Times [Chinese state media] the same day accused the Commission of having “waved the white flag” to Washington’s tariffs while acting as its “accomplice”.
articles.why: the measure (14:30 edition, 25 Nov) is a global safeguard, not an anti-China duty, and Beijing’s tone is measured because it says a prior understanding exists. CEAFE’s point is the contrast: Brussels uses trade defence against China while accepting the US Section 301 “overcapacity” tariff of 15% without retaliation.

articles.headline: Gulf supply shock: Houthi strike on Ras Tanura and mines in Hormuz lift Brent towards US$95; Qatar’s LNG exports reach a war-time high at much higher insurance costs
articles.summary: Brent closed 3.5% higher on Wednesday 25 November and WTI 2% higher, after Yemen’s Houthis said they had attacked Saudi Arabia’s Ras Tanura refinery and Riyadh’s financial district. Iranian state media and the Iranian army, cited by Fars, said tankers struck mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz. Early on Thursday Brent traded at US$94.71 and WTI at US$84.03 (CNBC/Reuters). Prices later eased (Reuters, 13:00 Madrid). OPEC+ ministers meet on 29 November to set 2027 output, without the UAE, which has left the group. Qatar’s LNG exports are on track for their busiest month since the US–Iran war began at the end of February. Kpler counts 36 berthings at Ras Laffan so far in November, against 35 in October and 21 in September. Exports remain at around 40% of pre-war levels (analysts via Reuters), or about half (Bloomberg). War-risk insurance for ships entering the Gulf has risen from about 0.25% of hull value at the start of 2026 to as much as 5%, adding US$2.5–12.5 million per voyage for a modern US$250 million LNG carrier (Wood Mackenzie via Reuters).
articles.why: Europe competes with Asia for the same scarce LNG cargoes, and the insurance premium ends up in European gas and electricity prices. As ECFR warned on 25 November, the US could supply up to 80% of EU LNG imports by 2030. Every Gulf shock deepens Europe’s dependence on US LNG.

articles.headline: Germany’s 2027 budget: record €561 billion, €210 billion of borrowing and €139 billion for defence, more than double France’s €63.4 billion
articles.summary:
The Bundestag is holding its final debates on the 2027 federal budget. Spending will be just under €561bn, a record, with record borrowing of about €210bn (DW). Defence gets €109bn in the core budget, €27bn more than in 2026. With the debt-financed Bundeswehr special fund, the total reaches €139bn (DW; Defence24 gives €139.4bn = €109.7bn + €29.6bn). France’s 2027 defence budget is €63.4bn, up from €57bn in 2026 (Politico Europe). Chancellor Merz said that “if we don’t change course, in a few years… all federal revenue will have to be spent on social programmes, interest payments, and defence.” The labour and social affairs budget exceeds €200bn. The AfD called it a “debt budget” and attacked aid to Ukraine (posts reposted by @F_CEAFE).

**CEAFE comment:** No member state, on its own, has the scale of the powers it hopes to sit beside at the same table.

<!-- ceafe-chart: gasto_militar_ue -->

**Key facts**

- 2027 federal spending about €561bn; new borrowing about €210bn (DW, 25 Nov).

- Defence 2027: €109bn core + special fund = €139bn (DW); France €63.4bn (Politico Europe).
articles.why: a single member state spending more than twice as much as France changes the balance within the EU. Even so, it does so on debt and at the expense of social spending, proof that no member state can carry rearmament alone. The case for common European financing and joint procurement is stronger than for national budget races.
