articles.headline: Actualización: chips de Nvidia para China: un senador de EE. UU. pide «preguntas difíciles» al secretario de Comercio, Lutnick
articles.summary:
**El senador republicano John Kennedy dijo el domingo que el secretario de Comercio, Howard Lutnick, debe responder ante el Congreso a «preguntas difíciles» sobre si su departamento permitió a empresas chinas «eludir» las normas de exportación y obtener chips de IA de Nvidia (The Washington Post).**

«Me parece, y subrayo "parece", que el Departamento de Comercio ha permitido al Partido Comunista de China…», declaró. Sus palabras siguen a la afirmación del secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent, de que Washington «aún necesita respuestas» de Nvidia (edición de las 20:30 del 22 de noviembre) y a la revelación del Comité de Asuntos Exteriores de la Cámara de 879.868 chips de Nvidia y AMD con licencia de la Oficina de Industria y Seguridad (BIS) para China (20 de noviembre). En el periodo no se publicó ninguna nueva medida de la BIS ni de la OFAC.

**Qué vigilar:** si el Congreso cita a Lutnick a declarar; cualquier endurecimiento de la BIS; la reacción china en la rueda de prensa de Exteriores de este lunes.

**Fuentes:** [The Washington Post](https://x.com/i/status/2124627739453816835), [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2124587510596575679), [Bloomberg Opinion](https://x.com/i/status/2124595054475899085)
articles.why: el debate en Washington es ahora si Comercio concedió demasiadas licencias a China; cualquier endurecimiento se aplicaría también a los centros de datos de los Estados miembros de la UE en virtud de la norma de la BIS sobre acceso remoto del 16 de noviembre, una decisión en la que Europa no tiene voz.

articles.headline: Actualización: la caída de la IA llega a Asia: el Kospi se desploma hasta un 5,8 %
articles.summary:
**Los mercados asiáticos prolongaron este lunes el desplome tecnológico del viernes: el Kospi de Seúl, dominado por Samsung Electronics y SK Hynix, llegó a caer un 5,8 % antes de moderar las pérdidas al 3,2 % a las 05:30, hora de Madrid (Al Jazeera).**

El Hang Seng y el CSI 300 cedieron cerca de un 0,6 %, mientras el Taiex de Taiwán giró a un alza del 2,5 %; Tokio cerró por festivo. El viernes el S&P 500 había cerrado con un descenso del 3,7 %, entrando en corrección, y el Nasdaq Composite perdió un 5,3 %; el lunes por la mañana los futuros del S&P 500 y del Nasdaq subían un 2,2 % y un 2,9 % (Al Jazeera). El WSJ informa de que el mercado de deuda espera que los bonos de Anthropic reciban calificación de bono basura. Las exportaciones anuales de Corea del Sur superaron por primera vez el billón de dólares, con las de chips de los primeros 20 días de noviembre un 294,4 % por encima del año anterior (Bloomberg).

**Contexto:** la corrección comenzó tras el estreno bursátil de Anthropic el 19 de noviembre.

**Qué vigilar:** la apertura europea; la reapertura de Tokio el martes; los valores de chips.

**Fuentes:** [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/23/south-koreas-stock-market-tumbles-as-ai-bubble-fears-mount), [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2124712062139908200), [Bloomberg (emergentes)](https://x.com/i/status/2124679362368704635), [Bloomberg (exportaciones coreanas)](https://x.com/i/status/2124659231592783951), [WSJ](https://x.com/i/status/2124720471933440314)
articles.why: tanto el auge como la corrección giran en torno a empresas estadounidenses y asiáticas de chips e IA; Europa tiene pocos grandes actores en esa carrera.

articles.headline: La electricidad a plazo en Europa, cerca de 200 €/MWh: una acería alemana para por horas
articles.summary:
**Los contratos de electricidad a plazo para cada uno de los tres próximos meses cotizan en torno a 200 euros por megavatio hora, aproximadamente el doble que el invierno pasado, por el encarecimiento del gas, informa Bloomberg, que habla de «la segunda gran crisis energética de Europa en menos de cinco años».**

La acería del grupo Feralpi en Riesa (Alemania), propiedad de la italiana Feralpi, consulta dos veces al día los precios eléctricos del día siguiente y ha parado varias veces la producción este otoño aun teniendo pedidos. El gas europeo subió a primera hora del lunes por las previsiones de frío, con unas reservas ya mermadas por las interrupciones de las exportaciones ligadas a la guerra entre EE. UU. e Irán (Bloomberg). La producción de petróleo de Libia cayó tras la interrupción de un oleoducto de su mayor yacimiento.

**Contexto:** las reservas de gas de la UE estaban al 70,5 % el 21 de noviembre, y el índice TTF rondaba los 90 €/MWh la semana pasada (edición del 21 de noviembre).

**Qué vigilar:** el cierre del TTF de hoy; las extracciones de las reservas de la UE.

**Fuentes:** [The Japan Times (Bloomberg)](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/2026/11/23/europe-power-market-economy/), [Bloomberg (gas)](https://x.com/i/status/2124700753172308415), [Bloomberg (petróleo libio)](https://x.com/i/status/2124741018524229929), [Reuters (petróleo)](https://x.com/i/status/2124742281252978853), [Die Sachsen](https://www.diesachsen.de/meissen-news/feralpi-stahlwerk-in-riesa-geht-stundenweise-vom-netz-3181510)
articles.why: la industria intensiva en energía de los Estados miembros de la UE deja de producir cuando se dispara la electricidad; Europa sustituyó buena parte de su gas ruso por GNL estadounidense y paga la prima de precio de la guerra del Golfo.

articles.headline: Actualización: la COP31 termina sin acuerdo; la UE rechaza un texto sin combustibles fósiles
articles.summary:
**La COP31 de Antalya se cerró el domingo sin un acuerdo global tras dos días de prórroga, la cumbre climática de la ONU más larga de la historia (Noticias ONU).**

La Unión Europea se opuso formalmente a la decisión final al no aceptar un texto que omitía toda referencia a los combustibles fósiles o a la transición para abandonarlos, una omisión que calificó de «inadmisible»; las Islas Marshall tampoco la apoyaron. Arabia Saudí, en nombre del Grupo Árabe, defendió las referencias a la captura de carbono; Reuters señala el peso de la influencia saudí en el resultado. El secretario general de la ONU, António Guterres, se mostró decepcionado, y China (Global Times, medio estatal chino) expresó su «profunda decepción». La COP32 se celebrará en Adís Abeba.

**Qué vigilar:** las conclusiones del Consejo de la UE; el debate sobre el objetivo de la UE para 2040.

**Fuentes:** [Noticias ONU](https://news.un.org/en/story/2026/11/1168855), [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2124732212494897643), [Bloomberg](https://x.com/i/status/2124572402868801678), [Global Times](https://x.com/i/status/2124713902789492895), [Al Jazeera](https://x.com/i/status/2124642815384727799)

**En breve:** el Partido Popular promete amplias rebajas fiscales si gana las elecciones generales anticipadas del 29 de noviembre ([Bloomberg](https://x.com/i/status/2124733470140178712)). IQVIA (EE. UU.) / Quotient Sciences (Reino Unido): aún sin anuncio formal.
articles.why: la UE mantuvo su posición pero no logró arrastrar a la conferencia, mientras sus propias normas climáticas pesan sobre el coste de la energía en casa (véase la noticia anterior).

articles.headline: Actualización: el jefe de la inteligencia de EE. UU. dice que los mejores chips de Nvidia se quedan en EE. UU.; Pekín responde que los controles ya no frenan a China
articles.summary:
**En los programas políticos del domingo, el director de Inteligencia Nacional de EE. UU., Jay Clayton, expuso la línea del Gobierno sobre la exportación de chips: «Queremos reservar la capacidad de computación más exquisita para EE. UU. […] Así que sí queremos chips estadounidenses, solo que no los más exquisitos» (Fox News).**

En *This Week*, de ABC, dijo que las normas de exportación de tecnología avanzada «son restricciones, no prohibiciones», que Comercio y el Tesoro se dedican a «dosificar» el acceso, y confirmó que el Departamento de Justicia investiga a Alice Huang, exdirectiva de Megaspeed International, con sede en Singapur, y a su empresa. El secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent, dijo a CBS que el Gobierno «aún necesita respuestas» de Nvidia sobre sus ventas de chips (Bloomberg). Un editorial de *Global Times* (medio estatal chino) respondió que «el impacto marginal de nuevos controles de exportación estadounidenses sobre la industria china de IA disminuye rápidamente» y que las restricciones debilitarán a los fabricantes de chips de EE. UU. en los mercados mundiales.

**Contexto:** la norma de la BIS del 16 de noviembre sobre acceso remoto abarca también a centros de datos en la UE; California investiga si Nvidia vendió ilegalmente chips avanzados a China.

**Qué vigilar:** los próximos pasos de Comercio para hacer cumplir las licencias; la investigación del Departamento de Justicia; un posible comunicado del MOFCOM el lunes.

**Fuentes:** [Jay Clayton en Fox News](https://x.com/i/status/2124531991085207941), [transcripción de ABC News](https://abcnews.com/Politics/week-transcript-11-22-26-director-national-intelligence/story?id=138345755), [Bloomberg](https://x.com/i/status/2124543467439174101), [The Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/world/united-states/spy-chief-says-us-probing-alleged-spy-tied-to-former-nvidia-ceo), [Global Times](https://www.globaltimes.cn/page/202611/1374822.shtml)
articles.why: Washington decide qué nivel de capacidad de computación recibe cada país, y Europa, sin un chip propio de gama alta, recibe el nivel «menos exquisito» salvo licencia.

articles.headline: El grupo estadounidense IQVIA, cerca de comprar la británica Quotient Sciences por unos 1.100 millones de dólares
articles.summary:
**IQVIA Holdings, el grupo estadounidense de investigación clínica, está a punto de cerrar la compra, por unos 1.100 millones de dólares, de Quotient Sciences (Nottingham, Reino Unido), empresa de desarrollo y fabricación por contrato de medicamentos en fase temprana, y el acuerdo podría anunciarse el lunes 23 de noviembre, según fuentes conocedoras citadas por Bloomberg.**

Quotient ayuda a las farmacéuticas a formular nuevos medicamentos, fabricarlos para ensayos clínicos y comprobar cómo se comportan. Pertenece desde 2019 al fondo de capital riesgo Permira. IQVIA y Permira declinaron hacer comentarios.

**Contexto:** la edición de las 14:30 recogió las compras estadounidenses de proveedores europeos de defensa (Steyr Motors, Truflo Marine, Tekne); CEAFE sigue las adquisiciones estadounidenses de empresas europeas estratégicas.

**Qué vigilar:** el anuncio formal; una posible revisión al amparo de la ley británica de Seguridad Nacional e Inversiones o de la CMA.

**Fuentes:** [Bloomberg](https://x.com/i/status/2124514525453959419), [Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/private-equity/iqvia-said-to-near-1-1-billion-deal-for-uks-quotient-sciences)
articles.why: otro eslabón de una cadena de suministro europea estratégica, el desarrollo temprano de fármacos y la fabricación para ensayos clínicos, pasaría a manos estadounidenses.

articles.headline: Tailandia prevé restringir la exportación de químicos usados en la minería de tierras raras de Birmania
articles.summary:
**Tailandia restringirá la exportación y el tránsito de productos químicos usados en la extracción y el procesado de tierras raras hacia Birmania y otros «países afectados», según el vice primer ministro Yodchanan Wongsawat, después de que la contaminación por arsénico de los ríos Kok, Sai y Ruak, en el norte de Tailandia, se vinculara a la minería de tierras raras en el estado birmano de Shan (Reuters).**

La medida está prevista, pero aún no en vigor: el Consejo de Seguridad Nacional elabora una lista de productos químicos, sin fecha de inicio publicada. Tailandia, China y Birmania celebran conversaciones ministeriales el 24 de noviembre y técnicas el 25 y 26.

**Qué vigilar:** las conversaciones trilaterales; la lista de productos químicos.

**Fuentes:** [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2124488153146835338), [Bangkok Post](https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/3359296/riverarsenic-control-plan-advances-public-confidence-low), [The Nation](https://www.nationthailand.com/news/general/40073770), [Thai PBS World](https://www.thaipbsworld.com/world/573123)
articles.why: las minas birmanas son una fuente importante de las tierras raras pesadas que se refinan en China; una restricción podría tensar el suministro de los imanes de los que dependen las industrias eólica, automovilística y de defensa europeas, y Europa apenas tiene capacidad propia de refinado.

articles.headline: China exige a EE. UU. revocar el veto de la FCC a sus operadoras de telecomunicaciones y amenaza con «medidas necesarias»
articles.summary:
**El Ministerio de Comercio chino (MOFCOM) instó el domingo a Estados Unidos a «revocar de inmediato» la prohibición de la Comisión Federal de Comunicaciones (FCC) que impide a China Telecom, China Unicom, China Mobile y otras operadoras de su «Lista Cubierta» obtener números telefónicos de internet en EE. UU., y advirtió de que China «tomará las medidas necesarias» para defender sus intereses.**

El MOFCOM afirmó que la FCC, que votó el 19 de noviembre, «abusó de su poder regulador» y generalizó «supuestos riesgos para la seguridad nacional» sin base fáctica, empujando el «desacoplamiento» entre EE. UU. y China en telecomunicaciones, ensayos y certificación, en contra del «importante consenso» alcanzado por los dos jefes de Estado. La FCC justificó la orden por la lucha contra las llamadas automáticas ilegales (The Straits Times).

**Contexto:** la disputa es el último paso de una cadena de acción y reacción: vetos de la FCC a Huawei y otros equipos chinos; la decisión de octubre de 2026 de impedir que laboratorios chinos certifiquen electrónica destinada a EE. UU. a partir de diciembre de 2028; el veto a la importación de transceptores ópticos; la prohibición del 19 de noviembre sobre recursos de numeración; y ahora la amenaza de represalias del MOFCOM, días después de que Xi recibiera a Trump en Shenzhen.

**Qué vigilar:** si China concreta represalias (lista de entidades no fiables, controles a la exportación de minerales críticos); cualquier posición de la UE sobre la norma de la FCC sobre laboratorios de ensayo.

**Fuentes:** [MOFCOM](https://www.mofcom.gov.cn/xwfb/sjfzrfb/art/2026/art_a8a703480a3a4720a247c584d9f77eeb.html), [The Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/china-slams-malicious-us-ban-on-telecom-firms-phone-number-access), [South China Morning Post](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3375364/beijing-vows-defend-interests-us-bars-chinese-telecoms-accessing-phone-numbers), [Global Times](https://x.com/i/status/2124322059748806687)
articles.why: Washington y Pekín están partiendo en dos bloques las telecomunicaciones, los ensayos y la certificación, decisión reguladora a decisión reguladora. Las operadoras y laboratorios europeos que trabajan en ambos mercados pueden verse obligados a elegir, y Europa no tiene voz ni en las listas de la FCC ni en las represalias chinas.

articles.headline: Actualización: el petrolero iraní «rompebloqueos» resulta ser falso mientras se acumulan petroleros en Jark
articles.summary:
**El domingo a primera hora MarineTraffic mostró un buque llamado «Khat Shekan» («rompe-línea» en persa) cruzando el estrecho de Ormuz, lo que se interpretó como el primer intento de Irán de romper el bloqueo naval de EE. UU.; TankerTrackers aseguró que era una señal falsa.**

Las imágenes de satélite no mostraban ningún buque, el indicativo de llamada pertenece a un petrolero con bandera de Liberia y el destino declarado implicaba un tiempo de tránsito imposible (Iran International, Euronews). Imágenes de satélite y datos de seguimiento muestran más de 14 petroleros concentrados en torno a la isla de Jark, principal terminal de exportación iraní, y el ministro de Exteriores, Abbas Araghchi, dijo el viernes que «hay que romper el bloqueo». El presidente Masud Pezeshkian afirmó que Irán sufre una «guerra económica silenciosa» más dura que la guerra de misiles.

**Contexto:** el bloqueo estadounidense cumplió el sábado 21 de noviembre su día 130 (Euronews). Según cifras de UANI, desde el 12 de julio no se ha confirmado que ningún petrolero cargado de crudo haya cruzado la línea del bloqueo. El ministro de Exteriores turco, Hakan Fidan, dijo que hace falta un alto el fuego para aliviar la «carga económica» de la guerra.

**Qué vigilar:** la salida, confirmada por satélite, de un petrolero desde Jark y la respuesta de EE. UU.; la mediación catarí; la reacción del mercado del petróleo el lunes.

**Fuentes:** [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/22/tracking-site-says-iranian-tanker-reportedly-sailing-through-strait-of-hormuz-does-not-exi), [Iran International](https://www.iranintl.com/en/202611211549), [The Week](https://www.theweek.in/news/middle-east/2026/11/22/the-mystery-of-khat-shekan-alleged-iranian-oil-tanker-challenging-us-blockade-does-not-exist.html), [Anadolu, Pezeshkian](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/iran-facing-silent-economic-war-that-is-tougher-than-missile-war-says-president-pezeshkian/4132988), [Al Jazeera, Fidan](https://x.com/i/status/2124355960420663559)
articles.why: el bloqueo es un instrumento de sanciones estadounidense aplicado en el mar, y su evolución fija los precios del petróleo que paga Europa sin que Europa tenga voz en él.

articles.headline: La COP31 de Antalya termina su prórroga sin acuerdo tras desaparecer los combustibles fósiles del texto
articles.summary:
**En su segundo día de prórroga, la presidencia de la COP31 (Turquía, con Australia como coanfitriona) publicó un nuevo borrador que no menciona los combustibles fósiles, y el domingo el presidente de la COP31, Murat Kurum, dijo en el plenario de clausura: «Entiendo que no hay acuerdo sobre este texto. Por eso, estas decisiones no se han adoptado»; a las 12:37 GMT añadió que no habrá un nuevo borrador (BBC).**

La UE, Panamá, los Estados del Pacífico y otros habían exigido una mención explícita a los combustibles fósiles; según los observadores, Arabia Saudí y otros productores de petróleo presionaron para excluirla (Al Jazeera, BBC). En nombre de la UE, el ministro irlandés de Clima, Darragh O'Brien, afirmó: «No respaldaremos una decisión de cobertura, ni un Pacto de Antalya, que ni siquiera menciona los combustibles fósiles» (AFP); la francesa Monique Barbut calificó la propuesta de paso «atrás». El borrador mantenía el objetivo de que el 35 % del consumo de energía sea eléctrico en 2035 y reconocía por primera vez que el mundo va camino de superar 1,5 °C (BBC, Carbon Copy).

**Contexto:** el primer borrador, del lunes, mencionaba seis veces los combustibles fósiles; el segundo, del jueves, ninguna (BBC).

**Qué vigilar:** el cierre formal de la COP31 y los próximos pasos del proceso climático de la ONU; las obligaciones de COP anteriores siguen vigentes.

**Fuentes:** [BBC, directo](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/crly5w901n20t), [BBC](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cq7827z2841zo), [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/22/fossil-fuel-impasse-pushes-cop31-climate-talks-into-second-day-of-overtime), [AP](https://apnews.com/article/climate-un-turkey-fossil-fuels-global-warming-f6e36c4caf13ec6fed57c9f077cbd067), [Carbon Copy](https://www.carboncopy.info/cop-31-final-text-no-transition-away-from-fossil-fuels-no-120-billion-adaptation-finance-target-includes-35-by-35-electrification-and-ccus), [dpa](https://x.com/i/status/2124460588382179822), [AFP](https://www.afp.com/en/eu-will-not-endorse-climate-deal-throwing-cop31-deal-doubt)
articles.why: la UE es el principal bloque que impulsa el abandono de los combustibles fósiles, mientras importa la mayor parte de su petróleo y su gas y paga precios de crisis por Ormuz; sin un acuerdo global, su industria soporta costes que sus competidores no tienen.

articles.headline: Japón prevé declarar productos críticos los químicos orgánicos por Ormuz
articles.summary:
**El Gobierno japonés estudia añadir productos químicos orgánicos, como el etileno y el propileno obtenidos de la nafta, a la lista de «productos críticos especificados» de su Ley de Promoción de la Seguridad Económica, según fuentes citadas por Jiji (The Japan Times).**

Son insumos para los plásticos y para materiales de alto rendimiento usados en la fabricación de semiconductores. Un panel de expertos lo debatirá con el objetivo de modificar la orden del Gabinete antes del final del año fiscal 2026 (marzo de 2027). El detonante es la perturbación del tráfico por el estrecho de Ormuz: Japón importa de Oriente Próximo la mayor parte del petróleo con el que fabrica la nafta, su producción química cae y crece su dependencia de China. Los productos designados reciben apoyo público para garantizar su suministro; la lista actual tiene 12 categorías, entre ellas semiconductores, baterías, imanes permanentes y minerales críticos.

**Qué vigilar:** la lista del panel y la orden del Gabinete.

**Fuentes:** [The Japan Times](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/11/22/japan/organic-chemicals-critical-items/), [Japanese Law Translation](https://www.japaneselawtranslation.go.jp/en/laws/view/5008/en)
articles.why: Japón tiene una sola ley y una sola lista nacional para las cadenas de suministro críticas, con apoyo asociado, y la actualiza a los pocos meses de una crisis; la industria química europea sufre la misma presión de los precios de la energía con herramientas repartidas entre la Ley de Materias Primas Críticas, la Ley de Chips y los programas nacionales.

articles.headline: Senadores de EE. UU. proponen prorrogar cinco años el crédito fiscal 48D a la inversión en chips
articles.summary:
**Los senadores John Cornyn (republicano, Texas) y Mark Kelly (demócrata, Arizona) presentaron el 19 de noviembre el proyecto de ley S.5809 para prorrogar cinco años el crédito fiscal a la inversión en fabricación avanzada de la sección 48D; el crédito, creado por la Ley CHIPS, expira a finales de 2026 (Congress.gov).**

La Asociación de la Industria de Semiconductores (SIA) afirma que el incentivo ha ayudado a movilizar más de 825.000 millones de dólares de inversión privada en semiconductores (cifra de la SIA, que no indica el periodo). El proyecto se ha remitido al Comité de Finanzas del Senado.

**Qué vigilar:** la tramitación del proyecto en el Comité de Finanzas.

**Fuentes:** [SIA](https://www.semiconductors.org/sia-applauds-introduction-of-bipartisan-legislation-to-extend-semiconductor-investment-credit/), [SIA en X](https://x.com/i/status/2124222653602889949), [Congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-bill/5809)
articles.why: EE. UU. sigue pagando por atraer fábricas de chips, también de empresas europeas y asiáticas, mientras restringe a quién pueden vender; la Ley Europea de Chips no tiene un crédito fiscal comparable.

articles.headline: Update: Benghazi raid — Zelensky admits no coordination with Europeans; Rome says "case closed, alarm not"
articles.summary:
In a call with Giorgia Meloni on Friday, Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed that Ukraine's 22 November naval-drone operation against Russian vessels in the Libyan port of Benghazi "was carried out without prior coordination with partners". He undertook to ensure "full information sharing and direct, constant communication" (Palazzo Chigi). Meloni told him the operation "violated Libya's sovereignty and risks extending the conflict to the Mediterranean", and that Italy's support "cannot translate into the acceptance of initiatives that put the security of Italy and the region at risk". The call followed a BBC interview in which Zelensky had said Kyiv "never" acts without coordinating with allies. Defence minister Guido Crosetto said that "none" of the EU, NATO, France, Germany or the UK had known (Il Sole 24 Ore). Foreign minister Antonio Tajani said: "The government has never lied… Zelensky's apology makes everything definitively clear." He added that if Rome had been told in advance it would have objected: "violating Libya's sovereignty is a mistake and does not help Ukraine's cause". He asked all parties to refrain from further military action in Libyan territory and waters. Italy has military personnel, a navy ship and the Guardia di Finanza in Libya, as well as energy terminals supplying Italy.

**CEAFE angle (owner's posts):** @F_CEAFE reposted Zelensky's statement on the call and Tajani's "there was never any coordination with the allies" clip (Clash Report).

**Key facts:**

- 22 Nov: SBU says the corvette *Merkury* (Project 20380) and a Ka-27 helicopter were sunk, and the cargo ship *Angara* hit (Interfax-Ukraine).

- Libya's Government of National Unity (Tripoli) condemned the attack and asked Kyiv for an explanation.

- 27 Nov: the Meloni–Zelensky call; 28 Nov: Tajani's interview with Quotidiano Nazionale (republished by the Farnesina).

**Sources:** governo.it, 27 Nov 2026 https://www.governo.it/en/articolo/president-meloni-s-telephone-conversation-president-zelensky/33210; Farnesina https://www.esteri.it/it/sala_stampa/archivionotizie/interventi/2026/11/libia-zelensky-litalia-non-sapeva-tajani-ci-saremmo-opposti-al-raid/; Il Sole 24 Ore https://en.ilsole24ore.com/art/libya-attack-zelenskyy-corrects-himself-and-meloni-apologises-AJ7KdfVC; Interfax-Ukraine https://en.interfax.com.ua/news/general/1243862.html; Zelensky https://x.com/i/status/2126378091274527008; Italian MFA https://x.com/i/status/2126601558196408723; Clash Report (flotilla) https://clashreport.com/world/articles/russian-military-flotilla-cancels-libya-route-after-ukraine-sank-warship-4dai5ad5ybr; @F_CEAFE https://x.com/F_CEAFE/status/2126473366756524245, https://x.com/F_CEAFE/status/2126382892477456418
articles.why: Ukraine took a unilateral step on the EU's southern flank, in a country where Italy has forces and energy interests. It shows how little say Europeans have over the escalation of a war they finance. Clash Report also says a Russian convoy carrying military vehicles to Libya turned back in the Mediterranean after the sinking (not verified). Russia's "Libyan Express" logistics are a southern-flank issue for NATO and the EU.

articles.headline: Russian missiles over Poland: Canada summons Russia's ambassador; Moscow rejects the charge
articles.summary:
Global Affairs Canada summoned the Russian ambassador in Ottawa on Friday to condemn "Russian missile strikes in Poland, the latest example of Russia's reckless aggression, which heightens the risk of unintended escalation". It added: "Canada stands side by side with its Allies. We are fully committed to the defence of NATO territory and to supporting Ukraine." Polish prosecutors say they identified debris from three Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles that entered Polish airspace during the 20 November attack on Ukraine, found at Nowy Lipowiec (Lublin) and at Rudnik and Molodycz (Subcarpathia), and manufactured in Dubna in October or November (Anadolu). Poland's MFA summoned Russia's ambassador-designate on 24 November. **Russia's response:** Ambassador Oleg Stepanov said Russia rejects accusations of violating EU and NATO airspace. He said Moscow "is not interested in escalation or direct military confrontation with NATO" but will ensure its security "with all seriousness and resolve", and that the West made accusations "without convincing evidence" (Lenta.ru, Russian media). Russia's embassy in Warsaw had called the charges "baseless" (RBC).

**Sources:** Global Affairs Canada https://x.com/i/status/2126442344433975793, https://x.com/i/status/2126442375098593704; Anadolu (Turkish state agency) https://www.aa.com.tr/en/asia-pacific/canada-summons-russian-ambassador-over-missile-strikes-in-poland/4141083; Polish MFA, 24 Nov 2026 https://www.gov.pl/web/diplomacy/statement-on-the-summoning-of-the-russian-federation-ambassador-to-the-mfa; Lenta.ru https://lenta.ru/news/2026/11/28/long-ne-zainteresovana-v-eskalatsii-posla-rossii-vyzvali-v-mid-kanady-iz-za-intsidenta-v-polshe-chto-skazal-diplomat/; RBC https://www.rbc.ru/politics/28/11/2026/6b0a12c5aecf8074dd883463
articles.why: a NATO ally across the Atlantic is acting diplomatically over EU airspace, while Poland's request to intercept Russian missiles over Ukraine has found "no determination" among allies (see 26 Nov). The eastern flank's air defence remains the clearest case for common European capabilities.

articles.headline: Update: Gulf — France condemns Iranian attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain; Saudi alerts; drones at RAF Lakenheath
articles.summary:
France "condemns in the strongest terms the Iranian attacks on the Kingdom of Bahrain and the State of Kuwait in recent days, which killed two people of Italian nationality and injured several others". It calls them "unacceptable and unjustifiable" and urges "the utmost restraint" (France Diplomatie, 27 Nov). Pakistan's prime minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned "the recent drone attack on Kuwait". Bahrain had invoked the GCC principle that "any attack on one member state constitutes an attack on all" and UN Security Council Resolution 2817 (2026) (BNA, Bahraini state agency). On Saturday, Saudi Civil Defense issued several threat alerts for Jazan, Khamis Mushait and Abha (Anadolu), after the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile. CENTCOM rejected an Iranian commander's claims that the IRGC navy retook two tankers seized by the US: "Iran no longer has a navy." @F_CEAFE reposted an OSINT report that a UAE government-linked jet (A6-RJC) landed in Tehran on Saturday morning (purpose unknown; not confirmed officially). In the UK, US forces repelled about six drones near RAF Lakenheath on 13 November, with Iran suspected, according to the FT (via Reuters and Clash Report).

**Sources:** France Diplomatie (via Public) https://pubt.io/view/00AC7CAE2583A77735BC59AC0010E9CE175B68B1 and https://x.com/i/status/2126606756784832676; BNA https://www.bna.bh/en/BahrainstronglycondemnsrenewedIranianattacksonKuwait.aspx?cms=q8FmFJgiscL2fwIzON1%2BDnMiyRJzj3MT5tXt4Jq12BA%3D; Pakistan https://x.com/i/status/2126626432646516894; Anadolu https://x.com/i/status/2126645750096449850; CENTCOM https://x.com/i/status/2126467565253779814; Lakenheath (Reuters/FT) https://x.com/i/status/2126647370423140537, https://x.com/i/status/2126568654766579987; Hamad bin Jassim (Clash Report) https://x.com/i/status/2126603588239573219; @F_CEAFE https://x.com/F_CEAFE/status/2126637096131531004, https://x.com/F_CEAFE/status/2126635595493429460
articles.why: Europeans are among the dead in the Gulf war, and European bases are reportedly being probed. Yet EU policy appears mainly as national statements (France, Italy) rather than a common position. Former Qatari PM Hamad bin Jassim's call — "We genuinely need a NATO… joint air defence… technology that we develop together" — applies to Europe as well. Military detail is in Conflicts.

articles.headline: Asia-Pacific: Taiwan's local elections, PLA pressure, Manila vs Beijing, Japan weighs nuclear submarines
articles.summary:
Taiwan held local elections on Saturday. The KMT held Taipei, where Mayor Wayne Chiang fended off the DPP, and claimed Kinmen (Quemoy). The DPP retained Kaohsiung and the KMT lost the Changhua county seat (SCMP, Alibaba-owned Hong Kong daily). Taiwan's defence ministry detected 33 PLA aircraft sorties, 27 of them crossing the median line, plus 8 PLAN vessels and 4 official ships around the island up to 06:00 local time (reposted by @F_CEAFE). In Manila, coast-guard spokesman Jay Tarriela backed defence secretary Gilberto Teodoro: "China has no moral basis to lecture the Philippines on whom we should work with" (reposted by @F_CEAFE). Japan is expected to say in its year-end security-document revisions that it will "begin considering and reach a conclusion" on acquiring nuclear-powered submarines (Japan Times). Global Times (Chinese state media) reports that the J-35A stealth fighter has arrived in Zhuhai for its first static display (reposted by @F_CEAFE). South Korea's NIS is monitoring a possible visit to China by Kim Jong Un.

**Sources:** SCMP https://www.scmp.com/news/china/politics/article/3376140/kmt-holds-taipei-mayor-wayne-chiang-fends-fierce-dpp-challenge, https://www.scmp.com/news/china/politics/article/3376141/kmt-challenger-ko-chih-en-falls-short-dpp-retains-kaohsiung-stronghold, https://www.scmp.com/news/china/politics/article/3376137/kmts-wei-ping-cheng-loses-pivotal-changhua-county-magistrate-seat-taiwan-local-elections, https://www.scmp.com/news/china/politics/article/3376134/kmt-claims-first-win-taiwan-local-elections-chen-yu-jen-takes-quemoy; Taiwan MND https://x.com/i/status/2126481204736119281; Tarriela https://x.com/i/status/2126479392021070147; Japan Times https://x.com/i/status/2126609620604997906, https://x.com/i/status/2126596188044407235; Global Times https://x.com/i/status/2126558913604780451; @F_CEAFE https://x.com/F_CEAFE/status/2126636034305749110, https://x.com/F_CEAFE/status/2126636065771397467, https://x.com/F_CEAFE/status/2126632255510524293
articles.why: the Taiwan Strait and the South China Sea are where the US asks Europeans to send warships. The results of the Taiwanese vote and Japan's nuclear-submarine debate (AUKUS-style dependence on US technology) will shape those requests.

articles.headline: Kuwait drone strike: Italy says the drone that killed two Rheinmetall Italia technicians was Iranian-made; Iran offers a joint inquiry
articles.summary:
Italian foreign minister Antonio Tajani said Kuwaiti investigators found that the drone that killed two Italian technicians on 26 November was made in Iran. Iran says the drone was not launched from Iranian territory. Tajani replied that "Iran's proxies… have Iranian-made drones". Tehran says it is ready to join a commission of inquiry with Italy and Kuwait. The victims were Antonio Saccoccio, 65, and Emanuele Lo Russo, 36. They worked for Rheinmetall Italia on the antennas of the Skyguard air-defence system at a Kuwaiti military site (Italian Foreign Ministry; Reuters via NBC). "What is happening to the Gulf countries, which are not party to the war but are being constantly attacked, is unacceptable," Tajani said. United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres condemned the attack. He warned that renewed hostilities would have "devastating consequences" (Anadolu).

**Background (CEAFE archive):** the 20:30 edition of 26 November reported the strike, and the 08:30 edition of 27 November the Saudi condemnation. Kuwait has been a target since the summer: in June 2026 @F_CEAFE shared Reuters' report that Iran had launched missile and drone strikes on US bases in Kuwait and Bahrain (https://x.com/i/status/2071348746261012781).

**What to watch:** whether the joint inquiry goes ahead; an EU statement; Gulf responses.

Sources: Italian Foreign Ministry https://www.esteri.it/en/sala_stampa/archivionotizie/comunicati/2026/11/attacco-con-droni-in-kuwait-due-cittadini-italiani-deceduti/, Reuters via NBC https://www.nbcnews.com/world/middle-east/two-italians-killed-attack-kuwait-site-iran-denies-involvement-rcna611491, Al Jazeera https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/27/italians-killed-in-kuwait-why-is-iran-denying-responsibility, Clash Report (Tajani) https://x.com/i/status/2126351836466819525, https://x.com/i/status/2126351558002561429, Anadolu (Guterres) https://x.com/i/status/2126355045985706264, Reuters (June 2026) https://x.com/i/status/2071348746261012781.
articles.why: European civilians and a European defence company are now direct casualties of the Iran war in the Gulf. Rome, not Brussels, is leading the diplomatic response. Acting alone, a single member state has little weight with Tehran or Washington. A common European position would carry more.

articles.headline: Update: Poland signs a $300 million, five-year Palantir deal for military AI and defends it against "dependency" critics
articles.summary:
Poland's defence ministry signed a five-year agreement worth about $300 million for Palantir's Maven Smart System (Bloomberg; Reuters; Polish defence ministry). Maven is an artificial-intelligence (AI) platform that supports decisions. It fuses battlefield, sensor and logistics data. It will be deployed across the armed forces and commands. Defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said it would be "stupid and wrong" not to use it, citing its record in Ukraine (POLITICO Europe). Warsaw says the system will run on military infrastructure. Servers, encryption keys and data will be held only by the Polish military, with no remote access for Palantir. Polish systems (AIRON, NEFRYT) are being developed as possible successors. A post reposted by @F_CEAFE, apparently from Palantir, praised Poland's "undisputed leadership in defending a free, safe, and sovereign Europe". @F_CEAFE also reposted three Polish critics. Adrian Zandberg (Razem party) called the way the contract was signed "scandalous": "we are making Poland dependent on a foreign company". Jan Oleszczuk-Zygmuntowski warned of handing "control over the operational capabilities of the Polish army to a private foreign company".

<!-- ceafe-chart: polonia -->

**Background (CEAFE archive):** the 14:30 edition reported the contract without a value. In May 2026 a top NATO commander told POLITICO that the alliance had no viable alternative to Palantir's battlefield AI (https://x.com/i/status/2057418582473007212). On 16 November @F_CEAFE posted Reuters' report that Europe is hunting for Palantir alternatives as militaries seek to limit US dependence (https://x.com/i/status/2122265332274319486).

**What to watch:** contract details, such as audit and exit clauses; positions of other European militaries on Palantir; any European Defence Fund or other European alternative.

Sources: Bloomberg https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-27/poland-signs-300-million-palantir-deal-to-use-ai-for-defense (paywalled; headline and summary), POLITICO Europe https://www.politico.eu/article/wed-be-stupid-not-to-poland-defends-300m-military-ai-deal-with-palantir/, Polish defence ministry https://www.gov.pl/web/obrona-narodowa/wojsko-polskie-siega-po-nowoczesne-i-sprawdzone-technologie-wykorzystujace-sztuczna-inteligencje, Reuters https://x.com/i/status/2126370519482056985, @F_CEAFE reposts https://x.com/F_CEAFE/status/2126294840979964386 (statement, apparently Palantir's), https://x.com/F_CEAFE/status/2126336214844289196 (Zandberg), https://x.com/F_CEAFE/status/2126307213987992036 (Zygmuntowski), https://x.com/i/status/2057418582473007212, https://x.com/i/status/2122265332274319486.

**CEAFE:** This is not about diminishing this country, but about measuring its real weight against those already operating at a continental or global scale.
articles.why: Poland is buying the core of command and control from a US firm. Data on Polish servers does not remove dependence on the software, its updates or US export law. Each member state that signs alone weakens the case for a common European system. Only at EU scale could such a system be built and paid for.

articles.headline: Update: the Netherlands "will not be dictated to" on US chip curbs targeting ASML
articles.summary:
The Dutch government says it will lobby Washington against the proposed US MATCH Act. The bill would oblige allies to tighten controls on sales and servicing of ASML chipmaking equipment in China. If it is passed, The Hague will ask the US not to enforce it (Reuters via Investing.com; Bloomberg). Trade minister Sjoerd Sjoerdsma called the bill an attack on Dutch sovereignty over export policy. The Netherlands "will not be dictated to", he said (SCMP, owned by Alibaba). POLITICO Europe describes the Dutch stance as a rejection of an "unacceptable" US bid. China accounts for a large share of ASML's sales (Anadolu). Chinese state media (Global Times) framed the Dutch move as pushback against US "tech hegemony"; @F_CEAFE reposted that post. No official Chinese statement was found. In the same window, Reuters reported that Nvidia told partners to stop shipping servers with its chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia. It is another sign of how far US export controls reach into third countries.

**Background (CEAFE archive):** the 20:30 edition of 26 November reported that the Netherlands would ask Washington "not to enforce" the curbs, and the 08:30 edition of 27 November the first Dutch resistance. In September 2024 @F_CEAFE posted China's "dissatisfaction" with new Dutch export controls on ASML tools (https://x.com/i/status/1832892714976714988).

**What to watch:** the MATCH Act in Congress; Commission support for The Hague; an official Chinese reaction.

Sources: SCMP https://www.scmp.com/economy/global-economy/article/3376024/netherlands-will-not-be-dictated-trade-chief-says-fight-against-us-match-act, POLITICO Europe https://www.politico.eu/article/dutch-resist-unacceptable-us-bid-to-tighten-semiconductor-export-controls-asml/, Reuters via Investing.com https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/dutch-minister-says-us-chip-curbs-bill-would-hurt-europe-5052431, Bloomberg https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-26/netherlands-plans-to-fight-rollout-of-proposed-us-curbs-on-asml, Anadolu https://x.com/i/status/2126335269582299366, Global Times (Chinese state media) via @F_CEAFE https://x.com/F_CEAFE/status/2126336192786706586, Reuters (Nvidia) https://x.com/i/status/2126357884778733732, Reuters (2024) https://x.com/i/status/1832892714976714988.
articles.why: ASML is Europe's most valuable tech company and its main leverage in the chip supply chain. A single member state facing Washington and Beijing alone is easy to pressure. Trade policy is an EU competence, so EU backing would show whether Europe can defend its industry against an ally.

articles.headline: Ukraine peace talks: Kushner says a framework was worked out with Europe and "wouldn't rule anything out" on NATO
articles.summary:
US envoy Jared Kushner was interviewed by Axel Springer chief executive Mathias Döpfner (MD Meets, recorded on 25 November; clips posted by Kushner on 27 November). He said the US is "a mediator". It supports "whichever one ends the war": a freeze leading to a ceasefire, or Ukraine giving up the Donbas in return for NATO membership. On Ukraine in NATO, he said: "I wouldn't rule anything out." He said a possible peace framework was developed with Europe. In his view, Putin wants a post-war settlement before a ceasefire (WELT summary). On the ground, after Russian strikes and with winter, Ukraine halted all electricity exports. Its imports reached their highest level since mid-June (Euronews). Zelensky held a meeting of his military command on "potential threats" to Kyiv. He said Ukraine had hit oil and military facilities in 11 Russian regions over the past week (Kyiv Independent).

**Background (CEAFE archive):** on 25 November @F_CEAFE reposted Kushner saying Europe was not included in the Abu Dhabi talks because Putin "sees a lot of provocative statements" from Europe (https://x.com/i/status/2125697236055281758). In October it shared reports of the confrontation inside Trump's Ukraine negotiating team (https://x.com/i/status/2115400725593305255).

**What to watch:** the next round after Abu Dhabi, Moscow and Dublin; the wording of security guarantees; EU energy support to Ukraine.

Sources: Kushner https://x.com/i/status/2126367043859484834, https://x.com/i/status/2126369936536670323, https://x.com/i/status/2126373996769775661, https://x.com/i/status/2126363050890379381, WELT https://www.welt.de/politik/ausland/plus6b06a022d4a4a3142c5729fb/jared-kushner-im-interview-wie-ist-es-wladimir-putin-in-verhandlungen-gegenueberzusitzen.html (paywalled; summary), Euronews https://l.euronews.com/XhFb, Zelensky https://x.com/i/status/2126312809482891381, Kyiv Independent https://x.com/i/status/2126369726305870327, @clashreport https://x.com/i/status/2125697236055281758, @thetect0nic https://x.com/i/status/2115400725593305255.
articles.why: the terms of peace on the European continent are being described by a US envoy in a German media interview. The EU is not at the table as a party. Ukraine's power shortage also increases its dependence on EU electricity grids this winter.

articles.headline: Estonia will close its border with Russia on 1 December while Bulgaria holds up the EU's 22nd sanctions package
articles.summary:
Estonia will close all its border crossings with Russia on 1 December, for at least six months (Reuters). Bulgaria is blocking the EU's 22nd package of sanctions against Russia. It wants Russian iron imports to be allowed to resume (Kyiv Independent). Russian foreign ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova called "false" German media reports that Russia plans to put a spacecraft with a nuclear warhead into orbit (Russian foreign ministry; official Russian source). Greek foreign minister Giorgos Gerapetritis reaffirmed support for Ukraine's territorial integrity in a call with his Ukrainian counterpart, Andrii Sybiha.

**Background (CEAFE archive):** the 08:30 edition reported the Estonian closure and Moscow's warning that it would hurt "Estonia itself". In November 2023 @F_CEAFE reposted reports that Norway and Estonia might close crossings with Russia (https://x.com/i/status/1727643175668387930). The 21st package was agreed in July 2026, as EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas announced (https://x.com/i/status/2080232531002085381).

**What to watch:** talks among EU ambassadors on the 22nd package; Russia's response to the Estonian closure.

Sources: Reuters https://reut.rs/3V0VnLP (post https://x.com/i/status/2126349171011506464), Kyiv Independent https://x.com/i/status/2126357168983065049, Russian foreign ministry https://x.com/i/status/2126305709646340250, Greek foreign ministry https://x.com/i/status/2126354528714871077, Kyiv Independent (2023) https://x.com/i/status/1727643175668387930, Kaja Kallas https://x.com/i/status/2080232531002085381.
articles.why: sanctions need unanimity. One member state's trade interest can stall the whole package. Estonia's closure turns an EU and NATO border into a hard frontier.

articles.headline: Update: after the budget summit, Kubilius warns of cuts to big EU defence projects
articles.summary:
EU defence and space commissioner Andrius Kubilius told France 24 that big EU defence projects are threatened by the proposed budget cuts. In Vilnius he told BusinessEurope that the EU defence industry "must be free of dangerous dependencies in supply chains". In France, the stakes are rising. Marine Le Pen (National Rally), reposted by @F_CEAFE, said: "Despite all our friendship with Ukraine, we can no longer afford to commit financially… of the €90 billion loan, €17 billion weighs on France, not counting €2.5 billion a year in interest." Her figures are a political claim. Far-left candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon demanded a "thorough overhaul" of ties with Germany (France 24). Reuters asks why leaders struggle to "Le Pen-proof" the €1.6 trillion budget. Meanwhile Germany's Bundestag approved its largest budget ever, raising defence and infrastructure spending. DW puts it at €561 billion for 2027, about 40% financed by debt; Bloomberg gives €556 billion.

**Background (CEAFE archive):** the 08:30 edition reported the collapse of the budget summit, and the 14:30 edition Costa's plan for deeper cuts before the 17 December European Council. On 25 November Kubilius warned that the space industry saw a 30% cut to the defence and space line as making its plans impossible (https://x.com/i/status/2125661996825907429).

**What to watch:** Costa's new negotiating proposal; the 17 December European Council; French candidates' positions on the EU budget.

Sources: France 24 https://go.france24.com/HEWk (post https://x.com/i/status/2126361947222220930), Kubilius https://x.com/i/status/2126315335011934356, Le Pen via @F_CEAFE https://x.com/F_CEAFE/status/2126336291495141688, France 24 (Mélenchon) https://x.com/i/status/2126369968170086793, Reuters https://x.com/i/status/2126373039994507645, DW https://x.com/i/status/2126346973804478737, Bloomberg https://x.com/i/status/2126357928797954070, @KubiliusA https://x.com/i/status/2125661996825907429.
articles.why: Germany spends more at national level while the common budget is cut. That budget carries the European Defence Fund and the defence-industrial lines. No member state can fund the largest projects alone. The French campaign could turn the Ukraine loan and the EU budget into national bargaining chips.

articles.headline: Update: Mecca defence pact — the Islamabad committee pledges support for Saudi security, and Indonesia says no
articles.summary:
The second meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee of the Makkah Alliance for Defence met in Islamabad on 27 November. The alliance groups Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Türkiye, which completed its ratification the same day. The joint statement reaffirms collective defence and mutual solidarity. It condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi civilians and infrastructure and pledges stronger support for Saudi security. It also agrees on continued political and military consultations, cooperation on defence industry, technology and training, and an Alliance Secretariat in Saudi Arabia (Saudi Foreign Ministry; Radio Pakistan). Defence ministers Prince Khalid bin Salman and Yaşar Güler and foreign ministers Prince Faisal bin Farhan and Hakan Fidan attended. Indonesia, the largest Muslim-majority country, ruled out joining the pact (Clash Report; Times of India).

**Background (CEAFE archive):** the 14:30 edition reported Türkiye's ratification of the pact, signed on 7 August, whose Article 2 treats an attack on one party as an attack on all. In May 2026 @F_CEAFE shared the SCMP's analysis of whether the Saudi–Pakistani pact would give Chinese arms risk-free exposure (https://x.com/i/status/2051735435005542791).

**What to watch:** entry into force; the Secretariat in Saudi Arabia; any operational role against the Houthis.

Sources: Saudi Foreign Ministry https://x.com/i/status/2126366199395025035, Pakistan Foreign Ministry https://x.com/i/status/2126360417563967536, Radio Pakistan https://radio.gov.pk/27-11-2026/pakistan-saudi-arabia-turkiye-vow-to-strengthen-defence-cooperation, Clash Report https://clashreport.com/world/articles/indonesia-rules-out-mecca-pact-46g50f2nthj, Al Jazeera https://x.com/i/status/2126360286764413280, SCMP https://x.com/i/status/2051735435005542791.
articles.why: a NATO member is building a parallel framework for collective defence and defence industry in the Gulf. Middle powers pool their weight. EU member states still struggle to do the same.

articles.headline: Update: after the budget-summit walkout, Costa prepares deeper cuts and leaders give themselves until 17 December
articles.summary:
POLITICO Europe reports that the "Sensible Seven" governments demanding a smaller 2028–2034 budget walked out of António Costa's small-group sessions on Thursday night; Denmark, Sweden, Belgium and Austria are named, and Austria said in a statement that "further sessions would not bring us closer to a solution". According to two EU diplomats quoted by POLITICO, Costa told leaders he will table a new proposal with a further €220–230 billion of cuts to the Commission's draft of about €2 trillion (he had already proposed €204 billion), falling mainly on competitiveness and foreign aid rather than cohesion and farming. Macron called the cuts "a strategic mistake" and said dragging talks into 2027 "is not democratically possible" before France's April election. Italy's Meloni said "I will not sign under these conditions" (Anadolu). Merz said Germany pays "around a quarter of the European budget" but receives "only around 8% … directly in return". On Friday von der Leyen said she was "pleased" at "wide support" for the proposed loan for Ukraine (Reuters). Talks resume at the European Council of 17 December.

**Background (CEAFE archive):** this follows the collapse of the special summit reported in the 08:30 edition. Two days earlier, on 25 November, EU Commissioner Andrius Kubilius warned that the European space industry considered a 30% cut to the MFF defence and space line would make its plans impossible (https://x.com/i/status/2125661996825907429).

**What to watch:** Costa's new "negotiating box"; the 17 December European Council; whether Ukraine's 2027 financing is decoupled from the budget.

Sources: POLITICO Europe https://www.politico.eu/article/eu-budget-summit-walkout-antonio-costa-leaves-one-month-negotiations-drama/ (post https://x.com/i/status/2126254874006327807), Anadolu http://v.aa.com.tr/4140092, France 24 https://x.com/i/status/2126240006754705723, Reuters (von der Leyen) https://x.com/i/status/2126248505815519440, @clashreport (Merz) https://x.com/i/status/2126210837593338008, @SMuresan https://x.com/i/status/2126249207728308603, @KubiliusA https://x.com/i/status/2125661996825907429.

**CEAFE:** Europe has resources; what it lacks, time and again, is the scale that only joint action can provide.
articles.why: the cuts Costa is now pointing to fall on competitiveness, the heading that carries defence-industrial and research money. A Union that trims its common budget while each capital buys alone cannot build the capabilities that no member state can afford by itself.

articles.headline: Germany and Austria want TikTok's European business under European ownership
articles.summary:
Germany and Austria called on Thursday for "a European ownership structure for TikTok's European business and European responsibility for the key technological infrastructure — from the recommendation algorithm to data access", Euronews and AFP report. German culture and media minister Wolfram Weimer said the Chinese-owned platform poses "fundamental security policy risks for Europe"; Austrian digital state secretary Alexander Pröll said TikTok "must not remain in the hands of a geopolitical systemic rival". The two will seek EU-wide support at the Telecommunications Council in Brussels on 2 December. The Commission preliminarily found TikTok in breach of the Digital Services Act on 6 November. TikTok said the proposal had "zero merit", citing its €12 billion "Project Clover" data programme.

**Background (CEAFE archive):** ByteDance ceded control of TikTok's US operations in January to a majority American-owned joint venture after a threatened US ban. CEAFE has followed the US pressure on TikTok since July 2020, when Washington weighed a ban and Microsoft held talks to buy the US business (https://x.com/i/status/1290245943498018816).

**What to watch:** the 2 December Telecommunications Council; China's reaction (MOFCOM/MFA); whether other member states join.

Sources: Euronews/AFP https://l.euronews.com/5D6Z (post https://x.com/i/status/2126249853563109866), EU Council (TTE background) https://x.com/i/status/2126280514738769960, @WSJ (2020) https://x.com/i/status/1290245943498018816.

**CEAFE:** Here is another example of why Europeans need to act together.
articles.why: the aim is control over strategic digital infrastructure, not regulation alone. The same reasoning applies to US platforms and cloud providers that hold European data under US law (CLOUD Act), a test of whether the principle is applied symmetrically.

articles.headline: Turkey completes ratification of the Mecca joint-defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan
articles.summary:
Erdoğan signed Presidential Decision No. 12017 on 26 November, published in the Official Gazette on 27 November, completing Turkey's ratification of the "Mecca Agreement for Joint Defense" with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, signed on 7 August. Article 2 states that "any external armed attack on any of the Parties will be considered an attack against all"; the text also covers logistic support (arms, ammunition, fuel), joint exercises and deployments, defence co-production and intelligence sharing. The Turkish parliament approved it by 279 votes to 119 (AP).

**Background (CEAFE archive):** in May 2026 CEAFE shared the SCMP's analysis of whether the Saudi–Pakistani defence pact would give Chinese arms risk-free exposure (https://x.com/i/status/2051735435005542791). The 08:30 edition covered Turkey's extension of its Iranian gas contract to 2032.

**What to watch:** deposit of the last ratification and entry into force; trilateral talks in Islamabad, with Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia on the agenda (Türkiye Today).

Sources: Türkiye Today https://www.turkiyetoday.com/nation/president-erdogan-signs-off-on-mecca-defense-pact-sealing-turkiyes-ratification-3233295, Official Gazette text (Lexpera) https://www.lexpera.com.tr/resmi-gazete/metin/turkiye-cumhuriyeti-pakistan-islam-cumhuriyeti-ve-suudi-arabistan-kralligi-arasinda-ortak-savunma-2, AP https://apnews.com/article/pakistan-saudi-turkey-meeting-trilateral-alliance-6c17e4827e5aef3e69f78cdb01d597dc, Reuters https://x.com/i/status/2126242158550118469, SCMP https://x.com/i/status/2051735435005542791.

**CEAFE:** The conclusion is the same once again: either Europe acts as one, or each country is left in a supporting role.
articles.why: a NATO member and EU candidate is building a collective-defence commitment outside NATO, in the Gulf, during the war with Iran. Middle powers act on their own interests; Europe, which has more weight together, still struggles to agree on a common budget.

articles.headline: Spain votes on Sunday: Sánchez frames the snap election as a choice on sovereignty and foreign policy
articles.summary:
Spain holds a snap general election on Sunday 29 November. In the final debate, Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez asked whether Spaniards want "an open, sovereign, peaceful Spain, or an impoverished, closed Spain subjected to the interests of oligarchs on the other side of the Atlantic", recalling that his government "said no to the war in Iran" (clip via Clash Report). PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo, the poll frontrunner, clashed with rivals over whether to call Israel's war in Gaza a genocide; Reuters describes Vox's Santiago Abascal as "tipped to be kingmaker". Euronews quotes a political scientist saying "it's not unthinkable that the socialists win".

**Background:** Spain has just secured the ECB presidency for Pablo Hernández de Cos (26 November, 20:30 edition) and is in the camp seeking a larger EU budget.

**What to watch:** turnout and seat count on Sunday night; whether a PP–Vox deal is needed.

Sources: Clash Report (Sánchez) https://x.com/i/status/2126261781030899987, https://x.com/i/status/2126261445297942612, debate https://x.com/i/status/2126262408297529442, Reuters https://x.com/i/status/2126240874472300755, https://x.com/i/status/2126242139667317027, France 24 https://x.com/i/status/2126254969363820627, Euronews https://x.com/i/status/2126273168965058578.
articles.why: Spain is the EU's fourth-largest economy. The result will shape Madrid's line on the EU budget, defence spending and relations with Washington before the 17 December European Council.

articles.headline: Israel: Eisenkot reaches 36 of the 61 seats he needs to replace Netanyahu
articles.summary:
Gadi Eisenkot (Yashar) struck coalition deals with Avigdor Liberman's Yisrael Beytenu and Yair Golan's Democrats, bringing his bid to 36 of the 61 Knesset seats needed ahead of his 6 December deadline, Clash Report and France 24 report. Naftali Bennett is still pushing for a unity government. Haaretz reports that UAL leader Mansour Abbas is set to declare Hamas a terror group amid talks with Eisenkot.

**Background (CEAFE archive):** on 7 November President Isaac Herzog said he would task Eisenkot with forming a government (Haaretz, https://x.com/i/status/2119163536496554083), after Arab-majority parties, the Joint List and Ra'am, backed him (Al Jazeera, https://x.com/i/status/2118838426287886790).

**What to watch:** the 6 December deadline; whether Arab parties' support becomes part of the arithmetic.

Sources: Clash Report https://clashreport.com/world/articles/eisenkot-coalition-deals-liberman-golan-64hrud2vubo, France 24 https://x.com/i/status/2126270315818819894, Haaretz https://x.com/i/status/2126281167183688111, https://x.com/i/status/2119163536496554083, Al Jazeera https://x.com/i/status/2118838426287886790.
articles.why: a change of government in Israel would reset EU–Israel relations: the Association Agreement review, Gaza reconstruction and sanctions on violent settlers.

articles.headline: Update: EU budget summit collapses as seven "frugal" countries boycott Costa's talks; leaders now aim for a deal "this year"
articles.summary:
The special European Council of 26 November ended without a deal on the 2028–2034 budget. According to Rapporteur, UNN and POLITICO Europe, seven countries (Denmark, Germany, the Netherlands, Austria, Finland, Sweden and Belgium) refused to take part in Costa's small-group format, and leaders dropped the planned second day. Costa's compromise of €1.78 trillion in current prices (a 10% cut on the Commission draft) was attacked from both sides, Euronews reported. Costa said the meeting was "a necessary step", adding: "Everybody knows that we cannot fail Europe, and we need to have a new budget from the 1st of January 2028." Merz said positions are "still far apart" but he is confident of a deal "this year – for a strong economy and a secure Europe"; von der Leyen asked leaders to "maintain our ambition" on size, new own resources and timing. Russian state agency TASS reported that the €45 billion extra aid for Kyiv also stalled (this is TASS's claim; EU sources say Ukraine's 2027 financing was discussed).

**CEAFE angle (owner's reposts):** @F_CEAFE reposted Greek Prime Minister Mitsotakis: "If we continue to insist on further cuts to the EU budget, we can throw the Draghi report and its lofty ambitions into the dustbin of European history." He also quoted the FT on the Franco-German clash over "Made in Europe" in the EU defence budget, and reposted the FT report that the UK will pay an extra "participation fee" as the price of its EU reset deal.

**What to watch:** next attempt at the December European Council; whether "Made in Europe" survives in the defence chapter; Ukraine's 2027 financing.

**Sources:** EUCO post https://x.com/i/status/2126133907628404785; Costa press conference https://x.com/i/status/2126115892102864972; Merz https://x.com/i/status/2126075461256061359; von der Leyen https://x.com/i/status/2126101384093180286; Euronews https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/27/a-lot-of-political-theatre-eu-summit-ends-in-disarray-as-leaders-cling-to-red-lines; Rapporteur https://www.rapporteur.com/news/euco-costas-special-eu-budget-summit-fails/; POLITICO Europe https://x.com/i/status/2126106325071302754; TASS (Russian state media) https://x.com/i/status/2126153335870791698; Mitsotakis via @F_CEAFE https://x.com/i/status/2126039517136142453; FT via @F_CEAFE https://x.com/i/status/2126035143634604516, https://x.com/i/status/2126034979293700104.

**CEAFE:** Acting together is not a political ornament: it is the only way to reach a scale that others already have.
articles.why: the budget is where common defence money (European preference, EDIP, a successor to SAFE) is decided. A Union that cannot agree on 1.1% of GNI cannot build the domestic capabilities that no member state can afford alone. The "frugals" who walk out are also among those who buy US systems.

articles.headline: EU prepares new loans and grants to replace US war-fighting capabilities, while Washington delays its Europe force-posture review
articles.summary:
Bloomberg reported on 27 November that the EU is preparing "tens of billions of euros in new loans and grants to replace US war-fighting capabilities as the continent pushes to cut its reliance on Washington", citing people familiar with the matter. It would follow the €150 billion SAFE loan scheme (a second SAFE call of €21.3 billion opened on 29 October, prioritising air and missile defence, drones, counter-drone systems, ammunition and missiles, according to the Commission). At the same time, RFE/RL reported that the US deputy ambassador to NATO told allies that Washington will publish its Europe force-posture review after the provisional 1 December deadline, missing next week's NATO foreign ministers' meeting; the Pentagon is preparing five options and is still assessing European offers to backfill US forces and equipment. Trump said allied pledges to raise defence spending toward 5% and to buy "750 F-35" jets "made me feel a little bit differently" about cutting the roughly 80,000 US troops in Europe.

**What to watch:** the size and rules of the new instrument (European preference or not); the posture review options; NATO foreign ministers next week.

**Sources:** Bloomberg https://x.com/i/status/2126183012136071446 https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-27/eu-plans-new-funds-to-help-replace-us-war-fighting-capabilities (paywalled; headline and lede); European Commission, SAFE second call https://defence-industry-space.ec.europa.eu/commission-invites-member-states-use-eur213-billion-under-safe-boost-defence-readiness-and-support-2026-10-29_en; RFE/RL https://www.rferl.org/a/trump-putin-europe-ukraine-russia-aggression/33906739.html; Palantir item via @F_CEAFE https://x.com/i/status/2126039195739115627.
articles.why: this is the core of CEAFE's line. Replacing US enablers with European ones builds sovereignty, jobs and R&D. Paying for US withdrawal by buying 750 F-35s does the opposite: it locks in dependence (software, spare parts, export permission). Same day, @F_CEAFE reposted a report that Berlin ruled out Palantir's Maven for the Bundeswehr over "kill switch" fears (reported by @piotrmiecz; not yet confirmed by an official German source).

articles.headline: Trump to troops: Iran's missiles "can reach Europe", NATO is "in various parts of Iran" and "we got Greenland"
articles.summary:
In Thanksgiving calls to US troops in the Gulf and remarks at Mar-a-Lago on 26 November, Trump said Iran has missiles capable of reaching Europe and that without peace in the Middle East there could be a "nuclear holocaust" (Al Jazeera, Dawn, Times of India). He said "we have victory at hand" in the Iran war, "whenever I want it to be", that the US is giving Tehran "every chance to make a deal", and that if strikes resume "we will definitely hit Pickaxe Mountain". He downplayed Russian and Chinese intelligence help to Iran: "involvement to me would mean shooting, not giving them little information… We do the same thing." He also said NATO is "involved with us… in various parts of Iran", that "we got Greenland", that "we don't need Middle East oil" and the US is there "protecting Israel", and that Putin may attend the G20 at Doral. Kyiv Independent noted that Trump added Ukraine to his warning against expanding the war, unlike the published joint statement with Rutte. Merz welcomed Trump's call on Putin to end hostilities.

**What to watch:** Danish and Greenlandic reaction to "we got Greenland"; NATO's comment on its role in Iran; any resumption of strikes.

**Sources:** Al Jazeera https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/27/trump-downplays-russia-china-support-for-iran-during-talks-with-us-troops; Washington Times https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2026/nov/26/trump-phones-troops-thanksgiving-victory-hand-iran/; Times of India https://x.com/i/status/2126186760652877876; clips (aggregators, verified against the reports above) https://x.com/i/status/2126106646753747435, https://x.com/i/status/2126106408823185862, https://x.com/i/status/2126105660181844301, https://x.com/i/status/2126103388500992156; Kyiv Independent https://x.com/i/status/2126144600897429619; Merz via ClashReport https://x.com/i/status/2126094821936734473; Reuters on G20 https://x.com/i/status/2126137700478558392.
articles.why: Europe is cited as a target in a war in which Europeans are not party to the decisions, while NATO is described as already involved. "We got Greenland" concerns the territory of an EU member state's realm and was not explained.

articles.headline: Estonia closes its land border with Russia on 1 December; Moscow says it will hurt "Estonia itself"
articles.summary:
Estonia will close all five road crossings with Russia (Narva-1, Narva-2, Koidula, Luhamaa, Saatse) at 07:00 on 1 December for an initial six months, after a series of Russian attacks including one on the defence industry, according to ERR and the Estonian government; rail freight through Narva continues. Russian MFA spokeswoman Zakharova replied that Moscow is "monitoring the tense situation on our western border, caused by the openly hostile actions of the Baltic states" and that the closure "will deal a painful blow – primarily to Estonia itself". She also attacked Kallas for calling for Russian databases on participants in the war to be obtained, and welcomed Tajikistan's withdrawal from the Rome Statute of the ICC.

**Background (CEAFE archive):** @F_CEAFE has followed the Estonian–Russian border for years: in November 2023 it reposted reports that Norway and Estonia might close crossings with Russia (https://x.com/i/status/1727643175668387930); in May 2024, that Russia had removed the buoys marking the border on the Narva river (https://x.com/i/status/1793708062655779082); and in October 2026, that Estonia was moving troops permanently closer to the border under an "active defence" strategy (https://x.com/i/status/2107026546913689796).

**What to watch:** Russian countermeasures; Finnish and Latvian follow-up; families cut off on both sides (Al Jazeera).

**Sources:** ERR https://news.err.ee/1610201515/estonia-to-close-land-border-with-russia-from-december-1; Estonian MFA https://www.vm.ee/en/news/foreign-minister-tsahkna-border-closure-russias-hostile-activities-against-estonia-and-europe; Al Jazeera https://x.com/i/status/2126179865619554669; Russian MFA (official Russian source) https://x.com/i/status/2126018146264096997, https://x.com/i/status/2126023180372324536, https://x.com/i/status/2126028218486734943.
articles.why: the EU's external border is being hardened state by state. A common EU decision would carry more weight than national measures.

articles.headline: Switzerland votes on Sunday on loosening its arms-export rules
articles.summary:
On 29 November Swiss voters decide on the amendment to the War Material Act passed by Parliament on 19 December 2025. It would let the Federal Council allow exports to certain partner states even when they are in an armed conflict (Bloomberg: 36 mostly Western countries), allow exceptions to the export criteria and reduce re-export declarations. Opponents say it would hurt neutrality (SECO, Bloomberg).

**What to watch:** the result on Sunday evening.

**Sources:** Bloomberg https://x.com/i/status/2126186792021852174; SECO https://www.seco.admin.ch/en/referendum-wma; swissinfo https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/votes/swiss-vote-should-switzerland-loosen-its-arms-export-rules/92277204.
articles.why: Swiss re-export bans blocked ammunition for Ukraine and pushed buyers away from Swiss suppliers. A "yes" would make Swiss industry a more reliable European supplier.
