In brief

articles.headline: The EU tables its 22nd sanctions package: Russian banks, crypto platforms, a ban on Russian teams at EU sports events and a visa ban on ex-combatants
articles.summary:
On Monday 23 November the Commission proposed the 22nd package of sanctions against Russia, and on Tuesday President Ursula von der Leyen presented it in a statement. She said the package presses Russia "in three ways": it strikes "harder at Russia's ways to finance its war by targeting its banks and crypto platforms", it isolates the country further by "shutting the door" to its participation in European sports and cultural events, and it tightens visa rules and enforcement. For sport, it would ban Russian teams and athletes competing under the Russian flag at any sports event in the EU, ban the display of official Russian symbols, restrict financial flows from Russian sponsors to European sports and cultural associations, and restrict Russians holding posts in the governing bodies of European sports federations. Von der Leyen also proposed a visa ban for Russian ex-combatants, citing "an escalation in non-conventional kinetic activities of Russian operatives in Europe": "Russian ex-combatants pose a security risk to Europe."

Alongside the package, the Commission adopted revised visa guidelines: member states should no longer recognise non-biometric Russian passports, apply a "very strict approach" to tourist visas, run interviews and systematic fingerprint checks against the Schengen Information System at the external border, and give specific attention to Russian-sponsored individual artists. The package has to be approved unanimously by the Council. A letter dated 23 November from the leaders of Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland and Sweden to von der Leyen and Council President António Costa, seen by the Kyiv Independent, calls the visa guidelines "crucial" and says the matter "is too urgent to wait" for the 2027 visa-code reform. TASS (Russian state agency) reported the tourist-visa proposal; no Russian government reaction to the sports and visa measures had been found by 12:55.

**What to watch:** Council discussions before the 26–27 November European Council; the position of Hungary (now under Péter Magyar) and Slovakia; a Russian reaction; enforcement against third-country crypto platforms.

**Sources:** EEAS, statement by President von der Leyen on the 22nd package: https://www.eeas.europa.eu/delegations/ukraine/statement-president-von-der-leyen-22nd-package-sanctions-against-russia_en, European Commission press release IP/26/2521 (visa guidelines, 23 Nov): https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/api/files/document/print/en/ip_26_2521/IP_26_2521_EN.pdf ; Commission visa measures page: https://commission.europa.eu/topics/eu-solidarity-ukraine/eu-sanctions-against-russia-following-invasion-ukraine/visa-measures_en, Kyiv Independent (seven leaders' letter; package summary): https://kyivindependent.com/exclusive-7-countries-back-eu-push-to-limit-russian-visas-for-tourists-sports/ ; https://kyivindependent.com/eu-proposes-package-of-russian-sports-sanctions-visa-bans-and-a-krygyzstan-crypto-blockade/, Euronews explainer on the sports targeting (on X): https://x.com/i/status/2125195081611391162 ; TASS (Russian state agency) on the tourist-visa proposal (on X): https://x.com/i/status/2125154102804132002
articles.why: the package shows two things at once: the Union keeps adding sanctions on its own initiative, and it is the one actor that has chosen to link the war to Europe's internal security (sabotage, hybrid operations, ex-combatants moving freely in Schengen). Border and visa policy is still national, so the package is only as strong as its weakest border guard and the unanimity of 27 governments. The bloc is also still outside the negotiating room on the war itself (story 2).

articles.headline: Peace table: Moscow says it "does not understand" what Europe could add to the Abu Dhabi talks, as Rutte flies to Mar-a-Lago and the EU leaders prepare their summit
articles.summary:
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov, speaking in Minsk, said that "Europeans insist on a four-party format" for the Abu Dhabi talks, but "so far, we don't understand what added value the Europeans could bring to the peaceful settlement process"; the date of the next round has not been set (TASS, RIA Novosti, Vedomosti: Russian state or Russian-language outlets). The previous trilateral round (Russia, Ukraine, United States) took place in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 November (APA). Vedomosti recalls that on 23 November the Commission spokesperson Paula Pinho said Europe is not ready to negotiate a new security architecture before a ceasefire and that any such talks must involve NATO and EU member states. TASS adds that Russia expects new contacts with the United States at the G20 summit in Miami in mid-December and that "the EU rejects Moscow's proposal on security dialogue".

On the Western side, NATO announced that Secretary General Mark Rutte will travel to Florida on 24–25 November and meet President Donald Trump at Mar-a-Lago on 25 November, with senior administration officials. Costa announced that EU leaders will meet on 26–27 November to discuss his proposal for the next long-term budget (MFF) and Ukraine's financing needs. Bloomberg reports that Volodymyr Zelenskyy told it he has a plan if Trump cannot convince Putin to end the war by the end of the year, including looking to a new US Congress.

*CEAFE:* An invitation to an international table does not change the proportions: size does matter here, and it is measured in capacity.

**What to watch:** the Rutte–Trump meeting on 25 November; the European Council of 26–27 November (MFF, Ukraine financing, the 22nd package, Russia's space threat); the date and format of the next Abu Dhabi round; whether Moscow's invitation to a European delegation in Moscow (Putin, 19 November) is taken up.

**Sources:** TASS (Russian state agency): https://tass.com/politics/2223897 ; RIA Novosti: https://ria.ru/20261124/peregovory-2133603537.html ; Vedomosti: https://www.vedomosti.ru/politics/news/2026/11/24/1414733-peskov-moskve-poka-neyasna ; APA: https://en.apa.az/cis-countries/kremlin-spokesperson-next-round-of-abu-dhabi-peace-talks-has-yet-to-be-scheduled-538239, NATO press (Rutte to Mar-a-Lago, on X): https://x.com/i/status/2125178725884920130 ; European Council President Costa (on X): https://x.com/i/status/2125137726999597483 ; Bloomberg on Zelenskyy's plan (on X, @business): https://x.com/i/status/2125183973546455288 ; TASS (G20 Miami, EU rejection of Moscow's security-dialogue proposal; Russian state agency, on X): https://x.com/i/status/2125172645884788805
articles.why: this is the clearest statement yet of the peace-table problem: the party that is funding, arming and bordering Ukraine is told by Russia that it adds no value, while Washington talks directly to Moscow and Kyiv. Europe asks for a seat; it does not yet have a single voice or a single envoy to occupy it. Rutte's trip to Florida the day before the Brussels summit shows where the decisions are taken.

articles.headline: Berlin and NATO answer reports that Russia is readying a nuclear-armed satellite, "Sputnik-S"; Moscow calls them propaganda
articles.summary:
German public broadcasters NDR and WDR and the Süddeutsche Zeitung reported on Monday, citing Western intelligence and Bundeswehr sources including the BND, that Russia could launch a satellite called Sputnik-S carrying a nuclear warhead within 60 days of early November, possibly in December. The satellite is said to have been fully built and stored near Moscow for years; a detonation in low orbit would disable satellites in that zone within months. Chancellor Friedrich Merz, at a joint press conference with Rutte in Berlin, called the news "nothing new, but … no less shocking", saying it "shows the extent to which Russia is evidently prepared to escalate" (DW relayed it on X on Tuesday). Government spokesman Stefan Kornelius said Berlin takes the reports "very seriously" but sees no "immediate threat" and warned against "undue anxiety"; the Foreign Office said such a deployment would be "a flagrant breach" of the 1967 Outer Space Treaty. Rutte answered that "we will always make sure that we defend every inch of NATO territory, and that includes … the space element". ESA Director General Josef Aschbacher called nuclear weapons in space "the ultimate nightmare scenario" (Handelsblatt, via BBC).

Russia's side: the Russian embassy in Berlin rejected "unfounded allegations" as "part of a propaganda campaign"; Peskov said he had not seen the reports and that stories citing "unknown sources" are "hardly worth taking seriously" (BBC). No official Russian military statement had been found. Merz said European leaders will discuss the matter in Brussels this week.

**What to watch:** a Russian launch notice in December; a NATO North Atlantic Council discussion; Russian statements at the UN on the Outer Space Treaty; whether the EU puts space resilience into the summit conclusions.

**Sources:** BBC: https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c9x2er1ry2mzo ; DPA via Yahoo: https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/merz-report-russia-may-put-184846535.html ; Anadolu (Turkish state agency): https://www.aa.com.tr/en/politics/nato-chief-says-space-part-of-defense-pledge-as-russia-reportedly-readies-nuclear-satellite/4134906 ; AeroTime: https://www.aerotime.aero/articles/russia-nuclear-armed-satellite-launch-warning, DW (Merz), on X: https://x.com/i/status/2125181690796441952 ; France 24 (on X): https://x.com/i/status/2125152619031068975
articles.why: Europe's civil and military life depends on orbit (navigation, communications, Earth observation, Galileo, IRIS²), yet it has no autonomous capability to defend its satellites. The report adds a space item to the 26–27 November summit agenda and strengthens the case for common European space defence rather than national programmes.

articles.headline: Update: Washington holds up about 60 Patriot interceptors already paid for by Europeans
articles.summary:
The Financial Times reported on Tuesday (Reuters and Interfax-Ukraine relayed it) that US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has not approved the transfer of about 60 Patriot interceptors to Ukraine: 40 PAC-3 (eight due in September, ten in October, ten in November, twelve in December, none yet cleared) and about 20 older PAC-2. Some are held in European arsenals and are financed by Kyiv's Western allies, but because they are US-made Washington must authorise their re-export. A separate approval for Ukraine to build its own Patriot interceptors is also reported to be delayed. A Pentagon spokesperson told the FT "there has been no change in the Department of Defense's policy regarding support for Ukraine"; the NASAMS missiles that were also awaiting approval have since been cleared. Zelenskyy said on Sunday: "It is very important that America allows the transfer of missiles for Patriot systems that our partners have already paid for", and on Monday warned of intelligence that Russia is preparing new strikes; Anadolu reports he urged Washington to authorise the transfers. Russian attacks over the past day killed 9 and injured 77 across Ukraine and hit a residential building in Zaporizhzhia (Kyiv Independent); Zelenskyy said the strikes targeted electricity distribution in the Zhytomyr region.

@F_CEAFE reposted the FT scoop and Zelenskyy's coordination-call summary.

**Background (CEAFE archive):** in July 2025 @F_CEAFE flagged that the US diverted Patriot systems ordered by Switzerland to Ukraine (Defense News); in June 2026 it noted the NATO PURL scheme, under which European allies and Canada pay for US weapons that are then transferred to Ukraine. Delivery stays a decision taken in Washington.

**What to watch:** Hegseth's decision; the PURL funding discussion at the European Council; a European interceptor production announcement.

**Sources:** Reuters (via Investing.com): https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/usdefense-chief-has-yet-to-approve-patriot-missiles-already-allocated-to-ukraine-ft-reports-5047103 ; Interfax-Ukraine: https://en.interfax.com.ua/news/general/1241316.html ; Kyiv Post: https://www.kyivpost.com/post/91035 ; LIGA.net: https://news.liga.net/en/war/news/ft-pentagon-delaying-delivery-of-about-60-patriot-missiles-to-ukraine, FT (reposted by @F_CEAFE): https://x.com/i/status/2125097631416299748 ; Zelenskyy (reposted by @F_CEAFE): https://x.com/i/status/2125159968995176659 ; Kyiv Independent (on X): https://x.com/i/status/2125194936035238171, [CEAFE, Jul 2025](https://x.com/i/status/1945863519997460741), [CEAFE, Jun 2026](https://x.com/i/status/2069076784142823919)
articles.why: the clearest example this week of the US double standard on control: European money, European stockpiles and a European priority (Ukraine's air defence) are all blocked by a US export-control decision, while Washington asks Europe to buy more American weapons. It argues for a European air-defence supply chain (SAMP/T, IRIS-T, common interceptor production) that does not need a US signature.

articles.headline: China pauses its mineral export ban for the US until 27 January while it threatens the EU with the WTO over hybrid-car quotas
articles.summary:
> **ALERT (economic coercion and reciprocity rule): not posted or reposted by @F_CEAFE.** China's Ministry of Commerce extended, to 27 January 2027, the suspension of its ban on exports of gallium, germanium, antimony and superhard materials to the US, and of the stricter graphite checks, just hours after Trump helped reinstate Jensen Huang at Nvidia. On the same day it warned the EU, which will cap hybrid-vehicle imports from 1 December, that it will "resolutely safeguard" its industries. Washington gets a bargain; Europe gets a threat of retaliation.

**China and the US.** MOFCOM said on Tuesday that the suspension of the second clause of its December 2024 dual-use announcement, which was due to expire on 27 November, will stay in effect from 28 November 2026 to 27 January 2027. The measure generally bars exports of dual-use items related to gallium, germanium, antimony and superhard materials to the US; a separate ban on dual-use exports to US military users stays in force (MLex, Chinese state media China Daily, SCMP, Bloomberg Law). The decision follows the Trump–Xi summit in Shenzhen last week and the reinstatement of Nvidia's chief executive Jensen Huang, who had resigned 11 days earlier. Reuters reports the board acted "following pressure from President Donald Trump and US assurances"; Anadolu reports Trump said he spoke to board members "directly and indirectly". Bloomberg says Beijing is holding back a response to Washington's latest chip curbs. China's Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun was asked about Huang's return at the regular briefing (Global Times, Chinese state media); Bloomberg reports Beijing warns his return does not remove the risk of more US chip controls. Singapore is meanwhile investigating the Nvidia-linked cloud firm Megaspeed after US blacklisting (Reuters).

**China and the EU.** The EU announced provisional import quotas on hybrid vehicles from 1 December, including a Chinese cap of about 191,780 vehicles over 200 days (roughly 350,000 a year), also applying to other large exporters (DW, Lianhe Zaobao). The Commission's account: "We have to restore a level playing field that has been distorted by global overcapacity." China's MOFCOM says the EU must honour the bilateral understanding reached in consultations (under which, it says, China's quota could not be lower than any other source's), follow WTO rules and the principle of non-discrimination, and reserves WTO dispute settlement and compensation rights; Xinhua and Global Times (Chinese state media) carried the statement.

**What to watch:** whether China files at the WTO or targets EU goods; Washington's next chip-control step; the Chinese Foreign Ministry on the EU quotas; the EU–China summit calendar.

**Sources:** MLex: https://www.mlex.com/mlex/articles/2559003/china-extends-suspension-of-tighter-us-bound-dual-use-export-controls-until-jan-2027 ; China Daily (Chinese state media): https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202611/24/WS6b0569ade4b03ebf8519e6c2.html ; SCMP (owned by Alibaba): https://www.scmp.com/economy/global-economy/article/3375609/china-approves-2-month-extension-select-us-export-restrictions ; Bloomberg Law: https://news.bloomberglaw.com/environment-and-energy/china-extends-pause-on-us-minerals-ban-to-maintain-truce-1 ; TradingView/Dow Jones: https://www.tradingview.com/news/DJN_DN20261124001683:0-china-to-suspend-some-critical-material-export-curbs-to-u-s-until-january/, EU hybrid quotas: Lianhe Zaobao: https://www.zaobao.com.sg/en/news/china/eu-announces-temporary-limits-hybrid-car-imports-china-urges-bloc-honour-consensus ; China Daily: https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202611/24/WS6b05765ae4b03ebf8519e6cd.html ; MOFCOM: https://english.mofcom.gov.cn/News/SpokesmansRemarks/art/2026/art_9c5d95356d984390af922150976cc853.html ; MLex: https://www.mlex.com/mlex/trade/articles/2559001/china-signals-possible-wto-challenge-to-eu-safeguards-on-hybrid-vehicle-imports ; DW: https://www.dw.com/en/eu-imposes-import-quotas-for-hybrid-vehicles-from-china/a-80029981, European Commission (on X): https://x.com/i/status/2125194573626343593 ; Xinhua (on X): https://x.com/i/status/2125196047580578021 ; Anadolu on Trump and Nvidia (on X): https://x.com/i/status/2125171377745318193 ; Reuters on Megaspeed (on X): https://x.com/i/status/2125163766589640900
articles.why: the contrast is the point of the owner's reciprocity line. Beijing answers Washington's controls with calibrated pauses and keeps its own export bans as a lever; it answers a European trade-defence measure with a legal and political threat. Europe applies US-driven restrictions on China without a reciprocal lever against Washington, and has few levers of its own on critical minerals. Both the Chinese pause and the Nvidia reversal were decided in a US–China channel, without Europe.

articles.headline: Hungary's Magyar meets Zelenskyy in Zakarpattia: Russia is "the aggressor", but no weapons or troops; Strasbourg debates the rule of law in Hungary
articles.summary:
Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar is holding talks with Zelenskyy in western Ukraine and will meet leaders of the ethnic Hungarian community in Zakarpattia, a region hit by a Russian drone attack near Mukachevo in mid-November (Euronews; security is tight). His first bilateral meeting with Zelenskyy had been conditional on Kyiv meeting Budapest's demands on minority rights. Magyar told parliament on Monday that Russia is the aggressor and Ukraine the victim, and that Hungary will support Ukraine "not with weapons or troops, but with humanitarian aid and diplomatic backing"; he accused Viktor Orbán's government of a "hate-inciting" campaign against Ukraine. Foreign Minister Anita Orbán accompanies him. In Strasbourg the European Parliament held a debate (09:00 Madrid) on "the restoration of the rule of law and fundamental values of the Union in Hungary" following the 2026 parliamentary elections, with Commissioner Michael McGrath and the Irish Presidency, and an 18:45 debate on eastern border security.

**What to watch:** the outcome of the minority-rights file between Kyiv and Budapest; Hungary's vote on the 22nd package and the MFF; the Strasbourg debate's conclusions.

**Sources:** Euronews: https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/24/hungarys-magyar-meets-zelenskyy-in-ukraine-in-sharp-break-with-orban-era ; RBC-Ukraine: https://newsukraine.rbc.ua/news/magyar-calls-russia-an-aggressor-confirms-1795442808.html, European Parliament press (on X, plenary "EP today", 07:40 UTC): https://x.com/i/status/2125132525441823194
articles.why: a Hungarian government that names Russia as the aggressor and visits Zelenskyy removes a long-standing veto risk from the sanctions and enlargement files, which helps the 22nd package (story 1). The limit (no arms) shows that even a pro-EU Budapest will not join a common military effort without a common framework.

articles.headline: Indo-Pacific: Solomon Islands drop their security pact with China, Russian aircraft near Korea draw a protest, Japan snubs the nuclear-ban conference
articles.summary:
- **Solomon Islands.** The Solomon Islands told China it will not renew its 2022 security agreement, which expires in April 2027, while its prime minister is in Canberra to sign a new treaty with Australia (ABC News, AFR). Albanese welcomed the visit; Beijing says its Pacific cooperation "does not target third parties" (Lianhe Zaobao; Global Times, Chinese state media, was asked to confirm the report). Sources: https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-24/china-solomon-islands-security-pact-australia/107421976 ; https://www.afr.com/politics/federal/solomon-islands-ends-security-pact-with-china-in-strategic-win-for-australia-20261124-p61gvb ; https://www.zaobao.com.sg/en/news/china/solomon-islands-plans-end-china-pact-and-turn-australia-beijing-says-cooperation-should-not-target

- **Update — Russian aircraft near Ulleung.** South Korea's Defence Ministry lodged a "strong protest" over the unannounced entry of several Russian military aircraft into its air defence zone (KADIZ) and near Ulleung's airspace on Tuesday; Seoul scrambled fighters and briefly issued a shelter alert (ROK MND on X; Yonhap, Reuters, Al Jazeera). Russia's response not yet found. https://x.com/i/status/2125140585887756576

- **Japan.** Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi said Japan will not attend the first review conference of the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons even as an observer (Kyodo, Anadolu; @F_CEAFE posted the story); Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi told ICC President Akane Tomoko that Japan will keep supporting the court, which is under US sanctions (Kyodo, @F_CEAFE; MOFA Japan). Reuters, reposted by @F_CEAFE: Japan is using its auto industry's manufacturing expertise for its biggest military build-up since 1945. Sources: https://english.kyodonews.net/articles/-/92473 ; https://english.kyodonews.net/articles/-/92466 ; https://x.com/i/status/2125164977090936992

- **China.** Xinhua, Global Times (Chinese state media), SCMP (owned by Alibaba) and Bloomberg report that Shanghai party chief Chen Jining, a Politburo member, is under investigation for suspected serious violations of discipline and law. https://www.scmp.com/news/china/politics/article/3375640/shanghai-party-chief-faces-corruption-probe ; The Chinese and Cambodian militaries will hold the "Golden Dragon-2026" exercise in Cambodia from late November to mid-December (China Military Bugle, on X: https://x.com/i/status/2125169384109093026).
articles.why: the Solomon Islands reversal shows that a middle power can turn to a security partner and away from Beijing when the offer is credible; Japan's refusal to attend the nuclear-ban meeting follows the US nuclear umbrella logic that Europeans also depend on.

articles.headline: In brief
articles.summary:
- **Rutte on resilience.** On 23 November, the NATO Secretary General told the NATO Parliamentary Assembly that societies must be resilient so that, in a war, "the lights stay on, homes stay warm and communications keep working" (quoted in French by Florian Philippot, whose post @F_CEAFE reposted, calling the speech "absurd"; NATO transcript below). https://www.nato.int/en/news-and-events/events/transcripts/2026/11/23/address-by-the-secretary-general-to-the-npa

- **Poland: third Miecznik frigate.** @F_CEAFE quoted PGZ's post on the keel-laying of the third Miecznik frigate in Gdynia: the ships are built on Babcock's British Arrowhead 140 design, with PGZ leading a consortium with CRIST, Thales UK and MBDA UK (contract signed 27 July 2021). https://x.com/i/status/2125168956558147941 (also relevant to the Defence Industry section).

- **Ariane 6 launch.** ESA's Ariane 6 lifted off from French Guiana carrying 36 Amazon Leo satellites: a European launcher lifting a US constellation (ESA on X). https://x.com/i/status/2125188391474229624

- **Germany first to get DELTA.** Ukraine's Defence Ministry says Germany will be the first country with access to DELTA, Ukraine's combat digital ecosystem; the Bundeswehr will use it (Clash Report on X).

- **Norway–Germany gas.** Norway's Equinor signed an 18-year gas supply deal with Germany's VNG (Reuters on X; see Economy).

- **Spain.** The People's Party (Feijóo) would take a more hawkish approach to trade with China if it wins the 29 November election (Bloomberg on X); the postal-vote deadline for the 29N election has been extended to 26 November (Moncloa).

- **EU Mozambique mission.** The EU extended its military assistance to Mozambique's forces in gas-rich Cabo Delgado (Bloomberg on X).

- **Russia–Brunei.** Lavrov met Brunei's second foreign minister in Moscow (Russian MFA, official Russian source).

- **US–NATO.** The US Ambassador to NATO met Bulgaria's PM Rumen Radev, President Iliana Iotova and Defence Minister Stoyanov in Sofia and welcomed Bulgaria's commitment to higher defence spending (US Mission to NATO on X).

items.title: World — 2026-11-24 08:30
headlines: Update: Le Pen wants to negotiate tariffs with Washington alone and keep France's UN seat national; CEAFE: "exactly what other powers want: a divided Union"
Update: Libya — Kyiv confirms it sank the corvette *Merkury*; Tripoli warns of being "dragged" into the war, Moscow speaks of a "very dangerous trend"
Germany turns: 53% now oppose military aid to Ukraine as the AfD promises to cut defence spending and stop arms deliveries
Visegrád Four and Austria reject the EU's 2028–2034 budget proposal; Magyar: Ukraine aid should not be in the EU budget
Qatar signs a critical-minerals framework with Washington under the US-led Pax Silica
Iran: Washington hits the "shadow banking" network; Tehran's speaker denounces a "no war, no peace" stalemate
In brief

articles.headline: Update: Le Pen wants to negotiate tariffs with Washington alone and keep France's UN seat national; CEAFE: "exactly what other powers want: a divided Union"
articles.summary:
Marine Le Pen (National Rally) argued in a video posted on X that the United States "is a historic ally" and that US tariffs "hit France hard because they are applied to the whole European Union"; if France "talked with the United States" on its own, she said, the tariffs "could disappear, because there is no trade surplus". In the same interview, given to Indian presenter Palki Sharma, she said France "will not share" its permanent seat on the UN Security Council ("I know that Germany is eyeing our seat… We will not share that with the European Union") and that France's nuclear force "will remain French". The UN-seat remark was noted in the 14:30 edition of 23 November; the new element is @F_CEAFE's answer.

@F_CEAFE quoted Le Pen's tariff remark: "This is exactly what other powers want: a divided Union. Under its current leadership, the EU too often fails to defend its citizens, but alone and divided, no EU member state can negotiate with the global giants or influence their decisions." He also reposted the UN-seat clip.

*CEAFE:* The EU as a whole can bear comparison; each capital on its own cannot. That is the difference that matters.

**What to watch:** whether other National Rally figures repeat the bilateral-trade idea; any response from the Commission or the French government; the French presidential campaign debate on the EU's common commercial policy.

**Sources:** [@F_CEAFE's quote](https://x.com/i/status/2125049705960710152), [Le Pen's post](https://x.com/i/status/2124596449044578640), [UN-seat clip (Clash Report, aggregator)](https://x.com/i/status/2124800736517370087), [full interview (YouTube)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=atgYJmPGgxo)
articles.why: trade is an exclusive EU competence, so a bilateral tariff deal between Paris and Washington is not legally available. What the proposal offers instead is the "special relationship" logic CEAFE criticises: a member state hoping to be treated better alone than as part of a bloc of some 450 million people. The US tariffs are applied to the EU as a whole because the EU negotiates as a whole, and that is the source of its weight. Le Pen's two positions point the same way: trade talks without the Union, and a Security Council seat kept away from it.

articles.headline: Update: Libya — Kyiv confirms it sank the corvette *Merkury*; Tripoli warns of being "dragged" into the war, Moscow speaks of a "very dangerous trend"
articles.summary:
On Monday President Zelensky confirmed that seven Ukrainian naval drones, launched from a "mother ship" according to the SBU, sank the Russian corvette *Merkury* at the Benghazi naval base on Sunday and hit the Russian dry-cargo ship *MV Angara*. He said Moscow had used the cargo ship to carry weapons (Reuters, AP, The Guardian). Satellite images showed the corvette capsized, with only the bow above water (Vantor, via Al Jazeera); local authorities reported at least 10 injured. The 20:30 edition of 23 November reported the attack as unconfirmed.

**Reactions overnight:** Libya's Presidential Council called the attack a "declaration of war against the Libyan state" and asked the UN Security Council for an emergency session (statement relayed on X; not yet checked against the Council's own channels). Prime Minister Abdul Hamid Dbeibah (Tripoli), meeting Italian Ambassador Gianluca Alberini, warned that armed groups acting on their own risk dragging Libya into both the Russia–Ukraine war and Sudan's, a "dangerous gamble", and condemned the military use of civilian ports (Anadolu, Turkish state agency). The eastern government asked the UN to investigate "suspicions" that the drones came from western Libya. UNSMIL called for an independent investigation. **Russia's response:** Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov called the Libya and Baltic attacks a "very dangerous trend", referred questions to the Defence Ministry, and said Russia's daily strikes have "very painful consequences for the Kiev regime" (TRT World). At the UN Security Council, Russia's envoy accused Kyiv of "criminally expanding the scope and geography" of maritime attacks and said Ukraine had targeted more than 200 commercial vessels since July. He also ruled out "any new grain deal". Ukraine answered that Russia "bears full responsibility for this war" and asked for more Patriot PAC-3 interceptors (Anadolu).

**What to watch:** a Russian Defence Ministry statement on *Merkury*; a UN Security Council emergency session on Libya; Italy's response; any Russian retaliation in the Mediterranean.

**Sources:** [Reuters (via Investing.com)](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/zelenskiy-says-ukraine-sank-russian-warship-in-libya-5044753), [AP](https://apnews.com/article/ukraine-russia-zelenskyy-warship-attack-libya-c382f8eb06dca7d87e89bc6c18ba7d61), [The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/ukraine-naval-drones-strike-russian-warship-libya), [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/23/russian-ships-hit-by-drones-off-libya-coast-what-do-we-know), [Anadolu (Turkish state agency), Dbeibah](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/russia-ukraine-war/libyan-prime-minister-warns-military-groups-against-dragging-libya-into-russia-ukraine-war/4135211), [UN Security Council](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/world/russia-ukraine-clash-at-un-over-attacks-on-black-sea-shipping-energy-strikes/4135194), [TRT World (Turkish public broadcaster), Peskov](https://www.trtworld.com/article/ad4249812e76), [Libyan Presidential Council statement (relayed by @Archer83Able)](https://x.com/i/status/2124974405717516766), [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2125076947600302453), [UN News (DiCarlo on energy strikes)](https://x.com/i/status/2125063858213855647)
articles.why: the war has reached the southern shore of the Mediterranean, in a country where Italy (an EU member state) and Türkiye both have a military presence and where Europe's migration and energy interests meet. Dbeibah chose the Italian ambassador to deliver his warning. Rome and Brussels are the first European capitals that Libyan factions will hold to account.

articles.headline: Germany turns: 53% now oppose military aid to Ukraine as the AfD promises to cut defence spending and stop arms deliveries
articles.summary:
The Körber-Stiftung's annual *Berlin Pulse* survey (Forsa, 1,501 eligible voters, 15–28 September 2026, published 24 November) finds that military support for Ukraine no longer has a majority in Germany. 46% are in favour (59% in 2025) and 53% against (39% in 2025). Germans are split 50–48 on whether Ukraine's defence also protects Germany and Europe. Only 11% of AfD supporters back military aid and 75% want relations with Russia normalised; in the east, support is 31% (west: 48%). On Monday evening, AfD co-leader Alice Weidel promised "cuts amounting to tens of billions in excessive defence spending", sharply lower payments to the EU, and an end to "payments and weapons deliveries to Ukraine". Co-leader Tino Chrupalla attacked the 2027 federal budget (about €210 billion of new debt). Meanwhile Ukraine's Defence Ministry says Germany is its largest military-aid partner in 2026 (€11.5 billion), as Defence Minister Evgeniy Khmara met Boris Pistorius in Berlin with air defence as the priority before winter.

**What to watch:** the Bundestag's 2027 budget vote; federal and state polls; whether Berlin keeps its 2026 pledges for air defence.

**Sources:** [Körber-Stiftung press release](https://koerber-stiftung.de/presse/mitteilungen/trendwende-wunsch-nach-aussenpolitischer-zurueckhaltung-waechst/), [Forsa report (PDF)](https://koerber-stiftung.de/site/assets/files/58448/the_berlin_pulse_2026_forsa_ergebnisbericht_sperrfrist.pdf), [DW](https://www.dw.com/de/studie-mehrheit-der-deutschen-gegen-mehr-waffen-f%C3%BCr-ukraine/a-80020315), [Bloomberg](https://x.com/i/status/2125097111666438331), [Weidel (Clash Report)](https://x.com/i/status/2124946252031013092), [Chrupalla](https://x.com/i/status/2124943847096561859), [Ukrainian Defence Ministry](https://x.com/i/status/2124981088187548149)
articles.why: Germany is the largest European backer of Ukraine and the EU's largest economy. If its public support collapses, Europe's main instrument in the war rests on a narrowing domestic base. The AfD platform joins three things: less defence, less EU and no aid to Ukraine. A purely national retreat of this kind would leave Germany neither sovereign nor safe, because no EU member state can defend itself alone. Europe's answer has to be common capability, so that defence does not depend on one government's electoral cycle.

articles.headline: Visegrád Four and Austria reject the EU's 2028–2034 budget proposal; Magyar: Ukraine aid should not be in the EU budget
articles.summary:
Meeting in Bratislava on Monday with Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker, the prime ministers of Slovakia, Czechia, Poland and Hungary criticised the revised proposal for the next Multiannual Financial Framework (Euronews, ORF, TASR). Hungary's Péter Magyar said it was not "an acceptable starting point for negotiations". He wrote to European Council President António Costa that there was little point in the special summit planned for later this week ("no point spending two days in Brussels not agreeing on anything"). He also argued that support for Ukraine should not be built into the budget in a way that makes contributions mandatory. Czechia's Andrej Babiš attacked the cost of the European Parliament's three seats. Poland's Donald Tusk stressed that Kyiv's defence is strategic for Europe, but opposed financing it through joint EU borrowing. Robert Fico said there was no joint position, but broad alignment on cohesion, farming and migration.

**What to watch:** the special European Council on the MFF this week (Costa's response to Magyar's letter); positions of the net contributors; how Ukraine funding is moved outside the MFF.

**Sources:** [Euronews (1)](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/23/visegrad-four-leaders-voice-concerns-over-eu-budget-proposal), [ORF](https://orf.at/stories/3449074/), [TASR](https://newsnow.tasr.sk/pm-fico-v4-and-austria-consider-eu-budget-proposal-to-be-unacceptable/), [Polskie Radio](https://www.polskieradio.pl/395/7785/artykul/3756220), [Euronews (2)](https://x.com/i/status/2125073883678019844)
articles.why: the MFF decides whether the Union can pay for common defence, industry and Ukraine on a European scale or falls back on national budgets. A regional bloc forming against the proposal before the summit, and a refusal of both mandatory contributions and joint borrowing, shrinks the tools that let a Union of mid-sized states act like a power.

articles.headline: Qatar signs a critical-minerals framework with Washington under the US-led Pax Silica
articles.summary:
At the eighth US–Qatar Strategic Dialogue in Washington on Monday, chaired by Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Qatari Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, the two countries signed a Critical Minerals Framework. Under Secretary for Economic Affairs Jacob Helberg said "Qatar has been a leader in Pax Silica since day one" and that the framework secures supply chains "from mining to refining" (The National, Anadolu). Qatar joined Pax Silica, the US initiative for secure supply chains for AI and advanced technology, in January 2026. Helberg then described it as a "coalition of capabilities" and named its signatories: Japan, South Korea, Singapore, the United Kingdom, Australia, Israel and Qatar. The January plan included joint investment in minerals "through vehicles like TechMet, in Africa and other third markets", new logistics corridors and AI data centres.

**Context:** Antecedentes: Pax Silica, a US-led initiative on technology and semiconductor supply-chain security, was unveiled in December 2025; on 14 December 2025 @F_CEAFE reposted Israel's announcement that it had joined ([X, 2025](https://x.com/i/status/2000164574826492141)), and on 16 December the US Under Secretary for Economic Affairs said the United States had "brought together a group of allied nations" to launch it ([X, 2025](https://x.com/i/status/2001007946789216462)).

**What to watch:** the text of the framework (not yet published); new Pax Silica accessions; EU–Gulf talks on raw materials.

**Sources:** [Helberg](https://x.com/i/status/2124970998193926202), [Rubio](https://x.com/i/status/2124999294566662468), [The National](https://www.thenationalnews.com/business/energy/2026/11/23/us-qatar-critical-minerals-framework/), [Anadolu](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/us-qatar-reaffirm-strategic-partnership-at-8th-dialogue-in-washington/4135206), [State Department, Helberg remarks of 12 January 2026](https://www.state.gov/remarks-on-the-accession-of-qatar-to-the-pax-silica-declaration)
articles.why: Washington is building a minerals and compute bloc with Gulf capital and Asian industry. No EU member state appeared on the signatory list Helberg read out in January. The Union negotiates critical-raw-materials partnerships of its own; the risk is that Gulf money and African minerals get locked into US-led structures that exclude cooperation with other powers, while Europe remains a customer. CEAFE's view is that Europe should cooperate with all actors on its own terms, not join exclusive blocs.

articles.headline: Iran: Washington hits the "shadow banking" network; Tehran's speaker denounces a "no war, no peace" stalemate
articles.summary:
The US Treasury ("Operation Economic Outcast") sanctioned more than two dozen exchange houses, front companies and individuals in Iran, the UAE, Türkiye and Hong Kong, which it says form Iran's shadow banking network. Secretary Scott Bessent called it "the last financial lifeline of a bankrupt regime" and said Treasury would continue "until we have buried the head of the snake". Iran's parliament speaker said the US seeks to impose a "no war, no peace" stalemate on Iran and that "sustainable deterrence" is key (Anadolu). US officials are investigating cyberattacks on up to 50 tankers, some of which received bomb threats, with Iran and Russia as possible suspects; Al Jazeera notes that Washington says it has no evidence of Iranian involvement (WSJ, Reuters, Al Jazeera). An account posting as "HormuzReport",, reported that Iran had begun firing anti-ship cruise missiles at US-escorted ships near Khasab (Oman) and that a tanker was hit. **This could not be corroborated by an official or major-outlet source by 06:00 UTC.** UKMTO had reported two tanker attacks near Khasab on 20–21 November.

**What to watch:** Iranian countermeasures; UKMTO or CENTCOM confirmation of any new Hormuz attack; EU position on the Treasury designations affecting Türkiye.

**Sources:** [US Treasury](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0699), [OFAC](https://ofac.treasury.gov/recent-actions/20261123), [Bessent](https://x.com/i/status/2124951217751429303), [Al Jazeera (1)](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/23/us-escalates-sanctions-on-iran-targets-shadow-banking-networks), [Anadolu (Iranian speaker)](https://x.com/i/status/2125054312975937653), [WSJ](https://x.com/i/status/2125089722821226574), [Al Jazeera (2)](https://x.com/i/status/2125088850083295612), [HormuzReport (unverified)](https://x.com/i/status/2124952108353061312), [UKMTO warning](https://www.ukmto.org/-/media/ukmto/products/20261121-ukmto_warning_215-26.pdf)
articles.why: Treasury designations in Türkiye and the UAE again apply US law to third countries' banks. European firms comply because of their exposure to the dollar, without any EU decision. At the same time, a "no war, no peace" Gulf keeps Europe's energy and shipping costs high.

articles.headline: In brief
articles.summary:
- **Coalition of the Willing in Poland:** the Multinational Force – Ukraine (MNF-U) completed several weeks of training in Poland "to deploy and contribute to regenerate and reassure" Ukrainian forces "whenever a ceasefire occurs"; it brought 2,800 personnel from 11 participating states, 1,100 of them French, under joint French–British command (French Armed Forces:).

- **Eastern flank (Update):** NATO's North Atlantic Council discussed last week's violations of Polish airspace: "a dangerous incident and Russia bears full responsibility" (NATO,:). Russia accused Estonia of hostile actions "on the verge of triggering open war" after the border-closure decision (Japan Times:). Zelensky warned of intelligence on new Russian strikes and asked for anti-ballistic interceptors.

- **US at the UN:** the US mission again called on Russia and Ukraine to halt attacks on energy infrastructure and food supply chains (:).

- **Myanmar:** the UK sanctioned five senior military figures and recognised the crimes against the Rohingya as genocide after the ICJ ruling (FCDO:). Spain and 13 other countries issued a joint statement on the ICJ ruling (Spanish MFA:).

- **China–Colombia, Taiwan:** China's embassy in Colombia protested an "improper" official visit to Taiwan by Colombian lawmakers (embassy statement:; Global Times, Chinese state media:). Taiwan's PLA monitoring: 3 sorties and 9 vessels (Taiwan MND:). Taiwan holds local elections on 28 November (Reuters:).

- **South China Sea:** Malaysia's Anwar calls Beijing "extremely reasonable" in talks (SCMP, Alibaba-owned:).

- **COP31:** MEP Valérie Hayer called the failure of COP31 "particularly worrying" and said the EU was right to refuse a deal that did not even mention fossil fuels.

- **Bangladesh:** ousted PM Sheikh Hasina, sentenced to death in absentia, plans to return from India on 16 December (AP:).

- **Gaza:** Israeli drone attacks killed at least nine Palestinians in 24 hours despite the October 2025 ceasefire (Al Jazeera:).

- **See Economía:** the FCC's "reciprocity" move against foreign satellite operators in the US market (:); the US Entity List addition of Megaspeed and six other Southeast Asian firms, and Malaysia telling data-centre operators not to serve them (Al Jazeera:; Bloomberg:). **See Industria de Defensa:** Eutelsat's US$60 million OneWeb contract with the US armed forces (:); Airbus Manching works council calls for a German sixth-generation fighter . **See Conflictos:** Ukrainian drone raid towards Moscow overnight (:); Russian strike on a Zaporizhzhia residential building, 2 killed, 22 injured (Kyiv Independent:).

articles.headline: Rutte against a European army: "you cannot also have national militaries"; Merz wants "a stronger, more European NATO"
articles.summary:
**Speaking in Berlin on the margins of the NATO Parliamentary Assembly, NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said: "If you have a European military, you cannot also have national militaries. The United States has one military… If Europe will be able to pull that off, fine. I don't think it will happen soon because it has to do with this big question of sovereignty."**

Rutte said he would "counsel against" national armies working together in NATO "and then on top of that having a big European structure". His reason: "if Putin attacks, we will first need two or three weeks to agree who will do what, and then he will probably end up in Rotterdam before we have decided". He added that there is "no principal problem against a European military", but no "big push for it". After meeting Rutte, Chancellor Friedrich Merz wrote that Germany's "perhaps most important lesson" from the Ukraine war is that "we are building, at high speed, a stronger, more European NATO". @F_CEAFE commented that Rutte is "an employee—an important one—of NATO, an organization led by the USA", and that Washington does not want the EU "to end up having its own army and being able to act independently of the USA".

*CEAFE:* When capabilities are compared — economic, technological or military — European unity stops being a slogan and becomes a condition.

**Context:** Antecedentes: on 15 October 2019 @F_CEAFE wrote that the EU's defence goals were "impossible to achieve without a European Army (#PESCO) equipped with European systems" ([X, 2019](https://x.com/i/status/1184143817735397376)). NATO's military commander (SACEUR) is always a US officer.

**What to watch:** reactions from the European Parliament (plenary in Strasbourg this week) and the Commission's defence portfolio; whether any EU government answers Rutte on the record.

**Sources:** [Rutte (clip 1)](https://x.com/i/status/2124845537463582917), [Rutte (clip 2)](https://x.com/i/status/2124846712158089700), [@F_CEAFE](https://x.com/i/status/2124921466114232709), [Merz](https://x.com/i/status/2124897355417989623), [NATO](https://x.com/i/status/2124918810004312139)
articles.why: the head of the Alliance is publicly arguing against a European army, the goal CEAFE defends as the route to European sovereignty. Rutte's "Rotterdam" argument assumes Europe stays a set of national armies coordinated by NATO. "A more European NATO" (Merz) still leaves strategic decisions, the nuclear umbrella and key enablers in Washington. The US has one army because it is one federal state, the integration step Europeans have not taken.

articles.headline: Update: Kh-101s in Poland: NATO meets, Merz demands an end to "dangerous provocations"; Finland summons Russia's ambassador, Moscow protests Estonia's border closure
articles.summary:
**NATO allies held an urgent meeting on Monday on a possible response to the Russian missiles that crashed on Polish territory on Friday (Washington Post). The Lublin prosecutor's office says all three objects were Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles.**

According to dpa, they were made in the fourth quarter of this year at a plant in Dubna, north of Moscow, and Poland will summon the Russian ambassador. At a joint press conference with Rutte, Merz said Russia "must immediately stop its dangerous provocations. Poland can count on our full solidarity. If necessary, NATO will of course defend every inch of territory." He called for stronger protection of the EU's and NATO's external borders. Rutte said the incident "clearly originated with Russia". France's Foreign Ministry also expressed solidarity with Poland. Finland summoned Russian Ambassador Pavel Kuznetsov and called Russia's "dangerous and irresponsible actions in Europe" unacceptable. It cited a suspected Russian helicopter incursion off Loviisa on Saturday (up to 4.1 km, per the Finnish Defence Ministry). Moscow, for its part, summoned Estonia's chargé d'affaires, Marek Ühtegi, over Tallinn's decision to suspend all road crossings (Narva-1, Narva-2, Koidula, Luhamaa, Saatse) from 1 December for six months. The Russian MFA called the move "openly confrontational", accused Estonia of tacitly letting Ukraine use its airspace for drones (Estonia rejects this) and warned of "the brink of an open war" (TASS, Russian state agency). There is still no Russian statement on the missiles in Poland (tagesschau).

**Context:** Antecedentes: on 15 November 2022 Poland's MFA said a Russian-made missile had fallen in Przewodów and summoned the Russian ambassador ([X, 2022](https://x.com/i/status/1592662645056081920)). Poland, Finland and Estonia are EU member states and NATO members.

**What to watch:** the outcome of NATO consultations (any Article 4 request); Poland's summons of the Russian ambassador; Russian "retaliatory measures" against Estonia; Zakharova's briefing on Thursday 26 November.

**Sources:** [tagesschau.de](https://www.tagesschau.de/ausland/europa/merz-rutte-nato-104.html), [Freie Presse/dpa](https://www.freiepresse.de/nachrichten/welt/merz-warnt-russland-vor-gefaehrlichen-provokationen-artikel14494075), [Merz](https://x.com/i/status/2124913878090060221), [Washington Post](https://x.com/i/status/2124922190160122078), [France Diplomacy](https://x.com/i/status/2124852808050483379), [Euronews (Finland)](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/23/finland-summons-russian-ambassador-as-it-condemns-russias-dangerous-and-reckless-actions-i), [Anadolu](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/eurasia/finland-summons-russian-ambassador-calls-moscows-dangerous-irresponsible-actions-in-europe-unacceptable/4134835), [Russian MFA](https://x.com/i/status/2124895755072684312), [TASS](https://tass.com/politics/2223407), [The Moscow Times](https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/11/23/moscow-summons-estonian-diplomat-over-border-closure-a94352), [Estonian government](https://www.kriis.ee/en/suspension-border-crossings), [ERR](https://news.err.ee/1610201515/estonia-to-close-land-border-with-russia-from-december-1)
articles.why: three EU member states are responding nationally on the same day, with summonses and border closures. Solidarity statements are many; a common EU instrument for border protection and air defence on the eastern flank is still missing.

articles.headline: Update: the peace track: Merz says Europe is ready to negotiate with Russia and calls 2008 a "mistake"
articles.summary:
**Merz said "Europe is ready to negotiate with Russia" and that talks "are expected to take place again soon at the adviser level, in a format involving Ukraine, Russia, Europe and the United States", possibly again in Abu Dhabi.**

He backed "Article 5-like" guarantees for Ukraine that would come "very close to NATO membership" (Der Spiegel). He also said that, in retrospect, not following the US proposal at the 2008 Bucharest summit to admit Ukraine was "a mistake… this war could probably have been prevented". Zelensky, by video to the Assembly, again argued that membership is better than guarantees that only resemble Article 5. Rutte replied that there is currently "no unanimity" among allies on Ukraine's membership and that "only NATO decides who can become a member". He said the US is making "enormous efforts" to start talks, but "Putin must also play along". Rutte also claimed Ukraine is "killing or seriously wounding up to 50,000 Russians each month". Kyiv Independent, citing media analysis of leaked Russian government data, reports a Russian death toll "likely near 700,000"; Bloomberg cites hacked documents showing at least 470,000 deaths (both unverified, different methods). Former Ukrainian PM Arseniy Yatsenyuk called the US-led talks "sham talks" (C-SPAN). The Munich Security Conference published a brief on E5 (Germany, France, Italy, Poland, UK) defence leadership.

**Context:** Antecedentes: on 13 November Russia's Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov said that bringing the Europeans into the Abu Dhabi talks "could undo progress" ([X, 2026](https://x.com/i/status/2121304238127263892)). The Shenzhen trilateral of 19 November excluded Europe.

**What to watch:** date and venue of the adviser-level round; who represents Europe (EU, E3/E5 or national advisers); Moscow's answer.

**Sources:** [Merz (clip 1)](https://x.com/i/status/2124891126318387547), [Merz (clip 2)](https://x.com/i/status/2124889679468065247), [Der Spiegel](https://www.spiegel.de/politik/deutschland/nato-treffen-in-berlin-friedrich-merz-und-mark-rutte-bekraeftigen-sicherheitsgarantien-fuer-die-ukraine-a-8466115a-c858-4447-907a-07adb51289ee), [Rutte](https://x.com/i/status/2124890067822883290), [TASS](https://x.com/i/status/2124920476359442573), [Kyiv Independent](https://x.com/i/status/2124925147576422809), [Bloomberg](https://x.com/i/status/2124911003171233996), [C-SPAN (Yatsenyuk)](https://x.com/i/status/2124923969635758086), [Munich Security Conference](https://x.com/i/status/2124904307698938279)
articles.why: Merz places Europe as a party at the table ("Ukraine, Russia, Europe and the United States") after Shenzhen. Whether "Europe" means the EU or a group of capitals is not said, and the format is still driven by Washington.

articles.headline: Update: Tajikistan, the fourth country to leave the ICC since the US push; the EU and the Assembly of States Parties object
articles.summary:
**The UN depositary received Tajikistan's withdrawal notice on 20 November 2026; it takes effect on 20 November 2027. Reuters says Tajikistan is the fourth country to withdraw since a US diplomatic push against the Court.**

An EU statement by High Representative Kaja Kallas says the ICC "does not target sovereign states, nor does it constitute a threat to their sovereignty". It urges Dushanbe to reverse the decision and recalls the withdrawals initiated this year by Niger, Burkina Faso, Mali, Chad, Venezuela and Nauru. The EEAS had criticised Tajikistan on 22 November for hosting Vladimir Putin on 19–20 November despite the ICC arrest warrant. The Presidency of the Assembly of States Parties said such decisions "risk undermining the collective pursuit of justice".

**Context:** Antecedentes: in October 2025 Germany said Hungary still had to honour the ICC warrant for Putin during the twelve-month withdrawal period ([X, 2025](https://x.com/i/status/1979508795819557121)).

**What to watch:** further withdrawals; the Assembly of States Parties session in December.

**Sources:** [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/11/23/tajikistan-statement-by-the-high-representative-on-behalf-of-the-european-union-on-tajikistan-s-withdrawal-from-the-rome-statute-of-the-international-criminal-court/), [ICC/ASP](https://www.icc-cpi.int/news/statement-presidency-assembly-states-parties-withdrawal-rome-statute-tajikistan), [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2124898311559610727), [2eu.brussels](https://2eu.brussels/en/news/eu-urges-tajikistan-to-reverse-its-withdrawal-from-the-rome-statute)
articles.why: the ICC is one of the pillars of the rules-based order the EU defends almost alone among the great powers. The US, Russia and China are not members, and the US is pushing others to leave.

articles.headline: London: Burnham rules out rejoining the EU without a referendum
articles.summary:
**UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said it would be "unthinkable" to rejoin the EU without a new referendum.**

He is not proposing one now. He said he would consult the public if his government later recommended rejoining, and that closer ties do not mean rejoining (Politico, ITV, Anadolu).

**Context:** Antecedentes: on 24 October 2026 London Mayor Sadiq Khan called Brexit "catastrophic" and said "it's time to rejoin the EU" ([X, 2026](https://x.com/i/status/2114026146811478017)).

**What to watch:** the scope of the UK–EU "reset" agenda.

**Sources:** [Politico Europe](https://www.politico.eu/article/rejoining-eu-without-referendum-unthinkable-andy-burnham/), [ITV](https://www.itv.com/news/2026-11-23/reversing-brexit-unthinkable-without-referendum-pm-says), [Anadolu](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/uk-premier-says-unthinkable-to-rejoin-eu-without-referendum/4135011)
articles.why: the UK is seeking a closer relationship with the EU without membership.

articles.headline: Geographical indications: Italy and 16 other EU member states ask for a common strategy against US pressure
articles.summary:
**Italy, backed by 16 other EU member states, is asking the EU for a common strategy to defend European geographical indications (Feta, Asiago, Gorgonzola, Parmigiano, Jerez…) against US legislative texts that would treat them as freely usable "common names" (Bloomberg; Italian Agriculture Ministry).**

*CEAFE:* No member state, on its own, has the scale of the powers it hopes to sit beside at the same table.

**Context:** Antecedentes: on 14 September 2020, the day the EU and China signed an agreement protecting 100 European geographical indications, @F_CEAFE noted that "some other key allies do not recognize Geographical Indications...guess who" ([X, 2020](https://x.com/i/status/1305574930851954689)).

**What to watch:** the Commission's response; whether the issue enters EU–US trade talks.

**Sources:** [Bloomberg](https://x.com/i/status/2124919692519157803), [Masaf](https://www.masaf.gov.it/IG-Lollobrigida-strategia-comune-UE), [Eunews](https://www.eunews.it/en/2026/11/23/italy-urges-the-eu-to-provide-greater-protection-for-geographical-indications-gis-against-unfair-us-practices/)
articles.why: a case of economic coercion on the EU's trade rules, answered here by a group of member states rather than one capital alone.

articles.headline: NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin: Rutte warns of "intensifying malign activities" and the EU's top soldier says Europe's defence is NATO's job
articles.summary:
**At the NATO Parliamentary Assembly's annual session in Berlin, Secretary General Mark Rutte warned of "intensifying malign activities targeting our nations": arson, drones over airports, sabotaged railways, cargo ships targeted at sea and "relentless" cyberattacks.**

Rutte cited Friday's "dangerous incident" in Poland and the Black Sea, where NATO works with Romania, Bulgaria and Türkiye. He called for more defence spending (several allies are projected to meet or exceed the 5% target this year) and more production of air defence, drones, counter-drone systems and deep-strike weapons, and said NATO would be able to produce about 4 million artillery shells a year by next year, nearly double the 2025 level. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said NATO will "defend every inch" of its territory, called on Putin to "stop this war" and "come to the negotiation table", and said Russia "is not seriously considering attacking NATO territory in the short term… because we are strong." The same morning, the Chairman of the EU Military Committee, General Seán Clancy, told Euronews: "The defence and deterrence in the Euro-Atlantic area, including Europe, is NATO's responsibility." In Belgium, Defence Minister Theo Francken blamed a far-left collective for three suspected arson attacks on defence suppliers near Liège, including the radar and counter-drone maker BATS; the intelligence services are still checking the claim (Anadolu).

{{chart: gasto_militar_ue}}

*CEAFE:* Without a common industrial, technological and defence base, Europe will remain dependent on decisions taken in Washington or Beijing.

**Context:** Antecedentes: in October 2019 @F_CEAFE already argued that a European army was the answer to Europe's exposure, under the tag #EUdefence ([X, 2019](https://x.com/i/status/1182634766744592384)). The 5% target was agreed at NATO's 2025 summit at US insistence.

**What to watch:** NATO decisions after Monday's North Atlantic Council on Poland; the Belgian arson investigation; the European Parliament plenary this week.

**Sources:** [Anadolu (Rutte)](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/nato-chief-warns-of-intensifying-malign-activities-targeting-alliance-nations/4134472), [NATO](https://x.com/i/status/2124812694624592166), [Anadolu (Wadephul)](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/germany-warns-russia-against-provocations-targeting-nato-territory-urges-peace-talks-on-ukraine/4134221), [Euronews (Clancy)](https://x.com/i/status/2124784922707574890), [Anadolu (Belgium)](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/intelligence-services-investigate-3-suspicious-fires-at-defense-companies-in-belgium-minister-accuses-left-wing-group/4134311), [SIPRI](https://www.sipri.org/databases/milex)
articles.why: the EU's most senior military officer says Europe's defence belongs to NATO, an alliance whose military commander (SACEUR) is a US officer, on the same day Rutte lists the threats on European soil. According to SIPRI, EU member states together spent about half as much as the US in 2025.

articles.headline: Nuclear signals from Moscow: Medvedev on the "obligation" to use nuclear weapons and a German warning about a nuclear-armed satellite
articles.summary:
**Dmitry Medvedev, deputy chairman of Russia's Security Council, wrote on Monday that Ukraine and NATO countries "have already created situations" in which Russia considers a nuclear strike, although events have so far "not created a state of direct necessity" to use nuclear weapons.**

Medvedev argued that if the conditions of Russia's doctrine are met, the head of state is "not only entitled but obliged" to use them, and that Western deliveries of nuclear weapons to Kyiv, "open or covert", or a massive use of non-nuclear means could justify a pre-emptive strike (Anadolu; TASS, Russian state agency). Separately, NDR, WDR and Süddeutsche Zeitung reported that the BND and Western partners warned that Russia may launch a nuclear-armed satellite, "Sputnik-S", before the end of the year; Defence Minister Boris Pistorius has been briefed. The Russian Embassy in Berlin rejected the reports as "unfounded allegations" and "part of a propaganda campaign".

**Context:** Antecedentes: in January 2023 @F_CEAFE posted Medvedev's warning to NATO of nuclear war if Russia were defeated in Ukraine ([X, 2023](https://x.com/i/status/1616049330573701122)).

**What to watch:** NATO and EU comments on the satellite reports; any Russian launch notice; whether other Russian officials repeat Medvedev's framing.

**Sources:** [Anadolu (Medvedev)](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/eurasia/russia-has-right-and-in-some-cases-obligation-to-use-nuclear-weapons-medvedev-says/4134527), [TASS](https://x.com/i/status/2124777339469127782), [Anadolu (satellite)](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/russia-may-put-nuclear-weapon-in-orbit-this-year-german-intelligence-warns/4134351)
articles.why: many European leaders treat Russia's arsenal as unusable; CEAFE holds the opposite view, because Moscow keeps signalling that a war with Europe would be short and nuclear, and its warnings usually leave out the US. The current escalation at sea (Libya, Baltic, Black Sea) is taking place under that rhetoric. A nuclear detonation in low Earth orbit would disable satellites for months, according to the German reports.

articles.headline: Five European states launch a defence-AI centre in Rennes, while Washington courts Polish and Italian industry
articles.summary:
**France's Ministry of the Armed Forces announced the launch of the International Center for Artificial Intelligence in Defence (ICAID): Germany, Italy, Poland and Sweden formally announced their intention to join France in it at a conference in Rennes on 19–20 November.**

The centre aims to speed up the adoption of military AI and share best practice and lessons from operations, and is open to other "affinity" states. The same morning, the US Ambassador to NATO promoted the "Transatlantic Defense Industry Access Forum", which brought together more than 500 participants from the US defence industry with counterparts from Poland, Italy and Ukraine "to forge new partnerships and expand business opportunities".

**Context:** France, Germany, Italy, Poland and Sweden are EU member states and NATO members. NATO chose Palantir's Maven system as its AI-enabled targeting platform.

**What to watch:** which other states join ICAID; its budget and governance; contracts coming out of the US forum.

**Sources:** [Ministère des Armées](https://www.defense.gouv.fr/sites/default/files/ministere-armees/Communiqu%C3%A9_A_Lancement%20de%20l%27ICAID%20%20quatre%20nations%20rejoignent%20la%20France%20pour%20cr%C3%A9er%20l%E2%80%99International%20center%20for%20artificial%20intelligence%20in%20defence.pdf), [Ministère des Armées on X](https://x.com/i/status/2124819143371186179), [US Ambassador to NATO](https://x.com/i/status/2124787857365606875)
articles.why: ICAID is the kind of intra-European cooperation CEAFE considers positive: states building a capability together instead of buying it. Poland and Italy appear on both sides on the same day; whether European defence AI stays European or depends on US software will decide who controls the data.

articles.headline: Update: "Article 5-like" guarantees: Zelensky asks who would fight; Moscow says it will sound out European capitals
articles.summary:
**After Washington's talk of "Article 5-like" guarantees (08:30 edition), Zelensky asked: "Which countries will support Ukraine if Ukraine is attacked again? What exactly will our partners do in response? Which troops will be stationed on our territory in advance?"**

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Moscow "will initiate contacts with European countries to determine their readiness to contribute to peace efforts" (TASS), while telling Vedomosti that Russia is in no hurry to appoint ambassadors to the UK and France because "there are no relations with these countries" (Anadolu). He called the Belgian prime minister's opposition to seizing frozen Russian assets "measured".

**Context:** the guarantees under discussion would rely mainly on the troops and money of the Coalition of the Willing's participating states.

**What to watch:** answers from the E5 and the Coalition of the Willing's participants; which capitals Moscow contacts.

**Sources:** [Zelensky](https://x.com/i/status/2124826721849356629), [Zelensky (2)](https://x.com/i/status/2124828072218128894), [TASS](https://t.me/tassagency_en/99523), [Anadolu](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/russia-in-no-rush-to-appoint-ambassadors-to-uk-france-amid-strained-ties-kremlin/4133948)
articles.why: Moscow chooses to talk to individual European capitals; Europeans count at the peace table only if they speak with one voice, not as a list of national governments.

articles.headline: Update: NATO Council meets today on the Kh-101s that fell in Poland; a former German defence minister admits Europe still depends on the US for air defence
articles.summary:
**The North Atlantic Council meets in Brussels on Monday to discuss the three Russian objects that entered Polish airspace on 20 November, all identified by prosecutors in Lublin as Kh-101 cruise missiles, whose debris was found at three sites.**

A NATO official told Anadolu that the meeting is part of the "regular consultations", not an emergency session. Poland, represented by Deputy Defence Minister Paweł Zalewski, will present proposals to reinforce air defence on the eastern flank, including under Eastern Sentry (Defence Matters). None of the three objects was intercepted. The NATO Parliamentary Assembly continues in Berlin, with President Zelensky joining by video, and Chancellor Merz receives NATO Secretary General Rutte in the afternoon (Deutschlandfunk). In an interview with Der Spiegel, former German defence minister Annegret Kramp-Karrenbauer said: "Although we have made tremendous progress, there are still a number of areas where we depend on the United States. For example, in the field of air defence."

**Context:** Poland is an EU member state and a NATO member. The missile fell on 20 November near Chmielek (Biłgoraj county), about 45 km inside Polish territory (14:30 edition of 20 November). Finnish lawmakers support studying tank traps and border fortifications in peacetime (Bloomberg). Antecedentes: since 2019 @F_CEAFE has questioned whether Poland's purchases of US weapons help integrate the EU ([X, 2019](https://x.com/i/status/1181430134437552128)).

**What to watch:** the outcome of the NAC and any new Eastern Sentry assets; the Merz–Rutte meeting; Zelensky's address to the NATO Parliamentary Assembly.

**Sources:** [Anadolu](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/nato-to-meet-over-polish-airspace-violation/4133560), [dpa](https://x.com/i/status/2124731813734080596), [Deutschlandfunk](https://www.deutschlandfunk.de/beratungen-ueber-verletzungen-des-polnischen-luftraums-durch-russland-102.html), [Defence Matters](https://defencematters.eu/nato-eastern-flank-air-defence-russian-missiles-poland/), [Kyiv Independent](https://x.com/i/status/2124646206236233760), [Axar.az (Der Spiegel interview)](https://en.axar.az/news/world/1151467.html), [@F_CEAFE](https://x.com/i/status/2124639289988284719), [Bloomberg](https://x.com/i/status/2124735979797827889)
articles.why: Russian missiles built this autumn landed on the territory of an EU member state without being intercepted, and the political response runs through NATO, whose military commander (SACEUR) is a US officer. Kramp-Karrenbauer's words come from someone who ran the Bundeswehr.

articles.headline: Kushner offers Ukraine "Article 5-like" guarantees and reassurance for Russia; the US intelligence chief says Putin is "not America's friend in Ukraine"
articles.summary:
**US envoy Jared Kushner wrote that President Trump's "willingness to consider Article 5-like security guarantees for Ukraine is a critical feature to achieving lasting peace", and that Russia's willingness to discuss them is "a major step forward".**

Kushner was quoting Zelensky's post that NATO membership is the clearest guarantee for Ukraine. He wrote: "We seek a future where Ukraine is secure, Europe is stronger, Russia has confidence that NATO is not seeking confrontation, and NATO and its partners have confidence that Russia will respect the sovereignty and security of its neighbors." The offer is guarantees "like" Article 5, not NATO membership. On ABC's This Week, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton defended Trump calling Putin a "friend" as "entirely appropriate", but said: "He is not America's friend in Ukraine. Not at all" (AP/Al Jazeera). Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the Shenzhen talks were "a more conceptual discussion" (TASS, Russian state agency). Tony Blair, in an interview reposted by @F_CEAFE, said that even after Trump "it's still going to be America First", in a world that is "a G2 — you may have a G3 in time with India".

**Context:** the US–China–Russia trilateral in Shenzhen (19 November) was held without the EU at the table.

**What to watch:** the text of any US guarantee offer and whether Europeans are asked to staff or pay for it; Moscow's reply.

**Sources:** [Jared Kushner](https://x.com/i/status/2124573146665955759), [Volodymyr Zelensky](https://x.com/i/status/2124187167077351761), [Al Jazeera / AP](https://aje.news/2n07f4), [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2124565379762823265), [TASS (Peskov)](https://t.me/tassagency_en/99489), [Tony Blair (Clash Report clip)](https://x.com/i/status/2124635678503735680)
articles.why: the security guarantees for Ukraine, and the reassurances for Russia about NATO, are being designed in Washington and discussed with Moscow. In Blair's G2 or G3, the EU is not among the powers that decide. No EU member state alone weighs enough to change that outcome.

articles.headline: Marine Le Pen on Ukraine: "only three outcomes" and a promise to "talk to everyone"
articles.summary:
**National Rally candidate Marine Le Pen wrote that in Ukraine "there are only three outcomes: either NATO enters the war and it is World War Three, or the conflict lasts for years, or all countries understand the consequences".**

She added: "If I am elected President of the Republic, I will talk to everyone." @F_CEAFE reposted her post. TASS (Russian state agency) reports that she does not plan to travel to Kyiv because she will make no trips abroad during the campaign. Also on Sunday, former European Commissioner Thierry Breton said Europeans must not let Xi Jinping become "the new emperor of the world".

**What to watch:** the other candidates' positions on Ukraine and European defence; reactions in Kyiv and Brussels.

**Sources:** [Marine Le Pen](https://x.com/i/status/2124599451285356940), [TASS](https://t.me/tassagency_en/99483), [Thierry Breton](https://x.com/i/status/2124568883294277789)
articles.why: France is the EU's only nuclear power and the EU member state with a permanent seat on the UN Security Council, so its presidential campaign is also a debate on Europe's position on the Ukraine war.

articles.headline: Poland says Russian intelligence tried to kill a rapper on its soil, after a similar Danish allegation
articles.summary:
**Polish authorities say Russian intelligence services tried to kill Ukrainian-American rapper Albert Vasiliev during a visit to Poland in August, Al Jazeera reports.**

Copenhagen had earlier said Moscow allegedly targeted the same man on Danish soil. No Russian response had been found by 07:30 Madrid.

**What to watch:** any Russian denial; whether Poland and Denmark ask for EU-level measures.

**Sources:** [Al Jazeera](https://aje.news/00g8g9), [Al Jazeera on X](https://x.com/i/status/2124707010218426512)

**In brief:** Belgium faces a national strike against austerity, with almost all flights cancelled on Monday ([Al Jazeera](https://x.com/i/status/2124710781543666020)). Sergey Lavrov said the UK and German defence ministers appear to be "in an inadequate state" after they defended Ukraine's deep strikes on Russia ([Anadolu](https://v.aa.com.tr/4133824)). COP31: see Economy.
articles.why: the same target in two EU member states points to an operation that crosses national borders inside the Union.
