articles.headline: Kubilius to EU Chiefs of Defence: CARD 2026 shows Europe risks missing its 2030 readiness target
articles.summary:
Defence and Space Commissioner Andrius Kubilius posted on 25 November, after his keynote to the EU Military Committee at Chiefs of Defence level, that "Russia continues to escalate", "we aren't producing enough for Ukraine" and that the CARD Report 2026 shows "we risk missing our strategic target of defence readiness by 2030" ([@KubiliusA](https://x.com/KubiliusA/status/2125700387936108785)). The EEAS readout says the Chiefs, chaired by General Seán Clancy, with an opening address by Kaja Kallas and a briefing by EDA Chief Executive André Denk, called for faster air defence for Ukraine before winter and for removing barriers to military movement across the EU by 2027; they welcomed the extension of the EU Military Assistance Mission for Ukraine to November 2028 (EEAS). The same evening Kubilius relayed the European space industry's warning that the proposed 30% cut to the MFF defence and space line "would make it impossible to deliver the EU's space ambitions" ([@KubiliusA](https://x.com/KubiliusA/status/2125655246529802255)).

**CEAFE comment:** When capabilities are compared — economic, technological or military — European unity stops being a slogan and becomes a condition.

**What to watch:** the European Council budget talks opening today in Brussels, and the publication of the CARD 2026 findings.

Sources: [EEAS](https://www.eeas.europa.eu/eeas/eu-chiefs-defence-call-faster-delivery-european-defence-readiness-0_en); [@KubiliusA](https://x.com/KubiliusA/status/2125700392642384340); [Commission speech page](https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/speech_26_2586) (page returned no text).
articles.why: the Commission's own review says fragmented national efforts are not enough to reach readiness by 2030; joint procurement and a defence budget at EU scale are the answer, not national silos. The space-cut warning is the industrial side of the same problem.

articles.headline: Bulgaria buys five more German IRIS-T SLM systems for about €925.9m with EU SAFE loans
articles.summary:
Bulgaria's parliament has ratified an agreement with Germany to buy five more IRIS-T SLM air-defence systems for about €925.9m, funded through the EU's SAFE loan programme, Global Defense Corp reports (its headline says four; the text says five). It is phase two of Bulgaria's IRIS-T programme under the European Sky Shield Initiative, bringing the two phases to about €1.106bn; an amendment to the contract with Diehl Defence is expected. The decision followed drone attacks on two merchant ships in Bulgaria's Black Sea exclusive economic zone. Each battery uses a Hensoldt TRML-4D radar.

**Background (CEAFE archive):** In November 2019 @F_CEAFE noted how close Bulgaria's defence relationship with the US was, leaving "not much room to cooperate in #EUDefence" (https://x.com/i/status/1196064454200512512); in June 2023 it greeted Germany's order for six IRIS-T SLM fire units with #BuyEuropean (https://x.com/i/status/1672224725693521921). A Bulgarian IRIS-T buy financed with EU SAFE loans marks that shift.

**What to watch:** the Diehl contract amendment and the planned IRIS-T SLX buy by 2032.

Sources: [Global Defense Corp](https://www.globaldefensecorp.com/2026/11/26/bulgaria-purchases-four-more-iris-t-slm-missile-defence-systems-using-eu-backed-funds/).
articles.why: a European buyer, a European system, EU money: exactly the intra-European procurement the SAFE instrument was built for, and a counter-example to European purchases of US air defence.

articles.headline: State Department approves a $621.9m F-16 support package for Ukraine, paid by Belgium, Denmark, the Netherlands and Norway
articles.summary:
The US State Department approved on 25 November a possible sale to Ukraine of F-16 maintenance support and related equipment worth about $621.9m, including aircraft pyrotechnic cartridges, laboratory equipment and transport support, The New Voice of Ukraine reports. Belgium, Denmark, the Netherlands and Norway will pay, with no US funds; contractors will be selected competitively. President Zelensky said in October that about half of Ukraine's F-16s were in Europe for maintenance, and on 17 November that Ukraine needs 40 more F-16s.

**What to watch:** the formal notice on the State Department site and which European firms win the work.

Sources: [The New Voice of Ukraine](https://english.nv.ua/nation/state-department-approves-622m-f-16-sale-to-ukraine-50662644.html).
articles.why: European taxpayers are financing a US support contract for a US jet. Europe already maintains these aircraft (Belgium's Sabena Aerospace Engineering is pictured in the report); the more of this work goes to European MRO firms, the more of the money stays in Europe. In the longer run Gripen and Rafale, not more F-16s, are the European fighter answer for Ukraine.

articles.headline: FCC authorises SpaceX to deploy up to one million "Starmind" data-centre satellites, and weighs reciprocity against foreign operators
articles.summary:
The FCC granted SpaceX authority for its "Starmind" orbital data-centre system: up to one million low-Earth-orbit satellites with a 15-year licence. Deployment must begin by 25 November 2033, with 100,000 satellites by 2035, 500,000 by 2038 and the full million by 2040; primary links are optical, with Ka-band only for backup telemetry, tracking and command (FCC order, Spaceflight Now, NBC). Separately, the FCC said it will consider reciprocal restrictions on foreign satellite operators, a post @F_CEAFE reposted ([@FCC via @F_CEAFE](https://x.com/F_CEAFE/status/2125720675419828569)). SpaceNews also carried the authorisation ([@SpaceNews_Inc](https://x.com/SpaceNews_Inc/status/2125662971418366315)).

**What to watch:** the FCC reciprocity proceeding and the EU's reply on IRIS² and 2 GHz (deal expected 1 December).

Sources: [FCC order (PDF)](https://eu-assets.contentstack.com/v3/assets/blt23eb5bbc4124baa6/bltf4cdf2af47159e12/6b071c5f5506bb38bca5b0ec/FCC_report_and_order_on_SpaceX_Starmind_AI_constellation_11-25-2026.pdf); [Spaceflight Now](https://spaceflightnow.com/2026/11/26/fcc-green-lights-spacexs-plan-to-launch-1-million-starmind-data-center-satellites/); [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/science/space/spacex-fcc-authorizes-1-million-satellites-data-centers-space-rcna611341).
articles.why: a licence for a constellation of this size would claim orbital slots and spectrum on a scale no European operator can match, and the reciprocity threat could be aimed at operators such as Europe's in the US market just as the EU defends its 2 GHz band and IRIS². Orbital and spectrum sovereignty is now industrial policy.

articles.headline: Senate appropriators move to bar sole-source Space Force contracts above $100m that went to SpaceX; White House seeks $5bn for Golden Dome in the stopgap
articles.summary:
A bipartisan group of senators is moving to limit SpaceX from winning non-competitive Space Force missile-defence contracts, Bloomberg reports ([@business](https://x.com/business/status/2125658367158788487)). According to search results citing the bill, Section 8127 of the Senate FY2027 defence bill bars the Space Force from using funds for sole-source contracts above $100m for the Space Data Network and space-based AMTI, both first awarded to SpaceX; the bill funds Golden Dome at $9.39bn. Meanwhile the White House OMB has asked Congress for a $5bn anomaly in the continuing resolution to keep Golden Dome going, and for help to replenish the MQ-9 fleet, ahead of the 11 December funding deadline (Air & Space Forces Magazine; [@ASForcesMag](https://x.com/ASForcesMag/status/2125707466939773171)).

**What to watch:** whether Section 8127 survives conference, and the CR text before 11 December.

Sources: [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-25/spacex-sole-source-deals-targeted-in-defense-spending-bill) (unreachable, timed out); [Air & Space Forces Magazine](https://www.airandspaceforces.com/pentagon-congress-help-with-golden-dome-mq-9/); [@AviationWeek](https://x.com/AviationWeek/status/2125724213663154195).
articles.why: Washington is actively avoiding dependence on a single space supplier (see the $2.29bn SDN Backbone award of 22 November) while Europe still relies on Starlink in Ukraine. The lesson for the EU is the same: competition and sovereign alternatives (IRIS²) before lock-in.

articles.headline: India's 76 naval utility helicopters (about Rs 15,000 crore) put Leonardo and Airbus in front
articles.summary:
The Indian Navy (51) and Coast Guard (25) are preparing to buy 76 Naval Utility Helicopters to replace the Chetak, in a programme estimated at about Rs 15,000 crore, likely under Buy and Make (Indian), which requires foreign makers to team up with Indian firms, the Times of India reports. European manufacturers are expected to be front-runners: Leonardo's AW169M (Leonardo partnered with Adani Defence and Aerospace in February 2026) and Airbus, with HAL also in focus.

**What to watch:** the request for proposals and the Indian partners chosen.

Sources: [Times of India](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/defence/news/navy-coast-guard-helicopter-acquisition-puts-leonardo-airbus-and-hal-in-focus/articleshow/136152110.cms); [@timesofindia](https://x.com/timesofindia/status/2125733775770284163).
articles.why: a large European export opportunity in the Indo-Pacific, and an example of the cooperation with India that widens Europe's strategic options beyond US-led blocs.

articles.headline: Update: Poland seeks concrete UK and French air-defence help as CAMM-MR moves ahead
articles.summary:
Polish Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz is asking the UK and France to turn their security commitments into concrete air-defence, missile-defence and reconnaissance support, and Warsaw plans a no-fly zone along its eastern border by late December or early January (Anadolu, PAP; [@anadoluagency](https://x.com/anadoluagency/status/2125669599593025729)). Aviation Week adds that Poland wants to expand its commitment to MBDA's CAMM family with the medium-range version developed with the UK, following the intergovernmental agreement of 24 November covered on 24–25 November ([@AviationWeek](https://x.com/AviationWeek/status/2125707359603351651); Janes). Cross-reference: see World/Conflicts for the no-fly zone.

Sources: [PAP](https://www.pap.pl/en/news/poland-introduce-no-fly-zone-east-amid-russian-missile-threat); [Aviation Week](https://aviationweek.com/defense/missile-defense-weapons/poland-cements-camm-mr-missile-interest-uk-handshake-agreement); [Janes](https://www.janes.com/defence-intelligence-insights/defence-news/sea/poland-and-uk-advance-camm-mr-missile-project-three-years-after-concept-unveiled).
articles.why: Poland turning to European partners and a European missile (PGZ–MBDA UK) is the positive trend; the test is whether London and Paris deliver.

articles.headline: US round-up: SLCM-N, KC-46 price rise, MV-75 delay and SpaceX shares for "Trump Accounts"
articles.summary:
- **SLCM-N:** the US Navy selected Raytheon to advance the nuclear-armed sea-launched cruise missile toward prototype demonstrations (RTX, 24 Nov, via [Army Recognition](https://www.armyrecognition.com/news/navy-news/2026/u-s-navy-taps-raytheon-to-advance-new-submarine-launched-nuclear-missile-toward-prototype-demonstrations)).

- **KC-46 Lot 13 (Update):** the $2.82bn award for 15 tankers puts the unit cost at just under $188m, up more than 14% on Lot 12; Boeing has 203 KC-46s on contract or in service ([Air & Space Forces Magazine](https://www.airandspaceforces.com/air-force-boeing-2-8b-contract-more-kc-46s/)). Europe's A330 MRTT is the alternative.

- **MV-75:** the Army officially missed its goal of receiving the first Bell MV-75 for testing in 2026 after FY2026 funds ran out in July ([Breaking Defense](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/11/delivery-of-first-mv-75-for-testing-officially-delayed-amid-funding-setbacks-army/)).

- **SpaceX:** committed to give one Class A share to every active "Trump Account", with Musk matching (SpaceX IR, CNBC; [@SpaceX](https://x.com/SpaceX/status/2125671356339499494)).

- **BlackSky** showed imagery of China's Shaodong air base delivered 17 minutes after collection ([@BlackSky_Inc](https://x.com/BlackSky_Inc/status/2125665884865790259)); **HII** on the USS Enterprise (CVN-65) going for dismantling in Mobile ([@WeAreHII](https://x.com/WeAreHII/status/2125773728122544355)).

articles.headline: Aerospace and space: MaiaSpace ships to Kourou, Terran R stage mated, Korea moves Nuri production to Hanwha
articles.summary:
- **MaiaSpace** (ArianeGroup) shipped full-scale mechanical models of both Maia stages from Vernon via Le Havre on the Canopée to French Guiana for combined tests in H1 2027 ([European Spaceflight](https://europeanspaceflight.com/maiaspace-ships-maia-mechanical-models-to-launch-site/)).

- **Relativity** mated Terran R's first stage (13 Aeon R engines, over 3.4m lbf), next stop Stennis ([@relativityspace](https://x.com/relativityspace/status/2125689450818933079)); **Stoke** lifted Nova stage 1 for wet dress ([@stoke_space](https://x.com/stoke_space/status/2125676892292563335)); **Vast** integrated all 15 COPVs on Haven-1 ([@vast](https://x.com/vast/status/2125755510075031646)); **Rocket Lab** set a 4h45 wet-dress record for its next Synspective mission ([@RocketLab](https://x.com/RocketLab/status/2125710834244686121)).

- **NASA** nuclear propulsion demo to make only limited use of nuclear propulsion (SpaceNews headline, not fetched) ([@SpaceNews_Inc](https://x.com/SpaceNews_Inc/status/2125727845225787884)).

- **South Korea:** KARI, KASA and Hanwha Aerospace completed transport checks of Nuri stage mock-ups; from the 6th launch the stages will be assembled at Hanwha's Suncheon site ([@kari2030](https://x.com/kari2030/status/2125773907492065571)).

articles.headline: RoW and Europe round-up
articles.summary:
- **Elbit** unveiled SPECTRO 12, a 25 kg multispectral EO/IR payload with laser designation for UAS and light helicopters ([@ElbitSystemsLtd](https://x.com/ElbitSystemsLtd/status/2125821795295019229)).

- **Türkiye:** EHSİM continues serial production of electronic-warfare systems and new capacity investments; ASELSAN's general manager visited ([@EhsimResmi](https://x.com/EhsimResmi/status/2125675572080550288)).

- **China:** AVIC's Y12F atmospheric survey aircraft ([@_AVICINTL](https://x.com/_AVICINTL/status/2125823640604471684)); China unveiled a 2030 roadmap for a next-generation communications network (Xinhua via [@globaltimesnews](https://x.com/globaltimesnews/status/2125751759025156181)).

- **Ukraine:** the Carmine Sky Blysk 4 kW laser reportedly downed a Russian jet-powered drone for the first time (Kyiv Independent, Ukrinform; see Conflicts); Fire Point promotes its domestic ballistic missiles ([@FirePointUA](https://x.com/FirePointUA/status/2125664127846912140)).

- **Lockheed in Europe:** Portugal's first UH-60L Black Hawk and Lithuania's first UH-60M test flights ([@LMEuropeNews](https://x.com/LMEuropeNews/status/2125680780689256454)): non-European helicopters where Airbus (H145M/NH90) and Leonardo (AW149) offer European options.

articles.headline: Update: Hera reveals a stadium-sized crater on Dimorphos, the asteroid humanity moved
articles.summary:
ESA said on 25 November that its Hera mission, arriving at the Didymos–Dimorphos binary, found that the 151-metre moonlet Dimorphos now has one face flattened by a stadium-sized crater left by NASA's DART impact of 26 September 2022, is tumbling chaotically, and that hundreds of previously unknown boulders encircle the pair (ESA). DART had shortened Dimorphos's orbit by 33 minutes, far more than predicted; Hera was sent to measure what the impact actually did. The probe's onboard computer (ADPMS-3) is supplied by US firm Redwire, through its Belgian unit (Redwire).

**Background (CEAFE archive):** @F_CEAFE reposted ESA's Hera launch on a SpaceX Falcon 9 (7 Oct. 2024) and, on 17 Nov. 2026, ESA's update that Hera was studying Didymos from 28.5 km away.

**What to watch:** the full Hera science results and any follow-up ESA planetary-defence mission (Ramses/Apophis) in the ESA budget.

Sources: [ESA](https://www.esa.int/articles/about-us/directorates/operations/space-safety/hera/hera-reveals-stadium-sized-asteroid-crater-left-after-spacecraft-impact); [@esa](https://x.com/esa/status/2125653121208656145); [SpaceNews](https://x.com/SpaceNews_Inc/status/2125651988130021783); [@Redwire](https://x.com/Redwire/status/2125581360676950290).
articles.why: planetary defence is one of the few space fields where Europe leads a mission end to end. It shows what ESA can deliver when member states pool funding, the opposite of the budget cuts Commissioner Kubilius warned against at 14:30.

articles.headline: Israel adds about $5bn to its 2026 defence budget to buy "blue-and-white" national systems
articles.summary:
Israel's Joint Committee on the Defence Budget approved an addition of about NIS 17.3bn (about $5bn) to the 2026 defence budget, Breaking Defense reports. Defence Minister Israel Katz said it will allow "blue-and-white self-reliance in long-term procurement in space, attack helicopters, air defense, and other classified areas". The 2026 budget was approved in March at a record $45bn and has since received several supplements (August, September, and an October deal to fund Apache purchases).

**CEAFE comment:** Without a common industrial, technological and defence base, Europe will remain dependent on decisions taken in Washington or Beijing.

**What to watch:** Israeli contracts for national space and air-defence systems, and Israeli exports to Europe (Arrow 3, SkyStriker).

Sources: [Breaking Defense](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/11/israel-increases-defense-budget-by-5-billion-as-concerns-continue-over-future-funding/) (via [@BreakingDefense](https://x.com/BreakingDefense/status/2125644247277658253)).
articles.why: a country of fewer than 10 million people is spending to cut its dependence on foreign suppliers, while many European states still buy off-the-shelf from the US. European self-reliance needs the same political will, but it only works at the EU scale, since no member state is big enough on its own.

articles.headline: Embraer and ALADA sign a framework to sell the KC-390 and A-29 government-to-government in Latin America and Africa
articles.summary:
Embraer and ALADA (Empresa de Projetos Aeroespaciais do Brasil) signed a framework agreement at Mostra BID in Brasília on 25 November. It opens the way to offer the KC-390 Millennium transport and the A-29 Super Tucano to countries that buy through government-to-government (G2G) models, starting with Latin America and Africa. It follows a memorandum signed at FIDAE in April 2026 (Embraer).

**Background (CEAFE archive):** The KC-390 is a constant in the CEAFE archive as a European purchase: Portugal's deliveries (2024) and sixth aircraft (June 2025), and Colombia's selection (5 Aug. 2026).

**What to watch:** the first G2G contracts under the framework, and KC-390 campaigns in Europe.

Sources: [Embraer](https://www.embraer.com/media-center/en/?mediatype=NEWS&detail=34074-Embraer-and-ALADA-Sign-Agreement-for-Government-to-Government-Sales-of-the-KC-390-Millennium-and-A-29-Super-Tucano); [@embraer](https://x.com/embraer/status/2125599315490222443).
articles.why: a G2G channel backed by the Brazilian state makes the KC-390 more competitive against the European A400M and C295 in third markets. Several EU states have already chosen the KC-390 over the A400M. Europe needs a similar joint export-support tool to back its own aircraft.

articles.headline: US Army declares its first Dark Eagle hypersonic battery fully fielded
articles.summary:
Lt. Gen. Frank Lozano, the Army's acquisition executive for fires, told Breaking Defense on 19 November that the first Long Range Hypersonic Weapon (Dark Eagle) battery "is fully fielded. It is ready to go". He did not say when or where it was fielded. The programme first aimed to field the battery in 2023 and then missed a September 2025 target. Bloomberg reported that it was still not completely fielded as of October 2026.

**Background (CEAFE archive):** @F_CEAFE has followed Dark Eagle since an aborted test at Cape Canaveral (Sep. 2023) and CENTCOM's request for its deployment (30 Apr. 2026).

**What to watch:** whether Dark Eagle is deployed to Europe, and how ELSA (European Long-Range Strike Approach) progresses.

Sources: [Breaking Defense](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/11/first-dark-eagle-hypersonic-battery-fully-fielded-lozano-says/) (via [@BreakingDefense](https://x.com/BreakingDefense/status/2125587309076595192)).
articles.why: the US now has a land-based hypersonic strike capability, and Europe has no operational equivalent. European hypersonic work, such as the EU-funded interceptor studies, is still in early stages. That gap leaves European long-range strike dependent on US decisions.

articles.headline: Navantia's BAC combat supply ship for the Spanish Navy passes its critical design review
articles.summary:
Navantia announced that the BAC (Buque de Aprovisionamiento en Combate) programme for the Armada has passed its Critical Design Review. The new ship will add protection, digitalisation and the ability to operate uncrewed vehicles (Navantia).

**What to watch:** the start of construction, and Navantia's Industry Day in Chile on 1 December (Exponaval).

Sources: [@NavantiaOficial](https://x.com/NavantiaOficial/status/2125582461677732008).
articles.why: naval logistics ships built at home keep shipbuilding capacity in Europe. Navantia has already built replenishment ships for export to Australia.

articles.headline: US round-up: lasers against drones, autonomous surface vessels and the missile production problem
articles.summary:
- **Lockheed Martin Sanctum:** at the Department of War directed-energy shoot-off, Lockheed is showing its Sanctum counter-drone system, which integrates IPG Photonics CROSSBOW lasers with existing C2 systems ([@LockheedMartin](https://x.com/LockheedMartin/status/2125586975998828791)).

A long continuing resolution is also in view: the Pentagon is asking for a list of "anomalies" ([@BreakingDefense](https://x.com/BreakingDefense/status/2125601665881342155)).

- **SpaceX:** says it will invest more than $50bn in a supercompute site in Cochise County, Arizona (company claim) ([@SpaceX](https://x.com/SpaceX/status/2125637438710153247)).
articles.why: the US gap in interceptor production (PAC-3, SM-6) is an opening for European suppliers such as SAMP/T NG and MBDA, but only if Europe expands its own production first.

articles.headline: Aerospace and space: Boeing's big China order, Cygnus XL, Landsat and Chinese lunar missions
articles.summary:
- **Xiamen Airlines** signed for 50 Boeing 737-8s, the largest Boeing order from China since 2017, per Aviation Week ([@AviationWeek](https://x.com/AviationWeek/status/2125630096153166193)). This is a setback for Airbus in a market where it had gained ground while Boeing was shut out.

An intra-European frigate deal would be the positive alternative to the US–UK frigate proposal reported on 20 November.

articles.headline: Indra's Forward2030: Spain's defence champion aims to more than double in size by 2030
articles.summary:
At its investor day on 25 November, Indra Group presented its Forward2030 strategic plan (Indra press release). Targets: revenue above €12bn in 2030 (more than double the 2025 close), EBIT above €1.5bn with a margin over 12.5%, cash generation over €3.1bn in 2026–2030, and an ambition of €20bn revenue in 2035 with 50% earned abroad. Indra will put €1bn of its own money into R&D and €240m into reskilling. The group is reorganised around three axes, Defence and Space, Intelligent Technology and Critical Infrastructure, with IndraMind (sovereign AI, command and control and integration; portfolio of €400m) as the transversal layer. Its order book is over €22bn. Bloomberg reports that Indra raised its guidance as new chairman Ángel Simón presented the strategy.

**Context:** Antecedentes: @F_CEAFE has followed Indra's role in European programmes: in July 2024 it reposted Lockheed Martin's SPY-7 radar manufacturing orders to Indra for Spain's F-110 frigates (a US radar at the heart of a Spanish ship); in February 2026 OCCAR signed the co-funding contract for the Indra-led REACT II electronic-attack programme ([X, Feb. 2026](https://x.com/i/status/2020096115614335173)); and on 9 November 2026 it reposted reports that Spain is negotiating with Germany to produce the future fighter, with Airbus and Indra taking on the project ([X, Nov. 2026](https://x.com/i/status/2119759031082315902)).

The contrast in scale makes clear that national strategies, however ambitious, are not enough against competitors of a different order of magnitude.

Sources: [Indra Group](https://www.indragroup.com/es/noticias/indra-group-da-un-salto-al-futuro-y-doblara-su-tamano-como-lider-global-en-tecnologia-dual-para-sectores-criticos-conectando-sus-capacidades-y-potenciandolas-con-indramind); [Bloomberg post](https://x.com/business/status/2125487178926997732); [@IndraCompany](https://x.com/IndraCompany/status/2125552743159095401).
articles.why: a Spanish group setting out to become a "product company" in defence and space adds European scale. Even at €12bn, Indra would stay far below the large US primes; European growth plans only close that gap if they are joined to common programmes (FCAS, ESSOR, EDF) rather than run as national champions.

articles.headline: Belgium opens Europe's largest satellite factory, which will build IRIS² satellites
articles.summary:
King Philippe inaugurated on 24 November Aerospacelab's "megafactory" in Charleroi, presented as the EU's largest satellite factory, with an annual capacity of about 500 satellites (Euronews/AFP). It is to produce satellites for the EU's IRIS² secure-connectivity constellation, the European answer to Starlink, with IRIS² production to start by the end of 2028. CEO Benoit Deper said the company grew from a "tiny startup" in 2018 to a player in Europe's "space sovereignty".

**Context:** Antecedentes: @F_CEAFE has followed IRIS² since November 2022, when it argued that the EU should build R&D facilities so that new technologies are developed and mastered in Europe, "as with Galileo & Iris2" ([X, Nov. 2022](https://x.com/i/status/1594387040610623490)). In December 2024 ESA agreed to support the constellation's development; on 31 August 2026 SES awarded OHB a contract worth almost €1bn for 18 MEO satellite platforms ([X, Aug. 2026](https://x.com/i/status/2094485921127170265)); and on 1 November 2026 Canada's MDA Space secured a €64m IRIS² antenna agreement.

Sources: [Euronews](https://l.euronews.com/eLw0) (via [@euronews](https://x.com/euronews/status/2125526486501228975)).
articles.why: mass satellite production in a former industrial city is the kind of intra-European capacity that reduces dependence on SpaceX/Starlink; it only pays off if IRIS² keeps its funding (see item 3).

articles.headline: Update: Kubilius warns a 30% cut to defence and space in the next EU budget would endanger IRIS² and EU defence projects
articles.summary:
EU Defence and Space Commissioner Andrius Kubilius wrote on X that "drastic cuts" to defence and space in the next Multiannual Financial Framework (30%, minus €39bn) would endanger the most important pan-European programmes: IRIS², the European Earth Observation Governmental Service (EOGS), and the European Defence Projects of Common Interest (Eastern Flank Watch, the drone defence initiative, air, maritime and space shields) and strategic enablers. "Putin escalates, EU cuts. Wrong signal!" The cut figures are his; the Council and Parliament negotiating texts were not checked this run.

Europe has resources; what it lacks, time and again, is the scale that only joint action can provide.

Sources: [@KubiliusA 1/2](https://x.com/KubiliusA/status/2125565352578859346), [2/2](https://x.com/KubiliusA/status/2125565356127268997).
articles.why: no member state can fund IRIS² or an air shield alone; cutting the common budget pushes capitals back to national, often US, off-the-shelf purchases.

articles.headline: Germany's 2027 budget lifts defence spending to €139.4bn
articles.summary:
Germany plans total defence spending of €139.4bn in 2027, up €31.2bn from €108.2bn in 2026: €109.7bn in the regular budget plus €29.6bn from the Bundeswehr special fund set up in 2022 (Anadolu, citing the budget approved by the Bundestag budget committee, to be voted this week). Procurement is planned to exceed €60bn. Development aid falls to €9.58bn from €10.05bn and UN contributions are cut.

Sources: [Anadolu](https://v.aa.com.tr/4137005).
articles.why: the biggest European procurement budget will shape the market; whether those €60bn+ go to European suppliers or to US systems (F-35, P-8, Arrow, Patriot) decides how much European industry gains.

articles.headline: Czech engine maker PBS Aerospace aims to double its US production capacity
articles.summary:
Defense News reports that Czech jet engine producer PBS Aerospace aims to at least double its manufacturing capacity in the United States, to grow as a supplier of small turbojets for US drones and missiles. Defense News also reports that Italian officials say Italy reached defence and domestic-security spending equal to 2.8% of GDP in 2026, a figure not visible in the defence budget itself. (Index summaries only; full articles not fetched.)

Sources: [Defense News Europe](https://www.defensenews.com/global/europe/).
articles.why: a European engine maker expanding in the US serves US programmes under US rules; Europe's own drone and missile programmes need the same small-engine capacity at home.

articles.headline: Space: Bulgaria's EnduroSat books two New Glenn launches; White House seeks $2bn more for Artemis
articles.summary:
- **EnduroSat on New Glenn:** the Bulgarian satellite maker has booked two dedicated Blue Origin New Glenn launches from 2029 for its customers, as SpaceX winds down its Falcon 9 rideshare programme (SpaceNews). A European satellite firm again turns to a US launcher; Vega C, Ariane 6 and the coming European micro-launchers (Isar, RFA, MaiaSpace) are the European alternatives.

- **Artemis:** the White House asks Congress for up to $2bn more for NASA's Artemis programme in 2027, with few details on its use (SpaceNews).

- **Orbital data centres:** European companies seek supporting roles in US and Chinese orbital data centre projects rather than compete directly (SpaceNews, Bremen) — another sign of Europe settling for subcontractor roles.

- **Hera:** ESA releases Hera's first close-up images of asteroid Dimorphos tonight at 19:45 CET from Berlin; Spain's GMV and JAXA's TIRI instrument are on the mission (ESA, GMV, JAXA).

<!-- ceafe-chart: lanzamientos -->

These figures show how the size of European states leaves them unable to compete alone against much larger global powers.

Sources: [SpaceNews EnduroSat](https://spacenews.com/satellite-maker-endurosat-books-two-dedicated-new-glenn-launches/); [SpaceNews Artemis](https://spacenews.com/white-house-seeks-an-additional-2-billion-for-artemis-in-2027/); [SpaceNews data centres](https://spacenews.com/european-companies-seek-supporting-roles-on-orbital-data-center-projects/); [@esa](https://x.com/esa/status/2125545327159869615).

articles.headline: Poland and the US sign a defence R&D agreement after 17 years of talks
articles.summary:
Polish Deputy Defence Minister Cezary Tomczyk and US Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering Emil Michael signed a Research, Development, Test and Evaluation (RDT&E) agreement at the Pentagon on 24 November (Polish MoD, Anadolu Agency). It ends 17 years of negotiations and sets a framework for joint research projects, technology development and exchange of technical data. Polish universities, research institutes and companies can now join US R&D, testing and evaluation programmes; the first pilot area is high-energy materials and ammunition (Polish MoD). During the same visit Polish officials discussed with Lockheed Martin faster delivery of F-35 simulators, full operational capability of Polish F-35s, a European service centre in Poland for PAC-3 Patriot missiles and technology transfer for HIMARS.

This is not about diminishing this country, but about measuring its real weight against those who already operate on a continental or global scale.

**Key facts:** signed 24 Nov 2026 at the Pentagon; signatories Tomczyk (PL) and Emil Michael (US); first pilot area: high-energy materials and ammunition.

**What to watch:** first joint projects named; whether the PAC-3 service centre and HIMARS technology transfer turn into contracts with PGZ.

**Sources:** https://x.com/i/status/2125461984258777466 (Anadolu); https://www.gov.pl/web/obrona-narodowa/od-badan-do-nowych-zdolnosci-polska-wzmacnia-wspolprace-obronna-z-usa ; https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/poland-us-sign-defense-research-agreement-after-17-years-of-negotiations/4136545
articles.why: Poland, the largest buyer of US equipment in the EU, is anchoring its defence research in a bilateral framework with Washington rather than in European ones (EDF, EDA, PESCO). Early-stage joint research shapes future requirements, so it tends to lock in US standards and suppliers, and anything developed together falls under US export rules (ITAR) that Europe does not mirror. A PAC-3 service centre in Poland would be a US-controlled node; Europe's own alternative for ground-based air defence is the SAMP/T NG (Eurosam: MBDA and Thales), and Poland is already co-developing CAMM-MR with MBDA UK (see the 24 Nov 20:30 brief).

articles.headline: Raytheon moves the US Navy's nuclear sea-launched cruise missile (SLCM-N) into development
articles.summary:
Raytheon (RTX) has been awarded an Other Transaction Authority agreement by the US Navy to move the Nuclear-Armed Sea-Launched Cruise Missile (SLCM-N) from concept work into a development phase that will mature the design, integrate subsystems and prepare prototype demonstrations (RTX release, 24 Nov). Contributors are Anduril Rocket Motor Systems, Divergent (which says it builds the airframe) and Williams International. No value was disclosed.

**Sources:** https://x.com/i/status/2125390434004500859 ; https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/rtxs-raytheon-selected-to-advance-development-of-new-submarine-launched-missile-for-us-navy-302948503.html
articles.why: SLCM-N adds a non-strategic US nuclear option at sea, relevant to extended deterrence in Europe, at a time when France and Sweden held their first joint nuclear-deterrence exercise (Defense News). The supply chain also shows how far US start-ups (Anduril, Divergent) are now inside top-tier strategic programmes.

articles.headline: Korea's KAI targets the UK Hawk replacement with the T-50
articles.summary:
Korea Aerospace Industries has started marketing the T-50 (offered as "TF-50") in the UK as a replacement for the BAE Systems Hawk used by the RAF, with adverts in AirForces Monthly; Lockheed Martin is named only as development partner and KAI says it is exploring partnerships with UK companies (Aviation Week, 23 Nov). The UK Jet Training System competition is still being defined.

**Sources:** https://x.com/i/status/2125372394894155941 ; https://aviationweek.com/defense/light-attack-advanced-training/kai-begins-uk-t-50-marketing-push
articles.why: the end of the Hawk leaves Europe's first jet-trainer exporter without a successor in its home market. A Korean–US trainer would be a non-European purchase; the European option already in service with Italy, Poland and Greece is Leonardo's M-346. CEAFE comment: a market fragmented country by country lets outside suppliers pick off each requirement one at a time.

articles.headline: Boeing: 15 more KC-46A tankers for $2.82bn; Malaysia Airlines chooses the 787
articles.summary:
The US Air Force added $2.82bn to Boeing's contract for 15 KC-46A Lot 13 aircraft plus support, subscriptions and licences, with work in Seattle due by 30 June 2030 (MarketWatch, DefenseBook; Boeing on X). Separately, Malaysia Aviation Group picked the Boeing 787 Dreamliner to expand its wide-body fleet, breaking Airbus' hold on its long-haul line-up (Bloomberg on X; article not fetched).

**Sources:** https://x.com/i/status/2125351764916396442 ; https://www.marketwatch.com/story/boeing-gets-2-82b-added-to-air-force-contract-15f148d6 ; https://x.com/i/status/2125436851108397238
articles.why: the KC-46 is the US tanker that beat the Airbus A330 MRTT; the MRTT remains Europe's tanker (Multinational MRTT Fleet). Losing a long-haul customer in Asia is a commercial blow for Airbus at a moment when Boeing is recovering.

- **Shenzhou-24** lifted off on a Long March-2F from Jiuquan on 25 November (early morning Beijing time) and docked with the Chinese space station, carrying Tang Hongbo, Wu Yi and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a fighter pilot and the first foreign national to visit Tiangong, under a China–Pakistan agreement (Xinhua, Global Times, Al Jazeera, Anadolu). https://x.com/i/status/2125407596974841992 ; https://x.com/i/status/2125467550893092923 ; https://x.com/i/status/2125389000990941416

articles.headline: US private-equity firm Cerberus buys Airbus's US satellite business
articles.summary:
Cerberus Capital Management (United States) announced on 24 November that it has agreed to acquire the Space Systems business of Airbus U.S. Space & Defense, the American arm of Airbus, with closing expected by the end of the year (Breaking Defense, SpaceNews). The unit builds satellites at a factory of about 200,000 square feet in Merritt Island, Florida, next to the Kennedy Space Center; SpaceNews notes that the deal brings a factory built for OneWeb's broadband constellation under American ownership. No price was disclosed, and Airbus does not break out the revenue of its US arm.

Airbus says its US subsidiary will "double down" on autonomous aircraft production; Cerberus says it will invest in the unit's engineering and products to meet demand for "U.S. spacecraft production capacity". **Background (CEAFE archive):** in September 2026 @F_CEAFE shared the news that Eutelsat had ordered 229 additional low-Earth-orbit OneWeb satellites from Airbus, on top of the 440 Airbus-built satellites already in the constellation.

*CEAFE:* Technological and defence dependence is not abstract: it shows up in the number of companies, in spending and in the presence on the ground.

**What to watch:** the CFIUS review; who will build Eutelsat OneWeb's replacement satellites; Airbus's plans for its US drone business.

**Sources:** https://x.com/i/status/2125271257029480613, https://x.com/i/status/2125260706480005557, https://breakingdefense.com/2026/11/investment-firm-cerberus-to-buy-space-business-of-us-airbus-arm/, https://spacenews.com/private-equity-firm-cerberus-to-acquire-airbus-u-s-satellite-business/, [CEAFE, Sep 2026](https://x.com/i/status/2098879154926104742)
articles.why: the factory that mass-produced the satellites of OneWeb, now part of Europe's Eutelsat, passes to a US financial investor just as Europe is trying to build IRIS² and its own sovereign constellations. A European prime withdraws from US satellite manufacturing. The asymmetry is plain: a European-owned plant on US soil works under US control rules (CFIUS review, FOCI mitigation, ITAR), which limit what Airbus can share with Europe; no equivalent common European regime protects Europe's own assets when US capital buys in.

articles.headline: Poland and the UK sign agreement to develop the CAMM-MR air-defence missile
articles.summary:
Poland and the United Kingdom signed an intergovernmental agreement on 24 November that opens the way to the joint development of CAMM-MR, a medium-range air-defence missile meant to reach beyond 100 km, according to Poland's Armament Agency. Secretary of State Magdalena Sobkowiak-Czarnecka signed for Poland and defence procurement minister Luke Pollard for the UK; MBDA, its Polish arm and the state group PGZ are on the industry side. The agreement does not fund the missile: it sets the "legal and financial conditions" for the detailed design contract, to be followed by an executive agreement and later a supply contract, timed with the end of deliveries of Poland's three Miecznik frigates. No dates or cost were given. The agency calls it the first international project to develop a missile for Polish air defence.

@F_CEAFE quoted the agency's post: "Why can't Poland buy 🇪🇺 weapons? 🇺🇸🇰🇷🇬🇧... Should we, the rest of the EU partners, keep funding them? #Polexit". **Background (CEAFE archive):** in April 2022 @F_CEAFE shared the Polish defence ministry's announcement that Poland would acquire elements of MBDA's CAMM system and integrate them with Polish components.

**What to watch:** the executive agreement and its work share; whether CAMM-MR is put forward for EU SAFE loans or EDIP funding, which favour EU content.

**Sources:** https://x.com/i/status/2125270201063371033, https://x.com/i/status/2125260499587563546, https://defence-blog.com/poland-uk-sign-deal-to-develop-camm-mr-missile/, [CEAFE, Apr 2022](https://x.com/i/status/1514676307501670419)
articles.why: MBDA is a pan-European group, but this programme is run with the UK, now outside the Union, and sits alongside Poland's large purchases of US and South Korean equipment. CEAFE's point is the double standard: an EU member state that receives EU cohesion and defence funds, and benefits from the European-preference rules of EU instruments, while equipping itself largely outside the Union.

articles.headline: MI5 warns British defence executives of Russian proxy arson and sabotage
articles.summary:
MI5, the UK's domestic security service, has warned British defence executives that they face a growing threat of arson and other sabotage carried out by proxies working for Russia, Bloomberg reported on 24 November; AP reports that firms aiding Ukraine have been told to brace for sabotage attempts. The full articles could not be checked.

**What to watch:** whether other European governments issue similar warnings to their defence suppliers.

**Sources:** https://x.com/i/status/2125245588086182115, https://x.com/i/status/2125263218088038676, https://apnews.com/article/uk-mi5-russia-sabotage-warning-europe-17406e53d24d5a71f3beaf551fdf1a99
articles.why: Europe's defence industrial base, which is ramping up production for Ukraine and for rearmament, is itself a target. Protecting plants and staff becomes a cost of production and an argument for common European industrial-security standards.

articles.headline: EU money for defence: EUROGUARD vessel and €68m proposed for space defence R&T
articles.summary:
The European Commission (DG DEFIS) says the EUROGUARD project has launched a 45-metre semi-autonomous vessel for sea surveillance and the protection of critical infrastructure, including undersea cables, with €65m from the European Defence Fund. Separately, the European Defence Agency says EU member states proposed €68m for space defence research and technology at its CapTech Space meeting in Italy; projects include ASSAI (AI to protect satellites) and LEO2VLEO (three satellites in very low Earth orbit).

**What to watch:** EDA's selection of the space projects and the vessel's trials.

**Sources:** https://x.com/i/status/2125288344859062384, https://link.europa.eu/tynmMH, https://x.com/i/status/2125259241438994624
articles.why: common funding buys capabilities that no EU member state would build alone, from seabed protection after the Baltic cable incidents to satellite defence. The sums remain small next to US programmes.

articles.headline: A US launcher builds its pad in Sweden; Canada joins the NATO Innovation Fund
articles.summary:
Firefly Aerospace (US) says construction of Launch Complex 3 at Esrange Space Center in Sweden is "well underway" in partnership with Sweden's SSC. Separately, Defense One reports from Halifax that Canada has joined the NATO Innovation Fund while promising "business as usual" with the US, a move Defense One describes as a reaction to dwindling cooperation from the Trump administration.

**What to watch:** the first Firefly launch date from Esrange; Canada's first investments through the fund.

**Sources:** https://x.com/i/status/2125272509222162672, https://x.com/i/status/2125230485307605133
articles.why: Esrange is one of Europe's few continental launch sites; giving a pad to a US launcher competes with Europe's own small launchers (Isar Aerospace, RFA, PLD Space, Orbex). Canada's step, by contrast, shows a NATO member diversifying towards European and multinational instruments.

articles.summary:

articles.headline: Airbus Manching works council rejects GCAP and demands a German sixth-generation fighter
articles.summary:
The works council at Airbus Defence and Space's Manching site (Bavaria) has "firmly rejected" Germany joining the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP) led by the UK, Italy and Japan, calling it "doomed to failure" for Germany because work shares are already allocated and Berlin would have little influence. It urges the federal government to launch a national sixth-generation fighter programme now, open to later partners, with a prototype first flight in 2032 and entry into service before 2040 (FlightGlobal, Aviation Week, Focus, 24 Nov). "We must not repeat the political mistakes made with France," the council says, in reference to the stalled Franco-German-Spanish FCAS.

**Background (CEAFE archive):** the German debate is not new. In November 2023 @F_CEAFE shared a Times report that Germany might leave FCAS (with France and Spain) for the British-Italian-Japanese Tempest/GCAP, and said it preferred Italy joining the European FCAS; in January 2025 the Airbus CEO said Europe's two fighter programmes could combine (Reuters); in January 2026 Italy's Crosetto called British secrecy on GCAP "madness" (Defense News).

*CEAFE:* The lag is not inevitable: it is the result of acting separately on a board that is already continental or global.

**Key facts:** prototype first flight 2032 and service entry before 2040 (council's proposal); GCAP partners UK, Italy, Japan.

**Sources:** https://x.com/i/status/2125189941797720222 (Aviation Week); https://www.flightglobal.com/defence/2026/11/germany-must-launch-own-sixth-generation-fighter-and-reject-gcap-role-airbuss-manching-works-council-says/ ; https://aviationweek.com/defense/budget-policy-operations/german-airbus-workers-reject-gcap-membership (members, not fetched in full); Focus online., [CEAFE, Nov 2023](https://x.com/i/status/1719781448272547905), [CEAFE, Jan 2026](https://x.com/i/status/2017622956269060135)

**Follow-up:** Berlin's response; Dassault and Airbus positions on FCAS phase 2; Spanish government and Indra.
articles.why: Europe now risks three separate combat-air efforts (GCAP, a rump FCAS/SCAF and a possible German national programme), while the US F-47 advances as one programme. No European state can fund a sixth-generation fighter alone at US scale; fragmentation is the strongest argument for a single European programme, or at least a common core of engines, sensors and combat cloud. Spain, a FCAS partner through Indra, is directly exposed.

articles.headline: Germany picks Israel's Elbit for the F-128 frigates' electronic warfare
articles.summary:
TKMS has awarded Elbit Systems Deutschland a five-year contract to supply Aqua Marine naval electronic-warfare suites for the German Navy's four F-128 frigates. The modular system provides radar electronic support measures and countermeasures for threat detection, self-protection and electronic attack. No value was disclosed (Elbit on X; Naval Today, hartpunkt, EDR, 24 Nov).

**Sources:** https://x.com/i/status/2125173782843162814 (Elbit); https://www.navaltoday.com/2026/11/24/elbit-to-supply-electronic-warfare-systems-for-german-navy-f128-frigates ; https://www.hartpunkt.de/elbit-systems-deutschland-liefert-selbstschutzsysteme-fuer-f128/
articles.why: another core sensor of a European warship goes to a non-European supplier, even if through its German subsidiary. European alternatives exist: HENSOLDT (Germany), Elettronica (Italy), Indra (Spain) and Thales (France) all build naval EW suites. Each such choice weakens the European base that the EDIP and SAFE instruments are meant to build.

articles.headline: Ariane 6 flies its tenth mission, with 36 satellites for Amazon Leo
articles.summary:
Ariane 64 flight VA271 (Amazon Leo LE-04) lifted off from Kourou at 11:14 UTC (12:14 Madrid) on 24 November, a day late after a ground-support-system problem on 23 November, carrying 36 Amazon Leo satellites to low Earth orbit (Arianespace, ESA, Bloomberg on X; Space.com). Satellite separation over about two hours was still to be confirmed at writing. It is Ariane 6's fifth flight of 2026 in our launch log.

**Sources:** https://x.com/i/status/2125192039461474353 (Arianespace); https://x.com/i/status/2125188391474229624 (ESA); https://x.com/i/status/2125197784106061844 (Bloomberg); https://www.space.com/space-exploration/launches-spacecraft/arianespace-ariane-6-amazon-leo-internet-satellite-launch
articles.why: the launch shows Ariane 6 in a regular commercial cadence, but its biggest customer is a US broadband constellation that competes with Europe's own IRIS² and Eutelsat OneWeb. Launch income helps the European launcher; the strategic asset in orbit is American.

articles.headline: Kongsberg delivers DESNA, a Norwegian–Ukrainian air-defence system, to Ukraine
articles.summary:
Kongsberg says it has delivered DESNA, developed with Norwegian and Ukrainian authorities and Ukrainian industry. It links Ukrainian-made air-defence missiles and launchers to Kongsberg's fire command and control centre, to protect people and infrastructure against drones and other aerial threats. It complements NASAMS, in Ukraine since 2022, and uses missiles that can be produced in large numbers at lower unit cost (Kongsberg, 24 Nov).

**Sources:** https://x.com/i/status/2125177274110517688 ; https://www.kongsberg.com/news/news-archive/2026/kongsberg-delivers-the-desna-air-defence-system-to-ukraine/ (image: https://www.kongsberg.com/globalassets/kongsberg/news-and-events/stories/2026/desna/illustration-desna.jpg)
articles.why: a European C2 backbone joined to cheap Ukrainian interceptors is the kind of co-production that reduces dependence on scarce US interceptors (see item 5).

articles.headline: Pentagon in talks with GM and Ford to mass-produce drones
articles.summary:
The Wall Street Journal reports that the Pentagon is in early talks with General Motors, Ford and other manufacturers to use their factories and supply chains to scale up military drone production; automakers would mainly supply components (motors, actuators, engines, sensors, lidar) to established drone makers, and GM is considering drone motors. No agreement is final (WSJ on X; Anadolu, US News, 24 Nov).

**Sources:** https://x.com/i/status/2125182412267118955 (WSJ, paywalled); https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/pentagon-in-talks-with-general-motors-ford-to-boost-military-drone-production-report/4135749
articles.why: the US is mobilising its civil industrial base for mass. Europe's car industry, now shedding jobs, is an obvious candidate for the same move.

articles.headline: JAXA reports a data breach in its Earth-observation distribution system
articles.summary:
JAXA says attackers breached its public Earth Observation Data Distribution System on 18 November through a command-injection flaw, installed a backdoor and stole the account names and encrypted passwords of about 2,000 users. The system was shut down that day; JAXA found no sign the satellite data were accessed and has set no date for restoration (JAXA press release, 24 Nov; Nikkei, IT Post).

**Sources:** https://x.com/i/status/2125150286289551512 ; https://global.jaxa.jp/press/2026/11/20261124-2_e.html

articles.headline: German industry sets up a joint trading house for critical raw materials, with Rheinmetall and BMW
articles.summary:
Forty-five German companies from the automotive, electrical and defence industries, among them Rheinmetall and BMW, back a planned German Raw Materials Trading House (Deutsches Rohstoffhandelshaus, DRH). It will pool demand, buy and trade critical materials jointly, build strategic reserves and may take stakes in supply chains, while each company keeps its own purchasing. The DRH is the core of a new "Zukunftsmodell Rohstoffsicherung" (raw-materials security model) presented by industry and the federal government on 23 November; the pre-founding phase runs until mid-2027, when it is due to be formally established (Handelsblatt, VDA, 23 Nov; Bloomberg on X).

- 45 companies; formal founding planned mid-2027 (Handelsblatt, 23 Nov).

- Sources: · · · Bloomberg article (unreachable: timed out)

**What to watch:** which defence firms join, state funding, and links to the EU joint-purchasing platform.

**Sources:** [X](https://x.com/business/status/2124966264535675091), [handelsblatt.com](https://www.handelsblatt.com/unternehmen/industrie/industrie-bmw-und-rheinmetall-planen-handelshaus-fuer-rohstoffe/100271875.html), [vda.de](https://www.vda.de/de/presse/Pressemeldungen/2026/261123_PM_Rohstoffe-sichern-Standort-staerken-Deutsche-Industrie-und-Politik-gehen-mit-der-Umsetzung-des-Zukunftsmodell-Rohstoffsicherung-gemeinsam-in-die-Offensive)
articles.why: defence production (rare-earth magnets, germanium, gallium, tungsten) depends on supply chains China dominates and has restricted. A national pool is a step forward, but a German-only buyer competes with other Europeans for the same tonnes; the EU's RESourceEU and Critical Raw Materials Act joint-purchasing tools carry more weight if the big national champions buy through them. Here again, size decides: in raw materials no single member state can bargain with Beijing on equal terms.

articles.headline: Germany's Aerodata flies the AeroForce X, an ITAR-free MALE drone prototype
articles.summary:
Aerodata AG flew the AeroForce X prototype (registration D-IAFX) for the first time on 14 November from Strausberg near Berlin, with a test pilot on board to check basic handling; all test objectives were met, the company says. The twin-engine, twin-boom aircraft weighs 5 tonnes, carries 1.3 tonnes of payload and has up to 40 hours' endurance. Company officials told Aviation Week it will be 100% German, engines, mission suite and communications included, and therefore free of ITAR (Aviation Week, 16 Nov; posted 24 Nov).

**Context:** Antecedentes: on 26 March 2022 @F_CEAFE noted the concerns raised about the European sovereignty of the Eurodrone because its engine comes from Avio Aero (a company of the US group GE, not the Italian rocket maker Avio S.p.A.), and that the company stressed the engine is not subject to ITAR, so no US approval would be needed ([X, 2022](https://x.com/i/status/1507784754174865417)).

- Sources: ·

- Image: — AeroForce X prototype (Aerodata AG).

**What to watch:** uncrewed flight, Bundeswehr interest, Eurodrone schedule.

**Sources:** [X](https://x.com/AviationWeek/status/2124931744608526449), [aviationweek.com (1)](https://aviationweek.com/defense/aircraft-propulsion/germanys-aeroforce-x-uas-makes-first-flight), [aviationweek.com (2)](https://aviationweek.com/sites/default/files/styles/crop_freeform/public/2026-11/aeroforcex_800px.jpg)
articles.why: European forces fly mostly US MQ-9 Reapers or Israeli Herons, with US export control over use and upgrades. A national, ITAR-free MALE is a sovereign option alongside the late Eurodrone (Airbus–Dassault–Leonardo); the risk is fragmentation if each country builds its own. Aviation Week understands it is powered by two Continental CD-300 Jet-A piston engines.

articles.headline: Update: BepiColombo safely in orbit around Mercury
articles.summary:
**ESA says BepiColombo is safe and in a stable orbit around Mercury after an eight-year journey, even though a software issue cut its orbit-insertion manoeuvre short (the thruster glitch reported in the 14:30 brief of 23 November). JAXA says the separation of its Mio orbiter remains scheduled for 10 December 2026 (Japan time), after nine flybys since the 2018 launch.**

**Context:** Antecedentes: BepiColombo is a joint ESA–JAXA mission whose European spacecraft was built by Airbus; @F_CEAFE has followed it since its Earth fly-by in April 2020 ([X, 2020](https://x.com/i/status/1246064783318814721)).

- Sources: · ·

**Sources:** [X (1)](https://x.com/esa/status/2124939363075100989), [X (2)](https://x.com/JAXA_en/status/2125082622087070021), [X (3)](https://x.com/JAXA_en/status/2125054598872490341)
articles.why: Europe's largest planetary mission, run with Japan, is back on track; a sign of what ESA achieves through partnership with non-US agencies.

articles.headline: US: Air Force withdraws a $16.1bn propulsion contract posted in error
articles.summary:
**On 20 November the Pentagon's contract roundup announced 58 companies for the Air Force's Advanced Propulsion Acquisition Contract (APAC), an IDIQ vehicle worth up to $16.1bn running to 2041. A spokesperson told Breaking Defense the notice was posted in error; the service still plans to award it, and the 23 November roundup carried the correction (Breaking Defense, 23 Nov).**

- Sources: ·

**Sources:** [X](https://x.com/BreakingDefense/status/2124983089742962835), [breakingdefense.com](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/11/propulsion-mega-contract-posted-in-error-air-force-says/)

articles.headline: US round-up: Ford into space hardware, Air Force G700s, Castelion, Intuitive Machines
articles.summary:
- **Ford–Revolution Space:** Ford takes a minority stake in Boston-based Revolution Space and will help scale spacecraft production; value not disclosed (SpaceNews, Bloomberg, 23 Nov). A US carmaker moving into space and defence supply, as German carmakers are being urged to do. ·

- **Air Force G700:** the USAF plans to field Gulfstream G700s to replace its C-37A/B executive jets, from FY2027 funding once appropriated (Aviation Week).

- **GE Aerospace:** defence unit chief Amy Gowder to step down (Reuters; article unreachable, 401).

- **Castelion:** the hypersonic missile start-up expands its Rio Rancho, New Mexico campus and now has Navy, Army and Air Force (CAMP) contracts; it plans to start manufacturing its Blackbeard missile by next year (Albuquerque Journal, 18–20 Nov).

- **Intuitive Machines:** preliminary design review completed for START, a compact space nuclear power system with AFRL.

- **Cygnus XL NG-25** is encapsulated in a Falcon 9 fairing for the ISS.

**Sources:** [X (1)](https://x.com/SpaceNews_Inc/status/2125007373378953603), [spacenews.com](https://spacenews.com/ford-takes-stake-in-revolution-space/), [X (2)](https://x.com/AviationWeek/status/2125014286330184107), [X (3)](https://x.com/Reuters/status/2125071968571465984), [X (4)](https://x.com/Castelion/status/2124935857048342600), [X (5)](https://x.com/Int_Machines/status/2125010855234289740), [X (6)](https://x.com/northropgrumman/status/2124984763974836598)

articles.headline: China's Tiangong will host its first foreign astronaut, a Pakistani air force pilot
articles.summary:
China will launch Shenzhou-24 on 25 November at 08:18 local time (01:18 Madrid) with commander Tang Hongbo, Wu Yi and Pakistani payload specialist Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, who will be the first foreign astronaut on the Chinese space station (Reuters; China Manned Space Agency via Xinhua and Global Times, Chinese state media). The mission includes four China–Pakistan joint experiments, according to Global Times. China will also rehearse a Long March-10A launch with the Mengzhou crewed spacecraft at Wenchang.

*CEAFE:* We see once again how a power with global reach operates at a scale that no European state can match on its own.

**Context:** Antecedentes: @F_CEAFE has followed China's Tiangong station since the Shenzhou-13 crew arrived in October 2021 ([X, 2021](https://x.com/i/status/1449333552009646080)); CEAFE has argued that Europeans should take part in Tiangong, a plan ESA dropped.

<!-- ceafe-chart: lanzamientos -->

**What to watch:** the launch on 25 November and docking; China's offer of Tiangong seats to other countries; ESA's next decisions on human spaceflight partners.

**Sources:** [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/science/china-launch-shenzhou-24-spaceship-with-first-foreign-astronaut-2026-11-24/), [Reuters (X)](https://x.com/i/status/2125075707206275099), [Xinhua](https://x.com/i/status/2125088705274929442), [Xinhua (2)](https://x.com/i/status/2125033870039105768), [Global Times](https://x.com/i/status/2125072971555565733), [Global Times (2)](https://x.com/i/status/2125063926174101527), [Chinese MFA spokesperson](https://x.com/i/status/2125069302802100231)
articles.why: ESA astronauts had trained with Chinese crews and planned to fly to Tiangong, but ESA dropped the plan. Today the first foreign seat on the only station not led by the US goes to Pakistan. Choosing partners in space, as on Earth, is a test of strategic autonomy. CEAFE argues that Europe should cooperate with every major space power on its own terms, rather than give up options to stay in line with a single partner.

articles.headline: RoW: Korea's KPS navigation system, India's anti-drone micro-missile, Japan's suppliers turn to defence
articles.summary:
- **South Korea:** KARI holds the integrated detailed design review of the Korean Positioning System (KPS) on 24–27 November, moving to manufacture, assembly and test.

- **India:** IG Defence says it has flight-tested JWALA MK-1, a home-grown micro-missile against drones (Times of India). The Indian start-up Digantara reports that 37 Chinese space objects increased their passes over Pahalgam before the April 2025 attack (Times of India). ISpA says Starlink will enter India "very soon".

- **Japan:** Reuters reports Toyota parts maker Aster is moving into defence as the car industry struggles against Chinese competition.

- **Turkey:** no news-bearing posts on the RoW list overnight (Teachers' Day messages).

HENSOLDT and THEON open a new night-vision plant in Wetzlar for the OCCAR programme

articles.headline: Eutelsat wins up to $64.46m to supply OneWeb connectivity to the US armed forces
articles.summary:
**The US arm of the French-led operator Eutelsat has a two-year contract with the US Space Force worth more than $60m, European Spaceflight reports.**

US procurement records put the ceiling at $64.46m, with $6.1m committed so far. The contract covers a shared pool of OneWeb low Earth orbit capacity, alternative positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) and technical support. It was awarded in June and announced on 17 November. According to the Space Force justification, the US military has already bought more than 500 OneWeb terminals.

*CEAFE:* Without a common industrial, technological and defence base, Europe will remain dependent on decisions taken in Washington or Beijing.

**Context:** Antecedentes: on 29 March 2023 @F_CEAFE shared an analysis on whether Eutelsat-OneWeb and the EU's sovereign connectivity constellation would "ever align" ([X, 2023](https://x.com/i/status/1641027201318387713)). The usual flow runs the other way, with European forces buying Starlink/Starshield services.

**What to watch:** how much of the $64.46m ceiling is drawn down; OneWeb's role in IRIS²; further US orders for terminals.

**Sources:** [European Spaceflight](https://europeanspaceflight.com/eutelsat-wins-60-million-us-space-force-contract/), [Andrew Parsonson on X](https://x.com/i/status/2124881761071219129)
articles.why: a constellation built up with European capital is now also serving US military programmes. Eutelsat does so through a US subsidiary, the FOCI-type arrangement Washington requires of foreign suppliers; the EU has no equivalent requirement for US firms. The contract also adds weight to OneWeb, and to IRIS², as European options for European armed forces.

articles.headline: HENSOLDT and THEON open a new night-vision plant in Wetzlar for the OCCAR programme
articles.summary:
**HENSOLDT THEON NightVision GmbH, the joint venture of Germany's HENSOLDT Optronics and Greece's THEON, has opened a new production facility in Wetzlar, Germany.**

HENSOLDT describes it as a multi-million-euro investment. The plant raises output for the Night Vision programme managed by OCCAR, the European organisation for joint armament cooperation. The programme began in 2022 with MIKRON night-vision goggle sets for the German and Belgian armed forces. It is open to other European countries interested in joining.

*CEAFE:* Acting together is not a political ornament: it is the only way to reach a scale that others already have.

**Context:** Germany, Belgium and Greece are EU member states and NATO members. OCCAR manages cooperative programmes on behalf of its participating nations.

**What to watch:** which other European countries join the programme; new orders placed through OCCAR.

**Sources:** [HENSOLDT](https://www.hensoldt.net/news/hensoldt-theon-nightvision-expands-production-capacity-in-germany-to-support-major-european-night-vision-programme), [HENSOLDT on X](https://x.com/i/status/2124888734927569215)
articles.why: a German–Greek joint venture supplying several European armies through a joint procurement framework keeps both production and know-how inside Europe. It is the kind of intra-European procurement CEAFE considers positive.

articles.headline: Update: The UK signs NATO's STARLIFT launch initiative and backs SaxaVord with $39m
articles.summary:
**The UK has signed NATO's STARLIFT initiative for a network of flexible satellite launch services and is backing it with $39m for SaxaVord Spaceport in Shetland, the UK Ministry of Defence announced.**

SaxaVord is the UK's fully licensed vertical orbital launch site. STARLIFT now has eleven nations. London says the announcement builds on the UK Space Strategy, which sets out more than £7.8bn for space. On the same day, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said it would be "unthinkable" to rejoin the EU without a new referendum.

**Context:** Antecedentes: on 17 November @F_CEAFE reported the launch of STARLIFT, with ten NATO Allies, including the UK, and the Republic of Korea committing to finance it ([X, 2026](https://x.com/i/status/2122769519185629490)). The UK is a NATO member and no longer an EU member state.

**What to watch:** whether STARLIFT links to ESA or EU launch programmes; whether it serves European launchers (Isar, RFA, Orbex, PLD) or US ones.

**Sources:** [UK Government](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/uk-reaches-for-stars-with-nato-space-launch-plan), [UK Defence in the US on X](https://x.com/i/status/2124925165196738974), [Politico Europe](https://www.politico.eu/article/rejoining-eu-without-referendum-unthinkable-andy-burnham/)
articles.why: STARLIFT gives European spaceports such as SaxaVord, Andøya and Esrange a NATO role. London is placing its launch capacity in a NATO framework rather than a European one, while Europe is short of sovereign launch capacity (Ariane 6, Vega C).

articles.headline: European space round-up: IRIDE at Kourou, Ariane 6 rescheduled, Isar Aerospace in Canada
articles.summary:
**The first batch of Italy's IRIDE Earth-observation satellites, including six synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites, has arrived at the European Spaceport in French Guiana for the final phase of preparations ahead of launch, Thales Alenia Space reports.**

**Ariane 6:** after a technical event on 23 November affecting the launcher's ground support systems, Arianespace says the necessary analyses and checks have been carried out. The VA271 launch, carrying 36 Amazon Leo satellites, is now scheduled for 24 November, in a window from 11:45 to 12:14 Madrid time. Arianespace says the launcher and satellites remain in stable and safe conditions.

**Isar Aerospace:** the German launcher company has started building a launch complex at Spaceport Nova Scotia (Maritime Launch), aiming for orbital launches from Canadian soil from 2028.

**Also:** ESA's Hera released imagery of Dimorphos casting a shadow on its parent asteroid Didymos; Leonardo has completed flight testing for AW09 certification.

{{chart: lanzamientos}}

**Context:** Antecedentes: earlier on 23 November @F_CEAFE shared Arianespace's update on the VA271 launch chronology ([X, 2026](https://x.com/i/status/2124760952730259740)).

**What to watch:** the Ariane 6 launch on 24 November; the IRIDE launch date.

**Sources:** [Thales Alenia Space on X](https://x.com/i/status/2124901144774459473), [Arianespace on X](https://x.com/i/status/2124858698530980085), [Isar Aerospace on X](https://x.com/i/status/2124840370068390190), [ESA Hera on X](https://x.com/i/status/2124869899314954686), [Leonardo Helicopters on X](https://x.com/i/status/2124866467514478636)
articles.why: IRIDE and Ariane 6 are pieces of European autonomy in Earth observation and access to space. The next Ariane 6 mission carries a US customer's constellation, and a German launcher is building capacity outside Europe.

headlines: Update: ICEYE's bid for Avio: Rome wants safeguards on solid rocket motors
EDF-funded EUROGUARD semi-autonomous vessel launched in Estonia
Thales Alenia Space wins more than €240m for the Sentinel-3NG Topography altimeters

articles.headline: Update: ICEYE's bid for Avio: Rome wants safeguards on solid rocket motors
articles.summary:
**Italy wants any takeover of Avio S.p.A. by Finland's ICEYE to keep the company partly Italian, preserve national sovereignty over solid rocket motors and keep Leonardo (18%) as a key shareholder, Reuters reports.**

**Buyer:** ICEYE (Finland), through its Italian vehicle Iris 2. **Target:** Avio S.p.A. (Colleferro, Italy), maker of the Vega C launcher and solid rocket motors, not GE Aerospace's Avio Aero. **Value:** about €2.05bn, all cash at €41 a share (a 21.3% premium), with a plan to delist from Milan and invest a further €1bn in Italy over five years (European Spaceflight; ICEYE). Defence Minister Guido Crosetto has urged caution, while Leonardo CEO Lorenzo Mariani welcomed the bid. The formal Golden Power review has not yet started.

*CEAFE:* If Europe wants to sit as an equal, it has to pool what is today fragmented.

**Context:** Antecedentes: on 17 November @F_CEAFE reposted ICEYE's announcement of the tender offer "to create a combined European sovereign space champion" ([X, 2026](https://x.com/i/status/2122611622774747212)). ICEYE presents the deal as a way to reduce Europe's reliance on providers such as SpaceX's Starshield.

**What to watch:** the Avio board's opinion; the Golden Power notification and conditions; Leonardo's stake; the French position (Vega C is operated by Arianespace for ESA).

**Sources:** [Reuters via Euronext](https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/exclusive-italy-seeks-security-safeguards-finnish-bid-rocket-maker-avio-sources-say), [European Spaceflight](https://europeanspaceflight.com/iceye-launches-e2-05b-takeover-bid-for-italian-rocket-builder-avio/), [ICEYE](https://www.iceye.com/iceye-announces-an-all-cash-public-tender-offer-in-respect-of-all-ordinary-shares-of-avio-to-create-a-european-sovereign-space-and-defense-champion)
articles.why: a European buyer, a European target and a stated aim of a sovereign group able to build, launch and exploit satellites. Rome's concern is that solid rocket motors also feed missiles. The case tests whether national Golden Power rules let European champions form while US groups scale up.

articles.headline: EDF-funded EUROGUARD semi-autonomous vessel launched in Estonia
articles.summary:
**The EUROGUARD vessel, a 45-metre semi-autonomous ship, was launched on 18 November in Nasva, Estonia, the European Commission announced on Monday.**

The project, started in 2022, brings together 29 organisations from 10 European countries and is coordinated by the Estonian shipyard Baltic Workboats. The European Defence Fund (EDF) contributes €65m of a total budget of about €95m. The ship can operate with or without a crew; its missions include maritime surveillance, mine detection and clearance, search and rescue, and the protection of undersea cables and energy infrastructure.

*CEAFE:* Europe has resources; what it lacks, time and again, is the scale that only joint action can provide.

**Context:** Estonia is an EU member state and a NATO member; the Baltic has seen repeated undersea-cable incidents.

**What to watch:** sea trials; whether EU member states order production units (EDIP/SAFE); links with NATO's Baltic Sentry.

**Sources:** [European Commission (DG DEFIS)](https://defence-industry-space.ec.europa.eu/edf-funded-euroguard-vessel-launched-estonia-2026-11-23_en)
articles.why: a joint programme financed from the EU budget for an urgent Baltic need: ten countries and one budget achieve what no small coastal state could fund alone. It is the kind of intra-European procurement CEAFE considers positive.

articles.headline: Thales Alenia Space wins more than €240m for the Sentinel-3NG Topography altimeters
articles.summary:
**Thales Alenia Space, the joint venture of Thales (67%) and Leonardo (33%), has signed a contract worth more than €240m with OHB System AG, the prime contractor, for the two altimeters on the first Copernicus Sentinel-3 Next Generation Topography satellite.**

They are a nadir SAR altimeter for continuity and a new wide-swath interferometric altimeter that will give near-complete ocean coverage in five days (Thales Alenia Space). OHB had earlier won the €554m prime contract for the satellite (OHB).

**Context:** Copernicus is the EU's Earth-observation programme, implemented with ESA.

**What to watch:** the Sentinel-3NG Optical contract; the choice of launcher.

**Sources:** [Thales Alenia Space](https://www.thalesaleniaspace.com/en/press-releases/copernicus-sentinel-3ng-topography-thales-alenia-space-forefront-europes-next), [OHB](https://www.ohb.de/en/news/ohb-awarded-eur-554-million-contract-for-new-copernicus-sentinel-3-next-generation-topography-satellite), [European Defense Industry list](https://x.com/i/status/2124783025611485658)
articles.why: an all-European value chain (German prime, Franco-Italian payload) financed by the EU and ESA. Copernicus data is dual-use (maritime awareness, Arctic ice) and keeps Europe from depending on US commercial imagery.
