articles.headline: Lukoil International changes hands: a US-led consortium with a direct US Government stake signs to buy Lukoil's foreign assets, including refineries in Bulgaria, the Netherlands and Romania
articles.summary:
**Lede.** A consortium led by Todd Boehly's Eldridge signed a definitive agreement to acquire LUKOIL International GmbH, the portfolio of Russia's Lukoil outside Russia. Its partners are the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC), which takes an equity interest and a board seat, UAE-based Catena Investment Holding and Xtellus Partners. The consortium says the aim is "to secure critical global energy assets under American and allied ownership".

**Context.** Payment is a swap of frozen Lukoil shares (restricted Lukoil and other Russian shares) worth about $10 billion at face value, held in a UAE custodial account for five years or until sanctions are lifted (Reuters). The portfolio includes three refineries — Burgas in Bulgaria (the largest in the Balkans), Zeeland in the Netherlands and Petrotel in Romania — with about 350,000 barrels a day of capacity. It also includes the LITASCO trading arm, more than 2,000 retail stations in 16 countries and upstream production of about 350,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day. Reuters values the portfolio at about $16 billion. CSIS puts the DFC's profits interest at about 15%, with no upfront cost. A DFC official told Reuters that "moving strategic energy infrastructure assets into US or allied partners' hands is a key policy priority of the administration". The deal is pending approval by the US Treasury's OFAC and other regulators; closing could take up to a year. CSIS notes that the US Government is "both bidder and decider".

**Background (CEAFE archive):** @F_CEAFE has followed the sale since Lukoil was sanctioned by OFAC on 22 October 2025: Carlyle (13 Nov. 2025) and Chevron (18 Nov. 2025) explored bids, Kazakhstan asked Washington for the local assets (28 Jan. 2026), and Reuters reported Boehly's planned securities swap on 3 November 2026.

**CEAFE comment:** Figures that illustrate, once again, why European sovereignty is only credible if it is exercised together.

**What to watch:** the OFAC review and other regulatory approvals; the positions of the Bulgarian, Dutch and Romanian governments and of the Commission; any reaction from the Kremlin or Lukoil (none found by 19:00 Madrid).

**Sources:**

- https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261125144720/en/American-Led-Consortium-Announces-Agreement-to-Acquire-LUKOIL-Internationals-Global-Energy-Portfolio (consortium statement, Business Wire, 25 Nov. 2026 — original source)

- https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/25/investors-led-by-todd-boehly-to-buy-lukoil-oil-and-gas-assets-outside-russia.html (CNBC, 25 Nov. 2026)

- https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/exclusive-boehly-signs-us-backed-share-swap-deal-buy-lukoil-global-assets (Reuters via Euronext)

- https://www.csis.org/analysis/us-governments-deal-buy-lukoils-assets-explained (CSIS)

- https://www.bgnes.com/economy/us-billionaire-signs-deal-to-acquire-lukoil-s-international-assets-including-bulgaria-s-burgas-refinery (BGNES, Bulgaria)

- https://x.com/i/status/2125649254060552435 (Clash Report on X)

- https://x.com/i/status/2117741726509199821 (@F_CEAFE repost of Reuters, 3 Nov. 2026: the Boehly securities swap in preparation)
articles.why: refineries on EU soil and fuel networks in the Balkans and Northwest Europe move from Russian to US control, with a direct stake for the US Government and the final decision taken in Washington by OFAC. No European buyer leads the deal. Europe swaps one energy dependency for another and deepens its dependence on the United States, which is also set to become its main LNG supplier (see LNG item below). The case strengthens the argument for investment screening in Bulgaria, the Netherlands and Romania and for a common policy of European energy sovereignty.

articles.headline: Tariffs — USTR proposes a 10% tariff on Brazilian aircraft; Embraer falls almost 10%
articles.summary: In a separate step on the same day, USTR proposed to modify its Section 301 action against Brazil by ending the exemption for finished aircraft and applying a 10% ad valorem tariff on Brazilian aircraft imports, including Embraer’s (USTR Federal Register notice; Aviation Week). Comments are due by 30 December 2026, with a public hearing on 14 January 2027. Embraer shares fell almost 10% in São Paulo (Bloomberg); the company said it is analysing the proposal and defends the long-standing zero-tariff regime for civil aircraft (G1).
articles.why: the zero-tariff regime for civil aircraft is also what protects Airbus’s US sales; Washington is showing it will break it as leverage on a third country.

articles.headline: Energy — Le Figaro/ECFR: the US could supply 80% of the EU’s LNG imports by 2030
articles.summary:
Le Figaro reports, citing an ECFR study, that EU import dependence stands at 96.6% for oil products and 88% for gas, and that the US, which supplied 58% of EU LNG imports in 2025, could reach up to 80% by 2030. The think-tank IEEFA had projected the same 75–80% LNG share by 2030 if contracted US volumes materialise, equivalent to about 40% of total EU gas imports (not 80% of all gas, as some posts claim). @F_CEAFE reposted a post on the Figaro piece (“traded a bear for an eagle”). Separately, Bloomberg reports restrictions on tankers entering waters near some of the UAE’s main export hubs, as the Gulf producer protects its infrastructure; Houthi drone strikes on Saudi Arabia’s Ras Tanura refinery reported by accounts @F_CEAFE reposted are not independently verified here (see the Conflicts section).

**Key facts**

- EU import dependence: 96.6% oil products, 88% gas (ECFR via Le Figaro).

- US share of EU LNG imports: 58% in 2025; up to 80% by 2030 (Le Figaro; IEEFA).
articles.why: it quantifies the CEAFE energy line: Russia replaced by a single US supplier, at prices several times those paid by US industry.

articles.headline: Macro — US Q3 growth revised up to 4.3%; AI sell-off puts Nasdaq on course for worst November since 2008
articles.summary: The BEA’s second estimate puts US real GDP growth in the third quarter at an annualised 4.3%, revised up 0.9 points from the advance estimate on stronger investment and consumer spending (Q2: 2.2%). Real final sales to private domestic purchasers rose 5.8%. Reuters and AFP report that inflation is broadening, with the Fed’s PCE gauge at a three-year high (AFP). On markets, the Nasdaq sank about 4% and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq were on track for their worst November since 2008, with chipmakers leading (Reuters).
articles.why: a US economy growing above 4% while the euro area’s largest economy grew 0.1% in Q3 (14:30 edition) widens the transatlantic growth gap that underpins investment flows out of Europe.

articles.headline: Technology sovereignty — Commission proposes the Quantum Act and a Sovereign Tech Equity Fund
articles.summary:
The Commission proposed the Quantum Act, built on three pillars (research excellence, uptake of quantum technology, secure systems and supply chains) and delivered through a “Quantum Europe Framework Initiative” aligning EU and national programmes, including preparation for post-quantum cryptography (Commission press release). The proposal also lays the groundwork for a Sovereign Tech Equity Fund (STEF); the Brussels outlet 2eu.brussels reports an indicated €50bn target, a figure not in the Commission release excerpt read here.

**CEAFE comment:** These contrasts explain why CEAFE insists that Europeans organise ourselves as a single actor, not as twenty-seven markets.
articles.why: quantum is one of the few frontier fields where Europe leads in research; the Act is an attempt to stop that lead from turning into US-owned products, as in AI and cloud.

articles.headline: Takeovers and competition — CVC lines up €11bn of debt for a possible Verisure buyout; EU fines three fragrance makers €471.9m
articles.summary: Banks are offering CVC Capital Partners up to €11bn in debt financing for a possible take-private of the home-security group Verisure; no bid has been made and Hellman & Friedman (US), which owns about 44%, is expected to stay invested (Bloomberg via swissinfo). The Commission fined Givaudan (€252.4m), Firmenich (€137.7m) and IFF (€81.9m) a total of €471.9m for exchanging sensitive commercial information from 2019 to 2023 (Commission; Reuters via Investing.com). BP is transferring 3,000 finance staff to India’s Wipro (Reuters).

articles.headline: German gas overcost: the German-Russian Chamber of Commerce puts the extra bill since 2022 at €134 billion
articles.summary:
A calculation by the German-Russian Chamber of Foreign Trade (AHK), published on 16 November 2026, estimates that Germany paid some €134 billion extra for gas between January 2022 and September 2026, against the 2015–2020 average import price (€16.50/MWh): about €1,600 per inhabitant. The costliest year was 2022, at some €59 billion. In 2023–2025 the annual extra cost ran between €17.5 billion and €21.6 billion; in the first nine months of 2026 the chamber already counts some €17 billion. After inflation, it leaves the total at around €120 billion.

The method multiplies consumption (Federal Network Agency data) by the gap in Destatis import prices. That price covers pipeline gas only, not LNG, so the chamber itself presents it as an approximation. It also warns that the rise cannot be attributed solely to the loss of Russian gas (transit through Nord Stream 1 was already zero in early September 2022, before the 26 September explosions).

In a model scenario, restarting Nord Stream 2’s still-intact string B — 27.5 billion cubic metres a year — would cut the European gas price by around 16% and save Germany some €9.5 billion a year, starting from the 2027 forward price of €71/MWh (BDEW, 11 November). Under other assumptions the chamber’s range is €6.5–12.4 billion, falling to €4.9 billion if prices normalise to the 2025 wholesale average. These are scenarios, not a guaranteed saving. On 19 October 2026 the German government told the Bundestag that “the question of commissioning Nord Stream 2 therefore does not arise”; the European Commission rejected a restart on 28 October, including for the period after a cessation of hostilities.

**Antecedentes (CEAFE archive):** the CEAFE X archive holds 311 posts on Nord Stream since October 2019, peaking in 2021 (72) and around the September 2022 explosions; see also the CEAFE Nord Stream dossier.

**Key facts:**

- €134 billion extra cost, Jan. 2022–Sep. 2026 (AHK; ~€1,600 per inhabitant); ~€120 billion after inflation.

- 2022: ~€59 billion; 2023–2025: €17.5–21.6 billion a year; Jan.–Sep. 2026: ~€17 billion.

- One intact string: ~16% fall in the European price and ~€9.5 billion a year for Germany (range €6.5–12.4 billion; €4.9 billion if prices return to the 2025 average).

**Sources:**

- https://www.kammer-russland.ru/de/analyse/nord-stream-k-nnte-j-hrlich-9-5-mrd-euro-sparen-aber-kein-neustart-in-sicht/ (AHK Russland, Fokusanalyse, 16 Nov. 2026 — original source)

- https://www.berliner-zeitung.de/article/nord-stream-2-oeffnen-deutschland-wuerde-laut-studie-jaehrlich-95-milliarden-euro-beim-gas-sparen-10631680 (Berliner Zeitung, Jonas Prien, 24 Nov. 2026 — report of the calculation)

- https://x.com/berlinerzeitung/status/2125305001564119341 (original post on X)

- https://x.com/F_CEAFE/status/2125503851562496406 (@F_CEAFE repost, 25 Nov. 2026, 09:16 Madrid)

- https://dserver.bundestag.de/btd/21/087/2108720.pdf (German government reply to the Bundestag, published 19 Oct. 2026)
articles.why: Germany is the EU’s largest gas market; an extra bill of this size, even as a chamber calculation rather than an official aggregate, sits alongside the fossil-fuel overcost already estimated for the Union as a whole and the shift of imports towards LNG, much of it American. This item does not prescribe a course of action on the pipeline.

articles.headline: Update (extraterritorial sanctions) — China answers the Huawei verdict: Beijing “firmly opposes” US suppression of Chinese companies
articles.summary:
Asked about the Brooklyn jury verdict at Wednesday’s regular briefing in Beijing, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said: “The Chinese government firmly opposes the US suppression and containment of Chinese companies and firmly supports Chinese companies in safeguarding their legitimate rights and interests” (Reuters via Investing.com; AFP; ANSA; The Straits Times). The ministry announced no countermeasure. Huawei, in a statement posted on X, said the remaining charges are “without legal or factual merit” and that it will “take all necessary legal actions”; it argues that the five trade-secret disputes cited by prosecutors were civil matters settled over the past two decades and that no court had previously found it liable for wilful misappropriation (Reuters). The jury convicted Huawei on 10 of 12 counts on 24 November (bank fraud, wire fraud, sanctions violations, conspiracy to steal trade secrets); sentencing is set for 14 September 2027 (topic 1 of the 08:30 edition). The Chinese MFA’s English transcript for 25 November was not yet online at 13:05.

**Antecedentes (CEAFE archive):** @F_CEAFE has tracked US pressure on European governments over Huawei since at least January 2020, when it reported that key Republicans sought a ban on intelligence sharing with countries using Huawei ([X, Jan. 2020](https://x.com/i/status/1221932500928339968)); in February 2020 it reposted that Britain had admitted the "high risk" vendor, a decision London later reversed under US pressure.

**Key facts**

- MFA spokesperson Guo Jiakun, 25 November: China “firmly opposes the US suppression and containment of Chinese companies”.

- Huawei: will “thoroughly review the relevant verdicts” and appeal; its lawyer Brian Heberlig said the acquittal on racketeering vindicates its “good-faith compliance culture”.

- @F_CEAFE reposted the Justice Department’s posts (with images of a T-Mobile “Tappy” robot arm and a CNEX solid-state drive board presented as stolen technology) and Huawei’s statement.
articles.why: this is the action–reaction pair in full: a US court applies US sanctions law to a Chinese company’s business with Iran because the money went through US-dollar clearing, and Beijing answers with a verbal protest, for now without retaliation. Europe has neither half of the pair: it does not project its own law in this way, and when its companies are hit by US secondary sanctions it does not answer either.

articles.headline: Update (tariffs / economic coercion) — China rejects the reported US Section 301 “overcapacity” tariffs before they are published
articles.summary:
Asked about reports that the United States is about to announce tariffs on goods from China and other countries, Guo Jiakun said on Wednesday that “tariff wars and trade wars serve no one’s interests”, that “the so-called issue of overcapacity is a false proposition” and that China “opposes using it as a pretext for political manipulation”. He called on both sides to “deliver on the important common understandings between the two heads of state” and keep China–US trade growing steadily (Xinhua, Chinese state media; Global Times, Chinese state media; Asia Financial). The reports say the levies would also hit the EU, Japan and South Korea (Asia Financial). At the 08:30 edition USTR’s latest press release was dated 19 November; this run did not re-check USTR.

**Key facts**

- MFA, 25 November: “overcapacity” is “a false proposition” and “a pretext for political manipulation”.

- The reported US tariffs would cover China, the EU, Japan, South Korea and others (Asia Financial; topic 2 of the 08:30 edition).
articles.why: China is answering in advance, on the record, a measure that will also hit the EU. Brussels has said nothing comparable in public about tariffs that, by the reports, would hit European exporters just as directly.

articles.headline: Update (trade defence) — EU hybrid-car safeguard: provisional quotas from 1 December, China gets the largest share
articles.summary:
The European Commission on Tuesday 24 November issued provisional safeguard measures setting import quotas for certain hybrid vehicles from 1 December, for up to 200 days, saying they are meant to “protect EU industry against a sharp recent increase in imports of such vehicles” (Commission press release as quoted by Global Times, Chinese state media). Per Global Times the 200-day quotas are: China 192,000 units (350,000 annualised), Japan 171,000, Turkey 126,000, UK 105,000, South Korea 68,000, Mexico 34,000, Morocco 24,000, Serbia 19,000, US 18,000; all other countries 822 units. A Chinese chamber of commerce official says the EU first wanted to use the 2022–24 import average, which would have given China only about 70,000 units a year, and that China secured more than its 2025 exports to the EU (302,000 units). MOFCOM urged the EU to honour the bilateral consensus and WTO rules and “reserves all rights”, including WTO dispute settlement and compensation. Global Times reports that Japan, the UK, South Korea and Turkey complained at the WTO about the EU’s “separate pre-initiation consultations” with one partner.

**Key facts**

- Provisional quotas from 1 December 2026, up to 200 days; nine named partners.

- China: 192,000 units in 200 days (350,000 a year), above its 302,000 units exported to the EU in 2025.

- US quota: 18,000 units.
articles.why: the EU protects its car industry with a quota that applies to everyone, but the partner that negotiated hardest, China, came out with the largest share, while allies such as Japan and South Korea feel penalised. The quotas are also a measure of how far Europe’s carmakers have already lost ground in hybrids.

articles.headline: Energy — UK energy price cap jumps 26% from January as Europe outbids Asia for LNG
articles.summary:
Ofgem announced on 25 November that the household energy price cap will rise 26% for 1 January–31 March 2027: a typical direct-debit household goes from £1,723 to £2,166 a year. Gas unit rates rise from 7.97p to 10.96p per kWh and electricity from 26.32p to 32.69p. Ofgem blames “the continued conflict in the Middle East”; it says wholesale gas prices have “roughly tripled” since the conflict began, compounded by “historically low European gas storage” entering winter. The wholesale allowance rises 50% and now makes up 56% of the cap (47% last quarter). Adjusted for inflation the new cap is 31.8% higher than in the same period of 2026. Separately, Bloomberg reports that Europe’s high prices are drawing LNG tankers away from Asia across the Atlantic. @F_CEAFE reposted Reuters’ Ofgem story and a Berliner Zeitung post on a study saying Germany has paid €134 billion more for gas since 2022.

**Key facts**

- UK cap: £2,166 a year from 1 January 2027 (+26%); gas bills +33%, electricity +19% vs the October cap.

- Wholesale allowance +50%, 56% of the cap.

- Germany: €134 billion more paid for gas since 2022 (study cited by Berliner Zeitung, reposted by @F_CEAFE; study not verified this run).
articles.why: households and industry are paying for a gas market in which Europe, having cut Russian pipeline supply, competes with Asia for seaborne LNG, much of it American. Higher energy costs feed directly into the competitiveness gap with the US and into deindustrialisation.

articles.headline: Export controls — Asia’s data centres try to sell China-bound Nvidia capacity to US and Western European buyers
articles.summary:
Data-centre operators across Asia are trying to resell to US buyers computing capacity originally committed to Chinese customers, after the US required licences for advanced chip shipments to Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand and announced a global clampdown, from February 2027, on remote access by Chinese firms (Bloomberg via The Edge Malaysia and Bloomberg Law). Liquid Compute, a New York start-up that tracks over 200 “neoclouds”, says the cost of Nvidia B300 GPUs fell 7%, from $7.72 to $7.19 per GPU-hour between the end of October and 24 November; its CEO says many neoclouds want to remarket capacity “into the US and Western Europe”. Banks including Citigroup, Standard Chartered, DBS, OCBC and UOB are reviewing data-centre clients for compliance (Bloomberg via NDTV Profit). Singapore’s Prime Minister Lawrence Wong: “We do not enforce America’s export controls, but we do not want Singapore to be used and abused as a conduit.”

**Key facts**

- B300 rental price: $7.72 → $7.19 per GPU-hour (−7%), end-October to 24 November 2026 (Liquid Compute index).

- Licence requirement for advanced US chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand; remote-access clampdown from February 2027.
articles.why: the remote-access rule (lead story of the 17 November 13:30 edition) is already reshaping the market: capacity built for Chinese clients is flowing to the US and Western Europe, and third countries such as Singapore align with US enforcement. European data centres are covered by the same rule.

articles.headline: Macro — German growth revised down to 0.1% in the third quarter as machinery investment and exports fall
articles.summary:
Destatis revised Germany’s third-quarter 2026 GDP growth from 0.2% to 0.1% on the previous quarter (price, seasonally and calendar adjusted), citing weaker September exports and retail sales. Gross fixed capital formation fell 1.2%, and investment in machinery and equipment fell 3.5%, deepening a decline seen in the first half of the year. Total exports fell 1.0% (goods −0.8%, services −1.7%), with lower exports of motor vehicles, chemicals and metals. Year on year GDP grew 1.2% (price adjusted).

**Key facts**

- Q3 2026: +0.1% q/q (first estimate +0.2%); +1.2% y/y.

- Machinery and equipment investment −3.5% q/q; exports −1.0% q/q.
articles.why: Europe’s largest economy is barely growing, and the weakness is in industrial investment and exports, the sectors most exposed to energy prices and US tariffs.

articles.headline: US jury convicts Huawei of defrauding banks over its Iran business and stealing trade secrets
articles.summary:
A federal jury in Brooklyn (New York) found Huawei guilty on Tuesday 24 November of 10 of the 12 counts it faced, including bank fraud, wire fraud, sanctions violations, conspiracy to defraud the United States and conspiracy to steal trade secrets; it acquitted the company of racketeering conspiracy and conspiracy to obstruct justice (Reuters via Investing.com; France 24/AFP; CNN). According to the Department of Justice, Huawei “lied about its activities in Iran to banks to obtain billions of US dollars and access to US-dollar clearing services”; the trade-secret counts concern source code and manuals for routers, antenna technology and robot-testing technology taken from US firms. The case began in 2018; Huawei was put on the US Entity List in 2019. Sentencing by Judge Ann Donnelly is set for 14 September 2027; penalties are not yet known. US Attorney General Todd Blanche: “No person or company is above the law.” Huawei said the acquittal on racketeering “vindicates our consistent position over the past eight years”, called the remaining charges “without legal or factual merit” and said it will take “all necessary legal actions”; its lawyer said it expects to appeal. **China’s response:** the Chinese embassy in Washington did not immediately comment, and there was no Foreign Ministry statement yet at the time of writing; in September the MFA said China “firmly opposes the US side’s suppression and containment of Chinese enterprises”. @F_CEAFE has not posted this story.

**Key facts:**

- Court: US District Court for the Eastern District of New York; trial of more than two months, more than 60 prosecution witnesses and 15 for the defence.

- Verdict: guilty on 10 of 12 counts; acquitted of racketeering (RICO) conspiracy and obstruction conspiracy.

- Sentencing: 14 September 2027 (CNN/Reuters).

- Reaction: Huawei statement rejecting the remaining charges; no Chinese government statement yet — watch today’s MFA press conference and MOFCOM.

In the CEAFE archive: @F_CEAFE has followed the US case against Huawei since 2020, when Canada was holding Huawei CFO Meng Wanzhou for extradition to the United States (https://x.com/i/status/1315698697695526916, https://x.com/i/status/1392768106028732416).

**Sources:**

- https://x.com/i/status/2125328627210305866 (New York Times)

- https://x.com/i/status/2125374482294722914 (France 24)

- https://x.com/i/status/2125406950343016657 (CNN)

- https://x.com/i/status/2125408010193215799 (Japan Times)

- https://x.com/i/status/2125422701523169287 (Al Jazeera English, Huawei statement)

- https://x.com/i/status/2125348584875053277 (Huawei, statement on the verdict)

- https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20261124-new-york-jury-convicts-huawei-of-stealing-trade-secrets

- https://edition.cnn.com/2026/11/24/china/china-huawei-iran-conviction-intl-hnk

- https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/chinas-huawei-convicted-at-us-criminal-trial-stemming-from-iran-business-5048943 (Reuters reprint)

- https://apnews.com/article/huawei-racketeering-trial-verdict-b39ac780e2e31140015a1be02f0329ab (AP; blocked to direct fetch, facts from search extract)

**What to watch:** Chinese MFA/MOFCOM reaction; any penalty estimate; Huawei appeal; effect on the US–China trade truce.
articles.why: the verdict confirms how far Washington’s reach goes: a Chinese company is convicted in a US court for doing business with a third country (Iran) because that business passed through US-dollar clearing. Any European company or bank using the dollar is exposed to the same logic, which is why European firms comply with US sanctions on Iran even when the EU disagrees with them. The EU has a Blocking Statute but has never made it bite; it has no comparable tool to project its own law. On Huawei specifically, many European governments have already removed it from 5G networks at US urging, without asking for anything in return.

articles.headline: Update: US Section 301 “overcapacity” tariffs on China, the EU and 14 others still not published
articles.summary:
The announcement expected on Tuesday night did not come. At 07:05 Madrid, USTR’s press-release page showed nothing newer than 19 November. Overnight, AP and Reuters again reported, citing people familiar with the matter, that the administration is “set to unveil” new tariffs after its probe into excess factory capacity, covering China, the European Union and 14 other economies. Markets reacted to the prospect: US stocks fell on Tuesday, led by chipmakers, as “new US plans for tariffs reignited trade concerns” (Bloomberg), and gold held its decline as the tariff plans reinforced expectations of a further Fed rate rise (Bloomberg). Separately, Bloomberg reports that cheaper Asian steel imports are gaining ground with US buyers despite Section 232 tariffs, because the data-centre construction boom is squeezing domestic supply.

**Key facts:**

- Status at 07:05 Madrid: no USTR determination, rate or product list published.

- 16 economies under investigation since 11 March 2026 (see 20:30 edition, topic 1).

- **Reaction:** no EU or Chinese statement yet.

**Sources:**

- https://x.com/i/status/2125394431343837377 (AP)

- https://x.com/i/status/2125387773955768594 (Reuters)

- https://x.com/i/status/2125347419395125561 (Bloomberg)

- https://x.com/i/status/2125313554190320094 (Bloomberg, US stocks)

- https://x.com/i/status/2125407910758891766 (Bloomberg, gold)

- https://x.com/i/status/2125390299186753974 (Bloomberg, US steel imports)

- https://ustr.gov/about-us/policy-offices/press-office/press-releases (checked 07:05, no new release)

**What to watch:** USTR publication; Commission and MOFCOM responses.
articles.why: the EU still does not know the rate it will pay under the new legal basis, a year after accepting a 15% ceiling in its 2025 deal. Uncertainty itself is a cost for European exporters; a common EU answer must be ready before the list is published, not after.

articles.headline: North Korea expels Switzerland’s envoy over Swiss sanctions on a camp linked to deported Ukrainian children
articles.summary:
North Korea’s Foreign Ministry declared Sylvain Astier, head of Switzerland’s newly reopened diplomatic office in Pyongyang, persona non grata, gave him 48 hours to leave and demanded the office’s closure (KCNA, North Korean state media). The stated reason is Switzerland’s decision to put the Songdowon International Children’s Camp (Wonsan) on its sanctions list; Bern says the camp is part of programmes bringing Ukrainian children from Russian-occupied territory to North Korea for pro-Russian indoctrination. The UK sanctioned the camp in May 2026 and the EU in September 2026; Switzerland, which adopts EU Russia sanctions, followed. The office had reopened on 19 October during Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis’s visit (Euronews). Kim Yo Jong had threatened the move on 24 November (noted in the 08:30 edition of 24 Nov). Separately, Bloomberg reports that Russian assets frozen by Switzerland under the EU-aligned sanctions have risen to $10.2 billion.

**Key facts:**

- Retaliation: envoy expelled (48 hours) and office closure demanded, 25 November (KCNA).

- Sanctioned entity: Songdowon International Children’s Camp — UK (May 2026), EU (September 2026), Switzerland (November 2026).

- Swiss freeze of Russian assets: $10.2 billion (Bloomberg; date of the figure as reported on 24 November).

**Sources:**

- https://x.com/i/status/2125462025090293790 (Bloomberg)

- https://x.com/i/status/2125314804009091480 (Bloomberg, Swiss frozen Russian assets)

- http://www.kcna.kp/en/article/detail/66b6fd73f166f5a43a756e54cee318d6 (KCNA, North Korean state media)

- https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/25/north-korea-expels-swiss-diplomat-and-orders-berns-new-pyongyang-office-to-close

- https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/north-korea-expels-swiss-representative-over-sanctions-related-to-childrens-camp (Reuters reprint)

- https://www.nknews.org/2026/11/north-korea-expels-swiss-diplomat-over-sanctions-on-childrens-camp/

**What to watch:** Swiss response; whether the EU or UK missions are targeted.
articles.why: a non-EU European state that aligns with EU sanctions pays a diplomatic price on its own, losing one of the few Western channels to Pyongyang. It shows both the reach of EU sanctions when partners align and the limited weight of any single European state when the target retaliates.

articles.headline: EU will not return to Russian energy whatever the US–Russia talks produce, says Energy Commissioner Jørgensen
articles.summary:
EU Energy Commissioner Dan Jørgensen told Euronews (24 November) that the EU will “never again” import Russian energy, regardless of the outcome of US-led peace talks: “We will never again, if it’s up to me, import as much as one molecule from Russia.” He stressed that the EU has adopted legislation permanently phasing out Russian gas — “stronger than sanctions because sanctions have to be renewed every six months” — and that no Washington–Moscow deal can override EU law. Euronews notes that the US administration eased restrictions on Russian diesel last month and has indicated it could support Russia’s return as an energy player, including to Europe, after a peace deal. The EU has cut Russian gas from 45% to about 10% of its imports and expects to end them next year. Jørgensen warned of a difficult winter at the pump; average European gas prices rose 163% year on year in October. He rejected an EU-wide windfall tax requested by Austria, Germany, Italy, Poland, Portugal and Spain, preferring national decisions and lower electricity taxes (about 29% of the average household bill).

**Key facts:**

- Russian share of EU gas imports: from 45% (before the full-scale invasion of February 2022) to about 10% (2026); full end expected in 2027.

- Six member states, including Spain, asked for an EU windfall levy; the Commission declined.

**Sources:**

- https://x.com/i/status/2125354392903934199 (Euronews)

- https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/24/eu-rules-out-russian-energy-return-regardless-of-us-russia-peace-talks-jorgensen-tells-eur

**What to watch:** US position on Russian energy in the peace framework; winter gas prices.
articles.why: the peace table is being set in Washington and Moscow, but the EU’s energy rules are made in Brussels — the one area where the bloc has turned a sanctions policy into permanent law. The cost is real (prices up 163% year on year in October), and European dependence has partly shifted to US LNG.

articles.headline: US–China managed trade: first agricultural working group under the “Board of Trade”, and China’s biggest Boeing order since 2017
articles.summary:
China and the United States held the first meeting of the agricultural working group under the China–US Board of Trade in Beijing on 23–24 November, with “candid, in-depth, constructive” exchanges on farm-product regulation, market access and trade, MOFCOM said on 25 November. On the same evening, Xiamen Airlines (55% owned by China Southern) signed a contract for 50 Boeing 737-8 aircraft, list price about US$7.4 billion, with deliveries in 2031–2034; the actual price is lower because of Boeing discounts, and the deal still needs Chinese state approval (Hong Kong exchange filing). Aviation Week calls it the largest Boeing order from China since 2017. Global Times (Chinese state media) linked it to Boeing’s efforts to rebuild its China business.

**Key facts:**

- Board of Trade first met by video on 13 November (MOFCOM, 19 November).

- Boeing order: 50 × 737-8; catalogue US$7.4 bn (about RMB 49.7 bn); state approval and shareholder approval pending.

**Sources:**

- https://x.com/i/status/2125467175398080960 (Global Times, Chinese state media — agricultural group)

- https://x.com/i/status/2125466741103006193 (Global Times, Chinese state media — Boeing)

- https://www.mofcom.gov.cn/xwfb/rcxwfb/art/2026/art_6e6ac6c48c544802b6f2b68e4ef07522.html (MOFCOM, Chinese)

- https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/1124/2026112401223.pdf (China Southern filing)

- https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/25/china-xiamen-boeing-deal.html

- https://aviationweek.com/air-transport/airlines-lessors/chinas-xiamen-airlines-signs-50-boeing-737-maxs

**What to watch:** further Board of Trade working groups; Airbus orders from China.
articles.why: while Washington prepares to tariff the EU as an “overcapacity” economy, it is negotiating sector-by-sector purchases with Beijing — farm goods and aircraft, the latter in direct competition with Airbus, whose China market share is a European industrial asset. A US–China managed-trade arrangement can be made at Europe’s expense.

articles.headline: Iraq moves to take control of Kurdish oilfields and rejects OPEC+ capacity assessment before the weekend meeting
articles.summary:
Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered the oil ministry to manage all fields it owns that are currently under the Kurdistan Regional Government, and federal forces to take control of oilfields and border crossings in Kurdish-controlled areas, citing alleged oil smuggling (Bloomberg; Al Jazeera). Iraq has also rejected an assessment of its production capacity commissioned by OPEC+, setting up a potential clash at this weekend’s meeting on output targets (Bloomberg). Oil prices fell more than 1% on Wednesday morning as the prospect of a supply glut outweighed fears of Middle East disruption (Reuters). ExxonMobil said Guyana output will top 1 million barrels per day within weeks (posted by @F_CEAFE).

**Sources:**

- https://x.com/i/status/2125469586845741509 (Bloomberg)

- https://x.com/i/status/2125334052597276865 (Al Jazeera English)

- https://x.com/i/status/2125323613167390844 (Bloomberg, OPEC+ assessment)

- https://x.com/i/status/2125469639178076556 (Reuters, oil prices)

- https://x.com/i/status/2125292076346511782 (@F_CEAFE, Exxon Guyana)

**What to watch:** OPEC+ meeting at the weekend.
articles.why: Europe imports almost all its oil; OPEC+ quarrels and new non-OPEC supply (Guyana, US) drive the prices Europeans pay this winter, already pressured by gas.

articles.headline: WHO chief calls on the US to lift its fuel blockade on Cuba
articles.summary:
WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, visiting Havana, urged the US to lift its fuel blockade on Cuba, saying “the intensification of fuel restrictions and sanctions is causing direct harm to the Cuban people, especially the most vulnerable”; the UN allocated US$2 million for immunisation and medical equipment (Al Jazeera; Reuters). OFAC issued new Cuba FAQs on 23 November (OFAC recent actions).

**Sources:**

- https://x.com/i/status/2125452067422499248 (Al Jazeera English)

- https://x.com/i/status/2125451950745440315 (Reuters)

- https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/25/who-chief-urges-end-to-us-fuel-blockade-on-cuba

- https://ofac.treasury.gov/recent-actions
articles.why: US secondary pressure on third countries’ shipping and trade with Cuba also hits European firms (notably Spanish ones present on the island), and the EU has never effectively used its Blocking Statute to protect them.

headlines: Update: US chip controls reach Southeast Asia — Alibaba calls the blacklisting of its Singapore unit “erroneous”, Singapore pledges to work with Washington
China’s BYD in exclusive talks to buy INEOS’s French car plant as INEOS moves production to the US
Japan pays its 2027 ICC contribution early to shield the court from US sanctions
The Commission’s Autumn Package flags the EU’s growing financial exposure to the United States
Briefly noted

articles.headline: Update: US chip controls reach Southeast Asia — Alibaba calls the blacklisting of its Singapore unit “erroneous”, Singapore pledges to work with Washington
articles.summary:
The US Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security added seven Southeast Asian entities to its Entity List on Monday, among them Alibaba’s Singapore subsidiary Apex Enterprise Solutions and Megaspeed International, a cloud company under US investigation for suspected circumvention of chip export controls, citing a “significant risk” of diverting advanced computing products; the other listed firms are in Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand (Global Times, Chinese state media, citing Reuters and Bloomberg). Alibaba responded: “Adding Apex Enterprise Solutions to the Entity List is erroneous because Apex has never diverted advanced computing chips subject to US export restrictions… We will seek all legal avenues to protect our rights and reputation” (statement to The Straits Times; Reuters). According to a person cited by Reuters, Apex paid around $4.2 billion to Megaspeed and other firms as prepayment to rent computing capacity in Southeast Asia and took some of their assets as a pledge. Singapore’s Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said his country is “working with the US” to stop companies “exploiting” it to transship and divert chips, and is running its own investigation (SCMP, owned by Alibaba).

The listing requires a licence for all items subject to US export rules, with a presumption of denial; the rule is due for publication on 25 November. The Global Times frames it as Washington “increasingly” extending chip controls to overseas subsidiaries, while Mike Kuiken, vice-chair of the US–China Economic and Security Review Commission, told Bloomberg that China is doing “everything they can to smuggle” or “steal” advanced US chips. At its 24 November briefing, China’s foreign ministry had nothing further to add on Megaspeed (14:30 edition). Chinese state media are already asking whether the Netherlands “may face a choice” as its foreign minister visits China (Global Times opinion).

**What to watch:** Alibaba’s legal challenge; a formal reaction from China’s Ministry of Commerce; any Dutch or EU statement during Foreign Minister Berendsen’s China visit.

**Sources:** The Straits Times: https://www.straitstimes.com/business/alibaba-disputes-us-blacklisting-of-singapore-subsidiary-over-chip-rerouting-risks, Global Times: https://www.globaltimes.cn/page/202611/1374969.shtml, Global Times on X: https://x.com/i/status/2125218181925265745, Global Times on the Netherlands: https://x.com/i/status/2125243500648358021, SCMP: https://www.scmp.com/news/asia/southeast-asia/article/3375560/pm-wong-vows-stop-firms-exploiting-singapore-ai-chip-re-routing, Bloomberg (Kuiken): https://x.com/i/status/2125213475852943629, Reuters on Megaspeed: https://x.com/i/status/2125285870169206963, Reuters (Investing.com reprint): https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/us-to-blacklist-megaspeed-chip-firm-linked-to-nvidia-scandal-source-says-5046337
articles.why: US export controls now reach a Chinese group’s subsidiary in a third country for renting computing capacity there, and third states such as Singapore help enforce them. The same extraterritorial logic applies to European firms and data centres — ASML is the prime example — and Europe has no reciprocal tool and no plan to answer it.

articles.headline: China’s BYD in exclusive talks to buy INEOS’s French car plant as INEOS moves production to the US
articles.summary:
BYD, China’s largest carmaker, said on 24 November that it has entered exclusive negotiations to buy the Hambach plant in Moselle, France, from INEOS Automotive, subject to consultation with works councils; the amount was not disclosed. According to Reuters, it would be the first purchase of a European car plant by a Chinese automaker: rivals have preferred to rent space (Dongfeng and Leapmotor at Stellantis plants in France and Spain; Geely at a Ford plant in Spain). French President Emmanuel Macron welcomed the project as “a direct consequence” of his economic policy.

On the same day INEOS Automotive (UK, owned by Jim Ratcliffe) announced that it will begin producing its Grenadier and Quartermaster in the United States in 2028, as the US accounts for 70% of Grenadier sales, with a final site decision “within the next few months”; Bloomberg says the shift aims to avoid US tariffs. Production would continue at Hambach in the medium term. Hambach is the former Smart/Mercedes-Benz site bought by INEOS in 2020. BYD wants European production ahead of the EU’s planned “Made in Europe” local-content rules and will start mass production in Hungary in early 2027; an EU cap on imports of Chinese hybrid vehicles applies from 1 December 2026 (France 3 Grand Est).

**What to watch:** works-council consultation at Hambach; INEOS’s choice of US site; the final shape of the EU’s “Made in Europe” rules.

**Sources:** Bloomberg: https://x.com/i/status/2125269510684840091, Emmanuel Macron: https://x.com/i/status/2125256912199422358, INEOS: https://www.ineos.com/news/american-made-ineos-will-produce-the-grenadier-4x4-in-the-usa-to-drive-the-brands-worldwide-growth/, Reuters (Investing.com reprint): https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/chinas-byd-in-talks-to-buy-french-car-factory-from-ineos-automotive-5048383, France 3 Grand Est: https://france3-regions.franceinfo.fr/grand-est/moselle/metz/le-constructeur-chinois-byd-annonce-etre-entre-en-negociations-exclusives-pour-l-acquisition-de-l-usine-ineos-automotive-d-hambach-en-moselle-3455360.html
articles.why: one story shows both sides of the pressure on European industry. US tariffs push a European-based producer to move production to the US, with jobs and supply chain following, while Chinese capital fills the gap to secure access to the EU market under the coming local-content rules. Europe keeps the plant, but depends on others’ decisions: the owner relocates to the US, and the buyer is Chinese.

articles.headline: Japan pays its 2027 ICC contribution early to shield the court from US sanctions
articles.summary:
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi told International Criminal Court President Tomoko Akane on 24 November that Japan will pay its full 2027 contribution to the court by the end of 2026, after the ICC sought early payment from its largest contributor (CNA, Reuters). Japan supplies about 15% of the ICC budget, followed by Germany, France, the UK, Italy, South Korea and Canada; the early payment gives the court funds before US sanctions take full effect in April 2027 (CNA).

In the CEAFE archive: in December 2025 the ICC rejected new US sanctions designations against two of its judges, and in August 2026, when Takaichi called US sanctions on the Japanese ICC chief “very unfortunate”, @F_CEAFE commented that Japan was doing the same as the Europeans — “just words”. Tuesday’s payment is the first concrete step.

**What to watch:** whether Germany, France, Italy or the EU follow with early payments or use of the Blocking Statute before April 2027.

**Sources:** Reuters: https://x.com/i/status/2125263217551143077, CNA: https://www.channelnewsasia.com/east-asia/japan-accelerates-icc-funding-us-sanctions-threaten-court-6577621, AP: https://apnews.com/article/japan-icc-takaichi-akane-sanctions-bbb7371ca6eb08710b5c2d50ee1cbb2c, ICC (Dec 2025): https://www.icc-cpi.int/news/icc-strongly-rejects-new-us-sanctions-designations-against-two-icc-judges
articles.why: a close US ally acts to blunt US sanctions on an international court, while no similar step was reported in this window from the EU member states that follow Japan in the ranking (Germany, France, Italy). The EU has its own instrument against extraterritorial sanctions, the Blocking Statute; the question is whether Europeans will defend the court as a bloc.

articles.headline: The Commission’s Autumn Package flags the EU’s growing financial exposure to the United States
articles.summary:
The European Commission adopted the 2027 European Semester Autumn Package on 24 November in Strasbourg. Its new European Macroeconomic Report highlights “the EU’s growing financial exposure to the United States, underlining the need for deeper integration of European capital markets”, and says the EU is narrowing the gap with the US in AI adoption.

The euro-area recommendation calls for deepening the Single Market, advancing the Savings and Investments Union and making room for higher investment in defence, energy and innovation; the Commission projects a marked rise in the aggregate government deficit in 2026 and a rising debt-to-GDP ratio.

**What to watch:** progress on the Savings and Investments Union and how EU member states make room for defence investment under the fiscal rules.

**Sources:** European Commission: https://reforms-investments.ec.europa.eu/publications-0/2027-european-semester-autumn-package_en, European Commission (euro-area recommendation): https://economy-finance.ec.europa.eu/economic-surveillance-eu-member-states/euro-area-recommendation_en, EU Science & Innovation: https://x.com/i/status/2125256903592673558, IEU Monitoring (Commission press release): https://ieu-monitoring.com/editorial/semester-autumn-package-eu-commission-flags-fiscal-risks-in-13-member-states/1255451
articles.why: European savings that finance the US economy instead of European firms are another form of dependence; the Commission itself now names it.

Briefly noted

articles.headline: Update: Beijing declines to add to its Megaspeed position; Singapore keeps investigating
articles.summary:
At the Chinese MFA’s 24 November briefing, asked by AFP about the US blacklisting of Singapore-based Megaspeed International (topic 1 of the 08:30 edition), spokesperson Guo Jiakun said: “We have made clear China’s position on the relevant issue more than once. I have nothing further to add.” On Jensen Huang’s reinstatement at Nvidia: “We have no comment on this.” Singapore’s Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said Singapore will keep investigating Megaspeed (Reuters). The Global Times (Chinese state media) argues in a “GT Voice” editorial that Huang’s return “is unlikely to silence his opponents” as Washington has tightened chip restrictions over the past two weeks; Bloomberg reports Beijing warning that the comeback does not end the risk of further US chip controls.

**Sources:** MFA transcript, 24 Nov 2026: https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/eng/xw/fyrbt/lxjzh/202611/t20261124_12066262.html, Reuters on X: https://x.com/i/status/2125163766589640900 , https://x.com/i/status/2125157509648220437 ; Reuters Business https://x.com/i/status/2125171316105863437, Global Times (Chinese state media) on X: https://x.com/i/status/2125197756503568657 , https://x.com/i/status/2125133157783756953 ; Bloomberg on X: https://x.com/i/status/2125170090597384404, *Images:** https://pbs.twimg.com/media/HX3Stx9a0AEmXHv.jpg ; https://pbs.twimg.com/amplify_video_thumb/2125156013666156544/img/XJfFHoMYU2b8uIF9.jpg
articles.why: Beijing’s low-key answer contrasts with the speed with which Malaysia and Singapore aligned with Washington’s listing: the extraterritorial measure is being enforced by third states while the target keeps its powder dry for the trade talks.

articles.headline: China warns Mexico over tariffs on Chinese goods and “third-party interference”
articles.summary:
China’s Commerce Minister Wang Wentao urged Mexico to take seriously China’s “grave concerns” over tariffs on Chinese goods, to use trade remedies prudently, to address problems faced by Chinese investors and to safeguard bilateral trade “from third-party interference” — a reference to US pressure on Mexico (Global Times; SCMP). Mexico’s Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard said Mexico was open to an institutionalised tariff dialogue with China (Global Times).

**Sources:** Global Times (Chinese state media): https://www.globaltimes.cn/page/202611/1374945.shtml ; X https://x.com/i/status/2125141404716519819 ; SCMP: https://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3366663/china-warns-against-third-party-interference-after-reports-us-pressure-mexico

**Images:** https://pbs.twimg.com/media/HX4E0vCboAADlc1.jpg
articles.why: Mexico is being squeezed between Washington’s demand to raise barriers against China (as the USMCA review approaches) and Beijing’s counter-pressure — the same choice the EU faces each time it is asked to align its trade defences with US priorities.

articles.headline: Equinor and Germany’s VNG sign an 18-year gas contract, the longest Norwegian deal since 1986
articles.summary:
Norway’s Equinor will supply up to 15.3 TWh (about 1.4 bcm) of natural gas a year to Leipzig-based VNG from 1 January 2027 to the end of 2044, delivered at Trading Hub Europe; pricing reflects market terms, other details are confidential (Equinor). It is the longest Norwegian gas sales agreement since the Troll agreements of 1986. The contract was signed in Oslo on 24 November by Equinor CEO Anders Opedal and VNG CEO Ulf Heitmüller. Germany is Equinor’s largest gas market.

**Key facts:** volume up to 15.3 TWh/yr (~1.4 bcm/yr); term 1 Jan 2027–end-2044; first Norwegian gas to eastern Germany in 1996 (Equinor).

**Sources:** Equinor: https://www.equinor.com/news/20261124-vng-18-year-gas-sales-agreement ; Reuters on X: https://x.com/i/status/2125195265581674752 ; R&D list (Reuters Tech) https://x.com/i/status/2125154996266119577
articles.why: a long-term European pipeline contract, between a Norwegian and a German company, is a rare counterweight to the growing dependence on US LNG (US supply: 58% of EU LNG imports in 2025, per ACER, as reported on 18 November). Intra-European energy deals of this kind reduce exposure both to Russia and to Washington’s “energy dominance” leverage.

articles.headline: European gas rises with the cold snap and storage at 68.9% while oil falls to three-month lows
articles.summary:
The Dutch TTF front-month gas contract rose about 1.25% to €90.89/MWh in early trading on 24 November as forecasts pointed to a prolonged cold spell (Investing.com/Reuters). EU gas storage was only 68.9% full on 23 November, against a five-year average of 89% and about 82% a year earlier (Gas Infrastructure Europe via OilPrice.com). Oil moved the other way: Brent touched its lowest since 27 August and traded around $88.6–89.1 a barrel, WTI around $79.5–80, as Libya’s Sharara pipeline reopened and analysts pointed to a supply surplus despite the Hormuz closure and new mine incidents (CNBC/Reuters; The Independent). Japan is poised to buy more spot LNG as gas-fired power becomes profitable again, and Chinese refiners have stepped up crude purchases to rebuild stocks (Bloomberg).

**Sources:** Investing.com: https://www.investing.com/news/forex-news/european-gas-bucks-energy-selloff-as-lingering-cold-snap-offsets-crude-slump-5047347 ; OilPrice.com: https://oilprice.com/Latest-Energy-News/World-News/European-Gas-Prices-Climb-as-Cold-Snap-Threatens-Depleted-Reserves.html ; CNBC: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/24/oil-wti-brent-hormuz-supply.html ; ENGIE EnergyScan: https://energyscan.engie.com/daily-news/brent-breaks-90-as-cold-snap-lifts-european-gas-and-power/ ; Bloomberg on X: https://x.com/i/status/2125143664598884811 , https://x.com/i/status/2125109692309327967 , https://x.com/i/status/2125108434320158774 ; Reuters on X: https://x.com/i/status/2125191480377561326
articles.why: Europe pays a premium for gas in winter just as Asian buyers return to the spot LNG market; with Henry Hub around $3.2/MMBtu (ENGIE EnergyScan), the price gap with the US that weighs on European industry persists.

articles.headline: Spain’s People’s Party promises a tougher trade line on China if it wins the 29 November election
articles.summary:
Spain’s conservative People’s Party (PP), leading the polls before the 29 November general election, would back a more hawkish trade approach to China if its leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo becomes prime minister, its economy spokesman Alberto Nadal told Bloomberg: Spain’s stance would align with those who see that “China is different” and that “Europe needs a clear China policy”. Nadal said future Chinese investment should involve Spanish partners and not be mere assembly plants to obtain a “Made in Europe” label; a PP government could review contracts with Chinese suppliers such as Huawei (Bloomberg via Placera/Headliner). Spain’s trade deficit with China was $41.1 bn in 2025; a Fedea study counts about €14.5 bn of completed and announced Chinese projects since 2019 (Bloomberg, as reported by Headliner).

**Sources:** Bloomberg on X: https://x.com/i/status/2125182684208967682 ; Placera (Nyhetsbyrån Direkt): https://www.placera.se/telegram/spanien-hogerregering-redo-for-tuffare-hallning-mot-kina-20261124 ; Headliner: https://www.headliner.nl/artikelen/spaanse-volkspartij-hint-hardere-lijn-tegen-china-verkiezingen-november-271663 ; context (AJP, 18 Nov): https://www.ajupress.com/view/20261118033602675
articles.why: the Sánchez government has been one of the EU’s most China-friendly; a shift in Madrid would change the balance inside the EU on trade defence. Requiring local partners and real value added is a sound industrial demand; excluding suppliers such as Huawei, as Washington asks, closes European options without a European alternative in place.

articles.headline: Demand for Fujitsu’s Monaka server chips beats expectations as buyers seek alternatives to US and Chinese suppliers
articles.summary:
Initial demand for Fujitsu’s new 2-nanometre, Arm-based Monaka server CPUs is exceeding expectations, driven by clients in Japan, the US and Europe seeking alternatives to US and Chinese suppliers for defence, finance, manufacturing and the public sector, CTO Vivek Mahajan told Bloomberg. Most of the 45 companies that received samples in August are likely to order; Fujitsu is in talks with TSMC for more capacity. It expects ¥35 bn (about $220 m) of Monaka sales next fiscal year and ¥500 bn a year by 2035. “We are… probably [the] only ones outside the U.S. that make such a cutting-edge CPU,” Mahajan said (Japan Times/Bloomberg).

**Sources:** Japan Times: https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/2026/11/24/companies/fujitsu-chips/ ; X https://x.com/i/status/2125162291792326972 ; Bloomberg on X: https://x.com/i/status/2125129832853917830 ; Fujitsu (14 Sep 2026): https://global.fujitsu/en-global/pr/news/2026/09/14-02
articles.why: European buyers are turning to a Japanese CPU (made in Taiwan) for “sovereign” infrastructure because Europe has no cutting-edge server processor of its own in volume production — a measure of the gap the EU Chips Act has yet to close.

articles.headline: Germany’s ifo index rises for a seventh month; an ECB hawk talks of rate hikes
articles.summary:
The ifo Business Climate Index rose to 90.6 in November from 90.1 in October, the seventh consecutive increase and the highest since May 2023 (Trading Economics); current conditions 89.4, expectations 91.9. articles.headline: Washington blacklists Megaspeed and six other South-east Asian firms; Malaysia and Singapore fall into line
articles.summary:
The US Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) added seven companies to its Entity List in a final rule filed for public inspection on 23 November (Federal Register document 2026-23999, publication scheduled for 25 November): MSFusion Sdn. Bhd., PT Megaspeed International and Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd (Malaysia); Apex Enterprise Solutions (Singapore) Private Limited, Megaspeed International Pte. Ltd. and Swiftdata Pte. Ltd. (Singapore); and Megaspeed (Thailand) Co., Ltd. The End-User Review Committee cites “the significant risk of these entities being or becoming involved in the diversion of advanced computing commodities to unauthorized end uses or end users”; any export, re-export or transfer of items subject to the EAR now needs a licence, reviewed under a presumption of denial. Megaspeed is the cloud firm at the centre of the Nvidia affair: US officials accuse its former executive Alice Huang of working with China’s Ministry of State Security; Beijing calls this “groundless speculation” (Al Jazeera). Al Jazeera reports that Commerce had declined to list the firm for months, drawing criticism from China hawks including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, and acted only after the scandal broke. The reaction came within hours: Malaysia’s trade ministry (MITI) said MIDA will tell every data-centre operator in the country not to host, lease space to or serve the seven firms, adding that Malaysia “will not allow itself to be used as a channel to circumvent export controls”; Singapore’s Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said the Megaspeed investigation continues and that Singapore will not be a conduit to circumvent US chip controls.

*CEAFE:* What these figures reveal is an asymmetry of power, not a difference in talent or political will.

**Key facts:**

- 7 entities: 3 under Malaysia, 3 under Singapore, 1 under Thailand; licence for all items subject to the EAR, presumption of denial; 30-day savings clause for shipments en route (Federal Register PI 2026-23999; The Star/Straits Times).

- Signed by Deputy Assistant Secretary for Strategic Trade Julia Khersonsky; filed 23 Nov, publication 25 Nov 2026.

- Malaysia (MITI, 24 Nov): only Speedmatrix and MSFusion are Malaysian companies; Speedmatrix is wholly owned by Megaspeed International Pte Ltd (Singapore); PT Megaspeed International is not a data-centre operator or tenant in Malaysia (The Star).

- Malaysia holds more than half of South-east Asia’s data-centre capacity under construction (DC Byte via AFP/Straits Times).

**What to watch:** Chinese MFA and MOFCOM reaction (24 Nov briefing); Thailand’s response; Federal Register publication on 25 Nov; Huang’s Senate testimony on 3 December. @F_CEAFE has not posted this story.

**Sources:** [BIS rule, public inspection copy](https://public-inspection.federalregister.gov/2026-23999.pdf), [federalregister.gov](https://www.federalregister.gov/public-inspection/2026-23999/additions-to-the-entity-list), [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/11/24/us-adds-megaspeed-firm-at-centre-of-nvidia-scandal-to-export-control-list), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2125089527375245531), [The Star (MITI statement)](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2026/11/24/miti-data-centre-operators-to-be-advised-against-hosting-us-blacklisted-entities), [The Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/malaysia-advises-data-centres-to-cut-links-with-us-blacklisted-firms), [straitstimes.com](https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/spore-working-with-us-on-chip-export-enforcement-as-megaspeed-probe-continues-pm-wong), [Singapore PMO (Wong in Canberra)](https://www.pmo.gov.sg/newsroom/pm-lawrence-wong-at-the-q-a-segment-of-the-joint-press-conference-with-australia-pm-anthony-albanese-in-canberra-australia-nov-2026/), [Singapore MHA](https://www.mha.gov.sg/media-room/newsroom/singapore-investigations-into-alice-huang-huang-le-and-megaspeed-international-pte-ltd/), [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2125056837875609732), [Reuters on (2)](https://x.com/i/status/2125089537575584077), [R&D list (Reuters Tech)](https://x.com/i/status/2125054321439989790), [R&D list (Reuters Tech) (2)](https://x.com/i/status/2125088275446616193), [Bloomberg](https://x.com/i/status/2125085237252067392), [Bloomberg on (2)](https://x.com/i/status/2125082012180484325), [NYT](https://x.com/i/status/2124987975196922318)
articles.why: a US administrative listing turned within a day into binding practice in two sovereign states that host South-east Asia’s data-centre boom — the extraterritorial reach of US export controls at work. The same EAR rules (including the 16 November remote-access rule) apply to European cloud and data-centre operators; Europe has no comparable instrument and no say in Washington’s End-User Review Committee. The contrast noted by an NYU analyst quoted by Al Jazeera is also telling: Washington blacklists a middleman for moving Nvidia chips to China while licensing Nvidia’s H200 sales to China in exchange for a 25% cut.

articles.headline: Congo bans cobalt exports again from 30 November to push prices up
articles.summary:
The Democratic Republic of Congo, which supplied about three-quarters of the world’s mined cobalt before its restrictions began, will suspend all cobalt exports from 30 November until further notice, its strategic-minerals regulator ARECOMS said on 23 November. The ban covers industrial and artisanal output and even previously authorised volumes not shipped by 30 November; quotas allocated for 2026 and 2027 will not be automatically reinstated. ARECOMS cites a “significant and sustained decline in cobalt prices” since mid-year, rising inventories and speculation, and will review the measure after four months. It is the second halt since February 2025, when a first ban was replaced in October 2025 by export quotas. Shares in Chinese cobalt producers jumped on the news (Bloomberg); CMOC (China), Glencore and Eurasian Resources Group hold the largest quotas.

**Key facts:**

- Congo exported 61,441 t of contained cobalt in January–September 2026 (DRC Ministry of Mines via S&P Global).

- European cobalt metal (Rotterdam) at $18.15/lb on 20 Nov 2026, down 24% since the start of 2026 (Platts).

- Cobalt hydroxide more than quadrupled after the 2025 measures, then almost halved from an April 2026 peak (Fastmarkets via Bloomberg/Mining Weekly).

**What to watch:** price reaction on 24 Nov; EU and US reaction (both court Kinshasa for minerals deals); impact on European battery makers.

**Sources:** [S&P Global (ARECOMS communication)](https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/metals/112326-drc-temporarily-suspends-cobalt-exports), [Reuters via CNBC Africa](https://www.cnbcafrica.com/2026/congo-halts-cobalt-exports-again-to-tackle-oversupply-support-prices-industry-regulator-says), [Bloomberg via Mining Weekly](https://www.miningweekly.com/article/top-cobalt-producer-congo-will-ban-exports-again-as-prices-slide-2026-11-23), [Bloomberg on X (Chinese cobalt shares)](https://x.com/i/status/2125069463494000928)
articles.why: cobalt is on the EU’s critical raw materials list and essential for batteries and defence alloys. Europe neither mines nor refines it at scale; a supply squeeze set in Kinshasa benefits the Chinese groups that dominate mining in Congo and refining in China, and the No. 2 producer Indonesia (Chinese-financed nickel plants). Another reminder that the EU’s Critical Raw Materials Act targets remain far from reality.

articles.headline: The FCC proposes “reciprocity” rules against foreign satellite operators in the US
articles.summary:
FCC Chairman Brendan Carr announced on 23 November that the Commission will vote next month on a proposal to apply to foreign satellite operators in the US “the same types of restrictions” that their home countries apply to American operators. Carr argues that foreign nations “have begun applying one set of regulations to their own satellite companies and a very different one to American satellite providers”, creating an asymmetry that disadvantages US operators. The move follows a March 2026 public notice (DA 26-208) on satellite market-access reciprocity, which notes that about a quarter of the over 200 satellite systems approved under the FCC’s Part 25 rules are licensed by foreign administrations. @F_CEAFE reposted Carr’s post.

**Key facts:**

- Vote at the FCC’s December open meeting (Bloomberg Law; FCC).

- Earlier record: GN Docket 26-48, comments closed 1 April and 16 April 2026 (FCC).

**What to watch:** text of the draft order; Commission and ESA reaction; link with IRIS² and the EU Space Act.

**Sources:** [FCC Chairman’s blog “The Good and the Bad”, 23 Nov 2026](https://www.fcc.gov/news-events/blog/2026/11/23/good-and-bad), [FCC news release (via Public)](https://www.pubt.io/view/864BBA12D6BF80A9BE146D335D4FE1EC21505A53), [FCC public notice DA 26-208](https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/DA-26-208A1.txt), [Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/tech-and-telecom-law/fcc-to-vote-on-new-rules-for-foreign-satellite-systems-in-us), [@BrendanCarrFCC](https://x.com/i/status/2124970983056379978), [@BrendanCarrFCC (2)](https://x.com/i/status/2125002145329992062), [Eutelsat contract (@AndrewParsonson)](https://x.com/i/status/2124881761071219129), [Eutelsat contract (@AndrewParsonson) (2)](https://x.com/i/status/2124946286420152594)
articles.why: the proposal names no country, but it lands in the middle of the European battle with Starlink over spectrum (the 2 GHz band row, covered on 22 November) and EU rules favouring European constellations. European operators such as Eutelsat-OneWeb and SES sell services in the US — Eutelsat has just won a $60 million contract to provide OneWeb services to the US armed forces. Washington is again using market access as leverage to protect a dominant US firm, while Europe has no equivalent tool it is willing to use.

articles.headline: Swiss Clariant and US fund CD&R in talks to buy US chemicals maker Ashland (~$3.3bn)
articles.summary:
Clariant (Switzerland) confirmed in an ad hoc announcement on 23 November that it is in talks to acquire Ashland Inc. (US) in partnership with the US private-equity firm Clayton, Dubilier & Rice; it said there is no certainty of a deal. Bloomberg reported an all-cash deal valuing Ashland close to its Friday share price — a market value of about $3.3 billion. Ashland, based in Wilmington, Delaware, makes additives and specialty ingredients for pharmaceuticals, construction and personal care; it put itself up for sale in July under activist pressure.

**Key facts:**

- Ashland market capitalisation $3.32bn (LSEG via Reuters); other bidders contacted included Advent, Apollo, Carlyle and Standard Industries (Reuters).

**What to watch:** signing and price; whether a European partner keeps operational control.

**Sources:** [Clariant ad hoc announcement](https://www.clariant.com/en/Corporate/News/2026/11/Clariant-confirms-talks-regarding-a-potential-acquisition-of-Ashland), [Reuters via US News](https://money.usnews.com/investing/news/articles/2026-11-23/switzerlands-clariant-cd-r-in-talks-to-buy-chemicals-firm-ashland), [Bloomberg Deals](https://x.com/i/status/2124993983344464064)
articles.why: a rare deal in the opposite direction — a European industrial buying in the US — but done jointly with a US fund, and in specialty chemicals, a sector where European producers are cutting capacity at home because of energy prices. It is not a US takeover of a European firm; no such deal was announced in this window.

articles.headline: Japan and the IEA launch an Asian oil-security hub as Hormuz mines hit more tankers
articles.summary:
Japan launched an Asian oil-security task force and, with the International Energy Agency, an “IEA-Japan Oil Security Hub for Asia” in Tokyo, to help Asian countries build emergency oil stocks, share storage (including spare Japanese tanks) and coordinate releases during Gulf supply disruptions (IEA joint statement; Euronews). Overnight Iran’s IRGC said three “non-compliant” tankers under US air escort hit naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, while Tehran said security could be restored quickly if the US meets its conditions (Al Jazeera). Bloomberg reported that oil prices fell, easing inflation concerns in US Treasuries. In Germany, the government is pressing ahead with a three-month fuel price cap from 1 January 2027, with a cabinet decision due on 2 December (Bloomberg; German government).

**Key facts:**

- German cap: regulation valid three months from 1 Jan 2027, legal basis 12 months; cabinet on 2 Dec 2026 (coalition decision of 17 Nov; German government).

- IRGC: three tankers hit by mines (Al Jazeera live, 24 Nov).

**What to watch:** Brent and TTF on 24 Nov; German cabinet on 2 Dec; any EU-level stock coordination.

**Sources:** [IEA](https://www.iea.org/news/joint-statement-by-the-government-of-japan-and-the-international-energy-agency-on-the-establishment-of-the-iea-japan-oil-security-hub-for-asia), [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/23/japan-launches-asian-oil-task-force-amid-gulf-supply-disruptions), [X (1)](https://x.com/i/status/2125011846046400830), [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/11/24/iran-war-live-iran-says-three-ships-catch-fire-after-hitting-hormuz-mines), [X (2)](https://x.com/i/status/2125080719227494502), [X (3)](https://x.com/i/status/2125026612714319920), [Bloomberg on X (Treasuries, oil)](https://x.com/i/status/2125089558400290973), [(German cap)](https://x.com/i/status/2124953671137935639), [German government](https://www.bundeskanzler.de/bk-en/news/electricity-tax-fuel-price-cap-federal-government-2461874), [@HormuzReport post](https://x.com/i/status/2124952108353061312), [@HormuzReport post (2)](https://x.com/i/status/2124991927195942965)
articles.why: Asia is organising its own stockholding under IEA cover, while Europe responds country by country with price caps and tax cuts (Germany’s cap follows the “Tankrabatt” that ends in December). Europe’s exposure to the Gulf and to US LNG makes collective EU energy-security tools — joint stocks and joint buying — more urgent.

articles.headline: Update: The Huang rally spreads to Asia; the Fed’s Williams signals more rate hikes possible
