articles.headline: Brussels proposes a 22nd Russia sanctions package: some 60 more banks cut off from SWIFT
articles.summary:
**The European Commission presented on Monday its proposal for a 22nd package of sanctions against Russia, which extends the transaction ban to some 60 Russian banks, all of which would be removed from SWIFT.**

Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the package targets crypto and payment networks "in Russia but also third countries that help Russia evade our sanctions", with a new Crypto Sanctions Task Force. No European company could help build, operate or repair Russian energy infrastructure, notably refineries, and electricity services are covered for the first time. Over 70 more shadow-fleet ships would be listed, on top of more than 670 already denied EU ports and services, and all tankers insured in Russia would be banned (Euronews). Europeans could no longer sit on the governing bodies of companies in Russia. Russian ex-combatants would face an entry ban, and Russian teams and official symbols would be barred from sports events in the EU. All 27 EU member states must agree; Brussels aims for a deal in December. Alumina exported to Russia from Aughinish (Ireland) is left out because Brussels did not sense enough Irish support (Euronews). Swedish diplomat Lars Danielsson replaces David O'Sullivan as EU sanctions envoy.

**Context:** the oil price cap stands at $44 per barrel. Antecedent: on 23 July 2026 EU member states agreed the 21st package, targeting Moscow's financial system ([Kallas](https://x.com/i/status/2080232531002085381)).

**What to watch:** Coreper negotiations; Irish, Hungarian and Slovak positions; Russian and Chinese responses.

**Sources:** [European Commission](https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/statement_26_2563), [European Commission (visa ban guidelines)](https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/ip_26_2521), [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/23/eu-goes-after-russias-banks-soldiers-and-athletes-in-new-sanctions-package), [von der Leyen](https://x.com/i/status/2124880816438215059), [von der Leyen](https://x.com/i/status/2124881906588078185), [Bloomberg](https://x.com/i/status/2124922218350051636), [Politico Europe](https://www.politico.eu/article/eu-to-target-russian-ex-soldiers-banks-and-sports-in-new-sanctions-push/), [AP](https://apnews.com/article/europe-russia-sanctions-banks-crypto-visas-sports-ecad86868390f6602b346c70d1fa5757)
articles.why: sanctions are the EU's main collective tool. The focus on third countries moves them towards the extraterritorial reach Washington already uses, but with far less leverage over the dollar system. Unanimity remains the weak point, as the Aughinish case shows.

articles.headline: Update: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang after pressure from Trump; shares jump 30.6%
articles.summary:
**Nvidia's board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, CEO and director with immediate effect, less than two weeks after he quit following revelations of an affair with a woman whom US officials link to China's Ministry of State Security.**

The board says it "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and has created a National Security and Export Control Committee (Nvidia). The New York Times reports Trump directed a behind-the-scenes campaign to pressure the board. On Truth Social Trump wrote that the government has "no reason to believe" Huang's return poses a national-security risk. On CNBC he said that "if I were President Xi" he would have tried to hire Huang. He also said Taiwan "stole" America's chip business and that he expects China to buy 250 more Boeing jets (Bloomberg). Nvidia closed at $163.98, up 30.63%. The S&P 500 rose about 5% by noon in New York (AP). Huang will testify before a Senate committee on 3 December (Bloomberg). China's foreign ministry repeated that it "has made clear its position on U.S. export control measures".

**Context:** antecedent: on 17 November 2026 @F_CEAFE shared the New York Times account of the secret that led to Huang's downfall ([@F_CEAFE](https://x.com/i/status/2122584683045380473)).

**What to watch:** the Senate hearing on 3 December; any change to US chip export rules for China; Taipei's reaction.

**Sources:** [Nvidia](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-board-reinstates-jensen-huang-as-president-ceo-and-board-director), [NYT](https://x.com/i/status/2124912528866111940), [Truth Social](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/117666141823845971), [CNBC (Aaron Rupar)](https://x.com/i/status/2124903759495020901), [Bloomberg](https://x.com/i/status/2124917173030133829), [Bloomberg](https://x.com/i/status/2124919870949097608), [AP](https://apnews.com/article/nvidia-jensen-huang-39d4b34ffaa867b4e669893b5fd5028f), [BBC](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cq62pn6j42jko), [Chinese MFA](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/xw/fyrbt/lxjzh/202611/t20261123_12065575.html)
articles.why: a board decision steered from the White House moved world markets, a measure of how much the AI economy, Europe's included, depends on one US firm. Trade-offs with Beijing over chips, Taiwan and Boeing are being made without Europe at the table.

articles.headline: EU opens safeguard investigation into composite resins and glass fibre, mainly from China
articles.summary:
**The European Commission launched on Monday a safeguard investigation into surging imports of composite resins and glass-fibre materials, primarily from China.**

The materials go into renewable energy, electricity grids, transport, aerospace and defence. The probe is expected to last nine to 11 months. It could end in quotas or tariffs applying to imports from all trading partners, because Chinese producers had circumvented earlier anti-dumping duties by shifting production to third countries. Low-cost Chinese imports have risen 25% over the past year, and the EU's trade deficit with China has reached a record €1 billion a day (Euronews). Glass Fibre Europe's Ludovic Piraux said the case is about "industrial capabilities we need to… strengthen our defence". Global Times (Chinese state media) published an editorial the same day against EU tariffs on Chinese green products.

**Context:** on Friday EU member states backed the October EU–China deal on hybrid cars: quotas for 350,000 Chinese hybrids a year for four years, adjusted by 6% a year, from 1 December. Šefčovič is expected to speak with Commerce Minister Wang Wentao in January (Euronews).

**What to watch:** the notice in the Official Journal; MOFCOM's response.

**Sources:** [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/23/eu-targets-chinese-imports-in-fresh-trade-defence-investigation), [Global Times](https://x.com/i/status/2124925960449634319)
articles.why: glass fibre and resins go into wind blades, aircraft structures and defence equipment. Losing European producers would add a new dependence to the defence supply chain.

articles.headline: US Treasury adds some 20 Dubai, Turkish and Hong Kong firms to its Iran sanctions list
articles.summary:
**OFAC published new Iran-related designations on 23 November: eight Iranian individuals and more than 20 entities, including Iranian exchange houses and a string of companies registered outside Iran.**

The listings include Mellat Exchange Company and the Iran Center for Exchange of Currency and Gold. They also cover Dubai-registered trading companies such as Alam Al Sahra, Berkeley Trading, Dexterous Global DMCC and Integral Petro Energy Trading, the Türkiye-based Boğaziçi Gümrükleme and the Hong Kong-based Grandez Trading. Almost all are marked "secondary sanctions risk" under E.O. 13902: foreign banks dealing with them risk US penalties. The same day Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said US sanctions make it difficult to procure medicines, medical equipment and pharmaceutical raw materials (Al Jazeera).

*CEAFE:* The conclusion is the same once again: either Europe acts as one, or each country is left in a supporting role.

**Context:** the previous OFAC action, on 20 November, targeted oil trustees under "Operation Economic Outcast" (OFAC).

**What to watch:** the Treasury press release; responses from the UAE and Türkiye.

**Sources:** [OFAC](https://ofac.treasury.gov/recent-actions/20261123), [Al Jazeera](https://x.com/i/status/2124880667846811792)
articles.why: secondary-sanctions listings in the UAE, Türkiye and Hong Kong show the extraterritorial reach of US measures, which European banks and exporters must observe whatever EU policy is. EU sanctions (see the 22nd package above) and US sanctions now both target third-country intermediaries.

articles.headline: Eight EU member states, Spain among them, defend the ETS2 carbon market as an energy-security tool
articles.summary:
**In a letter dated 23 November to Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra, the climate ministers of Denmark, Finland, Germany, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, Spain and Sweden warn against further delays to ETS2.**

ETS2 is the carbon price on road fuels and heating, due in January 2028 after a one-year delay. The ministers argue that dependence on imported fossil fuels is a major economic and security vulnerability. The EU imported €340 billion of fossil fuels in 2025. Since the closure of the Strait of Hormuz earlier this year, higher prices have added €127 billion to the bill (Euronews). The Visegrad Four, Italy and Greece want ETS2 softened or delayed. Czech Deputy PM Karel Havlíček said implementing it now "does not seem reasonable" given "exceptionally high energy costs". Global Times (Chinese state media) published a cartoon the same afternoon: "Power costs keep soaring, holding Europe's economy hostage."

**Context:** ETS2 was already postponed by one year to January 2028.

**What to watch:** the Commission's ETS2 impact assessment; the December Environment Council.

**Sources:** [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/23/eight-eu-countries-join-forces-to-defend-carbon-market-against-calls-for-delay), [Jorge Liboreiro](https://x.com/i/status/2124808743674347811), [Global Times](https://x.com/i/status/2124918404075368738)
articles.why: the split runs between member states that want to cut import dependence through electrification and those whose households cannot afford higher bills now. Neither side alone can change the price of the energy Europe imports.

articles.headline: Amazon buys Israeli start-up Decart's AI-chip technology and team for about $7.5bn
articles.summary:
**Amazon (US) signed an agreement to buy the proprietary technology behind Decart's Optimization Stack and to hire its three co-founders and engineering team.**

The work will support Amazon's Trainium and Inferentia chips against Nvidia's dominance (Amazon). Amazon did not disclose terms. Bloomberg puts the value at about $7.5 billion, paid in cash, stock and deferred instalments, part of it tied to performance over five years (Reuters via Investing.com; Calcalist). Decart (Israel), founded in 2023, was valued at about $4 billion in May and employs about 100 people. Anthropic and Nvidia had earlier held talks to buy it (Calcalist). Closing requires regulatory clearance.

*CEAFE:* These figures show how the size of European states leaves them unable to compete alone against much larger global powers.

**Context:** it is another "acqui-hire" in which a US hyperscaler absorbs a non-US firm's chip know-how.

**What to watch:** regulatory clearance.

**Sources:** [Amazon](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/company-news/amazon-decart-ai-optimization), [Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/amazon-to-buy-decarts-ai-chip-optimization-tech-in-latest-ai-talent-grab-5046000), [Calcalist](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/g0mtcg4mi), [Globes](https://en.globes.co.il/en/article-amazon-confirms-decart-acquisition-1001564520), [Bloomberg](https://x.com/i/status/2124868102752026968)
articles.why: the deal is part of the race to break Nvidia's grip on AI chips, a race run by US groups. Europe has no buyer of this size for such companies.

articles.headline: Europe's sovereign-cloud push gains ground, but US hyperscalers still hold over 70% of the market
articles.summary:
**A Reuters analysis finds that sovereignty is moving into cloud procurement in Europe, yet AWS, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud still control more than 70% of the European market.**

In April the European Commission awarded sovereign-cloud contracts worth up to €180m over six years to groups led by Post Telecom (Luxembourg) and Proximus (Belgium), plus StackIT (Germany) and Scaleway (France); the Dutch government, Denmark's DSB, Swiss federal bodies and German public broadcasters have added sovereignty criteria. Nextcloud reports demand up roughly fivefold since Trump's second term began, and T-Systems more than fourfold since mid-2025. According to a Commission draft of the Cloud and AI Development Act, EU providers' share fell from 29% in 2017 to 15% in 2022 and has stagnated since. Only a single-digit percentage of IONOS's public-sector talks turn into contracts.

*CEAFE:* Figures that illustrate, once again, why European sovereignty is only credible if it is exercised together.

**Context:** US providers are answering with their own "sovereign" offerings, while the new US AI-chip rules reach data centres outside the US (Bloomberg).

**What to watch:** negotiations on the Cloud and AI Development Act.

**Sources:** [@F_CEAFE](https://x.com/i/status/2124819328076001694), [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2124756864218874029), [CNA (Reuters)](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/analysiseuropes-cloud-sovereignty-push-gains-ground-us-hyperscalers-remain-dominant-6574046)
articles.why: the figures measure the dependence: Europe's own share of its cloud market halved between 2017 and 2022. Procurement rules help, but no single member state's market can build a challenger.

articles.headline: Norway's Vår Energi buys ConocoPhillips' Norwegian business and its Teesside terminal stake for $4.425bn
articles.summary:
**Vår Energi (Norway) agreed on Monday to buy the entire Norwegian upstream business of ConocoPhillips (US), anchored by the operated Greater Ekofisk Area, plus its 40.25% interest in, and operatorship of, the Teesside oil terminal in the United Kingdom.**

The agreed enterprise value is $4.425bn; ConocoPhillips expects net cash proceeds of about $2.5bn after a remaining 2026 tax liability of about $1.4bn, and will use part of them for share buybacks. The assets include interests in eight partner-operated fields and the Norpipe oil pipeline, and produced about 120,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day in 2025. Closing is expected around the end of the first quarter of 2027, subject to approval by Norway's Ministry of Energy. Vår Energi says it will become Europe's largest independent producer.

**Context:** Norway is not an EU member state but is part of the European Economic Area and a NATO member, and is Europe's main pipeline gas supplier.

**What to watch:** Norwegian approval; whether other US majors sell North Sea assets.

**Sources:** [Vår Energi](https://news.cision.com/var-energi-asa/r/var-energi-to-acquire-conocophillips--norwegian-business--and-related-uk-infrastructure--strengtheni,c4427939), [ConocoPhillips](https://www.conocophillips.com/news-media/story/conocophillips-announces-agreement-to-sell-norway-business-and-teesside-asset-to-var-energi-2/), [Bloomberg](https://x.com/i/status/2124757371909996594), [WSJ](https://x.com/i/status/2124767231217176844), [Offshore Energy](https://www.offshore-energy.biz/2026/11/23/dollar44-billion-play-for-conocophillips-norwegian-oil-and-gas-assets-and-uk-infrastructure-expands-var-energis-north-sea-footprint)
articles.why: it is the reverse of the flow CEAFE usually tracks: a US major leaves and a European operator takes control of a historic North Sea hub. Control of European hydrocarbons matters as Europe pays far more for energy than the US and depends on US LNG, but it is one Norwegian company's deal, not a European energy strategy.

articles.headline: ABB to buy German fan and motor maker Ziehl-Abegg for $2.65bn
articles.summary:
**Swiss-Swedish engineering group ABB has agreed to acquire Ziehl-Abegg of Künzelsau (Baden-Württemberg), a family-owned maker of high-efficiency fans, electric motors and ventilation controls, for an enterprise value of $2.65bn (equity value $2.22bn).**

Ziehl-Abegg expects about $1.4bn of revenue in 2026 and employs about 6,300 people; its products go into HVAC, data centres, clean rooms, medical technology and industry. ABB highlights its ferrite-magnet technology, "which reduces dependence on rare earth materials". Closing is expected in the second half of 2027 and the headquarters will stay in Künzelsau (ABB; tagesschau/SWR). Vontobel called the valuation "rich" (Bloomberg).

**Context:** the sale followed the death of owner Uwe Ziehl in June 2026 (tagesschau).

**What to watch:** job guarantees at Künzelsau; regulatory approvals.

**Sources:** [ABB](https://new.abb.com/news/detail/140614/abb-to-acquire-ziehl-abegg-expanding-offering-for-hvac-and-industrial-cooling-applications), [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2124798900007506346), [swissinfo (Bloomberg)](https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/abb-buys-german-data-center-cooling-firm-for-%242.2-billion/92422021), [tagesschau/SWR](https://www.tagesschau.de/inland/regional/badenwuerttemberg/swr-milliardendeal-in-hohenlohe-schwedisch-schweizer-unternehmen-abb-uebernimmt-ziehl-abegg-100.html)
articles.why: a German Mittelstand technology firm passes to a European group rather than a US or Chinese buyer, and its rare-earth-free motor technology matters given China's grip on rare-earth magnets. The deal is driven by data-centre cooling demand for an AI build-out that Europe mostly hosts rather than owns.

articles.headline: Abu Dhabi's IRH agrees terms for a possible £353m takeover of Irish miner Kenmare Resources
articles.summary:
**The boards of Kenmare Resources (Ireland; London-listed mineral sands producer operating in Mozambique) and Abu Dhabi-based International Resources Holding (IRH) agreed in principle on a pre-conditional possible cash offer of 380 pence per share.**

That values Kenmare's share capital at about £352.8m and implies an enterprise value of about £487.1m, a 52% premium to Friday's close. It is not yet a firm offer: pre-conditions include consents from the Government of Mozambique. Kenmare shares jumped 24% (Proactive Investors).

**Context:** Ireland is an EU member state; the EU's Critical Raw Materials Act seeks secure supplies of minerals.

**What to watch:** a firm offer or walk-away; Mozambique's consent.

**Sources:** [Joint statement](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/11/23/3408030/0/en/joint-statement-regarding-agreement-of-a-pre-conditional-possible-cash-acquisition-of-kenmare-resources-plc-by-international-resources-holding-rsc-ltd.html), [Bloomberg](https://x.com/i/status/2124811474761605449), [RTÉ](https://www.rte.ie/news/business/2026/1123/1600256-kenmare-resources-offer/)
articles.why: a European-listed raw-materials producer heads to a Gulf state-linked buyer, part of a pattern in which Gulf, US and Chinese capital buys the mining assets Europe says it needs.

articles.headline: Update: Beijing restates its position after Trump's "older chips only" remark; NYT details Alice Huang's contacts with China's Ministry of State Security
articles.summary:
**Asked about President Trump's 20 November remark that the US wants to sell China "only older chips", Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said only that China had already made its position on US export controls clear (Global Times, Chinese state media).**

The New York Times reports, citing people familiar with US intelligence reports, that Alice Huang, former head of Singapore-based Megaspeed, a major Nvidia customer, was in touch with an officer of China's Ministry of State Security from spring 2025 to autumn 2026, overlapping with her relationship with Jensen Huang, who stepped down as Nvidia CEO this month. US officials say they have not concluded she spied for China (Reuters). Bloomberg reports that Washington's new AI-chip rules threaten a multibillion-dollar cloud business serving South-East Asian data centres.

**Context:** on 17 November Guo had called US controls "economic coercion and long-arm jurisdiction".

**What to watch:** the MFA transcript; a possible MOFCOM statement; a congressional hearing for Commerce Secretary Lutnick.

**Sources:** [Global Times](https://www.globaltimes.cn/page/202611/1374863.shtml), [Beijing Daily](https://news.bjd.com.cn/2026/11/23/12040721.shtml), [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2124797643440161243), [The Hindu (Reuters)](https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/alice-huang-in-touch-with-chinese-spy-agency-during-affair-with-nvidia-ceo-says-nyt/article71733237.ece), [NYT](https://cn.nytimes.com/technology/20261123/alice-huang-china-spy-agency-nvidia/), [Bloomberg](https://x.com/i/status/2124753933071433828)
articles.why: the affair pushes Washington to meter chips more strictly everywhere, including through European data centres, and a bilateral US–China chip deal would be negotiated without a European seat.

articles.headline: Update: Nvidia chips for China: US senator demands "hard questions" for Commerce Secretary Lutnick
articles.summary:
**Republican Senator John Kennedy said on Sunday that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick should face "hard questions" from Congress about whether his department allowed Chinese companies to "circumvent" export rules and obtain Nvidia AI chips (The Washington Post).**

"It appears to me, I emphasize 'appears', that the Department of Commerce has allowed the Communist Party of China…", he said. The remarks follow Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's statement that Washington "still needs answers" from Nvidia (20:30 edition of 22 November) and the House Foreign Affairs Committee's disclosure of 879,868 Nvidia and AMD chips licensed by the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) for China (20 November). No new BIS or OFAC action was published in the window.

**What to watch:** whether Congress calls Lutnick to testify; any BIS tightening; China's reaction at Monday's MFA briefing.

**Sources:** [The Washington Post](https://x.com/i/status/2124627739453816835), [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2124587510596575679), [Bloomberg Opinion](https://x.com/i/status/2124595054475899085)
articles.why: the debate in Washington is now whether Commerce licensed too much to China; any tightening would also apply to data centres in EU member states under the BIS remote-access rule of 16 November, a decision in which Europe has no say.

articles.headline: Update: AI sell-off spreads to Asia: Kospi falls as much as 5.8%
articles.summary:
**Asian markets extended Friday's tech-led rout on Monday: Seoul's Kospi, dominated by Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, slid as much as 5.8% before paring losses to 3.2% at 05:30 Madrid time (Al Jazeera).**

The Hang Seng and the CSI 300 fell about 0.6%, while Taiwan's Taiex reversed to a 2.5% gain; Tokyo was closed for a holiday. On Friday the S&P 500 had closed 3.7% lower, entering a correction, and the Nasdaq Composite lost 5.3%; on Monday morning S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures were up 2.2% and 2.9% (Al Jazeera). The WSJ reports the debt market expects Anthropic's bonds to be rated junk. South Korea's annual exports passed $1 trillion for the first time, with chip exports in the first 20 days of November up 294.4% year on year (Bloomberg).

**Context:** the correction began after Anthropic's market debut on 19 November.

**What to watch:** the European open; Tokyo's reopening on Tuesday; chip stocks.

**Sources:** [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/23/south-koreas-stock-market-tumbles-as-ai-bubble-fears-mount), [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2124712062139908200), [Bloomberg (emerging markets)](https://x.com/i/status/2124679362368704635), [Bloomberg (Korea exports)](https://x.com/i/status/2124659231592783951), [WSJ](https://x.com/i/status/2124720471933440314)
articles.why: the boom and the correction both turn on US and Asian chip and AI companies; Europe has few large players in the race.

articles.headline: Europe's forward power prices near €200/MWh: a German steel mill stops by the hour
articles.summary:
**Forward power contracts for each of the next three months are trading around €200 per megawatt-hour, roughly double last winter's levels, driven by surging gas prices, Bloomberg reports in what it calls "Europe's second major energy crisis in less than five years".**

The Feralpi Group steel plant in Riesa, Germany, owned by Italy's Feralpi, checks next-day power prices twice a day and has repeatedly halted production this autumn even with orders to fill. European gas rose early on Monday on forecasts of colder weather, with inventories already depleted by export disruptions linked to the US–Iran war (Bloomberg). Libya's oil output dropped after a pipeline from its largest field was disrupted.

**Context:** EU gas storage stood at 70.5% on 21 November, and the TTF benchmark had been near €90/MWh last week (21 November edition).

**What to watch:** today's TTF settlement; EU storage withdrawals.

**Sources:** [The Japan Times (Bloomberg)](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/2026/11/23/europe-power-market-economy/), [Bloomberg (gas)](https://x.com/i/status/2124700753172308415), [Bloomberg (Libya oil)](https://x.com/i/status/2124741018524229929), [Reuters (oil)](https://x.com/i/status/2124742281252978853), [Die Sachsen](https://www.diesachsen.de/meissen-news/feralpi-stahlwerk-in-riesa-geht-stundenweise-vom-netz-3181510)
articles.why: energy-intensive industry in EU member states stops producing when power prices spike; Europe replaced much of its Russian gas with US LNG and pays the price premium of the Gulf war.

articles.headline: Update: COP31 ends without an agreement; the EU objects to a text without fossil fuels
articles.summary:
**COP31 in Antalya closed on Sunday without an overarching agreement after two days of overtime, the longest UN climate summit on record (UN News).**

The European Union formally objected to the cover decision, saying it could not accept a text that omitted any reference to fossil fuels or a transition away from them, an omission it called "unconscionable"; the Marshall Islands also withheld support. Saudi Arabia, for the Arab Group, defended references to carbon capture; Reuters reports that Saudi influence loomed large over the outcome. UN Secretary-General António Guterres said he was disappointed, and China (Global Times, Chinese state media) voiced "deep disappointment". COP32 will be held in Addis Ababa.

**What to watch:** EU Council conclusions; the debate on the EU's 2040 target.

**Sources:** [UN News](https://news.un.org/en/story/2026/11/1168855), [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2124732212494897643), [Bloomberg](https://x.com/i/status/2124572402868801678), [Global Times](https://x.com/i/status/2124713902789492895), [Al Jazeera](https://x.com/i/status/2124642815384727799)

**In brief:** Spain's Partido Popular promises sweeping tax cuts if it wins the 29 November snap general election ([Bloomberg](https://x.com/i/status/2124733470140178712)). IQVIA (US) / Quotient Sciences (UK): no formal announcement yet.
articles.why: the EU held its position but could not carry the conference, while its own climate rules weigh on energy costs at home (see the previous story).

articles.headline: Update: US intelligence chief says the best Nvidia chips stay in America; Beijing says controls no longer hold China back
articles.summary:
**On Sunday's US talk shows, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton set out the administration's line on chip exports: "We want to reserve the most exquisite computing capability for the U.S. … So, we do want U.S. chips — just not the most exquisite" (Fox News).**

On ABC's *This Week* he said export rules on advanced technology "are restrictions, they are not bans", that Commerce and Treasury are "in the business of metering" access, and confirmed that the Justice Department is investigating Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed International, and her company. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CBS the administration "still needs answers" from Nvidia on its chip sales (Bloomberg). A *Global Times* editorial (Chinese state media) replied that "the marginal impact of further US export controls on China's AI industry is diminishing rapidly" and that the restrictions will weaken US chipmakers in global markets.

**Context:** the BIS remote-access rule of 16 November also covers data centres in the EU; California is investigating whether Nvidia illegally sold advanced chips to China.

**What to watch:** Commerce's next steps on licence enforcement; the DOJ probe; any MOFCOM statement on Monday.

**Sources:** [Jay Clayton on Fox News](https://x.com/i/status/2124531991085207941), [ABC News transcript](https://abcnews.com/Politics/week-transcript-11-22-26-director-national-intelligence/story?id=138345755), [Bloomberg](https://x.com/i/status/2124543467439174101), [The Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/world/united-states/spy-chief-says-us-probing-alleged-spy-tied-to-former-nvidia-ceo), [Global Times](https://www.globaltimes.cn/page/202611/1374822.shtml)
articles.why: Washington decides which tier of computing power each country receives, and Europe, without a top-end chip of its own, gets the "less exquisite" tier unless licensed otherwise.

articles.headline: US group IQVIA nears a $1.1 billion takeover of the UK's Quotient Sciences
articles.summary:
**IQVIA Holdings, the US clinical-research group, is closing in on a takeover of about $1.1 billion of Quotient Sciences (Nottingham, UK), a contract development and manufacturing organisation for early-stage medicines, and a deal could be announced as soon as Monday 23 November, according to people familiar with the matter (Bloomberg).**

Quotient helps drug-makers formulate new medicines, manufacture them for clinical trials and test how they behave. It has been owned by the private-equity firm Permira since 2019. IQVIA and Permira declined to comment.

**Context:** the 14:30 edition covered US takeovers of European defence suppliers (Steyr Motors, Truflo Marine, Tekne); CEAFE is tracking US acquisitions of strategic European companies.

**What to watch:** a formal announcement; any review under the UK National Security and Investment Act or by the CMA.

**Sources:** [Bloomberg](https://x.com/i/status/2124514525453959419), [Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/private-equity/iqvia-said-to-near-1-1-billion-deal-for-uks-quotient-sciences)
articles.why: another link in a strategic European supply chain, early-stage drug development and clinical-trial manufacturing, would pass to US ownership.

articles.headline: Thailand plans to curb exports of chemicals used in Myanmar's rare-earth mining
articles.summary:
**Thailand will restrict the export and transit of chemicals used in rare-earth mining and processing to Myanmar and other "relevant countries", Deputy Prime Minister Yodchanan Wongsawat said, after arsenic contamination of the Kok, Sai and Ruak rivers in northern Thailand was linked to rare-earth mining in Myanmar's Shan state (Reuters).**

The measure is planned, not yet in force: the National Security Council is compiling a list of chemicals, with no start date published. Thailand, China and Myanmar hold ministerial talks on 24 November and working-level talks on 25–26 November.

**What to watch:** the trilateral talks; the published chemical list.

**Sources:** [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2124488153146835338), [Bangkok Post](https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/3359296/riverarsenic-control-plan-advances-public-confidence-low), [The Nation](https://www.nationthailand.com/news/general/40073770), [Thai PBS World](https://www.thaipbsworld.com/world/573123)
articles.why: Myanmar's mines are a major source of the heavy rare earths refined in China; a curb could tighten supply of the magnets on which European wind, automotive and defence industries depend, and Europe has little refining capacity of its own.

articles.headline: China demands the US revoke the FCC ban on Chinese telecom operators and threatens "necessary measures"
articles.summary:
**China's Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) on Sunday urged the United States to "immediately revoke" the Federal Communications Commission's ban on China Telecom, China Unicom, China Mobile and other carriers on its "Covered List" obtaining US internet telephone-number resources, and said China "will take necessary measures" to defend its interests.**

MOFCOM said the FCC, which voted on 19 November, "abused its regulatory power" and generalised "so-called national-security risks" without a factual basis, pushing US–China "decoupling" in telecoms, testing and certification against the "important consensus" reached by the two heads of state. The FCC justified the order by the fight against illegal robocalls (The Straits Times).

**Context:** the dispute is the latest step in a chain of action and reaction: FCC bans on Huawei and other Chinese equipment; an October 2026 decision to bar Chinese laboratories from testing US-bound electronics from December 2028; the optical-transceiver import ban; the numbering-resources ban of 19 November; and now MOFCOM's threat of countermeasures, days after Xi hosted Trump in Shenzhen.

**What to watch:** whether China names concrete countermeasures (unreliable entity list, export controls on critical minerals); any EU position on the FCC testing-lab rule.

**Sources:** [MOFCOM](https://www.mofcom.gov.cn/xwfb/sjfzrfb/art/2026/art_a8a703480a3a4720a247c584d9f77eeb.html), [The Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/china-slams-malicious-us-ban-on-telecom-firms-phone-number-access), [South China Morning Post](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3375364/beijing-vows-defend-interests-us-bars-chinese-telecoms-accessing-phone-numbers), [Global Times](https://x.com/i/status/2124322059748806687)
articles.why: Washington and Beijing are splitting telecoms, testing and certification into two blocs, one regulatory decision at a time. European operators and test labs working in both markets may be asked to choose, and Europe has no say in either the FCC's lists or China's countermeasures.

articles.headline: Update: Iran's "line-breaker" tanker turns out to be a spoof as tankers gather at Kharg
articles.summary:
**Early on Sunday MarineTraffic showed a vessel named "Khat Shekan" (Persian for "line-breaker") sailing through the Strait of Hormuz, which was widely read as Iran's first attempt to break the US naval blockade; TankerTrackers said it was a spoof.**

Satellite imagery showed no vessel, the call sign belongs to a Liberian-flagged tanker and the listed destination implied an impossible transit time (Iran International, Euronews). Satellite images and tracking data show more than 14 tankers gathered around Kharg Island, Iran's main export terminal, and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Friday that "the blockade must be broken". President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran faces a "silent economic war" tougher than the missile war.

**Context:** the US blockade reached its 130th day on Saturday 21 November (Euronews). No crude-laden tanker has been confirmed crossing the blockade line since 12 July, according to UANI figures. Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said a ceasefire is needed to ease the war's "economic burden".

**What to watch:** a satellite-confirmed tanker leaving Kharg and the US response; the Qatari mediation; Monday's oil-market reaction.

**Sources:** [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/22/tracking-site-says-iranian-tanker-reportedly-sailing-through-strait-of-hormuz-does-not-exi), [Iran International](https://www.iranintl.com/en/202611211549), [The Week](https://www.theweek.in/news/middle-east/2026/11/22/the-mystery-of-khat-shekan-alleged-iranian-oil-tanker-challenging-us-blockade-does-not-exist.html), [Anadolu, Pezeshkian](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/iran-facing-silent-economic-war-that-is-tougher-than-missile-war-says-president-pezeshkian/4132988), [Al Jazeera, Fidan](https://x.com/i/status/2124355960420663559)
articles.why: the blockade is a US sanctions instrument enforced at sea, and its course sets the oil prices Europe pays, without Europe having a say in it.

articles.headline: COP31 in Antalya ends its overtime without agreement after fossil fuels are dropped from the text
articles.summary:
**On its second day of overtime, the COP31 presidency (Türkiye, with Australia as co-host) published a new draft that does not mention fossil fuels, and on Sunday COP31 President Murat Kurum told the closing plenary: "I understand that there's no agreement on this text. For that reason, these decisions have not been adopted"; at 12:37 GMT he said there would be no new draft (BBC).**

The EU, Panama, the Pacific states and others had demanded explicit fossil-fuel language; observers said Saudi Arabia and other oil producers pushed to keep it out (Al Jazeera, BBC). Speaking for the EU, Irish Climate Minister Darragh O'Brien said: "We will not endorse a cover decision, or an Antalya Pact, that does not even mention fossil fuels" (AFP); France's Monique Barbut called the proposal a "backward" step. The draft kept a target of 35% of energy consumption from electricity by 2035 and, for the first time, acknowledged that the world is on course to exceed 1.5 °C (BBC, Carbon Copy).

**Context:** the first draft, on Monday, mentioned fossil fuels six times; the second, on Thursday, none (BBC).

**What to watch:** the formal closure of COP31 and the next steps under the UN climate process; previous COP obligations remain in force.

**Sources:** [BBC live](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/crly5w901n20t), [BBC](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cq7827z2841zo), [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/22/fossil-fuel-impasse-pushes-cop31-climate-talks-into-second-day-of-overtime), [AP](https://apnews.com/article/climate-un-turkey-fossil-fuels-global-warming-f6e36c4caf13ec6fed57c9f077cbd067), [Carbon Copy](https://www.carboncopy.info/cop-31-final-text-no-transition-away-from-fossil-fuels-no-120-billion-adaptation-finance-target-includes-35-by-35-electrification-and-ccus), [dpa](https://x.com/i/status/2124460588382179822), [AFP](https://www.afp.com/en/eu-will-not-endorse-climate-deal-throwing-cop31-deal-doubt)
articles.why: the EU is the main bloc pushing a transition away from fossil fuels while it imports most of its oil and gas and pays crisis prices because of Hormuz; without a global agreement its industry carries costs that competitors do not share.

articles.headline: Japan plans to list organic chemicals as critical products because of Hormuz
articles.summary:
**Japan's government is considering adding organic chemical products, such as ethylene and propylene made from naphtha, to the list of "specified critical products" under its Economic Security Promotion Act, sources told Jiji (The Japan Times).**

They are inputs for plastics and for high-performance materials used in semiconductor manufacturing. A panel of experts will discuss it, with the aim of amending the Cabinet order by the end of fiscal 2026 (March 2027). The trigger is the disruption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz: Japan imports most of the oil used to make naphtha from the Middle East, domestic chemical output is falling and dependence on China is rising. Designated products receive state support for stable supply; the current list has 12 categories, including semiconductors, batteries, permanent magnets and critical minerals.

**What to watch:** the panel's list and the Cabinet order.

**Sources:** [The Japan Times](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/11/22/japan/organic-chemicals-critical-items/), [Japanese Law Translation](https://www.japaneselawtranslation.go.jp/en/laws/view/5008/en)
articles.why: Japan has a single national law and list for critical supply chains, with support attached, and updates it within months of a shock; Europe's chemical industry faces the same energy-price pressure with tools spread across the Critical Raw Materials Act, the Chips Act and national schemes.

articles.headline: US senators propose a five-year extension of the 48D chip-investment tax credit
articles.summary:
**Senators John Cornyn (R-TX) and Mark Kelly (D-AZ) introduced bill S.5809 on 19 November to extend the Section 48D advanced manufacturing investment credit for five years; the credit, created by the CHIPS Act, is due to expire at the end of 2026 (Congress.gov).**

The Semiconductor Industry Association says the incentive has helped catalyse more than $825 billion in private semiconductor investment (SIA figure; it does not state the period). The bill has been referred to the Senate Finance Committee.

**What to watch:** the Finance Committee's handling of the bill.

**Sources:** [SIA](https://www.semiconductors.org/sia-applauds-introduction-of-bipartisan-legislation-to-extend-semiconductor-investment-credit/), [SIA on X](https://x.com/i/status/2124222653602889949), [Congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-bill/5809)
articles.why: the US keeps paying to attract chip plants, including those of European and Asian firms, while restricting where they can sell; the EU Chips Act has no comparable tax credit.

articles.headline: Honeywell se queda con las patentes del motor SABRE de la quebrada Reaction Engines por 884.000 libras, tras unos 60 millones de libras de dinero público británico
articles.summary:
Los registros de patentes de EE. UU. muestran que el 28 de julio de 2026 las patentes de Reaction Engines Ltd, la empresa británica que desarrolló el motor cohete aeróbico SABRE y su preenfriador de microtubos, se cedieron a Honeywell Aerospace US LLC por parte de los administradores concursales de PwC (registro de Google Patents de la patente US11162424B2, «Heat exchangers», inventores Alan Bond y Richard Varvill). Reaction Engines entró en concurso en octubre de 2024 con deudas de más de 160 millones de libras. El informe de PwC (hasta finales de abril de 2026, fechado el 29 de mayo) indicó que la venta de la propiedad intelectual se cerró en abril con 884.000 libras en depósitos no reembolsables, el valor que le habían dado los administradores, pero no identificó al comprador (FlightGlobal, 14 de junio; Oxford Chronicle, 9 de julio). La identidad del comprador se ha conocido en X el 27 de noviembre a partir de la cesión de patentes. La Agencia Espacial del Reino Unido aportó unos 60 millones de libras al SABRE y la ESA validó el preenfriador en 2019 (Inngot, 16 de junio). Antes de quebrar, Reaction Engines suministraba intercambiadores de calor a un consorcio liderado por Honeywell en un proyecto de pila de hidrógeno del programa europeo Clean Aviation (FlightGlobal). Reacciones: ninguna declaración de Honeywell, del Gobierno británico ni de la ESA.

**Datos clave**

- Cesión de patentes a Honeywell Aerospace US LLC registrada el 28 de julio de 2026; cedentes: PwC y Reaction Engines Ltd (en concurso) (Google Patents).

- Venta de la propiedad intelectual cerrada en abril de 2026; 884.000 libras en depósitos; comprador no identificado en el informe de PwC (FlightGlobal, Inngot).

- Financiación pública: unos 60 millones de libras de la Agencia Espacial del Reino Unido para el SABRE (Inngot); unos 170 de 208 empleados despedidos en 2024 (Oxford Chronicle).
articles.why: es el patrón que el responsable de CEAFE denuncia desde hace años: tecnología iniciada con dinero europeo (el proyecto LAPCAT, financiado por la UE en 2008, y la ESA desde 2010, como recordó @F_CEAFE en 2021) acaba en manos estadounidenses. Treinta años de conocimiento en hipersónica y gestión térmica se han vendido por menos de un millón de libras, una pequeña parte del dinero público invertido, en una venta concursal en la que no pujó ningún comprador europeo. Ni el Reino Unido ni la ESA tenían un mecanismo para mantener esa propiedad intelectual en Europa. Una vez más, Europa paga la investigación y Estados Unidos recoge los resultados.

articles.headline: Actualización: Francia se suma a los Países Bajos contra la ley estadounidense MATCH, mientras Pekín mantiene su parte de la tregua
articles.summary:
El ministro francés de Comercio Exterior, Nicolas Forissier, dijo a Bloomberg el 27 de noviembre que Francia comparte la preocupación neerlandesa por el alcance extraterritorial de la ley MATCH, que obligaría a los aliados a endurecer los controles sobre equipos de fabricación de chips como las máquinas de litografía DUV de inmersión de ASML vendidas y mantenidas en China. «Todos los instrumentos de la Unión Europea siguen disponibles», afirmó, «pero no reaccionaremos de forma impulsiva». El proyecto se estudia para incluirlo en la ley anual de defensa de EE. UU., que suele aprobarse en diciembre. Los ministros de Comercio de la UE se reúnen en Bruselas el lunes 30 de noviembre, con el representante comercial de EE. UU., Jamieson Greer, por videoconferencia. Forissier advirtió también de la «erosión gradual de los beneficios del acuerdo de Turnberry» (Bloomberg vía Mint). El primer ministro neerlandés planea tratar la ley MATCH con Trump en el G20 (Reuters, X). El ministro neerlandés Sjoerd Sjoerdsma dice trabajar con la Comisión, Alemania y Francia contra el proyecto; un experto citado por Reuters menciona el Estatuto de Bloqueo de la UE (TrendForce). Por el lado de la reacción: China no ha respondido por ahora a las últimas restricciones estadounidenses a los chips. Su Anuncio n.º 59 del MOFCOM mantiene suspendida la prohibición de exportar galio, germanio y antimonio a EE. UU. desde hoy, 28 de noviembre, hasta el 27 de enero de 2027 (recogido el 24 de noviembre); Bloomberg lo interpreta como que Pekín «cumple su parte del acuerdo, por ahora».

**Datos clave**

- ASML: se espera que China aporte cerca de una quinta parte de sus ingresos en 2026 (Bloomberg).

- Ley MATCH: apoyo de ambos partidos; ampliaría las restricciones de la EUV a la venta y mantenimiento de la DUV de inmersión (Bloomberg, TrendForce).
articles.why: dos grandes Estados miembros dicen ya abiertamente que la ley estadounidense no debe decidir qué venden las empresas europeas. Una respuesta creíble exige que la UE actúe como bloque: el consejo de Comercio del lunes es la primera prueba. Es la reciprocidad que CEAFE reclama.

articles.headline: Actualización: Sanciones de la UE — Bulgaria bloquea el 22.º paquete contra Rusia para reabrir las importaciones de arrabio ruso
articles.summary: Bulgaria bloquea el 22.º paquete de sanciones de la UE contra Rusia y pide levantar las prohibiciones ya aprobadas de importar arrabio y equipos de minería rusos (Kyiv Independent, 27 de noviembre). También se opone a sancionar a una empresa química rusa, alegando el suministro de fertilizantes, y a una persona vinculada a una instalación nuclear de doble uso. Funcionarios europeos y ucranianos sospechan un motivo comercial. Italia también ha planteado objeciones, en su caso a la prohibición de que europeos formen parte de consejos de empresas rusas.
articles.why: las sanciones exigen unanimidad, así que un solo Estado miembro puede frenar el paquete. El arrabio es un insumo del acero, un sector en el que la industria ucraniana sufre los ataques rusos.

articles.headline: Comercio de EE. UU. — el déficit de bienes sube a 149.500 millones de dólares en octubre por un récord de importaciones ligadas a la IA
articles.summary: El déficit comercial de bienes de EE. UU. (dato avanzado) aumentó un 10,7 % en octubre, hasta 149.500 millones de dólares; las importaciones subieron un 6,1 %, hasta un récord de 365.300 millones, impulsadas por los bienes de equipo (+8,5 %, hasta 171.400 millones, cerca de un 80 % más que un año antes) vinculados a los centros de datos de IA; las exportaciones subieron un 3,2 %, hasta 215.800 millones (Oficina del Censo de EE. UU.; Anadolu; Reuters). Es el cuarto aumento mensual seguido (Bloomberg).
articles.why: pese a los aranceles, el déficit de EE. UU. sigue creciendo, lo que refuerza en Washington los argumentos para más aranceles de la Sección 301 contra sus socios, entre ellos la UE.

articles.headline: Tesla solicita comprar activos de EMAG, el fabricante alemán de máquinas-herramienta
articles.summary:
Tesla ha notificado a la Oficina Federal de Cárteles de Alemania (Bundeskartellamt) su intención de comprar activos del grupo EMAG, un fabricante de máquinas-herramienta con sede en Salach, cerca de Stuttgart (Reuters; tagesschau/SWR). La autoridad de competencia la registra como una adquisición de activos, expediente B5-132/26, notificada el 23 de noviembre y publicada el 27. Los mercados citados son las máquinas para el mecanizado de precisión y electroquímico de piezas metálicas y el procesado por láser. No se han dado a conocer ni el precio, ni la lista de activos, ni la plantilla afectada. Tesla declinó hacer comentarios y EMAG no respondió a Reuters. Tesla ya había creado una sociedad, «Tesla Machining Technologies Management SE», con domicilio en la sede de EMAG en Salach (tagesschau; Automotive World, citando a Business Insider). El Stuttgarter Nachrichten informa de que unos 220 empleados de EMAG pasarían a Tesla; ninguna de las dos empresas lo ha confirmado. EMAG fabrica tornos, rectificadoras y talladoras de engranajes para las transmisiones de los coches. Más recientemente, también las fabrica para los pequeños engranajes de precisión de las articulaciones de los robots humanoides, un punto débil conocido del robot Optimus de Tesla. EMAG se fundó en 1867. Según Business Insider, perdió unos 42 millones de euros con unos ingresos de 496 millones en 2024 y anunció 455 despidos en noviembre de 2025. Por ahora no ha habido reacción de EMAG, del Gobierno alemán ni del estado de Baden-Wurtemberg; el examen de competencia es el único control que consta.

**Antecedentes (archivo CEAFE):** es el último caso del registro de CEAFE sobre compras estadounidenses de empresas europeas. El 19 de octubre, el fabricante estadounidense de drones Red Cat lanzó una oferta de unos 205 millones de euros por la austriaca Steyr Motors, que fabrica motores para vehículos militares; la oferta está abierta hasta el 18 de diciembre y siguen pendientes las autorizaciones de inversión extranjera (https://ir.steyr-motors.com/en/2026/10/21/steyr-motors-ag-business-combination-agreement-signed-with-red-cat-holdings-inc-and-smot-acquisition-gmbh-binding-commitments-agreed-for-the-steyr-site-and-employees/). En 2024, Honeywell compró la italiana Civitanavi Systems, fabricante de sistemas de navegación, por unos 200 millones de euros. @F_CEAFE publicó hoy la noticia de EMAG como «Another 🇪🇺 tech gem acquired by the U.S.» («Otra joya tecnológica europea comprada por EE. UU.») (https://x.com/i/status/2126367050469638297).

**Qué vigilar:** la decisión de la autoridad de competencia (primera fase de un mes); si Berlín abre un examen de inversión extranjera; el precio, los activos y los empleos cuando Tesla o EMAG se pronuncien.

Fuentes: @F_CEAFE https://x.com/i/status/2126367050469638297, Reuters https://x.com/i/status/2126325232927461743 (reproducción https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/tesla-plans-acquire-german-manufacturing-systems-group-emag), tagesschau/SWR https://www.tagesschau.de/inland/regional/badenwuerttemberg/swr-tesla-uebernimmt-maschinenbauer-emag-spezialmaschinen-fuer-humanoide-roboter-100.html, Automotive World https://www.automotiveworld.com/news/tesla-files-plan-to-acquire-german-machine-maker-emag/, Servospace https://servospace.io/news/tesla-machining-technologies-emag-salach-220-staff-optimus-gears, Teslarati https://www.teslarati.com/tesla-bolster-optimus-company-acquisition-emag-germany/.
articles.why: EMAG es una típica empresa industrial alemana de tamaño medio, con 159 años de conocimiento difícil de reconstruir. El mecanizado de engranajes de precisión se está convirtiendo en un cuello de botella para los robots humanoides. La crisis del automóvil ha debilitado a la empresa, y ahora un comprador estadounidense puede llevarse máquinas, personas y conocimiento mediante una compra de activos, sin hacerse con todo el grupo. Es el patrón que CEAFE sigue todo el mes: la energía cara y la demanda débil debilitan a la industria europea, y el capital estadounidense compra las mejores piezas. Un fabricante de máquinas-herramienta no es una empresa de defensa, así que no es seguro que Alemania abra un examen de inversión extranjera. Ningún Estado miembro tiene por sí solo una herramienta para mantener esta capacidad en Europa, salvo que aparezca un comprador europeo.

articles.headline: Francia entra oficialmente en recesión: el PIB cayó un 0,2 % en el tercer trimestre
articles.summary:
El instituto de estadística francés, el INSEE, publicó sus cuentas detalladas el 27 de noviembre. El producto interior bruto (PIB) cayó un 0,2 % en el tercer trimestre, frente a una primera estimación del −0,1 %. El segundo trimestre también se revisó, del 0,0 % a un ligerísimo descenso. Francia está, por tanto, en recesión «técnica» desde el segundo trimestre (franceinfo; AFP vía France 24). El PIB ha caído ya tres trimestres seguidos, hasta 662.600 millones de euros. Las exportaciones bajaron un 1,6 % tras subir un 2,9 %, y el comercio exterior restó 0,6 puntos al crecimiento. La inversión empresarial cayó un 0,8 % y la inversión en bienes manufacturados un 1,8 %. El consumo de los hogares subió un 0,3 %. The Wall Street Journal relaciona la caída de las exportaciones con las olas de calor del verano, que frenaron las fábricas de Airbus. El crecimiento ya «adquirido» para 2026 es solo del 0,1 %, frente a la previsión del Gobierno del 0,5 %; según el INSEE, alcanzar esa previsión exigiría crecer un 1,4 % en el cuarto trimestre. El déficit público subió al 5,6 % del PIB en el trimestre. Esa misma tarde, dos miembros del Consejo de Gobierno del Banco Central Europeo, Joachim Nagel y Primož Dolenc, dijeron que el banco probablemente tendrá que volver a subir los tipos de interés en diciembre porque la inflación no cede (Bloomberg). Al Jazeera señala que la inflación de la zona del euro está en máximos de tres años, impulsada por los precios de la energía.

**Antecedentes (archivo CEAFE):** el 30 de enero de 2024, CEAFE difundió la información de Reuters según la cual la economía francesa no había crecido en el cuarto trimestre de 2023, según el INSEE (https://x.com/i/status/1752316330617839681). La edición de las 14:30 del 26 de noviembre comparó el presupuesto alemán de 2027, con 139.000 millones de euros para defensa, con el de Francia; la edición de las 08:30 de hoy recogió los recortes de empleo en SAP y los paros de fábricas de Stellantis.

**Qué vigilar:** el dato adelantado de inflación de la zona del euro, el 2 de diciembre; la reunión de diciembre del Banco Central Europeo; el debate presupuestario en París con un déficit del 5,6 % del PIB.

Fuentes: INSEE https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/9165918, France 24 (AFP) https://www.france24.com/fr/info-en-continu/20261127-france-le-pib-recule-de-0-2-au-troisi%C3%A8me-trimestre-apr%C3%A8s-r%C3%A9vision-%C3%A0-la-baisse, franceinfo https://www.franceinfo.fr/economie/croissance/le-pib-recule-de-0-2-en-france-au-troisieme-trimestre-apres-une-revision-a-la-baisse-de-l-insee_8302671.html, The Wall Street Journal https://x.com/i/status/2126345006419955875, Bloomberg https://x.com/i/status/2126362955906183217, BFMTV https://x.com/i/status/2126368613389205534, Bloomberg (Nagel) https://x.com/i/status/2126342820176740417, Bloomberg (Dolenc) https://x.com/i/status/2126331492963942794, Al Jazeera https://x.com/i/status/2126305037303615601.

**CEAFE:** Un recordatorio gráfico de que el mercado y la política de un solo Estado europeo no equivalen a los de una potencia global.
articles.why: la segunda economía de la zona del euro se contrae mientras el Banco Central Europeo sigue subiendo tipos contra una inflación impulsada por la energía. La industria queda atrapada por los dos lados: energía cara y dinero caro. La caída de las exportaciones y de la inversión manufacturera son las señales de desindustrialización que CEAFE sigue. Llegan mientras compradores estadounidenses se quedan con empresas europeas debilitadas, como EMAG hoy. Ningún Estado miembro puede arreglarlo solo; una política energética e industrial común es la única escala que funciona.

articles.headline: Actualización: controles de EE. UU. a los chips en el Sudeste Asiático — el freno a los envíos de Nvidia congela la financiación de centros de datos
articles.summary:
The New York Times confirmó el 27 de noviembre que los operadores de centros de datos de Malasia, Singapur, Tailandia e Indonesia tienen en suspenso sus pedidos de los chips más avanzados de Nvidia. El Financial Times añade que Aolani, una empresa de computación en la nube con sede en Singapur que pensaba alquilar capacidad de cálculo a ByteDance, está afectada: los bancos han parado unos 500 millones de dólares de crédito, y ByteDance podría abandonar el acuerdo. El freno sigue a la norma publicada el 16 de noviembre por la Oficina de Industria y Seguridad del Departamento de Comercio de EE. UU. La norma exige licencias para exportar chips avanzados a Indonesia, Malasia, Singapur, Tailandia y Brasil, y restringe el acceso remoto a ellos; los proveedores de nube tienen 90 días para obtener una licencia. «Hay una norma nueva, pero ninguna orientación sobre cómo aplicarla… Está causando un caos absoluto en la región», dijo un directivo del sector al Financial Times. Según el mismo diario, Nvidia contabilizó 104.000 millones de dólares de ingresos a través de su filial de Singapur en 2025. Mientras tanto, el presidente Trump prevé visitar la próxima semana una fábrica de chips en Phoenix (The Washington Post). Todavía no hay declaración oficial de los cuatro gobiernos ni de China.

**Antecedentes (archivo CEAFE):** la edición de las 08:30 del 26 de noviembre informó por primera vez de que Nvidia había congelado los envíos de servidores de IA (inteligencia artificial) a Malasia, Singapur, Tailandia e Indonesia. La norma del Departamento de Comercio del 16 de noviembre está en https://www.bis.gov/press-release/bis-issues-rule-addressing-remote-access-american-super-intelligence-technology.

**Qué vigilar:** las orientaciones de EE. UU. sobre el proceso de licencias; las reacciones de Malasia y Singapur; la rueda de prensa del Ministerio de Exteriores chino del lunes.

Fuentes: Reuters https://x.com/i/status/2126357884778733732, Financial Times https://www.ft.com/content/7838a715-07d4-4605-aa60-21f5af2b2370, The New York Times https://cn.nytimes.com/business/20261127/nvidia-southeast-asia-sales/dual/, Data Center Dynamics https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/nvidia-halts-server-shipments-to-malaysia-singapore-thailand-and-indonesia-in-wake-of-new-dept-of-commerce-export-rule-report/, Departamento de Comercio de EE. UU. https://www.bis.gov/press-release/bis-issues-rule-addressing-remote-access-american-super-intelligence-technology, The Washington Post https://x.com/i/status/2126307587448611085.
articles.why: es el poder extraterritorial de EE. UU. en la práctica: una norma redactada en Washington frena en pocos días la inversión privada en terceros países. La misma norma sobre el acceso remoto cubre también los centros de datos de la UE. Europa no fabrica chips de IA a gran escala, así que sus planes de nube e inteligencia artificial también dependen de licencias estadounidenses.

articles.headline: Actualización: Irak pide a la OPEP una cuota mayor en lugar de abandonarla, antes de la reunión de la OPEP+ del domingo
articles.summary:
El ministro iraquí del Petróleo, Basim Mohammed Judair, dijo el 27 de noviembre en Kirkuk: «Estamos negociando con la OPEP para elevar el techo de producción de Irak» (Bloomberg; Reuters vía Devdiscourse). Pidió a los miembros que tengan en cuenta las «circunstancias excepcionales» de Irak durante cinco décadas. También dijo que Bagdad quiere más inversión estadounidense en su sector petrolero (Shafaq News). La publicación especializada Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) informa de que Irak ha rechazado la evaluación independiente de la OPEP sobre su capacidad máxima sostenible, 4,9 millones de barriles diarios. Irak quiere que se le reconozcan unos 6 millones de barriles diarios; su cuota actual ronda los 4,4 millones. Los ministros de la OPEP+ se reúnen por videoconferencia el domingo 29 de noviembre y se espera que mantengan los objetivos actuales. El ministro inauguró además una estación de bombeo en el oleoducto Irak-Turquía rehabilitado, que arranca con 300.000 barriles diarios. En el Golfo, el Mando Central de EE. UU. dijo que inutilizó un buque mercante en el golfo de Omán el 26 de noviembre, después de que su tripulación intentara burlar el bloqueo naval estadounidense desde Bandar Abás. La OPEP no ha comentado la petición de Irak.

**Antecedentes (archivo CEAFE):** la edición de las 14:30 recogió una exclusiva de Reuters según la cual EE. UU. empujó a Irak y Venezuela a plantearse salir de la OPEP, y el Ministerio del Petróleo iraquí aconsejó pedir una cuota mayor (https://x.com/i/status/2126213852572639277). El 28 de agosto, CEAFE difundió una información de Bloomberg, a través de The Kobeissi Letter, según la cual Venezuela había hablado con responsables estadounidenses sobre su salida de la OPEP (https://x.com/i/status/2093242918030938214).

**Qué vigilar:** la decisión de la OPEP+ del domingo; cualquier declaración de Venezuela; el resultado de la petición de cuota de Irak.

Fuentes: Bloomberg https://x.com/i/status/2126350386130817194 y https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-27/iraq-talking-to-opec-about-its-production-ceiling-minister-says, MEES https://www.mees.com/2026/11/27/opec/iraqs-msc-rejection-clouds-opec-meeting-build-up/2037d770-ea6e-11f1-ab06-41c99db91919, Shafaq News https://shafaq.com/en/Economy/Baghdad-seeks-higher-OPEC-quota-US-oil-investment, Reuters (reproducción) https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/international/4013283-iraq-in-talks-with-opec-for-higher-oil-production-ceiling-minister-says, Mando Central de EE. UU. https://x.com/i/status/2126367015493603807, Agencia Internacional de la Energía https://x.com/i/status/2126338265103974871.
articles.why: Bagdad sigue la línea que describió Reuters: quedarse en la OPEP, pero pedir más barriles. Eso mantiene unida a la OPEP por ahora, pero la palanca estadounidense sobre el dinero del petróleo iraquí sigue ahí. Europa importa casi todo su petróleo. La Agencia Internacional de la Energía afirma que la crisis de Ormuz es ahora el principal motor de la nueva capacidad renovable en el mundo, que es también la vía de Europa para reducir su dependencia.

articles.headline: La Auditoría argentina: un tercio del oro del banco central está en Londres
articles.summary:
La Auditoría General de la Nación de Argentina (AGN) aprobó por mayoría, el 26 de noviembre, su informe sobre el traslado de oro al exterior por el Banco Central (BCRA). Entre junio y agosto de 2024, el Banco Central envió 1.000 lingotes de oro en cuatro envíos al Banco de Inglaterra, en Londres. El Banco de Inglaterra actuó como custodio para el Banco de Pagos Internacionales, el banco de los bancos centrales, con sede en Basilea. 115 lingotes se refundieron según los estándares del mercado de Londres (La Nación; El Cronista; Infobae). Las onzas se abonaron en una cuenta de «oro no asignado». Eso significa que Argentina tiene ahora un derecho sobre una cantidad de oro, no sobre lingotes concretos. La parte de sus 61,7 toneladas de oro que está en esa cuenta pasó del 11,3 % al 31,6 %. Los auditores no encontraron un procedimiento aprobado para el traslado ni una evaluación completa de riesgos, incluida una cláusula que somete las disputas a arbitraje en Zúrich. No tuvieron acceso a la póliza de seguro. También hallaron tres colocaciones de 32.000 onzas cada una a finales de 2024 que el Banco Central había negado. Pidieron una estrategia más prudente y la repatriación del oro (Perfil). El Banco Central sostiene que los envíos estaban documentados y aprobados, y que su desmentido se refería solo a 2025. Tres auditores votaron en contra del informe. El presidente de la AGN, Juan Manuel Olmos, es además apoderado del opositor Partido Justicialista (peronista) (La Nación). Algunas publicaciones en X afirman que el oro fue «robado» o enviado a EE. UU.; la auditoría no dice eso.

**Antecedentes (archivo CEAFE):** en agosto de 2024, CEAFE difundió publicaciones según las cuales el Gobierno del presidente Milei había empezado a enviar al exterior parte del oro argentino (https://x.com/i/status/1818974494712635538). La edición de las 14:30 de hoy trató el control estadounidense del dinero del petróleo venezolano e iraquí.

**Qué vigilar:** la respuesta formal del Banco Central; cualquier petición de repatriar el oro.

Fuentes: Auditoría General de la Nación (AGN) https://x.com/i/status/2126309467264524721 y https://x.com/i/status/2126309428559290660, La Nación https://www.lanacion.com.ar/economia/tras-el-envio-de-1000-lingotes-el-banco-central-paso-a-tener-casi-un-tercio-de-su-oro-en-el-exterior-nid26112026/, El Cronista https://www.cronista.com/economia-politica/oro-del-bcra-la-agn-aprobo-una-auditoria-con-hallazgos-que-complican-al-central/, Perfil https://www.perfil.com/politica/el-oro-argentino-esta-en-londres-y-el-pais-ya-no-tiene-custodia-fisica-de-los-lingotes-segun-auditoria-de-la-agn-aZBqT8U8aLA8, EFE https://efe.com/economia/2026-11-27/auditoria-envio-lingotes-de-oro-banco-central-argentino-inglaterra/, Infobae https://www.infobae.com/economia/2026/11/26/segun-la-agn-el-bcra-envio-1000-barras-de-oro-al-banco-de-inglaterra-y-fundio-115-lingotes/, Steve Hanke https://x.com/i/status/2126309075877048341.
articles.why: las reservas guardadas en el extranjero pueden congelarse o usarse como palanca, como muestran el oro venezolano en el Banco de Inglaterra y el control estadounidense del dinero del petróleo de Venezuela e Irak. Dónde guarda un país su oro es una cuestión de soberanía. Europa tiene el mismo debate sobre las reservas depositadas en Nueva York.

articles.headline: Actualización: aranceles de la Sección 301 — el consejo empresarial chino exige su retirada e India dice que su acuerdo con EE. UU. está casi cerrado
articles.summary:
Las empresas chinas, a través del Consejo Chino para el Fomento del Comercio Internacional, instaron a EE. UU. a retirar los aranceles adicionales propuestos contra China y otras 13 economías (Xinhua, medio estatal chino). Los aranceles derivan de la investigación estadounidense de la «Sección 301» sobre el «exceso de capacidad estructural». El ministro de Exteriores de Sudáfrica, Ronald Lamola, declaró: «Hemos sido muy cordiales. Por desgracia, la agresión ha venido de EE. UU.». Aun así, dejó la puerta abierta a seguir negociando (Bloomberg). El ministro de Comercio de India dijo que el acuerdo comercial entre India y EE. UU. está a punto de cerrarse (Reuters). Un análisis de Al Jazeera señala que los nuevos aranceles golpean sobre todo a China, semanas antes de que Trump y Xi vuelvan a reunirse en la cumbre del G20 en Miami. Reuters los describe como un intento de «arrancar el comercio mundial de las manos de China». Global Times, medio estatal chino, publicó un artículo de opinión según el cual la UE debería superar su «ansiedad por el déficit» en el comercio con China. Bloomberg informa de que el déficit comercial de bienes de EE. UU. aumentó en octubre por cuarto mes consecutivo. La Comisión Europea sigue sin responder.

**Antecedentes (archivo CEAFE):** el 25 de noviembre, la Oficina del Representante Comercial de EE. UU. afirmó que «con la Sección 301, el presidente Trump va país por país» (https://x.com/i/status/2125669000369917960). La edición de las 20:30 del 25 de noviembre trató el arancel propuesto del 15 % a todos los productos de la UE, y la de las 14:30 de hoy contó que Japón, India y Vietnam buscaban su propia salida.

**Qué vigilar:** la respuesta de la Comisión; el plazo de comentarios públicos sobre la medida de la Sección 301; la cumbre del G20 en Miami.

Fuentes: Xinhua https://x.com/i/status/2126295651642482711, Bloomberg (Lamola) https://x.com/i/status/2126296535361065439, Reuters (India) https://x.com/i/status/2126311366717780216, Al Jazeera https://x.com/i/status/2126312051551469731, Reuters https://x.com/i/status/2126313844779933733, Global Times https://x.com/i/status/2126338861760667840, Bloomberg (déficit de EE. UU.) https://x.com/i/status/2126321426449703119.
articles.why: cada socio vuelve a buscar su propia salida. La UE es uno de los 14 objetivos, pero no ha respondido. Una Unión de 27 que no responde como bloque invita a acuerdos por separado y convierte a sus miembros en clientes.

articles.headline: La Comisión autoriza sin condiciones la compra de Allfunds por Deutsche Börse por 5.300 millones de euros
articles.summary:
La Comisión Europea autorizó sin condiciones, el 27 de noviembre, la compra de Allfunds por Deutsche Börse (comunicado de la Comisión IP/26/2592; Deutsche Börse). Allfunds es la plataforma de distribución de fondos fundada en Madrid y que cotiza en Ámsterdam. La operación ronda los 5.300 millones de euros (Bloomberg). Aún necesita otras autorizaciones de supervisores y la aprobación de un tribunal inglés para el plan de reorganización (scheme of arrangement) en el Reino Unido. Deutsche Börse prevé cerrarla en el primer trimestre de 2027. Brussels Times señala que la autorización llegó pese a los solapamientos en algunos mercados.

**Qué vigilar:** las autorizaciones pendientes y el cierre en el primer trimestre de 2027.

Fuentes: Comisión Europea https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/api/files/document/print/it/ip_26_2592/IP_26_2592_EN.pdf, Deutsche Börse https://www.deutsche-boerse.com/dbg-en/media/news-stories/press-releases/Deutsche-B-rse-Group-Receives-Unconditional-Clearance-of-Allfunds-Acquisition-from-European-Commission--5789320, Bloomberg https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-27/deutsche-boerse-s-5-3-billion-allfunds-deal-gets-eu-approval, Reuters https://x.com/i/status/2126362972620468384.
articles.why: aquí un comprador europeo se queda con una empresa europea de infraestructura financiera, lo contrario del caso Tesla-EMAG. Contar con actores europeos más grandes en los mercados de capitales forma parte de la unión de ahorros e inversiones, pensada para financiar la industria y la defensa europeas.
